## Note AZ — cpm target removed (owner, 2026-10-15)

Owner rulings: the targets are `cs` and `vanilla`. Vanilla gains complex grass and complex material. Under vanilla a set packs the complex `_m` (the old cpm recipe) only when its shader is complex material; every other vanilla set keeps the env-mask `_m`, so existing vanilla output is unchanged. `cpm` anywhere is a hard error (unreleased, no alias). `presets/cpm-quality.toml` is deleted. Reverses ruling R1 of the complex-grass design for vanilla.

Supersedes, where they name `cpm`: M1 (the packed `cpm` `_m` is now the vanilla complex-material `_m`; channels and the height default 0 unchanged), M2 (the "AO and fuzz under `cpm`" unused inputs now apply to a vanilla complex-material set), M9 (`m` under `vanilla` only), AL1 (the `_orm` feeds the vanilla complex `_m` where it fed the cpm one), P4 and P22 (the borrowed-slot copies are vanilla only), P24 (see M1), R14 (`cpm-quality` no longer exists), AP9 and AP12 (two preset families, AZ6), S-shader-8 (vanilla only), X3 and the complex-grass design's R1 (vanilla has complex grass, AZ5).

- **AZ1 Hard error.** `Target` is `cs` or `vanilla`; `TargetArg` lost `Cpm`. Serde and clap reject `cpm` in `--target` (convert, validate, patch-header), `sdc.toml`, the user config and a preset's `target`. `--preset cpm-quality` and `base = "cpm-quality"` are unknown presets. No alias was added. The CLI exits 2 for each (tested). `sdc-project.toml` has no target field, so it has nothing to reject. A manifest is read leniently (its `target` is not deserialised as `Target`): an old cpm record no longer matches and re-encodes once under `if-changed`. A user preset in `%APPDATA%\sdc\presets\` with `target = "cpm"` is skipped with `CFG-PRESET-SKIPPED` (Note T6, unchanged; the run goes on), and the warning's reason names the unknown variant `cpm`; selecting that preset is then an unknown-preset error (review M3, tested).
- **AZ2 Trigger.** `pack::recipes_for_with(target, raw, pack_recipe, complex)` and `pack::predicted_suffixes(target, complex, roles)` take whether the set's shader is complex material. `plan_packing` passes `ctx.shaders[set].shader == ComplexMaterial`, so an explicit pick (GUI map, `--set set:<id>.shader`) or an auto pick both count. `cs` ignores the flag. An auto pick needs a member already typed `complex_material` (`ComplexM` rule) and no raw map that starts an `_rmaos` (roughness, glossiness, metallic, AO, `_orm`): those make the set a PBR set, whose `pbr` pick falls back to `default` under vanilla, so `complex` stays false. A raw-map-only set therefore needs the explicit shader. Under an auto pick the raw maps that can remain are height, specular, fuzz and opacity, and these vanilla cases change against main (all sanctioned by "explicit or auto"; tested by `packing::an_auto_picked_complex_material_set_packs_the_complex_m`):
  - **Complex `_m` member + height (with or without specular).** Before: height-only planned no recipe (height `PACK-UNUSED-INPUT`); with specular it planned the env mask. Now the complex `_m` is planned from the height (specular as the env mask). With the default `packing.prefer = prepacked` the existing `_m` is still what is written (bytes unchanged), but the set now gets `PACK-CONFLICT` on the `_m` where height-only had none, and the raw maps' reasons change. With `packing.prefer = raw` the packed complex `_m` replaces the file (before: the file was kept for height only, or replaced by a BC4 env mask with specular).
  - **Complex `_m` member + specular only.** Before: the env mask was planned (`PACK-CONFLICT`; with `prefer = raw` a BC4 env mask replaced the complex `_m`). Now no recipe: specular cannot start the complex `_m`, so it is `PACK-UNUSED-INPUT` ("nothing to pack: the complex _m needs …"), there is no `PACK-CONFLICT`, and with `prefer = raw` the original complex `_m` is kept.
  - Everything else (no complex_material member, or any `_rmaos`-starting raw map) is unchanged.
- **AZ3 Recipe id kept.** The recipe id stays `cpm_m` in events, manifests and the event schema; the Rust variant stays `RecipeKind::CpmM`, because `RecipeKind` serialises its variant name and a rename would change the JSON. Only its doc comment changed (it shows as the schema description).
- **AZ4 Prediction order.** The packing-suffix prediction (Note M7) ran before the shader picks, so an explicit complex-material set with only glossiness or height raw maps would not have predicted its `_m` (a `set_has = "m"` rule would miss it). `explicit_shaders` is now pure and runs before the prediction; its `SET-EDIT-STALE` warnings are still emitted at step 6a, in the same order. Tested by `pack_plan::set_has_sees_the_complex_m_of_an_explicit_complex_material_set`, which fails without the change.
- **AZ5 Complex grass under vanilla.** `Shader::available(Vanilla)` is `ALL[3..]` (the old cpm list, 11 shaders); the `VANILLA` list is gone. `suggest_grass` auto-tags under vanilla. `GRASS-VANILLA` is removed (92 codes; event and validation schemas regenerated). `policy::offered` still hides `complex_grass` from the sub-type pickers on both targets (X3, unchanged).
- **AZ6 GUI.** The Mode menu lists cs and vanilla; the vanilla hover text names complex material and complex grass. The preset creator has two families, PBR / Community Shaders then Vanilla; `family_of` is "cs only → PBR / CS, else Vanilla", so `complex_material` lands in Vanilla by derivation and AP12's hand placement is gone. `complex_grass` stays in PBR / CS by hand (AP9). The preset Target dropdown lists from the base, cs, vanilla. The set editor's 8-card limit (AO7) is untouched: the complex `_m` keeps its own card under the slot cards.
- **AZ7 Messages.** `TAG-SRGB-VANILLA` reads "_SRGB is not usable under vanilla shaders [D#4]". `PACK-UNUSED-INPUT` reasons say "the complex _m" where they said "the cpm _m".
- **AZ8 Byte identity.** The goldens and packing tests that ran under `Target::Cpm` run under vanilla with `set:<base>.shader=complex_material`. Checked against main 9fbe6bf: its `sdc --target cpm` and this branch's `sdc --target vanilla` with the set shaders on a 28-file fixture (12 raw-map sets, a loose complex `_m`, diffuse, glow, normal) wrote 16 of 16 identical DDS files, plain and with `packing.fill.height`/`packing.fill.metallic`; plain `--target vanilla` wrote 12 of 12 identical files on both.
- **AZ9 Docs.** README, wiki (Presets-and-Targets, CLI-Reference, GUI-Guide, Troubleshooting, FAQ, Home, Getting-Started, Project-Config, Texture-Types, Mod-Scanning), gui.md and presets-changelog describe two targets. Plans, specs and RULINGS are historical and keep `cpm`.

## Note BA — Head parts are head in the 3D preview (owner, 2026-10-15)

- **BA1 Rule.** Community Shaders treats every geometry under a `BSFaceGenNiNode` as head (skin `bodyTiling` = 1). That node exists only in game, so the preview counts a shape as head when ANY of: (1) its shader type is FaceGen (4), as before; (2) its NIF path is under `meshes/actors/character/facegendata/`; (3) its NIF is the model (MODL) of an HDPT record in the scanned plugins. Rules 2 and 3 are per NIF: every shape of such a NIF is head (type-5 mouths, teeth, etc.; RenderDoc capture 11178 ev 4269). The type-5 "counts as body" shortcut is gone.
- **BA2 Any HDPT.** Rule 3 matches any HDPT copy in the active plugins, not only winners: a mesh an overridden head part used to name is still a head mesh.
- **BA3 No schema bump.** The esp reader has captured HDPT MODL into `model_ref` since the first payload commit (78fb141, before schema 8), so existing stores already hold the rows; `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 8 and no rescan is forced. No scan or no plugins = rule 3 false.
- **BA4 Plumbing.** `modscan::Store::is_head_part_mesh(norm)` answers rules 2–3 once per mesh load (Meshes view `mesh_spec`, set preview `load_nif` off the UI thread); the GUI passes it as `MeshSpec::head_part` / `ParsedNif::head_part`; `render3d` keeps it per loaded NIF (`is_head` = rule 1 or the flag). No per-frame query.

## Note BF — Game-path keys fold ASCII (owner, 2026-10-16)

- **BF1 Rule.** Keys compared against scan/NIF paths fold ASCII only, matching `nif::path` (`slashes_lower`): `shader::mesh_key` / `colour_mesh_key` use `to_ascii_lowercase`. The old Unicode fold made a texture under a non-ASCII folder (`textures/Ärger/`) miss its scan row.
- **BF2 Unchanged.** Set ids (`sets.rs` `fold`/`fold_id`) and `[files]` keys stay Unicode-folded.

## Note BD — Audit REPORT 2026-10-16: render3d upload test, export save

- **BD1 Upload test (#13).** `render3d/tests/upload.rs` loads BC1 DDS files with full mip chains through `load_dds` (8×8 and non-square 16×8 2D, and an 8×8 cube; every block a distinct colour, so a short or swapped row pitch shows), copies every subresource back from WARP and compares it byte for byte with the file. The report suggested rendering at two sizes to sample mips 0 and 3; reading back every subresource checks the same per-face/per-mip pointer and pitch arithmetic exactly, without depending on the rasteriser's mip selection.
- **BD2 Export save (#2).** After an export, the JSON hash record (`last_json_sha256`, CS PBR and complex material hashes) saves `sdc-project.toml` only when it had no unsaved edits before the hash was set. Set edits and Undo stay enabled while an export runs; if the doc was dirty, the hash is kept in memory and the note "hash recorded; written with the next Save" is shown (once per export), so Save/Discard still decide about the user's edits. A stale on-disk hash only makes the next export ask before overwriting its own JSON.

## Note BE — Audit REPORT 2026-10-16: scan fixes (modscan)

Owner-authorised changes to the NIF team's `modscan` (branch `fix/modscan-scan-fixes`). Findings are REPORT #5, #12 (modscan part), #14 and readers-scan RS-4, RS-6.

- **BE1 Scan after PGPatcher (#5).** A reused copy that is a derive-source candidate but has no stored CRC goes back to the parallel pass, which hashes loose and BSA entries alike. `crc_of` is a map lookup; the serial `fs::read` fallback, `new_crcs` and `Store::set_derived`'s `crcs` parameter are gone. A BSA source now verifies (`match`) on a warm store instead of staying `unverified`. A candidate whose read fails has no CRC, stays unverified and is re-read next scan (accepted).
- **BE2 `tex_copy` (#14, option b).** Nothing writes `tex_copy` any more (`set_textures` takes only the winners). The empty table stays in `SCHEMA` with a comment: no schema bump, no forced rescan; drop it at the next bump. Stores scanned earlier keep stale rows nobody reads. Tests count `tex_winner`; the `scan_dump` fixture was regenerated without the `tex_copy` section.
- **BE3 ASCII filter (#12).** `Store::winning_nifs` folds the user's filter with `to_ascii_lowercase`, matching the ASCII-folded stored keys (`canon_mesh`) and SQLite's ASCII `LIKE`. Set ids and `[files]` keys stay Unicode (engine side is a separate branch).
- **BE4 `winners` (RS-6).** The `exclude` parameter was `|_| false` at every production call; removed. The source view is `winners(&nd_copies, ..)`.
- **BE5 Failed origins keep their cache (RS-4).** A BSA that fails to open (`Bsa::open` error) is left out of `enable_run`, so `delete_unseen` does not touch its copies; the problem line still reports it. The origin is simply absent from that run's lists and returns when it opens again. A loose root whose `read_dir` fails was not covered here; see BQ1.
- **BE6 Not done.** The write-only columns (`nif_copy.bsver`, `rec.txst_flags`, `rec.decal`, `plugin.flags`) are still written: `scan_dump` reads three of them and the writers span the esp and store code, so it is not trivial.

## Note BB — Memory admission counts RNM layers and complex grass (owner, 2026-10-15)

Owner go: a layered normal was admitted at its base size and complex grass at one image, so a batch could run several heavy jobs at once. A job's admitted bytes are now the base plus its peak extra working set. The three `shortcut:` comments (pipeline RNM blend, `BakeJob::peak_bytes`, `grass::build`) are gone.

- **BB1 RNM layer term.** `RnmJob::admission_bytes(spec, base)`: the largest of the blend's files (`RnmJob::inputs`: layers, used masks, used AO) by `bake::decode_peak` (the bake's existing model, lifted out of `BakeJob::estimated_bytes`: header dims × (decoded width + 16 + 16), PSD 0 + 32), plus one base-sized float image (16 B/texel) for its resample. Header only, never a decode. 0 when no header reads (the load fails on its own). An 8K layer on a 2K `_n` now admits the 8K decode.
- **BB2 Where it applies.** `api::job_bytes` adds it for `job.active_rnm()` at `resize::target_dims(input, resize)` (the blend runs on the preprocessed, resized base). `BakeJob::estimated_bytes` adds it for the bake's `rnm` at the `_n`'s resized size, since `load_lengths` blends the layers too. Both are sums, not maxes: the base or `_n` decode and the layer decode do not overlap in time, so this over-admits on purpose ("base + peak extra"). The mask and AO planes (4 B/base texel each, held while a layer loads) are not counted separately; the generic 3× base model already over-counts at blend time (only the 16 B/texel work image is alive then).
- **BB3 AV4 unaffected.** Plan pass 1's cache hit admits at 0 and stays correct: planning only stamps layer files (`rnm::plan`), it never decodes one, so a cached base hides no layer cost there. The layer term is a run-time term, and `run` has no `AnalysisCache`, so it reads one header per layer file per job; the cache's dims are not reused (one header read is cheaper than plumbing the cache into `run`).
- **BB4 Complex grass.** `job_bytes` adds one float chain (texels × 16 × 1.34) for `Subtype::ComplexGrass`: in `grass::build` both half Works, both half chains (one full chain together) and the stacked chain are live at once, one chain more than the generic model. That is about 1.33× the generic admission (tested inside 1.3–1.5×).
- **BB5 Scheduling.** `Budget::acquire` is unchanged: the bigger jobs simply run with fewer neighbours, and a job over the whole budget is admitted alone when nothing else is in flight, as any oversized file was, so it cannot deadlock (tested).
- **BB6 Bytes.** Admission only; goldens and output bytes unchanged.

## Note BC — Audit REPORT 2026-10-16 fixes, engine and CLI (owner, 2026-10-16)

Fixes from the owner-commissioned audit (`F:/ai/dds/REPORT.md`, made at main b5ad038; each re-checked on 395012a). One commit per finding.

- **BC1 Closed stdout pipe (#1).** Every stdout print in `crates/cli/src/verbs.rs` (and `say`) goes through `out!`/`out_raw!`, which ignore write errors, so `sdc validate --json | head -n1` exits with the report's code, not 3. Tested with stdout closed before sdc writes.
- **BC2 In-place output root (#3).** `discover` skips the output root only when it is strictly inside the input folder (case-insensitive both ways). An output root equal to the input folder (`-o` = the input, writing beside the sources) or above it skips nothing, where it used to find zero inputs and exit 0. The S6 guard is unchanged and now reachable in place: a re-encoded DDS that would overwrite itself fails and its bytes stay (tested). A later in-place run sees its own `.dds` outputs as DDS inputs, which are skipped unless re-encode is opted in; they stay in discovery (the S6 guard and `[files]` re-encode still see them). `run` folds those whose manifest record's `output_stamp` matches the file on disk into one batch-level `IN-DDS-SKIPPED` warning ("N earlier outputs in the input folder were not re-read", `data.count`) instead of a `file_skipped` per file (review M3, tested); any other DDS input is still skipped per file.
- **BC3 Complex grass coverage (#4).** A complex-grass job has no base coverage: its top half is preserved in `grass::build` and its bottom half's alpha is specular data, so coverage measured on the stacked image raised a false `VAL-COVERAGE` (tested with specular alternating 100/160). The top half's coverage is not validated separately.
- **BC4 Companion lookup (#6).** `sibling_outside` reads each folder once per plan (`bake::plan::Outside`, a lazy per-folder listing of the image and DDS files the batch does not hold), checks batch membership first and takes the file type from the directory entry (a link alone is followed with a stat). Messages and picks are unchanged; covered by the existing `bake_plan` tests (no new test: the report proposed none, and the change is performance only).
- **BC5 Glob typos (#7).** `policy::compile_glob` (the matcher `glob_match_input` caches) checks every glob where it enters: `parse_set`'s `file:<glob>` (usage error), `check_preset`'s own rule globs (preset error, so `sdc presets validate` and the GUI preset editor see it), and `check_up_front` for `file:` overrides built without `parse_set` (usage) and every rule glob of the preset chain, the alias presets and the configs (config error). The lazy cache stays.
- **BC6 Non-finite values (#8).** TOML's `inf`, `-inf` and `nan` become JSON null, which the merge ignores. `parse_set` refuses a value holding a null (usage error) and `ConfigFile::file_entries` refuses a `[files]` entry holding one (config error), both "not a finite number". Other config sections (`[defaults]`, sub-type tables, rule overrides) are unchanged.
- **BC7 Preset export (#16).** `sdc presets export --out` writes with `write_atomic`, so a failed or killed write leaves the old file whole. No new test (the report proposed none; the export tests cover the normal write).
- **BC8 `[files]` schema (#17).** The config schema's `FileEntry` gains `reencode` (boolean) and an `rnm` of its own (`FileRnmSpec`: `PartialRnmSpec` plus `target`, the `RnmTarget` enum), the two per-file selectors the loader already accepts and the GUI writes. `schema/config.schema.json` regenerated; a test walks every `FIELD_PATHS` path except `subtype` through the `FileEntry` schema.
- **BC9 Hung nvcompress (#18).** The per-level wait has a ceiling of 2 minutes plus 1 s per 4 000 texels (`nvtt::level_timeout`): Spike S7 measured BC7 Production at 0.036–0.07 Mpix/s on ~13 cores (the slow end is 1 s per ~36 000 texels), so the limit is about 9x the slow end, for smaller CPUs or a busy pool (~70 min at 4096², ~4.7 h at 8192²). It catches a hung process, not a slow one. Past it the process is killed and the level fails, so the file is `ENC-NVTT-FAILED` (its `file_failed` names it) and the NVTT slot is freed for the next file. Tested with the fake's `sleep` mode and the test-only `SDC_NVTT_LEVEL_TIMEOUT_MS` (read only with `test-hooks`).
- **BC10 Flush policy (#19): declined (owner, after review I1).** Every output keeps `write_atomic` with `sync_all`; the `write_atomic_nosync` change was reverted. Without the flush a torn output could pass as up to date after a power loss: `is_up_to_date` checks only the output's size and mtime, which NTFS can replay while the unflushed data comes back as zeros, and the small manifest line can reach disk first.
- **BC11 `overrides.subtype` on a rule (audit EC-4).** `finish_profile` overwrites it with the decided sub-type, so it did nothing. `check_preset` (own rules) and `check_up_front` (every rule of the chain, alias presets and configs) refuse it: "set the sub-type with `subtype =` on the rule, not in overrides". `target` and `category` were already unknown fields there.
- **BC12 NVTT temp folders (audit EP-7).** `nvtt::TempDir::new` creates its `sdc-nvtt-<pid>-<n>` folder with `create_dir` and moves to the next `n` when it exists, so a folder a crashed run left under a recycled pid is never reused; the level's output file is removed before nvcompress starts, so a stale one cannot pass for this run's. Tested in its own test binary.
- **BC13 Review minors (2026-10-16).** `bake::decode_peak` returns 0 for a header over `MAX_DIM` (a forged size could overflow the product; the load refuses it anyway). `nvtt::TempDir::new` creates a missing system temp folder before `create_dir`. Open, not fixed here: non-finite values in `[defaults]`, sub-type tables and rule overrides (BC6); the complex-grass top half is not coverage-validated (BC3, accepted).

## Note BI — GUI doc state and caches (audit 2026-10-16)

Branch `refactor/gui-doc-state-and-caches`: REPORT #15, #9, #11 and gui-model GM-4, GM-5, GM-6, GM-10, lean-crosscut LC-7 (`read_as_all`).

- **BI1 One file state (#15).** `project::TomlFile` holds path, document, disk stamp, dirty, error and rev, with open/reload/touch/text/restore/changed_on_disk/save (save through `engine::dds::write_atomic`, which keeps the flush). `ProjectDoc` and `SetsDoc` wrap it. `ProjectDoc` keeps its engine `[files]` check after a reload and `set_error`.
- **BI2 Rev after the change.** Every `SetsDoc` mutator edits, then `touch()`es (dirty + new rev). `write_path` counts pruning an emptied sub-table as a change. A call that changes nothing (read-only, removing an absent key, an ignored restore) no longer bumps rev; the only readers are caches and the recovery key. A new `[[sets]]` table made by `table_mut` bumps rev without dirty (as before, it is not an unsaved edit on its own). Reload bumps rev for both documents (`ProjectDoc::reload` did not); `ProjectDoc::set_error` bumps it (the document is replaced).
- **BI3 Entries cache (#9).** `SetsDoc::entries()` returns `Arc<Vec<SetEntry>>`, parsed once per rev. Mutators read the private `parse_entries()`: mid-edit the rev is not bumped yet (`rename_set` with no order list would otherwise read the old id). `build_views` copies the shared list (`to_vec`, once per view-key change) so its body stays as it is for the sets-column branch.
- **BI4 Scan stamp per frame (#9).** `AppModel::poll()` stats the scan database once per frame into `scan_stamp`; `view_key` reads it, with the database path in the key. An external CLI scan is seen on the next frame; code that rewrites the database in place without a frame (tests) calls `poll()`.
- **BI5 Delete hits (#11).** `delete_hits` returns `Arc<Vec<DeleteHit>>` cached in `ViewCache` under `view_key()`, like `export_blocks`.
- **BI6 Small items.** GM-6: `open_folder` resets `dds_patch`. GM-5: the mesh-evidence and known-paths read errors are Messages warnings ("Scan database: …"), each distinct text once (`scan_db_error`, cleared by a successful read and by `open_folder`). GM-4: `export_ended(Result)` serves `ExportDone` and the export `Panicked` arm (`Err("internal error: …")`): the pace clock stops, pending JSON/CS/CM are finished or noted, and an error is always logged before the dialog decision; the panic arm still shows its own error dialog. LC-7: `ProjectDoc::read_as_all` (no readers) is gone. GM-10: a model unit test replaces every mesh-evidence read with alternating GRAS sets and checks three plans, then the "sets changed while planning" refusal.

## Note BK — nif FieldOffsets removed (owner, 2026-10-16)

`nif::props::FieldOffsets` and `Lighting::field_offsets` are gone (audit LC-7): they were kept for an in-place patcher that does not exist and had no production readers. `decode_lighting` is otherwise unchanged.

## Note BJ — Audit follow-ups: shared constants, check_chain, by_set, manifest compaction (owner, 2026-10-16)

- **BJ1 One alpha gate (EC-8/LC-4).** `engine::analyse::CS_COMPLEX_GATE_CODE = 251` is CS's complex-material gate everywhere: `NEAR_OPAQUE_ALPHA`, validate's `_m` gate and height-clip check, the grass detector, the CLI's sub-type inference cutoff and the GUI's PGPatcher advice. `engine::config::ALPHA_THRESHOLD = 1..=254` is the `alpha.threshold` range for `check_profile`, the NIF clamp and the two GUI widgets. Messages are unchanged.
- **BJ2 One check_chain (EC-6).** `presets::check_chain(chain, configs, target)` holds the rule checks (glob compiles, no `overrides.subtype`, known field paths) and the per-sub-type profile builds. `check_preset` runs it per allowed target with no configs; `check_up_front` runs it for the batch chain with the configs and for each suffix alias chain, and keeps only the `--set` and `[files]` checks. Two consequences: `check_preset` checks the rules of the whole chain, not only the preset's own; and the batch now refuses a rule override path outside `FIELD_PATHS` (for example `target` or `category`, which `finish_profile` overwrote silently) in preset and config rules alike.
- **BJ3 by_set (EP-5).** `plan_bakes` indexes jobs by set once; `plan_packing` collects the waiting raw inputs once. `other_output` (explicit packed paths only), `prepacked_member` (scans jobs only for a member whose suffix matches the recipe) and `retag` still scan `jobs`, which the planning loop mutates.
- **BJ4 Manifest compaction (EC-5).** `Manifest::load` rewrites the manifest from its retained records when it is over 32 MB and has more than 3x as many lines as entries. It holds the process-wide append lock from the read to the rewrite. Another process appending at the same moment is not covered (there is no cross-process lock for appends either).

## Note BM — PBR Landscape material type (owner, 2026-10-16)

Owner-approved brief (2026-10-16): a `pbr_landscape` shader with its own card, replacing the generic CS PBR records panel for those sets. The calls not spelled out by the owner are marked *(call)*. Supersedes AD7's statics UI for PBR Landscape sets only (the `statics` key and rule are unchanged) and widens AD9's plane rule.

- **BM1 Shader.** `Shader::PbrLandscape` (`pbr_landscape`, "PBR Landscape"), CS only: `ALL` lists it third, after `pbr` and `pbr_grass`, so vanilla is `ALL[4..]`. Maps: albedo (`pbr_albedo`, `landscape_diffuse` or `diffuse`) and `_n` (`pbr_normal`, `normal`, `landscape_normal`) required; `_rmaos` and `_p` optional *(call: `_rmaos` optional as the brief lists it, so a set without one gets no SHADER-MISSING-MAP; `_g`, `_s`, `_cnr`, `_f` members get SHADER-EXTRA-MAP, warnings only)*. The slot cards follow `usable_slots`: a PBR Landscape set shows no empty emissive, subsurface, coat or fuzz cards, and a filled one is outlined as unused (review M8; CS's landscape shader binds none of them).
- **BM2 Byte-identical.** No member defaults, no member re-typing, not in `has_member_defaults`: a set resolves and encodes exactly as under `pbr` (engine test `pbr_landscape_is_auto_picked_and_resolves_exactly_like_pbr` compares the jobs; goldens 95/95 unchanged). FMT-LANDSCAPE-BC1 still guards `landscape_diffuse` members as before; nothing new was added for it.
- **BM3 Auto rule.** Inside the PBR rule: GRAS evidence → `pbr_grass` first *(call: the grass record is concrete evidence)*, then, under CS only, a landscape path (`textures/landscape/` or a `landscape` component) or a `[sets.cs_txst]` block → `pbr_landscape` (`auto:pbr_landscape`), else `pbr`. So it sits ahead of the mesh-majority vote, as the PBR rule always did *(call)*. CS only *(call: vanilla keeps falling back with `wanted: pbr`, as before)*. A texture-set block alone does not make a non-PBR set PBR Landscape *(call: "PBR maps and (path or block)")*; non-PBR landscape sets keep `landscape`. Owner note (review M1): the path rule also takes PBR sets under `textures/landscape/trees/`, `…/grass/` (when no plugin scan gave GRAS evidence, and always in the CLI) and mountain/rock textures that STAT meshes use; bytes are unchanged, the label, card and plane preview (BM9) are not. Pick `pbr` (or `pbr_grass`) in the Shader list for those.
- **BM4 Block plumbing.** `BatchRequest::cs_txst_sets` (set ids, folded once and matched like `set_shaders`) carries the GUI's blocks to `PickInput::cs_txst`; it is part of the GUI's `EngineInputs`, so adding or removing a block re-plans *(call: P7 narrowed; edits inside a block stay JSON-only; an Export clicked during that plan waits for it, as after any edit)*. Empty for the CLI.
- **BM5 Card.** "PBR Landscape" (open by default) in the set editor's right column and in the 3D settings window, for a CS set whose pick is `pbr_landscape`. It reuses `ui/cs_pbr.rs` and the `cs_pbr` model calls: the PGPatcher box first, then the texture set's fields (see BM13), template and EDIDs (with scan suggestions); it is drawn before the block exists, the first edit creates it, and it has no Remove *(call; review M5: Undo, or picking `pbr` to reach the Advanced panel's Remove, takes a stray block away)*. The material object section is the existing block (add/remove, template, fields, EDIDs).
- **BM6 PGPatcher box (owner, fix round).** "Also write into the PGPatcher JSON" replaces the statics selector in the card. Ticked = the entry is written (`AppModel::pgp_written` = `is_json_set` and `pgp_entry_wanted`). For a PBR Landscape set, auto with no usable scan (`NoScan`, a missing or unreadable database) **keeps** the entry; once a scan exists auto follows it (no non-LOD mesh → off). So the card's first edit, which creates the block, never flips the box or the badge (review I1). Plain PBR sets with a texture-set block keep AD7 (no scan → no entry), and the export's "left out, the scan database cannot be read" note leaves PBR Landscape sets out. A click stores `always`/`never`; **Back to auto** clears it *(call: the brief gave no way back to auto)*. A set that is not a PGPatcher JSON set (its colour map resolves to `landscape_diffuse`, not `pbr_albedo`) gets the box off and disabled with the reason and how to fix it (review I2).
- **BM7 Advanced panel.** The generic panel is now the collapsed "Advanced: CS PBR records", still drawn where it was (left column, 3D settings window) for any CS set except a PBR Landscape set, where it is hidden *(call: hide, not read-only: less code, and the card holds the same blocks)*. The set editor has no per-set Advanced area to move it into, so the header carries the name *(call)*. (Superseded in part by CC16: the panel is titled "CS PBR records" and sits in the set editor's right-hand panel.)
- **BM8 Badge (review I2).** `sets::badge_text` for a PBR Landscape set says what is written: CS records = a texture-set or material-object block with at least one EDID; PGPatcher = `pgp_written`. "PBR Landscape → CS + PGPatcher JSON", "→ CS JSON", "→ PGPatcher JSON (no CS records yet)", "PBR Landscape (no JSON yet)". Other badges are unchanged.
- **BM9 Preview.** A PBR Landscape set is shown on the plane like a set with a texture-set block (AD9).
- **BM10 Fixture.** The GUI tests' `landscape/rock01` set is now auto PBR Landscape. Tests of plain-PBR slot cards, the records panel and AD7's statics rule, the sphere/mesh preview and the 3D layout use `support::pbr_opened_plain` (rock01 picked as `pbr`); `pbr_opened` itself is unchanged. The CS export tests wait for the plan a new block starts.
- **BM11 3D layout (review M4).** The plane's toolbar label is "Mesh: Plane" (the explanation is its hover text), so a PBR Landscape set's toolbar stays one line and its 3D view keeps BH13's 72 % at 1024×768; `in_3d_the_viewport_takes_most_of_the_centre` checks a PBR Landscape case.
- **BM12 Card labels (owner).** Field rows show plain names ("Roughness scale", "Specular level", "Glint parameters", "Base colour scale", …; `cs_pbr::field_label`) with the exact JSON key as hover text, in the card and the Advanced panel alike *(call: one row widget)*. Where a name is ambiguous the hover also says what the value means (BM16). The PGPatcher panel uses some of the same names, so tests pick the first (card) match.
- **BM13 Rows landscape does not read (owner).** Evidence, CS AIO 2026-10-03 `Shaders/Lighting.hlsl`: the landscape TruePBR path reads per layer only `PBRParams` (`LandscapeTextureNPBRParams` / `PBRParams1`: roughness scale, displacement scale, specular level) and `LandscapeTextureNGlintParameters` (`Common/LightingLandscape.hlsli`, `LIGHTING_LANDSCAPE_BLEND_ONE_LAYER_PBR`); the subsurface (`PBRParams2`), two-layer coat and fuzz branches sit inside `#if !defined(LANDSCAPE) && !defined(LODLANDSCAPE)` (around line 1874), and the inner-layer displacement offset belongs to the coat's interlayer parallax. So `subsurfaceColor`, `subsurfaceOpacity`, `coatColor`, `coatStrength`, `coatRoughness`, `coatSpecularLevel`, `innerLayerDisplacementOffset`, `fuzzColor` and `fuzzWeight` (`cs_pbr::LANDSCAPE_UNREAD`) are hidden in the card while the PGPatcher box is off; with it on they show (meshes sharing the texture read them). A row with a stored value is never hidden, and one line counts the hidden rows. Roughness, displacement, specular and glint always show.
- **BM14 PGPatcher panel (review 7).** On a PBR Landscape set the TruePBR panel sits under "PGPatcher JSON settings": open, with "Roughness, specular, displacement, subsurface, coat and glint are the texture set's values above.", while the entry is written; collapsed and titled "… (not written: tick 'Also write into the PGPatcher JSON' above)" while it is not. Never hidden, so matching, slots and the unmapped keys stay editable. (Superseded in part by CC22: the off title is "PGPatcher JSON settings (not written)" and the hint is the body's first line.)
- **BM15 Scan reads per frame (review M2).** `CsPbrScan` follows the frame's database stamp from `AppModel::poll` (Note BI4) instead of a stat per call, and all reads in one frame share one open database, dropped at the next `poll`. A running scan that moves the stamp therefore costs one open per frame, not one per visible badge.
- **BM16 Shared fields (owner).** The card starts with "Shared (texture set, material object and PGPatcher JSON)". What counts as shared was checked in CS AIO 2026-10-03 `Shaders/Lighting.hlsl`, field by field:
  - **Glint parameters are shared.** CS reads the texture set's `glintParameters` and the material object's (as `SparkleParams`) as the same struct, and lerps one into the other where the material object projects.
  - **Roughness and specular are not shared.** The texture set's `roughnessScale` and `specularLevel` multiply the `_rmaos` channels (`rawRMAOS *= float4(PBRParams1.x, 1, 1, PBRParams1.z)`). The material object's `roughness` and `specularLevel` replace them (`rawRMAOS.xyw = lerp(…, float3(ParallaxOccData.x, 0, ParallaxOccData.y), …)`). They stay separate rows, and their hover text says which is a multiplier and which is absolute. No converted value is ever written.
  - So only `glintParameters` is shared (`cs_pbr::SHARED_FIELDS`).
  - A Shared edit writes the texture set and, when it follows, the material object, in one undo step (`set_shared_value`). The PGPatcher keys follow the texture set as before (AD2 overlay, when the box is on).
  - Unsync is offered per field, and only in the Material object section *(call: the texture set is the shared value, so this is the simpler choice that still lets one block differ)*. The PGPatcher JSON has no Unsync, because AD2 makes the texture set the single source of its mapped keys.
  - "Unsync" lists the field in the block's `unsynced = [...]` and keeps the value. "Sync <field>" copies the texture set's value and removes it from the list. Each is one undo step (`set_mato_synced`). `unsynced` is not a CS field, so it is never exported.
  - A material object counts as following only when the field is not listed and its value equals the texture set's. Blocks that already differ (older projects) therefore show as unsynced and are never overwritten on load.
  - The card's "Add PBR material object" starts the new block with the texture set's shared values, so it follows them.

## Note BN — Trace-debug 2026-10-16 fixes: GUI documents

Findings #9 to #12 of the trace-debug report of 2026-10-16. Each fix started from a failing test.

- **BN1 A wrongly blamed `sdc.toml` gets its edits back (#9).** When the engine rejects the config, the first failure is still blamed on `sdc.toml` tentatively (spec §7.4), but `ProjectDoc::set_error` now stashes the document and its dirty flag. When the plan without `sdc.toml` fails too, the culprit is elsewhere (the user config or a user preset; `check_chain` messages name no path, so the path test cannot tell), and `unblame()` puts the stashed document back, unsaved edits included, instead of reloading from disk. `reload` clears the stash. Undo history is still cleared on the first failure *(call: the read-only window cannot take edits, and keeping history across it needs more than this fix; owner may revisit)*. A plan that lands settles the blame (`apply_plan` clears `ignored_by_plan`), so a later user config or preset failure can never restore a document the engine rejected (review I1). While the blame is tentative, the stashed edits count as unsaved in `AppModel::is_dirty` and the recovery snapshot, so Reload, close and open still ask (review M1). Tests: `a_rejected_user_config_keeps_unsaved_sdc_toml_edits`, `a_settled_blame_is_not_undone_by_a_later_user_config_error`, `stashed_edits_count_as_unsaved_while_the_blame_is_tentative`.
- **BN2 The banner's Reload asks first (#10).** With unsaved edits in either document, **Reload** opens `Dialog::ReloadUnsaved`: **Discard and reload** or **Cancel**; Enter and Esc cancel *(call: the safe answer, as open and close already ask, AE3; no Save choice, because the banner usually means a file cannot be saved as it is)*. Without unsaved edits it reloads at once as before. `open_folder` already clears any dialog. docs/gui.md says so. Tests: `banner_reload_with_unsaved_edits_asks_first`, `banner_reload_when_clean_reloads_at_once`, `reload_unsaved_enter_cancels_and_the_button_discards`.
- **BN3 A press in a column ends text input (#11).** A primary press inside the Textures or Sets column calls `stop_text_input()` before the column draws, so a commit-on-focus-loss box in the centre (the input name box, AO1; colour fields and the JSON editor boxes alike) sees its focus loss on the next frame while the old set is still selected and drawn, and commits. Amends AO4: for a click in a column it is now the press, not the release, that ends the edit. egui's global focus surrender stays on release (switching it would break AO4's row click). `shortcut:` a press and release in the same frame still loses the edit, as do selection changes from dialogs and other panels; defer the selection a frame if that is seen. Renaming a set is `Dialog::Rename`, a modal whose backdrop takes the press, so no column text field is cut short. Touchpad tap-to-click and slow frames make a same-frame press and release more likely than with a mouse (review M3). Test: `a_click_on_another_set_commits_the_typed_name_first`.
- **BN4 Section removals run last (#12).** The JSON editor addresses delete sections by index, and a section's Remove is drawn before its match boxes, so the focus-loss edit came after the removal and landed on the shifted neighbour (or was lost). The frame's acts are stably sorted so `RemoveSection` runs after every edit. A remove with a focused box is therefore two undo steps (the edit, then the removal) *(call)*. Tests: `remove_section_with_focused_match_does_not_edit_next_section`, `remove_earlier_section_while_typing_in_a_later_one_edits_the_typed_section`.

## Note BP — Trace-debug 2026-10-16 fixes: engine and vfs

Branch fix/td-engine-readers, from the trace-debug report of 2026-10-16 (Important #1, #3, #4, #5).

- **BP1. #1 Loose walk follows links (vfs, NIF team's crate, owner-authorised).** `vfs::loose::walk` now runs walkdir with `follow_links(true)`, so files under a nested junction or symlink (MO2/Vortex link deploys) are found. Decision: a link is followed wherever it points, including outside the mod root, because link deploys point outside it by design. `norm` and `abs` stay the link path, so the game path is what the game sees. A cycle is cut by walkdir's ancestor check (it yields an `Err` entry, which the existing `filter_ok` drops); the walk always ends. A link back into the same tree lists its files twice under two paths, which is what the game sees too. Junctions to large unrelated trees make the scan slower; that is accepted.
- **BP2. #3 Set Rename keeps the skin `_wet` member.** `member_split` no longer needs the stem base to equal the set key base: in a set that lists `wet`, a suffix-less `*_wet` member splits to base + `wet`. `join_skin_wet` keeps the key check. Shortcut: another suffix-less `*_wet` moved into such a set also reads as its wet map.
- **BP3. #4 A raw map given a sub-type is not a packing role.** `policy::subtype_requested` (`[files]` or file-scoped/unscoped `--set subtype`). In `plan`, such a member's role leaves `set.suffixes` (before `join_skin_wet` and again after set edits) unless another raw member has the role, and it is left out of the `auto` suffix prediction, so Advanced skin detection follows the recipe actually built. Rule-named sub-types are not seen there (shortcut).
- **BP4. #5 BC5/RG8 normal sources rebuild Z.** Resolve sets `channels.reconstruct_z = true` (provenance `AnalysisFact("two-channel-dds")`) for a green-taking normal whose source DXGI is BC5 (83) or RG8 (49), unless the user set the field. Elsewhere BC5 is only an output format, and on a normal it is FMT-BC5-NORMAL (Blocking) because Skyrim reads Z directly; BC5_SNORM/RG8_SNORM are rejected by `read_dds`. Affected inputs get a new profile hash, so cached outputs rebuild.

## Note BO — Trace-debug 2026-10-16 fixes: GUI exports and rename

- **BO1 Inputs rename moves the set entry (#2).** `apply_rename` in Inputs mode now does what the input-name box does (AB1): each set whose own diffuse is renamed gets `retarget_auto(old, new)` in the same undo step, so its `sdc-project.toml` entry (TruePBR settings, locks, `output_name`, borrows) follows the new automatic id. The id computation is `AppModel::auto_retarget`, shared by both paths. `retarget_auto` no longer moves an entry onto an id another entry already has *(call: the entry stays under the old id rather than making two entries with one id)*; both paths then post a warning naming the set (`note_kept_entries`, review M1). A chain inside one Apply (x→y while y→z) is not ordered and can keep an entry behind (shortcut). With a read-only `sdc.toml` the rename dialog's Apply does nothing in Inputs mode, as the input-name box already refused (review I1). A read-only `sdc-project.toml` still leaves the entry behind (finding 33).
- **BO2 CS block colours are floats (#6).** `pgp_to_cs` divides by 255 only the pre-AG133 all-integer form (`rgb_is_legacy`); a float colour reaches the texture-set block as it is. `cs_to_pgp` reads block colours back as floats. So "Remove texture set block" now gives the set float colours, not 0–255 ints (P10 superseded by AG133 here too). Colours already damaged by the old double division stay damaged.
- **BO3 Preset pick rescans (#7).** `PresetsModel::select` rescans the presets folder first, so the draft's table, source and stamp are all read now; a file edited outside since the last rescan shows its edit and a save keeps it. `save_with` no longer rescans itself (its `select` does).
- **BO4 Complex material JSON case-only rename (#8).** `cm_json::finish` does what `cs_pbr_export` does (O6): when the record has the same path under another case and that file is sdc's own (hash matches) and the `.dds` exists, the old file is removed and the JSON written under the new name with a new record. A real hand edit is kept, with its note, and its record stays under the old key. Non-ASCII case changes are not matched, as in O6. On a case-sensitive filesystem a hand-edited `Iron_M.json` is kept and `iron_m.json` is written beside it; the old record is dropped, so the hand-edited file is no longer reported (review M5; nothing is lost).

## Note BQ — Trace-debug minor fixes: engine and CLI (controller, 2026-10-16)
Trace-debug report 2026-10-16, minor findings of the engine group (E1–E5, R2).
- **BQ1 One entry per file (#13).** `discover_reporting` keys each discovered file by its canonical path (absolute when `canonicalize` fails); the first input that reaches a file wins, the others skip it silently. A link and its target are one file. This settles the phase0-2 plan's deferred discovery minor ("the same file given twice … becomes IN-DUPLICATE").
- **BQ2 User preset retry (#15).** `add_dir` retries the files it refused while loading (id or alias clash) whenever the check pass removed a broken preset, until a pass removes nothing. Refusal warnings now come after the broken-preset warnings.
- **BQ3 NVTT working folder (#17).** nvcompress runs with the level's temp folder as its working folder and gets bare `l<N>.in.dds` / `l<N>.out.dds` names, because it reads argv in the ANSI code page. Its error text no longer names the folder. The test fake mangles non-Latin-1 argument characters to `?` like the real tool.
- **BQ4 Closed stderr (#18).** Every stderr write in the cli crate goes through `err!`, which ignores write errors (Note BC did the same for stdout). A closed stderr no longer turns into exit 101; the exit code is the command's own.
- **BQ5 rfaos and skin_rfaos together (#20).** A config or preset whose `[subtypes]` holds both `rfaos` (the old id) and `skin_rfaos` is refused (`MigrateError::DuplicateSubtypeAlias`), not merged: which table should win is the author's call.
- **BQ6 Read-only manifest read (#22).** `Manifest::read` is `load` without the compaction rewrite. Readers that write nothing (the IN-DDS-SKIPPED summary in `Engine::run`, so a dry run and `inspect`) use it; the converting load still compacts under the append lock.
- **BQ7 BC1 transparency on every level (#23).** patch-header decodes every stored BC1 level, not only mip 0, before refusing 1-bit alpha (S7).
- **BQ8 Nested textures folders (#24).** `discover::game_path` cuts at the first `textures` component at or below the input root's last component, else at the last one anywhere, else uses `rel`. A nested `textures/armor/textures/…` keeps both, as `nif::path::canon_texture` does. Engine side only; the nif crate is unchanged. Files under such a nested folder get new keys. Owner, 2026-10-16 (review I1): a `textures` folder below the input root wins, and the root's own `textures` counts only when none lies below it. An input root named `textures` that holds mod folders (`D:/Textures/MyMod/textures/landscape/rock.png`) keys from the mod's own folder (`textures/landscape/rock.png`), as before #24; an input `Data/textures` with `armor/textures/foo_d.dds` now keys `textures/foo_d.dds` (the two layouts cannot be told apart from the path).
- **BQ9 RNM layers in the map check (#25).** `map_members` leaves out jobs with status `NormalLayer` (layers and masks), so they get no SHADER-EXTRA-MAP.
- **BQ10 Stale sidecar removed (#27).** Under Note F / Y2: an encode without `--sidecar` removes the output's existing `.dds.json` when it reads as sdc's record for that output (a JSON object whose `output` is the output's key and that has `profile_sha256`); any other file of that name is not sdc's and stays (the complex-material export test keeps such a stub). A removal error other than NotFound fails the file at Write and removes the output. Owner, 2026-10-16 (review M2): superseded: a removal error other than NotFound is a warning, OUT-SIDECAR-KEPT, and the new DDS stays (the file counts as converted). An up-to-date output keeps its sidecar, which still matches.
- **BQ11 Grey skin_wet encodings (#31).** `policy::allowed_encodings_for(st, target, grayscale)` judges a grey `skin_wet` as `check_profile` does; `allowed_encodings` is the `grayscale = false` wrapper. Engine side only: the GUI picker and bulk apply (`gui/src/model/{fields,bulk,encoding_follow}.rs`) still call `allowed_encodings`, so the user-visible fix lands when the GUI passes `category == Grayscale`.
- **BQ12 Eye msn (#32).** SET-MISSING-COMPANION "_msn without an _s" is not raised for a job whose set's shader is Eye (the eye shader re-types `_n` to msn; eyes have no `_s`).
- **BQ13 Forced rfaos with fuzz (#34).** The PACK-RECIPE-UNBUILDABLE fallback note is attached only when the `auto` recipe is not `_rfaos`, so it stays the metallic-only case R-fills-1 describes.
- **BQ14 Not fixed here.** #28 (loose walk hides I/O errors): owner NIF team, and the fix changes `vfs::loose::walk`'s return type, whose callers are in modscan; left for them (BE5's open gap stands). #30 (OpenEXR premultiplied alpha): needs an owner ruling, since some writers store straight alpha in EXR; unchanged.
- **BQ15 OpenEXR alpha is un-premultiplied on load (#30; owner, 2026-10-16: follow the standard; EXR alpha is rare in practice, mostly height or colour without alpha).** Supersedes the #30 part of BQ14. `load::decode` divides RGB by A for an OpenEXR with alpha wherever A > 0, unclamped; A = 0 texels stay as stored. A straight-alpha EXR sets the per-file field `alpha.exr_straight = true` (`[files]`, `--set`, a preset), which the pipeline's load reads (`load_image_as`) to skip it; the field is left out of a profile's JSON while false, so profile hashes and goldens are unchanged (no golden uses EXR alpha). The pipeline load and the GUI encoded and source previews (`pipeline::prepare`) honour it. Plan-time analysis, plan thumbnails, packing sources, RNM layers and bakes load with the default (un-premultiplied). Alpha statistics do not change under the division, but colour statistics do: the grey test has an absolute tolerance, so a near-grey straight EXR with partial alpha may be planned as colour (the safe side) while the encode reads the stored values (review M1). The field has no GUI row; it is set in a `[files]` entry by hand.

## Note BT — Trace-debug minor fixes: render3d and modscan (2026-10-16)

Branch fix/td-minor-nifcrates, from the trace-debug report of 2026-10-16 (#21, #29, #36, #38, #40, #41, #42). render3d and modscan are NIF-team crates; the owner authorised the fixes. No schema bump.

- **BT1. #21 `settle` compiles keys the pool already took.** When the queue is empty, `settle` builds one job per distinct key a shape still waits on and runs it, so a sync load never returns `Pending` shapes. The pool's own result for that key lands later and only warms the memo (one extra compile on the overlap).
- **BT2. #29 An edit evicts only missing texture entries.** `set_material`'s sweep now drops an entry only when it is missing and has no texture. A decode-error entry stays for the rest of the load (an edit does not ask the resolver for it again), so `begin_all` keeps its white default instead of the missing fill.
- **BT3. #36 A tainted scan empties the winner tables.** Before `enable_run` in the tainted branch, `nif_winner`, `nif_winner_src` and `tex_winner` are cleared. Call: until a clean rescan, NIF lists show no winners ("Overridden" with no name) and missing/grass reads find nothing, instead of naming origins of the previous run. The banner and Retry already ask for that rescan.
- **BT4. #38 Tied separators follow modlist order.** A separator's `parent_origin` (unused for kind 3) holds its rank among the separators in modlist.txt, and `Store::mods` orders by it before `id`. Call: reuse a column rather than bump the schema. A store from before keeps the old order until its next scan.
- **BT5. #40** Meshes `reload` keeps the selected mod only when it is not PGPatcher-derived, so a mod that became derived closes with its NIF.
- **BT6. #41 Only a completed scan refreshes the Textures view's mesh evidence.** `MeshesModel::scan_completed` is true when the scan returned `Ok` (a tainted run included: its origins are enabled) and false after a pause, cancel, failure or panic. The app re-reads mesh votes and known paths only when it is true. Call: known paths are gated too, because with BT7 they read enabled origins only and a cancel would empty them the same way. The restart case stays (store design).
- **BT7. #42 Lock hover and path pickers read live lighting shapes only.** `used_by::slot_textures` and the texture part of `known_paths::read` require a lighting shape (`shader_kind = 1`) in a non-derived copy of an enabled origin (`LIVE_LIGHTING_TEXSET`). TruePBR shapes still count. The mesh-folder part of known paths (from `nif_winner`) is unchanged.

## Note BR — Trace-debug minor fixes: GUI model

Branch fix/td-minor-guimodel, from the trace-debug report of 2026-10-16 (Minor #19, #33, #35, #37, #39, #43 to #50). Each fix started from a failing test.

- **BR1 #19 An Inputs rename onto another file's output blocks.** `input_collisions` also compares a row's predicted output with every output this batch leaves alone (`job_key`, case-folded), so a rename onto a path another set's `output_name` writes is refused: "{other} already writes {path}". It blocks the same case on CS too.
- **BR2 #35 Case-only input renames are aliases.** Apply (and the input-name box) writes the alias unless the new name is exactly the file's own name, so Case=Lower/Upper does what the dialog shows. Going back to the exact own name removes the alias.
- **BR3 #33 Input names need a writable `sdc-project.toml`.** The set entry must follow the aliases (AB1), so `set_input_name` and an Inputs rename refuse while `sdc-project.toml` is read-only, as they already did for `sdc.toml` *(call: the whole Inputs rename is refused, even rows that move no set entry, matching P8's "set controls disabled")*. The input-name box shows the reason (one line in `ui/input_name.rs`).
- **BR4 #37 `add`/`remove` keys match as the engine does.** `SetsDoc::remove_member`, `add_member` and `list_edit`, and the model's `remove_member`, compare keys with `sets_doc::names_file` (`same_id` or `path_key_matches`). A hand-written extension-less `add = ["armor/wall"]` then names `wall.png`: removing it drops the key instead of refusing or writing a `remove`. Review M4: an extension-less key is dropped for a file only when no file of the same stem and another extension sits beside it on disk (`SetsDoc::names_only`); otherwise removing one of them writes its exact `remove` (applied after the moves), so `add = ["foo"]` keeps `foo.png` when `foo.tga` is removed. Known limit: such a kept key in another set's `add` still moves its first match there when a file moves (a `shortcut:` in `names_only`).
- **BR5 #39 Duplicate into set skips aliased names.** The free-name loop also skips a name another file is read as (its `[inputs]` alias), as the rename dialog does.
- **BR6 #43 PGPatcher JSON hash per file name.** New `[project] pgp_json_sha256` table: path under the export root → hash sdc last wrote there, one entry per name the JSON has had. An entry whose file is gone is dropped at the next record. `last_json_sha256` is still written (the current name's hash, for older builds) and is the record read when the table is absent (older projects). An export with a recorded old-name file still on disk notes it: "<old>: the PGPatcher JSON is now <new>; the old file was left in place and PGPatcher still reads it". The file is kept (AG90's keep rule). Renaming back finds sdc's own file, so there is no "edited outside" question. Undo keeps the table like the other hash records; they are put back in export order, so a restore that changes nothing else leaves the document clean. (amended by BV7, 2026-10-17: entries are keyed by absolute lower-case path, and an entry whose file is gone is kept)
- **BR7 #44 Cancel-and-leave racing a finished export.** When the export finished before the cancel was seen and raised the overwrite question, `run_after_export` answers it "keep" (the edited JSON stays, with the "kept as edited" note), then closes or opens. The note is also posted as a message, because opening another folder clears the export notes.
- **BR8 #45 An unreadable gui.toml is kept.** `save` keeps anything `load` fails on (not UTF-8, as well as unparsable) as `gui.toml.bad`. `AppModel::new` reads the file once more and records no stamp when it cannot (locked at launch), so the first save merges the file instead of replacing it. `shortcut:` a file that becomes readable between `load` and `AppModel::new` is still stamped; pass the load result in if that is seen. Review M3: the earlier `.bad` is replaced only by the rename that moves the broken file aside (`rename` replaces it in one step), so a gui.toml another program holds open fails the save and keeps the earlier `.bad`.
- **BR9 #46 A preset save may not break another user preset.** `PresetsModel::validate` re-checks every other user preset in the copied registry, so renaming a preset another one bases on (or any edit that would make one fail its check) is refused, naming that preset. This is broader than the rename case on purpose.
- **BR10 #47 A second crash keeps the first `.recovery`.** `write_recovery` renames an existing `.recovery` to `.recovery.<UTC stamp>` first. `shortcut:` the stamped copies get no banner line and are never cleaned up; add both if they pile up. docs/gui.md says so.
- **BR11 #48 Errors do not replace the overwrite question.** `raise_error` sends a plan failure's or a worker panic's message to the export notes while `Dialog::OverwriteJson` is open; otherwise it shows the error dialog as before.
- **BR12 #49 A refused CS EDID is not an orphan.** `PendingCs::refused` lists the refused paths. `finish` keeps their hash and skips the "no set binds this EDID" note; the refusal note already says why.
- **BR13 #50 CJK fallbacks.** `msyh.ttc`, `YuGothM.ttc` and `malgun.ttf` are loaded from `%WINDIR%\Fonts`, each optional, after Segoe UI Emoji in the proportional family and also in monospace. They are system fonts, so N10 holds. That is about 46 MB more font data on a machine that has all three.

## Note BS — Trace-debug minor fixes: GUI UI and preview (Claude, 2026-10-16)

Branch fix/td-minor-guiui, findings #14, #16, #26 and #51 to #59 of the trace-debug report of 2026-10-16 (sections G4, G5, G6). Each fix started from a failing test; one commit per finding.

- **BS1 A lost-device swap or edit is replayed (#14).** The 3D render thread logs a texture swap or material edit for replay on success and also when it failed with `DEVICE_REMOVED` (`log_for_replay`), since the rebuild that follows replays the log on the new device. The failure is still reported to the model as before.
- **BS2 A DDS above the preview limit is refused (#16).** `dds_preview` returns "WxH (the smallest mip) is above the preview limit of N" when no mip fits, instead of decoding the full level. `first_level_within` keeps its last-mip fallback (the engine's preview paths rely on it).
- **BS3 Worker panics carry their job id (#26).** As AF3 does for the NVTT probe, the preview (source, encode, DDS), heatmap and RNM thumbnail workers catch their own panic, send their id-tagged failure (`worker::or_send`), then unwind on so `spawn_guarded` still raises the error dialog. A stale job's panic is dropped by the id check like any stale result; the per-kind `*_panicked` handlers are gone. The failure text is the panic message, as before.
- **BS4 Slot cards take a drop only where they show (#51).** The hit test uses the card's `interact_rect` (clipped), so a drop on the header row or drawer over a card scrolled out of view opens the file's folder. (Slot cards are rows since CC1; the rule holds for rows.)
- **BS5 A folder change resets the Sets column modal and Slot commands (#52).** `AppModel::folder_epoch` is bumped in `open_folder`; when it differs from `ui::State::folder_epoch` (an `Option`: a fresh State adopts the epoch on its first frame), the UI resets all of `DropState` (the pending modal, the slot note and the flash) and `SlotCmdState` *(call: the whole state, not only `pending`, since the slot note and flash name a set id too)*.
- **BS6 A pending set-editor click belongs to its set and its passes (#53).** The single-click wait is keyed by set id and records the pass it was last seen in; a pass without the view drops it. This replaces the time-only `STALE_AFTER`.
- **BS7 The header Save waits for a focused field (#54).** As Ctrl+S (AG23): clicking **Save** while a text field has focus saves nothing and says "Save: leave the text field first" in the status line and the Messages log *(call: logged too, because the focus-loss commit's plan replaces the status line at once)*. egui surrenders the field's focus on the release (BN3), after the header has drawn, so the field still has focus when the click lands; it commits on the next frame. Test: `header_save_click_with_focused_field_does_not_save_stale_value` (press and release in separate frames).
- **BS8 Reordering a set to its own place is no edit (#55).** `reorder_set` returns whether it moved anything; Move down on the last set records no step, leaves `sdc-project.toml` clean and does not flash.
- **BS9 A match pill's mode switch is one undo step (#56).** The JSON editor pushes the unstore and the store as one `Act::Edits`: `set_json_values` for a set, the new `set_section_values` ("Change match") for a delete section. A renamed set can still refuse the store half (AN2), as before.
- **BS10 Esc cancels the remaining commit-on-focus-loss boxes (#57).** The JSON name field, the JSON editor's text boxes, the TruePBR card's match rows and its text keys (rename) skip the commit when Esc was pressed and still clear the edit buffer, as AG10 does for the hex box.
- **BS11 Writing the stored value is no edit (#58).** `write_path` returns false when the key already holds the value (compared as JSON, so `1` and `1.0` still count as a change), `set_project` returns early on an equal value, and `set_value`'s texture-set-block branch touches only on a real change. Review M7: `set_project` reads the stored value with `project::item_json` (moved from `cs_pbr`), so a hand-written standard `[project.cs_pbr_sha256]` table compares like the inline form: an equal rewrite is no edit and clearing it removes the table.
- **BS12 One rule for a set's derived match1 (#59).** `prefix::stored_set_match(n, typed, derived)`: slot 1 typed as the derived path (leading `textures\` and `.dds` aside) stores no key, so it follows a re-sourced diffuse; an empty typed or derived path never counts. The TruePBR card (via `Ctx::derived`) and the JSON editor both use it.
- **BS13 The GUI judges a grey skin_wet as the engine does (#31, BQ11's GUI side).** The format picker (`fields::encoding_options`), bulk apply's encoding skip (`bulk`) and encoding-follows-type (`encoding_follow::verdict`, which gains a `grayscale` argument) call `policy::allowed_encodings_for(st, target, profile.category == Grayscale)`. A grey `skin_wet` is offered R8, RG8 and BC5 and an explicit one is kept on a re-type; every other sub-type gets the same list as before, since only `skin_wet`'s category depends on the file.
- **BS14 The header Export waits for a focused field (#54 follow-up).** Export saves first (`start_export`), so it follows BS7: a click while a text field has focus does nothing and says "Export: leave the text field first" in the status line and the log; the field commits on the focus loss and the next click exports. Save and Export share `header::field_focused`. The command-palette Export is not guarded: the palette's own search box has the focus when it runs, and a palette command never runs while another field is being edited.

## Note BU — Loose walk reports I/O errors (NIF team, 2026-10-16)

* **BU1 `vfs::loose::walk` has an error channel.** It returns `(files, errors)`, errors as `(path, message)`: a root `read_dir` failure other than NotFound, directory-entry errors, walkdir errors (permission denied, link cycles, broken links) and metadata errors. A nonexistent root is empty, not an error. The files found are unchanged. `modscan` appends the errors to `report.problems` for both the mesh and texture walks. This closes only the reporting gap left open in BE5 (trace-debug finding #28): a failed loose origin still reaches `enable_run`/`delete_unseen`, so its cached rows are not protected the way a failed BSA's are (BE5); that part stays open. A top-level `meshes`/`textures` entry that cannot be read (broken link, no access) is reported, not skipped. Identical problems from the mesh and texture walks of one root are listed once.

## Note BV — Pre-v2 fix batch (owner rulings and audit fixes, 2026-10-17)

Branch fix/pre-v2, from the pre-v2 audits (`08-pre-v2-audit`, `08a` to `08f`) and the owner's fix-batch list. Each fix started from a failing test.

- **BV1 M9 amended for re-encoded DDS (audits 08b-1, 08e-2).** M9 said DDS members never conflict because they are never written; S6 later let a DDS be re-encoded, so a re-encoded `rock_rmaos.dds` and the raw-map recipe both wrote `rock_rmaos.dds`. `prepacked_member` now looks at every non-raw member that has a job: a re-encoded DDS conflicts like an image and follows `packing.prefer` (`PACK-CONFLICT`). A skipped DDS has no job and still never conflicts. M9's other rules are unchanged.
- **BV2 One output path, one job (audits 08d-1, 08e-3).** The last step of `plan` folds `output_key` over every Ready job, whatever made two of them meet (two recipes' default packed name after a raw map moved to another set, a file output on another job's path). The first in plan order keeps the path; each later one is skipped as `IN-DUPLICATE` ("two outputs map to one path (…); change an output path or move a file"). Before, both wrote the file (the last rename won) and the manifest got two records. No new code. A dropped recipe's raw sources were already taken out of the plan as consumed, so its sources other than the first (which carries the skip) leave the plan with it: no job, skip or failure, and in the GUI they drop out of the set until the conflict is fixed (review m6; the skip is blocking, so nothing is written wrongly).
- **BV3 One rule for replacing an existing file (audit 08a-2).** `engine::dds::may_replace(path, new, ours)`: absent → write; unreadable → kept (never treated as absent); bytes equal to `new` → write, and the writer records it as its own; `ours(bytes)` (the writer's record says it wrote them) → write; anything else → kept, with a note. The PGPatcher, CS PBR and complex-material JSON, the vanilla borrowed-slot copies, Patch header and `--sidecar` all use it. Changes: an unreadable PGPatcher or CS PBR JSON is no longer written over; a byte-identical complex-material JSON with no record is now adopted and recorded (supersedes Note AT's "not adopted, even if identical"); a foreign PGPatcher JSON still asks (P21). `ours` per writer: the JSON files compare the recorded SHA-256; a borrowed-slot copy compares its record, new in `[project] copy_sha256` (absolute lower-case path → hash; a copy now replaces only a file it wrote, so it follows its owner on later exports, and goes through `write_atomic`; P4's "not tracked by the manifest" still holds); Patch header accepts a file that ends with this DDS's payload (an earlier patched copy under any header, S7); `--sidecar` accepts a file that reads as sdc's record for this output (BQ10's test). DDS outputs keep their manifest check in `run`. *shortcut:* a copy record waits for the next Save when `sdc-project.toml` has unsaved edits (BD2); discarding them loses the record, and that copy is then kept until deleted by hand.
- **BV4 A sidecar write failure keeps the DDS (audit 08d-5).** The new DDS has already replaced the old output when the `--sidecar` write fails, so the failure is an `OUT-SIDECAR-KEPT` warning and the DDS stays (it counts as converted), as for an unremovable stale sidecar (BQ10). A foreign `.dds.json` kept by BV3 is the same warning. The next `if-changed --sidecar` run writes the sidecar from the manifest record: `sidecar_present` now rewrites a missing sidecar or sdc's sidecar of an earlier output (one whose JSON is not this record but has the same `output` and a `profile_sha256`), and leaves a file sdc did not write alone (review m10).
- **BV5 PBR grass under `textures/landscape/` is PBR (audit 08e-1; owner ruling (b), 2026-10-17: "sRGB is for PBR maps only, and grass albedo is PBR").** `pbr_grass` now has member defaults, so its members re-resolve at 6c, and `member_subtype` maps `landscape_diffuse` → `pbr_albedo` and `landscape_normal` → `pbr_normal` for it. The PBR grass map check then finds them (no false `SHADER-MISSING-MAP` / `SHADER-EXTRA-MAP`), and the albedo gets the PBR-grass detector note. **Bytes change** for this case only: the albedo is encoded as `pbr_albedo` (sRGB tag, `pbr_albedo` alpha policy) instead of `landscape_diffuse`. Goldens are unchanged (95/95). PBR grass outside `textures/landscape/` re-resolves to the same sub-types as before.
- **BV6 The export folder is per project (owner ruling, 2026-10-17).** Picking an export folder saves it as `[project] export_folder` in the open project's `sdc-project.toml` (GUI-only state, kept across Undo like the hash records; saved at once, or with the next Save while the file has unsaved edits, BD2). `export_root()` is the project's value, else `gui.toml`'s `export_folder` (what older versions saved for every project, now only a default that picking no longer changes), else `<root>/sdc-out`. With no usable `sdc-project.toml` (none open, or one that does not parse) a pick goes to `gui.toml` as before. Opening another project no longer sends its outputs into this project's folder (audit 08c finding 5). The CLI is unaffected (`-o` names the folder).
- **BV7 JSON hash records name their file (audit 08c-1).** The PGPatcher, CS PBR and complex-material records are keyed by the absolute, `/`-separated, lower-cased path (`history::record_key`), not by the path under the export folder, so exporting to B and back to A still finds A's own files. A key from before (relative) is read as under the current export folder. A record is no longer dropped when its file is absent or under another folder (amends BR6's "an entry whose file is gone is dropped"); the old-name and orphan notes look only under the current export folder. O6's case-only rename reads the old spelling from the folder, since the keys are lower-case.
- **BV8 Set ids during a re-plan (audit 08c-3).** Reproduced: right after a new export folder is picked, set ids stripped the new folder from keys still under the old one, so an edit made before the re-plan landed was saved under the whole old path. Set ids, the set prefix and the input-name auto id now use the export folder the current sets were planned with (`AppModel::sets_root`).
- **BV9 Smaller behaviour changes.** A kept (skipped) DDS member fills the slot its suffix suggests, and a DDS that is the output of a job in its set (an in-place run's earlier output) is left out of the shader map check (08b-2). GRAS evidence is matched by the source's folder plus the output stem (`shader::gras_key`), so `g_basecolor.png` matches a NIF's `g.dds` (08b-3). `_crn` makes a set PBR like `_cnr` (08b-4). The skin `_wet` join folds Unicode like set keys (08e-10). A suffix alias that is an RNM layer term (`bump`, `bentmask`, …, Note W) is refused like a vocabulary term (08e-11). A packed output's stem falls back to the built-in §6.1 split when its first source carries a suffix rather than a vocabulary term (`rock_rmaos` → `rock_rmaos`, not `rock_rmaos_rmaos`; 08a-4; *shortcut:* preset aliases are not cut). Copy CLI command adds `--accept-suggestions high` (U3; 08c-2). The export notes are in the Markdown report under *Notes* and scroll in the drawer; the JSON Lines report stays the event stream (08c-4).
- **BV10 Export dialogs (audit 08f).** An export queued behind a plan never starts over an open dialog: it is dropped with "Export not started: answer the open dialog, then click Export again", and answering Open-unsaved while an export runs asks to stop it first (`ExportRunning`), as Open does (08f-1). "Proceed anyway" waits for a plan in flight and runs the guards again, like the other answers (08f-2). The end-of-export OverwriteJson question and error dialog never replace an open dialog: the JSON is kept with a note, and the error stays in the drawer and Messages (an unanswered `ExportRunning` is not in the way; it is dropped when the export ends) (08f-6). A refused context-menu pick says why in the status line and Messages (08f-8). An export-thread panic sets one error dialog: `export_ended`'s, else the panic arm's own when the user was leaving, which keeps BI6 (08f-9). (Superseded in part by CA1: ProceedAnyway, ExportBlocked and ExportWarnings are not dialogs. 08f-1 carries over to Review's queued export, CA13, and 08f-2 to `export_from_review`, CA3 and CA7. The drawer is the bottom panel's Files tab, CA16.)

## Note BW — A tainted scan unloads plugin rows (NIF team, 2026-10-17)

* **BW1 The tainted early return calls `store.unload_plugins()`.** After `set_textures(&HashMap::new())` the tainted branch of `scan::run` now clears `rec_winner`/`rec_inert` and `plugin.lo_index`, as the Folder path does. Before, the old winning records stayed while `tex_winner`/`nif_winner` were empty, so Plugin file references > Missing listed every path a winning record names (trace-debug wave 2 finding 7; display only). The cancelled and failed paths were checked: they leave via `discard_pending`/`Err` before any winner change and already have a test. Test: `a_tainted_scan_leaves_missing_and_unused_empty`.
* **BW2 A plugin pass cancelled at its start also unloads plugin rows.** `scan_plugins` returns `Cancelled` before touching `rec_winner` while the asset winners were already replaced, so Missing listed the previous load order against the new tables (pre-existing; Codex review of BV1). The `Cancelled` arm in `scan::run` now calls `unload_plugins()`; parsed records and the cache are kept, so the next clean scan restores the lists. Test: `a_scan_cancelled_at_the_plugin_pass_leaves_missing_and_unused_empty`.

## Note BX — Tests no longer reach `%LOCALAPPDATA%` through `SdcApp::new` (2026-10-17)

`SdcApp::new` and `SetPreview::from_settings` called `meshes::default_store_path()`, so every GUI test that built the app pointed the Meshes model and the set preview at the developer's real `scan.db`. Both now take the path from `model.scan_db` (set only by `main`; `None` in tests). The shipped app is unchanged. `SetPreview::from_settings` gains a `store_path` argument (`set_preview.rs` is a NIF-team file; the edit is one line). The shader-cache dir is only opened by the render thread, which tests do not start, and the crash log is installed by `main` alone, so neither changed. Test: `tests/app_no_local_store.rs`.

## Note BY — Trace-debug wave 2 fixes (main team, 2026-10-17)

Fixes for the important main-team findings of `.superpowers/sdd/trace-debug/2026-10-17-wave2-report.md` (#1–#6, #8, #9) and the two minors that touched files Tessalith did not write (#15, #48). Branch `fix/wave2`. #7 is the NIF team's (Note BW). The other minors are parked.

- **BY1 A `pbr_emissive` switched to BC7 drops an unpinned BC6H-only backend (#1; amends S3).** When the hdr-source fact turns BC6H into BC7, an explicit backend is kept only if it can write BC7 or was pinned (sub-type- or file-scoped `--set`, a rule), the rule `backend_follows_format` already uses. A preset or config `[subtypes.pbr_emissive] encoder.backend = "ispc_bc6h"` (what the preset creator writes for "Built-in") now gives bc7e, with the fact's provenance, instead of CFG-INVALID on every 8-bit emissive. A pinned BC6H-only backend still reports CFG-INVALID.
- **BY2 The rename dialog ignores Enter on the frame it opens (#2; extends AG11).** `dialogs::opened_before` is the was-open check `modal_keys` had; the rename dialog's Enter = Apply uses it, so the palette's Enter on "Rename" no longer applies the last recipe at once.
- **BY3 Only a user's save removes a crash `.recovery` file (#3; amends AR7).** Save, and Overwrite on the changed-on-disk question, delete the saved document's `.recovery` file. The saves Tessalith makes by itself (an export folder, BV6; a JSON hash record, BD2) keep it: they do not hold the recovered edits. The banner line still goes once the document is newer than the recovery file. docs/gui.md says so.
- **BY4 A slot link names the written output (#4; clarifies Z9 "Link value (R9)").** A member without a planned output path links to the folder of its game path plus its output's file name, as `colour_mesh_key`/`gras_key` take them: `leaf_normal.png` links as `textures\landscape\leaf_n.dds`, `moss_albedo.png` as `moss.dds`. The delete-section slot paths (G6 hits) use the same rule. Links saved before keep their old value; no migration.
- **BY5 Own known-texture rows have no source extension (#5; AF8/AO2).** The project's own rows in `known_textures` (input-name box, JSON editor pickers) are the game path without its extension (`textures/landscape/rock02`, not `.png`). They still name the source file, not the written output: a `_normal` member lists as `rock01_normal`. *shortcut:* matching them to the written name (BY4's rule) is left for when a picker needs it; a JSON match on `rename` differs anyway.
- **BY6 A plan while the scan store is unsettled keeps the mesh evidence (#6; extends BT6).** `AppModel::scan_store_unsettled` is set when a Meshes scan starts and cleared only by a completed scan. While it is set, the evidence read returns the votes, alpha, Tree_Anim and GRAS already held, and "Used by meshes" starts no read (a list already read stays; none read means hidden). *shortcut:* a restart after a cancel starts settled and reads the empty store; a store-level marker would cover it (owner call). Amended by Note CW (CW1, CW2).
- **BY7 A JSON editor pick stores `\` (#8; P26 unchanged).** A path picked from the editor's known-paths list is stored with `\`, so the set Exact pill no longer stores `textures/...` and blocks export; slot 1's own diffuse picked from the list stays derived. Typed values with `/` still block (P26). Values stored with `/` before stay red until re-picked.
- **BY8 A set's `path_contains` and `nif_filter` are written with `\` (#9; fills a gap in P26).** The set-entry writer converts `/` for these two keys, as the delete-section writer does. Conversion, not a block: P26 never covered these keys and the section writer already converts. `cubemap` (also free text) is unchanged. The set preview still compares the raw value.
- **BY9 A failure after the DDS write removes only a sidecar this run wrote (#15; BV3, BV4).** `FileTracker::sidecar_written` limits `run_one`'s cleanup, so a hand-made `.dds.json` kept as OUT-SIDECAR-KEPT survives a failed manifest append.
- **BY10 The case-only-rename cleanup needs a record (#48; O6, BO4).** `history::remove_own_case_twin` removes the old-case twin only when a hash record exists and the twin still hashes to it; the CS PBR and complex-material JSON exports both use it. An unrecorded or unreadable twin stays.

## Note BZ — bc7e tuning: the `max` level and patch 0002 (2026-10-18)

Study: docs/research/bc7e-tuning.md (Poly Haven CC0 corpus, 100 textures at 1k; bench `bc7-tune` and a near-exhaustive reference encoder).

- **BZ1 A new effort level `max`, off by default.** `encoder.effort = "max"` maps to bc7e's `bc7e_compress_block_params_init_sdc_max` (patch 0002): `veryslow`'s search with 4 partitions tried and fully refined, uber 4, two least-squares passes and a greedy ±1 search over the quantised endpoints. Measured against `veryslow` over 100 images: +0.12 dB RGB on diffuse, +0.069° and +0.40 dB RGB on normal maps, +0.16 dB on cutouts, +0.12 dB premultiplied on smooth alpha, every image better, at about 2.7× the time. No preset uses it. BC6H under `max` is ISPC `veryslow`, as under `slowest`.
- **BZ2 The default stays byte-identical.** Patch 0002 adds trailing fields and one export to `bc7e.ispc`; with its two flags off every existing level encodes the same bytes. `encoders-sys` `tests/level_identity.rs` pins the SHA-256 of every shipped level's output for both perceptual and both exact-opaque settings (and now the `max` level, checked only when the objects carry the patch); the goldens do not move. A change to a shipped level needs a new note and a version bump.
