- **BZ3 The endpoint search is a candidate for the default, not adopted here.** On its own it gives +0.05 dB colour, +0.065° / +0.34 dB on normals and +0.14 dB on cutouts at 1.4× the time, on 100 of 100 images. Turning it on in `veryslow` changes every BC7 output (goldens, version, an `if-changed` re-encode of every recorded output), so it is an owner ruling; the numbers are in the study.
- **BZ4 Partition breadth without refinement is not a lever.** bc7e refines only the winning partition once more than two are ranked, so widening the ranking lowers colour quality (4 tried: −0.044 dB); `m_refine_partitions` fixes that and is part of `max`. `slowest` is left as upstream defines it. Per-channel weights for normals lower the angular error but worsen Z, which Skyrim reads directly: not adopted.
- **BZ5 Objects are rebuilt on Windows.** The Linux ISPC 1.31.0 binary cannot emit COFF, so the vendored `ispc-objs/bc7e` objects and header still carry only patch 0001; `build.rs` detects the patch from the header, the shim has no level 7 without it, and `check_profile` refuses `effort = "max"` with `CFG-INVALID`. Owner step: `tools/regen-ispc.ps1 -Update -Bc7eOnly`, `tools/hash-vendor.ps1`, `cargo test -p encoders-sys`, the golden test. The study's timings come from Linux objects built from the same source and flags (plus `--target-os=linux --pic`), which reproduce the vendored objects' output byte for byte.
- **BZ6 Corpus.** Public CC0 Poly Haven 1k textures, one per material family, listed with hashes in `docs/research/bc7e-tuning/MANIFEST.tsv`. Poly Haven has no opacity maps, so the cutout and smooth classes are each asset's Diffuse with alpha built from its own Displacement or AO map (thresholded and blurred, or as is); their alpha numbers are a guide, not decal results.

## Note CA — GUI layout v2, branch 1 (main team, 2026-10-18)

Branch `feat/layout-v2-bottom`: the bottom panel (Problems, Review, Messages, Files), status colours, Review in place of the three export dialogs, and the PGPatcher JSON pre-answer. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-gui-layout-v2-design.md`. Letter CA is the next free one on `main` at 2026-10-18; rename it at merge if it collides. Rulings R1-R11 and R20 as built, then the controller rulings the user would notice.

- **CA1 Review is a tab, not a dialog (R1; supersedes the dialog half of N3, AG11/line 960, AG112's list, BV10).** `Dialog::{ProceedAnyway, ExportBlocked, ExportWarnings}` are removed. `AppModel.review: Option<Review>` holds only what the user answered (the pitfall ticks, the JSON pre-answer); blockers, undecided textures and pitfalls are derived live from `export_blocks`, `undecided_keys` and `export_asks`. Review is never `model.dialog`, so `queued_export_dropped`, `raise_error` and `finish_json`'s "another question is open" guards are unchanged. `plan_unsettled` and `export_folder_problem` stay `Dialog::Error`. Export opens Review when there is a blocker, an undecided texture, an `export_asks` pitfall or an edited PGPatcher JSON (CA7); otherwise it exports at once (C2).
- **CA2 Review never exports by itself (R2).** Deciding the last undecided texture only relabels the button ("Export 20 files (skip 2 undecided)" becomes "Export 22 files"). `refresh_undecided_dialog` and `refresh_if_settled` are gone. The only way out of Review is its Export button, and Enter does nothing there (R11, BS14 aside): `dialog_keys::enter_with_review_open_never_exports`. The "Dialogs" Enter/Esc rows in the shortcut table no longer name Proceed anyway or Export warnings (K1: the `dialog-enter` label is "Press the dialog's safe default").
- **CA3 Export from Review is `Continue::Review` (R3; K5b).** `export_from_review` is `export_clicked`'s front half (a plan in flight: wait; changed sources: plan again and wait), in `continue_review`, then `run_continue(Continue::Review)`, which runs `export_stopped` (plan settled, export folder, blocks) and the Review gate before `start_export`. Undecided textures are skipped, as N3's Proceed anyway did. `enum Continue` has this one variant. `run_continue(Review)` re-queues while a plan or the votes are pending and returns when `review` is `None`.
  - Pointer (Note CI24): `enum Continue` now has `Review` and `HalfSize { save }`.
- **CA4 Pitfalls: a tick each, plus Acknowledge all (R4; owner, 2026-10-17).** Each pitfall row has an Acknowledge tick and the Warnings column has **Acknowledge all**. Export stays disabled ("Acknowledge 2 warnings first") until every current pitfall is ticked. Ticks are keyed by the issue's exact text, so a changed or new pitfall needs a new tick. They count for one export only: cleared when the export starts, when Review closes and when a folder opens. Nothing is saved (no `sdc.toml`/`gui.toml` field).
- **CA5 "Warned" means `export_asks` (R5).** Texture and set warnings (`counts_toward_badge`) never open Review; they are in Problems and, as a count, in Review's Warnings column ("N other warnings - see Problems", A4).
- **CA6 What will be written (R6, C4).** Review hashes each JSON on disk against its record: absent: "will be written"; hash equals the record: "will be replaced (written by Tessalith)"; else "edited outside Tessalith"; unreadable: "cannot be read; kept". K13: a vanilla export, or a project with no PGPatcher entries, shows no PGPatcher line and `pgp_json_edited` is false. To list the CS PBR and complex-material files, `review_json` runs `cs_pbr_export::prepare` and `cm_json::prepare`, which build those JSON texts; the result is cached for 1 s per view key (CA22).
- **CA7 The PGPatcher JSON pre-answer (R6, K12).** An edited PGPatcher JSON is a fourth reason to open Review. Its line offers **Keep the edited file** / **Overwrite it**; neither is preselected. The answer stores the on-disk hash; `finish_json` applies it only when the file still has that hash, else today's `Dialog::OverwriteJson` asks after the export. `start_export` always moves the answer out of `review` into `pending_json_answer`, and `finish_json` takes it on entry, so a cancelled, failed or no-JSON export never leaves a stale "Overwrite" for a later one. No choice made: today's question after the export (BV10 08f-2 carries over to `export_from_review`).
- **CA8 CS PBR and complex-material JSON show their status only (R6).** Only the PGPatcher JSON offers a choice. An edited CS PBR or complex-material JSON does not open Review; its behaviour is unchanged (kept, with a note in the report). The JSON lines list scrolls in an area capped at 96 px.
- **CA9 Bottom panel placement (R7).** Full window width under the header, drawn before the columns, in both views. Collapsed it is one strip of tab buttons with their counts (its own panel id, so the strip's height never becomes the open panel's). State is `AppModel.bottom` (open, tab, Problems filter), so badge clicks, Export, Ctrl+M and tests pick tabs. The Review tab is listed only while `review` is `Some`; `close_review` collapses the panel when it showed Review and the tab listing falls back to Files when `review` is `None`. A "Go to ..." click in the Meshes view switches to the Textures view. Opening a folder or reloading calls `close_review` (K5).
- **CA10 Ctrl+M and the Messages tab (R8).** Ctrl+M and the header's Messages button open the Messages tab, or collapse the panel when it already shows Messages. `Messages::is_open` means "the Messages tab is showing" (set by `sync_messages_open`), so unread counting is unchanged. The floating Messages window is gone; toasts stay, anchored to the window's bottom-right, so over an open panel they cover its bottom-right corner (Review's Export included). They take no clicks, so Export still works under them; moving them above the panel waits (controller, final review). (Superseded in part by CD5: there is no Messages button in the header; Ctrl+M or the Messages tab opens the tab.)
- **CA11 Problems (A1, K8, K9, R9).** Rows are built once per change (key: the views key, `evidence_rev`, `export.revision` and whether an export runs) and only the rows on screen are drawn. Order: blockers, "Failed: ...", "Needs a decision: ...", `export_asks` pitfalls, texture warnings, set warnings, RNM notes, then the last export's per-file warnings once it has ended. An acknowledged code is no longer a Decide row, but the warning stays listed (K8). A row is one non-wrapping line. Its fix buttons (**Go to set**, **Set type…**, **Decide…**, **Acknowledge**) and the code are laid out at the right edge first and stay visible; the sentence is cut with an ellipsis to the room left, and hovering it shows it in full (final review I2: before, a long row pushed its buttons off-screen at 1280x800).
- **CA12 `fix_off()` is the one definition of "fix buttons off" (K11, K10).** `toml_read_only_reason()` first, else "Wait for the plan to finish" while a plan or the votes are pending. A running export does not disable them (edits stay live, BD2) and a read-only sets document does not either (decisions work there today). Review's Export is a different test, `review_gate`: it is **not** disabled by a plan in flight; a plan in flight queues the click (Review Focus 1), read-only `sdc.toml` disables it with the reason, and an export in progress says "An export is running".
- **CA13 A queued Review export is re-gated and can be dropped.** A click while a plan is in flight queues the export. When the plan lands the gate runs again on the new plan: a new pitfall stops it with "Export not started: Acknowledge 1 warning first", a new blocker stops it, and nothing exports on the stale plan. The 08f-1 guard in `finish_plan` also drops a queued Review export when a dialog is open, with the existing dropped-export note; "never a silent export" outranks R1's "unchanged", which meant the guard's existence. **Close** cancels a queued Review export (`close_review` clears `continue_after_plan`). `reload_documents` clears `export_after_plan` and `continue_after_plan` as `open_folder` does (K4).
- **CA14 The BS14 focus guard applies to Review's Export.** Review's Export saves first (`start_export`), so a click with a text field focused says "Export: leave the text field first", as the header Export does, and does not start the export (`header::field_focused`).
- **CA15 `plan_failed` keeps Review open; AF4 stays header-only.** A failed plan leaves Review open: the blockers stay visible and the gate still blocks. AF4 ("an edit during a scan-finished read cancels the queued export") stays for the header Export only; a queued Review export is re-gated on the new plan instead (CA13). The two buttons differ in feedback and are equally safe.
- **CA16 The export drawer's Warnings tab is gone (R9, C3).** The drawer is the bottom panel's Files tab; Export opens it. Per-file export warnings are reachable from each Files row's hover (`warning_line`) and as Problems rows that select the file once the export has ended; while it runs the Files tab shows them live. Grouping by code goes (`ExportModel::by_code` stays for the reports). `ExportModel.open` is removed.
- **CA17 A reload clears the pre-answer.** `reload_documents` also clears `pending_json_answer` (a reload mid-export falls back to today's question after the export): the safe side of never overwriting. Opening another folder or a reload closes Review and exports nothing (Review Focus 2).
- **CA18 The set editor's Warnings block becomes one line (R10).** "N problems in this set - Show in Problems" opens Problems filtered to the set (`set_problem_count`). A Textures column count "N need a decision" and a set's warning badge are buttons that open Problems narrowed (Undecided / Set). The recipe lines and "no file matches" lines stay.
- **CA19 Enter with Review open (R11).** Nothing: Review is not a dialog and its Export is a click only. Export blocked, Proceed anyway and Export warnings lose their Enter rules with their dialogs (AG11). **Esc** changes too: those dialogs closed on Esc, but Review does not; it closes only with **Close** (or by opening another folder, reloading or starting the export). Esc keeps its other meanings (clear the selection, close the preview).
- **CA20 Status colours (A12; K14).** One source, `ui/status.rs`, which defines `RED` and `AMBER` (`pub`); `ui/columns.rs` re-exports them (`pub(super) use super::status::{AMBER, RED}`) for its callers: `RED` blocks the export, `AMBER` is a warning or a decision, `GREEN` is a dot for "ready" on a texture tile, a set row and the header Export (a folder open, something to write, Problems empty); teal is the only non-status colour. The Export hover says "N files, M problems".
- **CA21 Copy.** "1 other warning", "1 DDS file": pluralised, same meaning as the plan's strings. Review's pluralisation and the late-pitfall test use `alphaprop_thresh = 128`. The Review gate order is: folder open, read-only `sdc.toml`, export running, blockers, unticked pitfalls.
- **CA22 Review's asks and blocks are cached per change (R-b).** `ViewCache` holds the `export_asks` result so Review draws it every frame for free; nothing else writes `known` directly. The JSON line cache is a `RefCell` on `AppModel` beside `views`, valid for 1 s and per view key, cleared with `review`.
- **CA23 The screenshot test is not committed (R20).** `ui_shots.rs` needs the removed `Dialog` variants and the drawer's old fields, so it lives on `scratch/ui-shots` and is copied, adapted and run per branch. This branch's adapted copy and its shots are in `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-1/` (untracked). `SdcApp::new` no longer reads `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (Note BX), so only `%APPDATA%` still needs redirecting to a temp folder.
- **CA24 Docs.** `docs/gui.md` has a new "The bottom panel" section (Problems, Review, Messages, Files); its Sets/Textures column statement now matches `ui/mod.rs` (two left panels, Textures then Sets, then the centre; Advanced at the right edge). `docs/wiki/GUI-Guide.md` and `Getting-Started.md` follow.
- **CA25 Review's columns stay above its footer (final review I1).** In egui 0.36.2 `ui.columns` sizes every column to the bottom of the whole panel, ignoring the footer (What will be written, the JSON choice, Close, Export), so column widgets drew over the footer and took its clicks. The columns now sit in `ui.allocate_ui(ui.available_size(), ...)`, so each column's scroll area ends at the footer's top and scrolls inside that space. A button low in a long column (for example **Accept all suggestions**) may need a scroll to reach. Test: `review_tab::the_columns_stay_above_the_footer`.

## Note CB — bc7e: patch-0002 objects on Windows, per-target level pins, `ep` re-check on Skyrim textures (main team, 2026-10-18)

Branch `feat/bc7e-max`. Follows Note BZ.

- **CB1 `effort = "max"` works.** The vendored `ispc-objs/bc7e` objects and header are rebuilt from the patch-0002 source with ISPC 1.31.0 on Windows (`tools/regen-ispc.ps1 -Update -Bc7eOnly`, `tools/hash-vendor.ps1`). A second regen run matches 12/12. `BC7E_MAX_NATIVE` is now true, and `policy_checks::effort_max_needs_the_patch_0002_objects` passes on the plan-cleanly side. This supersedes BZ5's "objects still carry only patch 0001".
- **CB2 Level hashes are pinned per ISPC target (coordinator's ruling, 2026-10-18).**
  - The problem: `level_identity.rs` failed on `main` 1cc91a3 for every row with the shipped patch-0001 objects, while the goldens passed. BZ's pins came from the cloud agent's Linux objects, and none of the 32 matches any Windows code path.
  - What differs: ISPC dispatches per CPU. On this machine sse2, sse4 and avx encode alike, and avx2 (FMA) encodes differently.
  - The fix: the shim's `sdc_bc7e_compress` takes a target (−1 = dispatch). A forced target runs its own table init once. `encoders_sys::bc7e_compress_blocks_on(…, Bc7Target)` routes the best supported target through the dispatcher, so the dispatcher's tables are never re-initialised under a running encode.
  - The test pins `[target][level][perceptual][exact]` and skips only the targets the CPU lacks.
  - The order was: re-pin from the patch-0001 objects first (commit `6ef3bbf`, goldens 95/95), then rebuild. Levels 0 to 6 kept every per-target hash; only level 7 was newly pinned.
- **CB3 Correction to BZ5 and the study.** BZ5 and the study say the Linux objects reproduce the vendored objects' output byte for byte. That is not true on Windows (CB2). bc7e output depends on the CPU's ISPC target, so two machines (avx2 against older) can write different BC7 bytes for the same input. This is a pre-existing property and nothing here changes it. The goldens pass on avx2 machines.
- **CB4 The endpoint search is not adopted in `veryslow` (owner's acceptance rule, Skyrim re-check).**
  - The sample: 60 diffuse, 60 normal (`_n`), 16 cutout and 14 smooth from the owner's 10k Skyrim PNG set, drawn by a seeded shuffle and listed in `docs/research/bc7e-tuning/skyrim-sample.tsv`. Measured with `sdc-bench bc7-tune`, `base` against `ep`, on the CB1 objects.
  - The results:

    | Class | Δ [95% CI] | Wins |
    |---|---|---|
    | diffuse | RGB +0.645 [±0.784] | 60/60 |
    | normal | angle +0.0285° [±0.0048] | 59/60, 1 tie |
    | cutout | RGB +0.133 [±0.142] | 16/16 |
    | smooth | premul +0.204 [±0.088] | 12/14, 2 ties |

    Time is 1.37 to 1.50×.
  - The rule needs four things: diffuse Δ RGB > 0 with a CI that excludes 0 and at least +0.025 dB; normal Δ angle > 0 with a CI that excludes 0 and at least +0.03°; no class significantly worse; and time at most 1.7×. The diffuse CI includes 0, because two near-flat images gain +11 and +21 dB. The normal Δ is 0.0015° short. So the claim does not hold.
  - Context for a re-ruling: with base PSNR over 60 dB excluded, diffuse is +0.079 [±0.019] and normal +0.0313° [±0.0049]. No image got worse on its class's primary metric. Details are in `docs/research/bc7e-tuning.md`, "Windows re-check on Skyrim textures (2026-10-18)".
- **CB5 Nothing else changes.** The default output, goldens and workspace version are unchanged, and no re-encode follows.

## Note CC — GUI layout v2, branch 2 (main team, 2026-10-18)

Branch `feat/layout-v2-set-editor` (commits 1cc91a3..58d6b7d, then the docs-only commit that updates this note): readable labels and framed groups, slot rows, a right-hand set panel with an Advanced tab, and the PBR material groups with header values. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-gui-layout-v2-design.md`. The letter CC is provisional: Note CB is taken by the unmerged `feat/bc7e-max` branch; rename this note at merge if CC collides. Rulings R12, R13 and the pre-flight rulings K1-K22 as built, then the controller rulings the user would notice.

- **CC1 Slot cards become rows and keep every card behaviour (A2; K1-K4).** `set_editor::rows` draws one `egui::Grid` of six columns (Slot, thumbnail, File, Format, Flags, Status) with the set editor's old card behaviours intact: lock cross, RNM outline, clash rows, Match on this, borrowed, Opaque, packed controls, the slot menu, the Explorer drop and the click / double-click wait. A grid cell cannot hold a row-wide click, so a row registers `ui.interact` on last frame's row rect before its cells (so the cells keep their own clicks); that response carries the slot menu and the drop (`interact_rect.contains(drop_at)`). The amber / `RNM_OUTLINE` stroke is painted on the same rect. The first frame has no rect, so no row menu then (accepted). The Status cell is a dot: `Failed`/`Error` is Blocks, `tile_ready` is Ready, anything else Warning. The reason texts ("borrowed from X", "not used by {shader}", "RNM, {n} layers") are on the dot's hover; the old hover texts are unchanged, so the kept tests match once. An empty slot shows **Assign…** in the Format column, which opens the slot menu. The complex `_m` parallax box stays in `unslotted_packed` (K2). A lock on a set that writes no JSON shows a weak info mark with `PGP_LOCK_UNWRITTEN` (A4). Supersedes the card wording of AG98 and BS4 (rows take the drop where they show).
- **CC2 Width rulings (2.2, 2.3).** Slot columns are compact: the file name truncates (name and size on hover), Flags are icon toggles with hovers (accessible names "Match on this" and "Opaque" unchanged; their role changed from CheckBox to a selectable Button), Status is a dot only; target about 440 px. The rows sit in a horizontal `ScrollArea` clipped to their column as the fallback: at a narrower centre they scroll sideways and are never drawn under a neighbour (the first build drew them under the PGPatcher panel, which took their clicks). The File cell takes the column width minus the other columns' widest content from the last frame, clamped to 60-240 px with an 8 px margin (without the margin a row exactly as wide as its column flipped the scroll bar every frame). The set panel's default width is 300 px, which is also its minimum (the brief's 420 left the rows 308 px; only 300 fits them at 1400 wide without sideways scroll), and its content uses `ScrollArea::both` (a vertical-only area let the PBR Landscape card, about 388 px, widen the panel past its range and the layout never settled). Cost: that card and the skin card scroll sideways at the default width. Panel range is `300..=(avail - CENTRE_MIN/2).max(300)` (K20), one `Id::new("set-panel")` for every set so a dragged width carries over (A10).
- **CC3 The right-hand set panel and its tabs (R12, K9, K10, K19).** In 2D a selected set gets a right panel with two tabs, **Material** (**Set** on a vanilla set) and **Advanced** last, bound to `settings.advanced_open`. `advanced::body(ui, &mut AppModel, &mut AdvancedState)` is the eight Advanced sections and applies its own actions (K9); `advanced::draw` keeps its signature. `ui::mod` shows the panel when `set_editor_shown(model, three_d)` and not 3D, and draws the window-edge drawer only when the panel is not shown; when the drawer is skipped `ui.skip_ahead_auto_ids(1)` keeps the later widgets' ids stable (without it a set pill's context menu closed on the next frame).
- **CC4 A6: `advanced_open` is shared by the tab and the drawer.** Choosing the Advanced tab on a set sets `advanced_open`, so the drawer opens when a texture is selected next, and the other way round. Intended ("remembered as today"). With a set selected, the Advanced texture fields section reads "Select a texture to edit its encoder and header fields." (A7).
- **CC5 3D routing.** In 3D the window-edge Advanced strip/drawer is drawn and the set panel is not (the set's settings are in the 3D settings window). With a texture selected, several sets selected, an expanded texture or a set no longer in the plan, the drawer is drawn and the panel is not. `set_editor_shown` mirrors `centre`'s routing and takes `three_d`; it is true for any 3D state, so the callers add the 2D/3D side. `set_panel::drawer_and_panel_never_both_or_neither` pins it for seven cases, four mutations of the predicate fail it.
- **CC6 K12: `pgp_fields::panel` is split.** `panel_main` (Material to Matching) and `panel_advanced` (Advanced TruePBR settings); `panel` = both, so `cs_pbr::pgp_panel` and the NIF 3D settings window call it unchanged. On a non-landscape JSON set the Material tab draws `panel_main`, `cs_pbr::section`, `panel_advanced`; a PBR Landscape set keeps `cs_pbr::pgp_panel`. Group order: Material, Features, Coat (Multilayer), Subsurface, Emissive, Parallax, Glint, Fuzz, NiAlphaProperty, Matching, CS PBR records, Advanced TruePBR settings.
- **CC7 Framed groups and readable labels (A8, K15, K17, K18).** `ui/group.rs::group` is a framed collapsing group; its title is a `Label` with `Sense::click` that toggles it (the collapsing icon alone toggles by default), the accessible label stays the title, and the value is a `RichText` right-aligned in the header (so Matching can use AMBER). `pgp_fields.rs` keeps its private `fn group`; the framed one is called by path (K17). Skin and complex-material keys show readable labels with the exact key on hover (initialisms AO, UV, RGB, SSS, F0: "SSS width", "Use SSS", "Fuzz F0"; A1). The key hover is on label rows only; checkbox kinds draw their label inside `control`, shared with `json_editor.rs` (A3).
- **CC8 Header values (2.4).** Features: "{n} on" or "none" (n counts `feature_on` in `eff`). Subsurface: Off, Standard, Foliage, or "Standard + Foliage (conflict)". Coat, Emissive, Parallax, Glint, Fuzz: "on" or "off". NiAlphaProperty: "set" or "off". Matching: "{n} match(es)" (all rows, including an empty one added by "+"), or "matches nothing" in AMBER. CS PBR records: "1 record" or "{n} records" (txst and mato blocks present, 0-2). The PBR Landscape card and "PGPatcher JSON settings" show no value (A12).
- **CC9 Feature groups are always listed, reading "off" while off (A3 header-value design).** Coat, Emissive, Parallax, Glint and Fuzz used to be hidden while off; now they are listed, closed and "off". An off group's body is empty except Coat, whose body holds the kept-values note (A13), and Subsurface, whose body holds the selector (CC12). A group's id is keyed by its on/off state (`("pgp", g, on, set)`), so a group opens when its feature turns on (K16).
- **CC10 Blocked-feature header semantics.** A feature that is on but blocked (multilayer while hair is on) reads "off" in its own header and stays closed, because the value and the default-open use `group_open` (on and not blocked). Features still counts it in "{n} on" (it counts `feature_on`). Subsurface's header shows `sub_mode`, so a stored but blocked Standard reads "Standard" while the group stays closed.
- **CC11 NiAlphaProperty starts closed**, even when a key is set (it used to open when set). The header value says "set".
- **CC12 Subsurface: the selector loses its own label.** The selector is the first row of the Subsurface group body and the group title names it; two equal labels would also make `get_by_label("Subsurface")` ambiguous. The combo is still named by its value. It moved from Features into the Subsurface group, which is collapsed while Off.
- **CC13 K13: titles changed, also in the NIF-owned 3D settings window.** "Coat settings" is "Coat", "Subsurface settings" is "Subsurface", "Advanced: CS PBR records" is "CS PBR records" (`cs_pbr::SECTION`). `the_3d_layout_truepbr_settings_show_the_coat_group` takes the new string. the NIF team's HANDOFF.md has two appended lines (K13, K14 and the list below).
- **CC14 K14: the JSON-editor button left `pgp_fields::panel`.** The 3D settings window therefore has no "Open the TruePBR JSON editor…" button any more. The Material tab has a small **TruePBR JSON editor…** button right-aligned on its header row (the set label on the left); the header's "PG JSON Editor" button and the palette still open the editor in 3D.
- **CC15 What the 3D settings window shows differently.** Every group is framed with its value in the header; the order is Material, Features, Coat, Subsurface, Emissive, Parallax, Glint, Fuzz (Subsurface used to follow Parallax); the five feature groups are always listed and closed while off; the Subsurface selector is inside the Subsurface group; NiAlphaProperty starts closed; the titles in CC13; no JSON-editor button; on a PBR Landscape set "PGPatcher JSON settings" and the "PBR Landscape" card are framed groups.
- **CC16 Used by plugins and Advanced move (C6, K12).** In the Material tab the order after the groups is the skin card, the complex-material card, CS PBR records (when not already drawn between Matching and Advanced TruePBR settings) and Used by plugins. CS PBR records now sit in the right panel, titled **CS PBR records** (was "Advanced: CS PBR records"), collapsed, header "1 record" or "{n} records". The Advanced drawer's content is the panel's last tab.
- **CC17 Group value parameter.** `group`'s value changed from `&str` to `Option<RichText>` in 2.4 (branch-owned 2.1 code), so the caller sets the style.
- **CC18 Tests, pre-flight items.** Finders: `slot_rect(h, label)` returns the leftmost match, because the Matching header has its own "Diffuse" row (K5); "Assign..." has four matches on `pbr_opened_plain` (K6); the size test waits for `size_of` (K7); `slot_commands_is_a_normal_button_after_the_rows` was a regression pin, not a RED test (K8: the button is wrapped in `ui.horizontal`); the tab "Material" and the group "Material" share a label, so tests find the tab by `Role::Button` (K11); `labels.rs` and `set_panel.rs` copy the helpers they need (K18, K19); the Multilayer checkbox is "Multilayer (coat)" (K21). A ScrollArea takes every scroll target set inside it, so `rows` re-issues a row's ScrollIntoView after the horizontal area ends.
- **CC19 K22: the shots.** The branch's adapted capture test and shots are in `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-2/` (untracked, R20), with shots of the set panel's Advanced tab on a vanilla set and on a PBR set (the texture drawer, shot 17, is unchanged by this branch).
- **CC20 Final review I1: header values stay inside the visible edge.** A group wider than the panel (the Coat or Emissive colour row, the ~390 px PBR Landscape card) widened the scroll content, and egui unions that into every later header row's `max_rect`, so the right-aligned values were drawn past the clip rect. `group`'s header row is now bounded by `min(max_rect.right, clip_rect.right - item_spacing.x)` (the inset keeps the last glyph off the clip edge) and fills that width (which also widens the value-less Material frame to the panel); the value sits in a right-to-left child bounded by it. Also fixes the NIF 3D settings window, which calls the same `group`. Test `set_panel::header_values_stay_inside_the_panel_with_coat_on`. Re-review: the fill width is measured from the cursor (egui's `Placer::set_min_width` does; measuring from the frame edge made every group ~18 px too wide, the collapser's width, so each PBR panel scrolled sideways and clipped the frame borders), and a title wider than the visible width skips its value instead of overlapping it; test `group::tests::a_group_header_never_widens_its_scroll_area`.
- **CC21 Final review I2: the scroll bars are drawn without hover.** egui 0.36's default floating `ScrollStyle` has dormant opacity 0, so the rows' horizontal bar (at 1280 px and narrower Format, Flags and Status are to the right) and the panel's bars only showed on hover. Both scroll areas use a scoped `ScrollStyle::thin()` (6 px, always drawn); a horizontal bar takes height, so the File-width margin of CC2 is unaffected. No kittest check: egui gives the bar no AccessKit node and its opacity is paint-only; the re-shot images in `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-2-fix/` are the evidence.
- **CC22 Shorter PGPatcher off title.** `PGP_PANEL_OFF` is "PGPatcher JSON settings (not written)"; the hint "Not written: tick 'Also write into the PGPatcher JSON' above." is the body's first weak line. The old ~85-character title used `TextWrapMode::Extend` and widened every group below it (CC20). Supersedes the title wording of BM14.

Pointers on older notes (append-only): AG98, AG101, AJ1, BM7, BM14 and BS4 carry a "Superseded in part by CC..." line.

## Note CD — GUI layout v2, branch 3 (main team, 2026-10-18)

Branch `feat/layout-v2-columns` (commits 9c2d1e5..d096412, then the docs-only commit that adds this note): one header row, set cards, the Textures and Sets filters and the start screen. The engine, goldens and `gui.toml` / `sdc.toml` schemas are unchanged apart from two new `[layout]` keys (CD11). Rulings R14 to R17 and R21 of the plan, plus the ones the user will notice:

- **CD1 One header row (A4, R14, R21).** The order is Open, Undo, Redo, MO2… + Mode (framed), the Preset combo, the view tabs, the column eyes (Textures view with a folder open only), then Export to ▾, Save and Export against the right edge. Save and Export are both twice the interact height tall. The tabs show "Textures" / "Meshes" and keep the accessible names "Textures view" / "Meshes view" (`widget_info`), so the NIF team's `meshes_view.rs` finds them unchanged. `view_toggle(ui)` keeps its signature.
- **CD2 The header wraps below about 1340 pt.** Measured: one row at 1360 pt and wider, and from 1320 pt down the Export to, Save and Export group wraps whole onto a second line with no overlap (AG126 still holds: nothing is drawn over anything). At 1024 pt the header is two lines. Accepted, cost if wrong: a tighter header at 1280.
- **CD3 Open and Preset (K5).** The menu label stays "Open" (egui's menu button draws no arrow). It holds Open folder…, a separator and the recent folders ("No recent folders", greyed, when there are none). The Preset popup always opens: preset entries are greyed out with "Open a folder first" while no folder is open, and its last entry, after a separator, is Presets…, which stays enabled.
- **CD4 Export to ▾ (A1, A2, K1, K8).** The button reads "Export to: {path} ▾" ("Export to: not set ▾" with none). A long path is cut from the middle, keeping the drive and the tail (`header::elide_middle`); the accessible name and the hover carry the whole path. The menu holds Choose export folder… (today's disabled reasons), Open export folder (statted only while the menu is open, greyed out with the error) and, when `shows_json_editor`, PGPatcher JSON editor… (S14 rename). PG JSON Editor is no longer a header button; it stays in the palette and the material panel. The Export button keeps its accent, progress bar, green dot and "N files, M problems" hover.
- **CD5 Messages leaves the header (R14).** Messages is the bottom panel's tab; its label counts unread entries and its hover reads "Notes and results of this session (Ctrl+M)" through `actions::keys_text`. Ctrl+M is unchanged. `messages::button` is deleted.
- **CD6 The Meshes view draws the app header (C7).** `app.rs` draws `header::draw` and then the bottom panel before `meshes::show` in the Meshes view; `meshes::page` is no longer called by anything (no src, no test): it is dead NIF-owned code, left for the NIF team to remove, and HANDOFF.md says so. Consequence: the status line and the banner now also show in the Meshes view, and `json_editor::draw` runs there too. No NIF file changed.
- **CD7 Set cards (A5, R15).** Each card: handle, name, a status pill (dot plus "skin", "PBR Landscape", "PBR → JSON" or "vanilla"), "⚠ n", the shader combo at full width, then slot chips. Every keyed card has a dot: Blocks (the set is in `export_blocks`), Warning (not ready) or Ready, so a set that is ready but blocked shows Blocks where it used to show green. A keyless created set also gets a pill, with a Warning dot. The long badge text, `owns …`, `no file matches …` and the recipe lines moved to the pill's hover. The pill of a complex-material set that writes cm JSON still says "vanilla set (no JSON)" on hover (A5, unchanged).
- **CD8 Slot chips (A3, K11 to K13).** A chip's letter is the slot suffix upper-cased (D, N, RMAOS, P, G, SK, CNR, F, S). The spec's example "M" (a `_m` env mask) has no `SlotKind`, so that member is a plain thumbnail after the chips. A filled chip is the 32 px member thumbnail with the letter on it and keeps drag, click-select, double-click-expand and the slot menu. A borrowed chip has a 2 px amber outline, the hover line "borrowed from {set}", and no drag payload. A missing entry is a red "?" chip with "no file matches {name}" on hover. Chips are named by their letter, so tests scope queries to the Sets column (`support::in_sets_column`, `outside_sets`).
- **CD9 Card highlight and the narrow fallback.** The open set's card is filled with the selection colour at 0.35 and keeps the selection stroke; the stroke is now visible while editing, where the drop zone used to hide it (the card look moved to an inner frame). When a card is narrower than 150 px (`WIDE_CARD`) the pill and "⚠ n" wrap to a second row and the kind text truncates, so `SETS_MIN` is unchanged.
- **CD10 Textures pills, Filter ▾ and the tile pair (A6, A7, R16).** The four toggles are pills with counts (`filter_counts`, keyed by `items_rev` only, so a test that writes item status must call `invalidate_views`). **Filter ▾** opens the five combos at 220 px: Sub-type, Output format, Encoder, Set membership and Sort; it reads "Filter (k) ▾" and k does not count Sort. **−** / **+** (Smaller tiles / Larger tiles) step the tiles by 16 within 64 to 192 after Filter ▾; a saved size off the grid loads as it is. The "N not in a set" heading link and the tile slider are gone. Clear filters keeps the sort and the tile size.
- **CD11 Sets filter (R17).** A "Search sets" box, the pills Needs attention / Ready / No JSON with counts, and a Filter ▾ popup with Any and the shaders ("Filter (1) ▾" while one is chosen). Matching is AND. The search folds like set ids (`fold_id`) and tests the id or the label, never the key. A saved shader that the Mode does not offer is still listed (A9). The pills (`sets_filters`) and the shader (`sets_shader`) are saved in `gui.toml` under `[layout]`, each read leniently (a bad name is dropped alone, a wrong type loads as the default); the search text is not saved, as the Textures search.
- **CD12 What the pills count.** Needs attention is every set that is not ready, so Needs attention plus Ready count every keyed set. Counts cover keyed sets only (K20); a keyless created set passes only an empty filter. No JSON uses `writes_json` (A8): a cm-JSON set and a PBR Landscape set that writes CS or PGPatcher JSON are not "No JSON".
- **CD13 Filters hide, never deselect (Review Focus 5).** A filter that hides the open set or part of a multi-selection keeps the selection, the editor and the bulk panel. Go to set from Problems on a hidden set selects it and leaves the filter on (K23). Shift-click ranges follow the visible sets. The Sets selection summary counts hidden sets: "2 selected (1 hidden by filter)".
- **CD14 Ctrl+A (K18).** Ctrl+A selects the visible sets (search and filters applied), as it selects the visible textures. Ctrl+A over nothing (every set or every texture hidden by the filter) is a no-op in both columns: the selection is kept, so a select-all over nothing never deselects. Cost if wrong: Ctrl+A cannot be used to clear a selection when everything is filtered out; Esc still does.
- **CD15 Reorder is off while filtering.** Dragging the ≡ handle and Move up / Move down are disabled while any Sets filter is on, even a search that hides nothing; the hover reads "Clear the filter to reorder sets". A filtered list would otherwise reorder against positions the user cannot see.
- **CD16 A new set stays hidden while a filter is on.** A set created while a Sets filter is on is hidden until the filter is cleared. No code; the "No sets match" line and Clear filter are the way back.
- **CD17 No false "No sets match".** While the first plan runs there are no views, so the no-match line and its Clear filter button (which would wipe pills restored from `gui.toml`) are not drawn until there is at least one set.
- **CD18 The start screen (A11).** With no folder open the centre shows the hint, one filled "Open folder…" button (240 x 44), the Recent list as links and "Or drag a folder onto the window.". The Textures and Sets columns and the Advanced drawer are not drawn without a folder (the bottom strip is, R7); the column eyes need a folder. The saved column widths survive the start screen and apply to the first folder (`column_widths::a_saved_column_width_survives_the_start_screen`). Drops are handled as before.
- **CD19 Tests.** The comment-only tests the plan listed for 3.1 to 3.4 got real assertions. `set_panel::drawer_and_panel_never_both_or_neither` gained the "no folder" case (K22). The shots of this branch are in `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-3/` (untracked, R20), with the adapted `ui_shots.rs` and an INDEX.md; after the final-review fixes, `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-3-fix/` re-shoots them and adds the narrow-card fallback (81), Filter ▾ with a combo open (82) and the drop-target outline (83).
- **CD20 The drop target is outlined (final review I1).** While a texture is dragged over a set card, the card gets egui's `widgets.active` stroke painted over its own frame (the drop zone's hover stroke sits under the inner card frame, CD9). Test: `set_cards::a_texture_dragged_over_a_card_outlines_it`.
- **CD21 Textures Filter ▾ stays open while its combos are used (final review I2).** egui keeps one open popup per viewport, so opening a combo closed a menu kept there and no value could be picked. Filter ▾ (`columns::combo_menu`) keeps its own open state; a click while one of its combos is open only closes that combo, so several filters are picked in one visit; a click outside, Esc or the button closes it. While it is open the shortcuts are held as for egui's popups (`actions::keys`). The Sets Filter ▾ has no combo (one pick closes it) and keeps `path_picker::menu`. Test: `textures_filter::two_filters_are_picked_through_the_filter_popup_without_reopening_it`.
- **CD22 Unselected pills are framed.** The Textures and Sets filter pills draw their button frame when off (`frame_when_inactive`, as the view tabs do), so a row of pills with counts reads as buttons, not statistics.

Pointers on older notes (append-only): AG126, BH3, BH4, BH5, BH6, BH7, BH8, BH10, BH12, BH14 and CA10 carry a "Superseded ... by CD..." line.

## Note CE — GUI layout v2, branch 4 (main team, 2026-10-18)

Branch `feat/layout-v2-dialogs` (commits 0b296b1..1f7ca43, then the docs-only commit that adds this note): one dialog frame, Presets placement, the preview toolbar and a minimum preview width. The engine, goldens and `gui.toml` / `sdc.toml` schemas are unchanged. Rulings R18 to R20 of the plan, plus the ones the user will notice:

- **CE1 One dialog frame (A7, R18, K2).** `dialogs::dialog(ctx, id, outside, width, title, buttons, body)` draws the title strip, the body and a right-aligned footer, on top of `modal_keys`. Each button is `(label, Role, enabled)`. `footer_order` sorts Plain, then Destructive, then Default (stable), so the Enter default is always rightmost. A dialog has at most one Default (`debug_assert!`). `dialog` never presses anything itself: each caller still maps `k.enter` to the answer it always had (AG11 unchanged), so the Default is only drawn.
- **CE2 The Enter default is filled, destructive is outlined (A3).** The Default is filled with `visuals.selection.bg_fill`; a Destructive button gets a 1.5 px outline in `status::RED`. Teal now means "selection and the one primary action" (the header Export, the start screen's Open folder… and Review's Export already did). Red is the existing "blocks export" colour. A dialog where Enter does nothing has no filled button.
- **CE3 Renamed buttons, one line per dialog.**
  - Close / Open unsaved: Cancel, Discard (destructive), Save (Enter). Body "Your edits are not saved." with a weak hint "sdc.toml, sdc-project.toml".
  - Reload with unsaved edits: Discard and reload (destructive), Cancel (Enter).
  - Export running: Stop the export and close, or Stop the export and open the folder (destructive), Keep exporting (Enter).
  - Changed on disk: Reload from disk, Overwrite with my changes (destructive), Cancel (Enter).
  - PGPatcher JSON edited: Overwrite {name} (destructive), Keep the edited {name} (Enter).
  - Error: OK (Enter). Reset all: Reset (destructive), Cancel (Enter). Delete set: Delete (destructive), Cancel (Enter). Set-drop Refused: OK (Enter), titled "Can't do that".
  - Fill from names: Cancel, Fill (Enter). Copy settings: Cancel, Apply, both plain. Discard changes? (preset creator): Cancel, Discard (destructive), no Default.
  - Set rename ("Rename {id}"): Cancel, OK, both plain (the field's own Enter renames).
  - Rename dialog ("Rename {n} inputs", "Rename outputs of {n} sets"): Cancel, Apply (Enter, filled while it is enabled; CE8).
- **CE4 K1: Replace has no Default.** Set-drop Replace is Replace {name} (destructive) and Cancel (plain). Enter did nothing there before (AG11, AG16) and still does nothing, so nothing is filled.
- **CE5 K5: set-drop Choice keeps its three answers in the body.** Move it here, Share (borrow its finished output) and Duplicate the source for this set stay stacked body buttons; the footer has only Cancel. The footer is `right_to_left` with `with_main_wrap(true)`, and its rows start one button tall (CE19), so a row too long for the dialog wraps onto a second row of the same height instead of widening the dialog. Long names are cut in the middle in the button labels; the body gives the whole name (CE19).
- **CE6 Slot commands' Close is Plain (A2).** It had no Enter handling; Esc and a click outside close it.
- **CE7 Dialogs take their full width cap.** The right-aligned footer fills the width, so a dialog is as wide as its cap: 420 for every ordinary dialog (Error and Refused included, which used to shrink to their text), 640 for Slot commands, 860 for rename. Cost if wrong: a fit-to-content tweak.
- **CE8 K4: the rename dialog uses the shared keys (refines AG11).** Rename no longer stamps `opened_before` itself or reads Enter and Esc raw. Enter applies only when no widget has keyboard focus: typing in Find and pressing Enter still applies (a single-line field gives up focus on that Enter), but with a row's tick or the Case combo focused Enter does nothing (before, it applied). Enter on the opening frame is still ignored (BY2). A click outside still does nothing.
- **CE9 Esc with a popup open closes the popup first.** In the rename dialog, Esc with the Case combo open now closes the combo and keeps the dialog (`Modal::should_close` ignores Esc while a popup is open); a second Esc closes the dialog. Before, Esc closed the dialog at once.
- **CE10 Copy settings: Apply is guarded (carry from 4.1).** Apply is enabled only when a field is ticked and the click path checks the same, so two clicks in one slow frame cannot apply nothing. After Check none, Apply turns disabled one frame late (the flag is computed before the body); a click cannot land in that frame.
- **CE11 Presets placement (A9, R19, K6, K7).** The preset creator opens below the header and over the centre column. `app.rs` records `below-header` (the rectangle before the bottom panel, after the scan row) and `centre-rect` (the central panel; in the Meshes view both are the same rectangle). `presets::place` pulls a saved rectangle below the header and into the area; the window also gets `constrain_to(area)` and `max_size(area.size())` every frame, because `constrain_to` alone lets an oversize window rise over the header. The JSON editor (an OS viewport), the Plugin refs window, the 3D settings window and the `meshes` / `viewport3d` modals are not changed (R19, NIF files).
- **CE12 The preview toolbar has three clusters (A10, K9, K10).** Channels, View and Encode are weak captions in one wrapped flow, with separators between them; the sRGB / UNORM pair and the mip control trail after Encode, and only ✕ Close stays in the `right_to_left` reservation (everything else on the right would take width from every row). No `Frame::group`: a framed cluster is laid out as one block and overflows a narrow toolbar. The row count is not pinned (all controls need three rows at 480 to 656 px); the pin is that every control lies inside the `preview-toolbar` panel rect and follows the Channels, View, Encode reading order. The flow is `left_to_right(Align::Min)` with `wrap_mode = Extend`: centring made the toolbar grow every frame, and a caption at a row end wrapped alone.
- **CE13 The toolbar repaints once when it gains a row.** `Panel::top` clips to last frame's height, so on the frame a row appears (the first draw, or a pin adding Compare and Unpin) the new row is drawn clipped. `preview::draw` calls `request_repaint()` when the stored height changed; a click that grows the toolbar is never run twice (`request_repaint`, not `request_discard`). One clipped frame can flash.
- **CE14 Encode now is filled only while it can encode (A9).** "The one filled button" means the one filled push button. Selected toggles (RGBA, Side by side, sRGB, Lens, …) keep egui's selected fill. The "Not encoded" pane's own Encode now button is unchanged.
- **CE15 The 520 px preview floor (K8).** `PREVIEW_MIN = 480` is the picture width. While a texture is expanded the centre floor is `ui::centre_floor` = max(`CENTRE_MIN`, `PREVIEW_MIN` + the 24 px strip + the central panel's 2 × 8 px margin) = **520** (K8 said 504; that left a 464 px viewport, measured). Advanced's upper bound and both `column_panel` ranges use it. The columns' chosen widths come back on collapse. Cost if wrong: 16 px less for the columns while a texture is expanded.
- **CE16 The preview's settings collapse into a strip (A6, A10, A12).** `preview-settings` shows while it fits beside a `PREVIEW_MIN` picture or once opened; otherwise `preview-settings-strip` (a separate id, `resizable(false)`, 24 px, as `advanced-strip`) holds a **Settings** button. The saved `preview-settings` width is never written by the strip. Once opened, the settings stay open until the preview closes, including a direct switch to another texture (`PreviewUi` resets only when nothing is expanded). At the default 1400×900 window the centre is 736 px, so the settings start collapsed there and at 1280×800; at 1600 they show, and opening Advanced there collapses them again.
- **CE17 The Advanced drawer: a minimum, an upper bound, and the chosen width.** `ADV_MIN = 260`; the upper bound leaves the columns their minimums and the centre its floor (CE15). The drawer keeps the width the user chose through the columns' `<id>/chosen` mechanism (`ui::chosen_width_panel`, shared with `column_panel`): the clamped width while a preview is open is not what gui.toml saves, and `layout::panel_width` / `restore_ctx` include `advanced`. A drawer that was never dragged is not saved (`capture` keeps the previous value); a saved width over the cap is restored and kept.
- **CE18 Shots.** Re-shot in `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-4/` (not committed): every dialog, Presets, and the preview toolbar at 1600, 1280 and 1100 with Advanced open and closed, plus pinned.
- **CE19 A wrapped footer keeps its height; names are cut in the button labels (final review I1).** `dialog()` lays the footer out with `allocate_ui_with_layout(vec2(available_width, interact_size.y), ..)`, the way `horizontal_wrapped` seeds its rows. With `with_layout` the rows took last frame's leftover height, so a footer that wrapped doubled the modal's height every frame and pushed the title, the body and the destructive button off screen (OverwriteJson and set-drop Replace with long names). `dialogs::short_name` cuts a name longer than 40 characters to its first 20 and last 16 around "…" in the Overwrite / Keep the edited / Replace labels; the body line keeps the whole name, on screen and in the AccessKit tree. A wrapped footer reads the Default top right and the other buttons on the row below (the A7 left-to-right order holds per row only); with the shortened labels OverwriteJson still takes two rows at 420. Pinned by a 200-character JSON name and a 120-character texture name over eight frames.
- **CE20 The preview settings panel scrolls on both axes (final review I2, A10).** The compact settings are wider than the 280 pt panel (most likely the Normals combo, which has no width cap), and egui 0.36.2 cuts an over-wide right panel from its left, so the toolbar and viewports drew over its left strip and its right edge was clipped (shots 15, 28; this predates branch 1). The panel's content is now `ScrollArea::both` with a scoped `ScrollStyle::thin()` (visible without hover). The panel stays 280 wide where it is, and the centre ends at its left edge. The toolbar beside it is then about 84 pt narrower, which showed that Heatmap and the sRGB / UNORM pair sat in `add_enabled_ui` scopes: a nested scope's first widget never wraps, so at 1600 wide Heatmap ran under ✕ Close. They are now one `add_enabled` widget each (same names and hover text); the K10 toolbar pin runs at 1600 with the settings open too. Giving the combos an exact-width slot, so nothing needs a sideways scroll, can wait.
- **CE21 A clamped window never overwrites its saved size (final review I3).** egui writes a size clamp into a window's own resize state, so `layout::capture` saved the clamped Presets rect and a saved 860×680 came back 604 tall at the next start after one session in a 1100×700 window. `layout::window_rect` keeps the saved width or height when the drawn one is at the clamp (within 1 pt of the area: below the header for Presets, the window for the 3D settings window), still takes the position, and saves nothing for a first rect that is clamped. `shortcut:` a user who drags a window to the full height keeps their previous height. Not fixed here: a saved W×H opens as (W+3)×(H+3) and that is saved back, so the size creeps by 3 points per start (measured at 1600×1000; it predates this branch).

Pointers on older notes (append-only): AM11 carries a "Superseded ... by CE..." line; AG11 is refined, not superseded, and its appended line points to CE1 to CE4 and CE8.

## Note CF — GUI motion and per-frame cost (main team, 2026-10-18)

Spec: `.superpowers/ui-review-motion/00-summary.md` (with 01-03 beside it). Plan rulings R1-R11: R1 drag-reorder stays with virtualisation, R2 reorder while a filter is on, R3 Move to… is a dialog, R4 virtualisation is a clip-rect skip, R5 the grab cursor needs no code, R6 toast motion runs on egui time, R7 worker polling, R8 the texel readout repaint stays, R9 the slot flash detects a changed fill, R10 Reduce motion leaves egui's stock motion alone, R11 Reduce motion comes first. The letter is provisional; it is chosen at merge.

- **CF1 Reduce motion (R10).** One checkbox, **Reduce motion**, in a new **Interface** section of the Advanced drawer, saved in `gui.toml` as `reduce_motion` (default off, so motion is on). `ui::draw_with_scan` mirrors it into an egui context flag every frame (`ui::motion`), so a painter reads it without the model. One rule for every animation this branch adds, and for the toast fade: movement (offset, scale, the progress glide, the press scale) takes 0 s through `motion::move_dur`; fades and colour changes are capped at `motion::FADE_CAP` = 0.12 s through `motion::fade_dur`. egui's stock motion (`Area` fades, collapsing headers, `Style::animation_time`) is not touched.
- **CF2 Toasts (R6).** The whole toast fades: `multiply_opacity` sits in a `ui.scope` around `Frame::popup`, so the frame and its shadow fade with the text (before, only the text faded and the solid box then vanished in one frame). A new toast fades in over 0.2 s (`emath::easing::quadratic_out`) and rises 8 pt to its place over the same entry; the rise runs only until the toast first reaches full opacity. The exit is a 0.2 s `quadratic_out` fade with no movement, starting when the toast's time left is at most the fade (`model::messages::FADE_OUT`; it was 500 ms). One `animate_bool_with_time_and_easing` per toast (`ui::messages::toast_anim_id`), seeded closed on the frame a toast is first seen. A toast starts exiting when `left <= fade` and keeps exiting until it is gone (`exiting = !hovered && (left <= fade || was exiting)`, target `!exiting`), so turning on Reduce motion mid-exit, which shrinks `fade`, never brightens it again; only a hover reverses an exit. The motion runs on egui time while the toast's life stays on the model clock, so a hovered toast (whose clock stops) still finishes its entry, and a toast hovered during its exit fades back up (the snap on that reversal is accepted). The toasts `Area` no longer fades in on its own (`fade_in(false)`), so the first toast doesn't fade twice. `Toast::opacity()` is removed. Reduce motion: no rise, and both fades are capped at 0.12 s. Repaint: the 50 ms poll for a toast's whole life is gone. A resting toast asks for one frame when its fade is due (`request_repaint_after` of the smallest time to a fade or, inside one, to removal), and the animate call repaints only while something moves. A hovered toast asks for no timer; its time stops from the last frame it was hovered (final review I2: `Messages` keeps the last tick's hovered set, so the frame a resting pointer leaves on, whose `dt` is the whole rest, charges it nothing). Tests: `messages::a_toast_rested_on_with_no_frames_keeps_its_time_after_the_pointer_leaves` and `a_hovered_toast_near_its_fade_asks_for_no_short_timer`. Accepted (preflight R-c): a pointer that leaves a toast inside its last 0.2 s lets the model remove it before the egui fade ends, a small pop at low alpha. Known limit (`shortcut:` in `ui/messages.rs`): an anchored `Area` places itself from last frame's size, so on a new toast's first visible frame the whole stack draws one toast-height low for one frame. Not fixed with `request_discard`, because a discarded pass can handle a click twice. The tests measure the rise against the other toast in the stack.
- **CF3 Keyboard-opened overlays appear at once (spec 01#2, Do first 4 and 11).** The Ctrl+K palette, the F1 shortcut sheet and the path autocomplete list no longer fade in: egui's 0.2 s `Area` fade made a key press wait for the overlay. `dialogs::modal_keys` takes a `fade_in` flag (the palette and the sheet pass `false`, building the `Modal` on `Modal::default_area(id).fade_in(false)`); the autocomplete `Area` in `ui/input_name.rs` sets `.fade_in(false)`. Mouse-opened dialogs keep egui's stock 0.2 s fade: `dialogs::dialog` passes `true`, and the few direct `egui::Modal::new` calls (`ui/meshes.rs`, `ui/viewport3d.rs`) use the stock area. Reduce motion does not touch either (stock motion is left alone, CF1). Tests: `keyboard::the_palette_and_the_sheet_open_without_a_fade` and `input_name_edit::the_path_list_shows_at_once_when_typing_reopens_it` compare the overlay's alpha on its first visible frame with its resting alpha (a repaint pin cannot tell, because any new `Area` asks for one repaint); the error dialog is the control that does fade. kittest zeroes `Style::animation_time`, so those tests set it back to 0.2.
- **CF4 Set order numbers (owner decision a).** Every set card shows its place in the full order, 1..N, as a monospace number at body size, in the handle's colour (`widgets.inactive.fg_stroke`, like the ≡ beside it; final review I1: the first small weak number measured 2.1:1 against ui-rules 4.7's 4.5:1), left of the ≡ handle. The slot is as wide as the laid-out `N`, so the names line up. The number counts every set in `sets::views`, a created set with no key included, because that is the order `reorder_set` uses, and it stays the same while a filter hides other sets. Its `Label` carries the AccessKit name "Position {n} of {N}" (preflight K6); the card's own response has no name. Tests: `set_order::each_card_shows_its_position_in_the_full_order_while_filtered` and `the_position_number_is_body_size_in_the_handle_colour`.
- **CF5 Move to… (owner decision b, R3).** A set's context menu has **Move to…** after Move up / Move down. It closes the menu and opens a dialog (`Pending::MoveTo`, `dialogs::dialog(.., "set-move-to", false, 420.0, "Move {id} to…", [Cancel])`), not a submenu or dropdown: the owner ruled that a dialog is easier to type in (2026-10-19), and it avoids the one-popup trap (CD21). It keeps egui's stock fade because a mouse menu opens it (CF3). The field (hint "Number or name", accessible name "Position or set name") takes the focus. Up and Down move the highlight (consumed before the field, with the palette's focus-lock filter). The list is `show_rows`, up to 240 pt; each row reads "{n}  {label}", with a weak "(hidden by filter)" for a set the filter hides. The rules (`sets_column::move_to_hits`): a blank query lists every set. A query that is all digits after trimming is a position only and never matches a name (controller ruling on review I1, which overrides the brief's "then the name matches"): `n` in 1..=N lists that one row; a number outside 1..=N (or too big to parse) lists no row and shows "Positions are 1 to N". Otherwise, "13" with 12 sets would have moved the set to one named "armor_13". A set named with digits only is found by typing a letter of its folder or label. Any other text lists the sets whose folded id or label holds the folded query (folded like the Sets search), in the full order. The highlight resets to the first row when the query changes. Enter (the field's own, so never on the opening frame) or a click picks the highlighted row. Enter with no row does nothing and the dialog stays open, saying "Positions are 1 to N" for an out-of-range number or "Nothing matches" for text, so a miss always says why. The pick is the final 0-based index for `reorder_set`, so moving down takes the target's place and the target shifts up one. One case is silent: picking the set's own position closes the dialog and changes nothing, with no message (`reorder_set` refuses it: no step, not dirty). Esc and Cancel close; a click outside does not (it holds typed text). Every reorder (drag, Move up / Move down, Move to…) now goes through `apply_reorder` (preflight K5: `pending_modal` runs after the column's act loop). The moved set flashes as before, and `nav.reveal_set` is set to its key when it has one, so a far move scrolls into view. That scroll glides with egui's stock scroll animation, and lands at once under Reduce motion (`scroll_to_rect_animation` with `ScrollAnimation::none()`; final review D2: these reorder triggers are new, so CF1's rule covers them; test `set_order::a_reveal_glide_lands_at_once_with_reduce_motion`). The reveal path is shared, so Go to set (Ctrl+K, Problems) to a card in or near view also lands at once under Reduce motion; this supersedes the CF7 wording that a card in view always glides. A move never changes the selection, the filter or the open set. On a read-only project the entry is disabled with the banner's reason, like the other entries. Tests: `set_order` (`move_to_*`, `a_number_past_the_end_never_picks_a_set_named_with_it`, `the_number_slot_has_one_width_for_one_and_two_digits`, `esc_closes_move_to_with_no_change`, `ctrl_z_does_nothing_while_move_to_is_open`) and `sets_column::tests::move_to_hits_reads_numbers_then_names`.
- **CF6 Reorder while a filter is on (R2).** Move to… stays on while any Sets filter is on: it moves by the real index and names the target number. Dragging the ≡ handle and Move up / Move down stay off while filtered; their hover now reads "Clear the filter to reorder sets, or use Move to…". `sets_filter::reordering_is_off_while_filtered` and `move_up_and_down_are_off_while_filtered` are unchanged.
  - CD15 is narrowed by CF6.
- **CF7 The Sets column lays out only the cards on screen; a set drag is dropped on the target card (owner decision c, R1, R4).** The changes the user can see are listed in the last item.
  - Virtualisation (R4) is a clip-rect skip in `sets_column::draw`, not `show_rows`, because cards differ in height (the narrow layout, the shader combo only on a set with a key, chip rows that wrap). Each card keeps its last laid-out height in `DropState::card_h` (by set id); a card never laid out uses `CARD_EST = 110` pt until any card is measured, then the mean. A card whose estimated rect is outside the clip rect only calls `ui.allocate_space` for that height (one auto id, the same as the card's `scope_builder`, so later cards keep their ids, context menus and drop targets; preflight K9). When a drawn card's height differs from the one used by more than 0.5 pt, one `request_repaint` lays the cards below it out again; it settles once they are measured. A reveal (Go to set, Move to…, any reorder through `apply_reorder`) of a card outside last frame's view jumps to the offset the known heights give, the least scroll that shows it (review I1: aiming `scroll_to_rect` once at an estimated rect landed tens of cards off with mixed heights). It aims again each frame, up to `REVEAL_TRIES = 8`, until the card is laid out with no height changing that frame. A card in or across the view still glides there with `scroll_to_rect`. Known limit (a `shortcut:` comment): heights of off-screen cards go stale when the column width changes, so the scroll bar length is off until they are drawn.
  - Drag-reorder stays (R1). The drop is now read on the card under the pointer with `Response::dnd_release_payload::<DragSet>()`, only while a set hovers that card (a stray take would eat a dragged texture, K9), and goes through `reorder_target` and `apply_reorder` as before. The ≡ handle still senses drag and sets the payload but no longer reads `drag_stopped()`, which never fires once its own card is skipped; egui keeps the payload while the source widget is gone and clears it at the end of the release pass, so a release outside any card moves nothing.
  - The limit the user can see is unchanged: egui 0.36.2 ignores the mouse wheel while a widget is dragged (`scroll_area.rs:1215-1217`) and has no edge auto-scroll, so a drag reaches only the cards on screen. Move to… (CF5) is the way to make a long move. Task 10 says so in docs/gui.md.
  - Tests (`set_order`): `a_reveal_lands_on_a_far_card_among_mixed_heights` (20 short cards first, the rest taller; RED landed on card 341 of the wanted 450), `the_sets_column_lays_out_only_the_cards_on_screen` (500 sets, `set_cards_drawn` counts `pill` calls; `run` settling within 16 steps is the settle pin, preflight K2), `a_palette_pick_scrolls_an_undrawn_set_into_view`, `a_drag_released_after_the_source_scrolled_away_still_reorders` (Review Focus 1; the content is shifted with `nav.reveal_set` because the wheel is off during a drag, K7), and the guards `the_wheel_does_not_scroll_the_sets_during_a_drag` and `a_drop_outside_any_card_moves_nothing`. Fixture: `support::many_sets`. `the_number_slot_has_one_width_for_one_and_two_digits` now uses a window tall enough to show all 12 cards, since cards off screen have no number label any more.
  - What the user can see changes (review I2):
    - Screen readers and Tab reach only the cards on screen: an off-screen card has no AccessKit node and is not in the Tab order, Tab from the last visible card leaves the column, and a focused card that scrolls off loses focus. Ctrl+K Go to set and Move to… still reach every set, and each card's label still says "of N".
    - A context menu or shader combo open on a card goes away while that card is scrolled out of view (neither is drawn for a skipped card).
    - The scroll thumb's length changes as card heights are learned. After a jump (a thumb drag or a far reveal), scrolling back up shifts the visible cards as each card above is measured (a `shortcut:` comment names the fix: anchor the top visible card).
    - A far reveal now jumps instead of gliding (above).
    - A release on a card that was not laid out on the previous frame is ignored and moves nothing (egui hit-tests against the previous frame's rects). It shows only when the content moves on the release frame, for example when a plan lands.
- **CF8 Per-frame cost (Task 6; ui-rules §9.1, §9.5, §7.7).** The only visible change: background reads (output sizes, the selected texture's used-by list and the locked-slot hover list, the report-save toast) can appear up to 250 ms later, because they are polled every 250 ms instead of 50 ms. Foreground jobs (export, plan, previews, the 3D view) still poll every 50 ms. The `export_files` cache holds only while every write to `items` calls `invalidate_views()`.
  - The Sets column fetches the flagged keys once per frame. `bottom::flagged` is public and returns `Arc<Flagged { sets, textures }>`, two plain key sets that replace the `s:`/`t:`-prefixed strings, so a lookup formats nothing. `sets_column::draw` fetches it once and works out each drawn card's `Status` (Blocks, Warning, Ready) with `bottom::set_ready_in`; `pill` and `status_pill` take that `Status` instead of the blocked flag. `sets_filter::visible_sets` and `set_counts` fetch once per rebuild too. `set_ready(m, v)` stays as `set_ready_in(&flagged(m), v)` for single lookups. `Flagged` is still reset with every `problems` build, so a set that gains or loses a problem changes on the next frame.
  - `AppModel::export_files` is cached in `ViewCache::export_files`, under the view key and the same `(evidence_rev, export.revision, export running)` tuple as `problems`, not `items_rev` alone. It reads only `items`, which is replaced only together with `invalidate_views`. The header dot, the Export hover and Review's button text and gate read it every frame.
  - `bottom::filtered(m, None)` returns the `problems` `Arc` itself, not a clone of the list; a filtered list is a new `Arc`. `ui/problems.rs::rows` stores it as is.
  - Counters for tests: `bottom::problem_lookups` (every call to `problems()`, cached or not) and `bottom::export_files_builds`.
  - Tests: `bottom_panel::set_cards_do_not_look_up_problems_per_card` (3 sets and 500 sets make the same number of `problems()` calls in a frame; before the fix 8 and 13, one per drawn card; the column was already virtualised by CF7, so the gap was about 8 cards, not 500), `bottom_panel::export_files_follows_a_decision_without_a_frame_of_lag` (Review Focus 3: no rebuild across idle frames, exactly one after the decisions, the cached count equals a fresh count after the decisions and after undo, and `export_dot` agrees), `bottom_panel::a_ready_set_that_gains_a_warning_loses_its_green_dot`, `problems::the_unfiltered_list_is_the_problems_list_itself`.
  - Worker polling (R7). `app.rs::worker_poll(visible, background)` asks for a frame every 50 ms (`POLL_VISIBLE`) while a result the user is waiting to see is pending (a plan, the heatmap, the RNM preview, a file picker, the mesh scan, a 3D load), and every 250 ms (`POLL_BACKGROUND`) while only background work runs (image sizes, used-by lookups, a report save). With neither, no timer, and the app sleeps. Background results can land up to 250 ms later than before. Wake-on-send would let a worker wake the UI at once, but workers hold only a `Sender` (`worker::spawn_guarded`), so every worker would need a `Context`; out of scope. The 3D panels' own 16 ms polls (`ui/viewport3d.rs`, `ui/set_preview.rs`) stay: they run only while that panel is drawn and busy. Test: `app::tests::worker_poll_is_slow_for_background_work_only`.
  - The texel readout's repaint stays (R8, no code). The readout is laid out in the notes strip before the viewports (`ui/preview.rs`), so a changed readout needs the next frame to show.
- **CF9 Drag ghost and dimmed source (Task 7; R5, K10).** While a `DragItem` is in flight, `columns::drag_ghost` paints a 40 x 40 thumbnail (75% white tint; a `weak_bg_fill` rect with no thumbnail yet) at the pointer + (12, 12) on a Tooltip-order layer. It is painted once per frame at the end of `ui::draw_with_scan`, from the payload and `pointer_interact_pos()`, not from the source widget, so it stays when a virtualised source (Sets cards, Textures `show_rows`) scrolls out. No fade. The source tile is drawn at 0.5 opacity while the payload names its key, like the dragged set card. Member chips are not dimmed (the brief dims the source tile only). The ghost keeps the thumbnail's aspect inside the 40 x 40 box. It asks for no repaint (final review D1; the first version asked every frame while the payload was present): it moves only with pointer events, and egui asks for one more frame after any pass with input, so the release frame is followed by a clean one. Test: `set_cards::a_still_drag_asks_for_no_frames_and_the_ghost_goes_one_frame_after_release`. The Grabbing cursor needs no code: egui's drag plugin sets it (R5); the tiles and chips also sense click, so `dnd_set_drag_payload` does not set Grab itself.
- **CF10 Hover and press looks (Task 7).** Instant, no animation, so no reduce-motion branch (CF1 has nothing to switch). `columns::interact_stroke` gives tiles and unselected member chips `widgets.active.bg_stroke` while pressed and `widgets.hovered.bg_stroke` while hovered; an AMBER or RED status stroke always wins; selected chips keep the selection stroke. A pressed strip fills with `widgets.active.weak_bg_fill` under its text. The dimmed drag source gets no press stroke, so it reads as dimmed rather than lit.
- **CF11 Export fades to the accent (Task 8).** When Export becomes available, the Review footer button and the header button fill fade from `widgets.inactive.weak_bg_fill` to `selection.bg_fill`, and the header dot fades in as `GREEN.gamma_multiply(t)`. One `animate_bool_with_time_and_easing` per paint (`review-export-ready`, `header-export-ready`, `header-export-dot`), `cubic_out`, `motion::fade_dur(0.15)` (so 0.12 s under reduce motion, CF1). Losing readiness snaps (0 s), and the call runs every frame, also while the gate is `Err`, so an untick resets the state to 0 and a re-tick fades again; the unready button keeps the disabled look. Only paint animates: the button is enabled and clickable on the frame the gate passes, the red reason vanishes at once, and the readiness inputs (`review_gate().is_ok()`, `can_export()`, `export_dot()`) and the click path are unchanged (ui-rules 7.1-7.2). Enter does nothing in Review (N3). Tests: `review_tab::export_fades_to_the_accent_and_snaps_back` (the fill is strictly between after one step, the accent after four more, the disabled fill again after the untick) and `reduced_motion_brings_the_export_accent_sooner_than_the_control` (one step in, against an unreduced control; final review M2). `the_review_export_works_on_the_frame_it_becomes_ready` is a guard, green before the change. The tests tick with `click()` plus `step()`, not `press()`, because `press()` runs the fade to its end.
- **CF12 Progress glide (Task 9).** The header's export bar and the Files tab's bar draw `ui::header::shown_progress(ctx, model.drawer_epoch, frac)`: `animate_value_with_time(Id::new(("export-progress", drawer_epoch)), frac, motion::move_dur(0.3))`, linear, so each step glides 0.3 s from the value on screen (0 s, today's jump, under reduce motion). The bar text stays the exact `done/total`, and `.animate(false)` stays. A new export bumps `drawer_epoch`, a new animation id whose first call returns its target, so a second run never sweeps back from the last run's value. egui returns the old value on the frame the target changes, so the glide starts one frame after the count. Test: `plan_progress::the_export_bar_glides_and_a_new_run_starts_at_its_own_value`.
- **CF13 Reorder flash timing (Task 9; preflight K13).** A moved set's border now holds full for 0.35 s (`sets_column::FLASH_HOLD`), then fades over 0.25 s (`FLASH_FADE`) with alpha `(1 - k)²`; it was a 1 s linear fade (`FLASH_SECS`, removed). `PillLook::flash` is the alpha. `sets_column::flash_now` asks for one frame at the end of the hold (`request_repaint_after_secs`) and for every frame only during the fade, so a flash costs about 15 frames, not 60. Reduce motion keeps the hold and shortens the fade to 0.12 s (`fade_dur`). A newer reorder replaces the flash. Test: `sets_column::tests::flash_alpha_holds_then_eases_out`.
- **CF14 Slot flash (Task 9; R9).** In the set editor, a slot whose member changed since the last frame the editor drew, in the same set, and now holds a member flashes its row with a 2 px accent (`selection.stroke.color`) outline on the same timing as CF13. The outline is `StrokeKind::Inside` (final review M1): `Outside` lost the first row's top edge to the slot `ScrollArea`'s clip. `set_editor::slot_changes` compares each slot's member key, by slot number, with `DropState::slot_seen`, so every way a slot changes flashes: a drop, Replace, Assign…, an Explorer file drop, and undo/redo (undo flashing the slot it restores is intended). A slot that only empties (a texture moved to another slot, an undone drop) does not flash, so a move from slot 1 to slot 5 flashes slot 5 (review M1). Only the first slot that got a member flashes; a newer change replaces it. Drawing another set (a switch) only records its slots and never flashes. Wherever the set editor is not drawn (another selection, a texture expanded, the set gone from the plan), `slot_seen` is cleared, so a change made meanwhile does not flash when the set shows again (review M2). Known limit: slots are keyed by slot number, and two kinds share some numbers (Emissive / Skin 3, Coat normal / Fuzz 7); with both filled, the last kind in slot order is compared, so a change to the other may not flash. Tests: `set_editor_ui::a_slot_that_gets_a_texture_flashes_and_a_set_switch_does_not` (also pins K13: a timer during the hold, an immediate frame during the fade), `undoing_a_drop_does_not_flash_the_emptied_slot_and_redo_does` and `a_slot_changed_while_the_editor_was_hidden_does_not_flash`.
- **CF15 Slot thumbnail press (Task 9).** While the pointer is down on a slot row's thumbnail, the image, its fill, its status border and the PGPatcher ✕ are drawn at 0.97 about the thumbnail's centre: `animate_bool_with_time_and_easing(resp.id.with("press"), is_pointer_button_down_on(), move_dur(0.1), cubic_out)`. The hit rect keeps its 56 pt. The brief's `with_visual_transform` is not used: its scope allocates a cell in the slot Grid and would shift the row's columns, so the painted rect is scaled instead, which is the same transform for these shapes (the 1 px border and 2 pt corners shrink by 3% too). A quick tap reverses mid-way; the up-to-1-pt jump at 0.97 is accepted (02#6). Reduce motion: no scale. Test: `set_editor_ui::a_pressed_slot_thumbnail_scales_to_097`.
- **CF16 The columns fade in when a folder opens (Task 9; preflight K1).** On the frame a folder opens, everything drawn after the Advanced drawer and before the end of the `CentralPanel` (the Textures and Sets columns and the centre) fades in over 0.25 s (`quadratic_out`; 0.12 s under reduce motion) through `ui.multiply_opacity(t)`, restored with `ui.set_opacity` after the `CentralPanel` (not `ui.scope`, which would take an auto id). The header, the bottom panel and the drawer do not fade. The columns take clicks from the first frame. The animate call runs every frame, and closing the folder snaps, so every open fades. The app opens no folder at launch (`SdcApp::new` and `main` call no `open_folder`); only a model that already has a folder on its first frame, a test path, starts at full opacity. K1: the opacity is applied only while a folder is open, so the start screen is never faded (as written, the spec's snippet would have drawn it at opacity 0). Tests: `ui_smoke::opening_a_folder_fades_the_columns_in_and_a_restored_one_does_not` (the start screen's "Open folder…" at full alpha, the Sets heading below full one step after opening and full six steps later, the header's "Sets" eye never faded) and `reduce_motion_shortens_the_folder_fade_in` (full within 0.15 s).
- **CF17 Not animated, by ruling (Task 10).** The bottom panel keeps snapping open and closed (owner agreed 2026-10-18; pass 2's `Panel::show_switched` 0.2 s slide is declined; Ctrl+M stays instant). People open it all day, by mouse and by key, and a frequent action should not animate. The spec's rejected list, copied so nobody adds these later (`00-summary.md`, "Rejected, as decoration or wrong for a tool used all day"):
  - Ctrl+M;
  - tab switches;
  - filter hide and show;
  - set panel swaps;
  - status dot colour changes;
  - a decided row leaving Review;
  - `ProgressBar::animate`;
  - thumbnails fading in as they load.
- **CF18 Shots (Task 10).** `.superpowers/ui-shots-after-motion/` (untracked, with an `INDEX.md`): 31 images at 1600x1000, 1280x800 and 1100x800 from the real `SdcApp` under egui_kittest with wgpu (step 0.05 s of egui time). Sets cards with numbers, unfiltered and filtered; Move to… with "1", "99" and a name; 500 sets scrolled to set 251 (`support::many_sets`); Advanced > Interface; Review with Export ready; two toasts; and the slot editor at rest, 0.1 s after a change and in the fade. The capture test (`crates/gui/tests/ui_shots.rs`) is not committed.
