Upgrade if the owner reports stutter. (F9) the `replay` and `golden` test modules are compiled into `tessalith.exe`; a cfg or feature split can come later. (F10) before the CS settings are read, the Meshes footer shows no off line while the set preview shows its full `OFF_FEATURES` list; cosmetic.

## Note CK — modscan: indexed lookup of a texture's users by canonical path (NIF team, 2026-10-20)
Main-team request (Track C, NIF HANDOFF 2026-10-20): the UV coverage overlay asked `nifs_using_texture(Contains)` for one texture, a scan of `path` (~840 ms on the owner's scan.db).
- **CK1** `Store::nifs_using_canonical_texture(slot, path, limit)` returns the same `MatchRow`s as `nifs_using_texture` (lighting shapes of the latest winners, a derived winner on its source copy, same order), for shapes whose slot resolves to `path`'s canonical form (`nif::path::canon_texture`). Every raw spelling of that file matches (`Data\Textures\a.dds`, `a.dds`). The condition is `path.p = ?`, so the `path` index answers it; a test pins the query plan (no scan of `path`).
- **CK2** A method, not a new `TexKey` variant: `TexKey` is matched exhaustively in the GUI (main-team `set_preview.rs`), so a variant would force a main-team edit. No raw-slot post-filter: the canonical path is what the game loads, and callers that need PGPatcher's raw form keep using `TexKey`. The shared query body moved to `match_sql` / `match_rows`; `nifs_using_texture` is unchanged.

## Note CN — v2 Track A: PBR to Vanilla and Complex Material "Also export" (owner, 2026-10-20)
Plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-17-v2-pbr-to-vanilla-cm.md` (its "Note CJ" reads CM: CI to CL are taken on main), spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-v2-pbr-to-vanilla-cm-design.md`, branch `feat/v2-pbr-to-vanilla-cm`. Each task appends its items here.
- **CN1 Track A inputs: `_rmaos` by channel, `_curves` and cavity roles (Task 1, TA1).** The C6/Track B split: the `_rmaos` and `_p` inputs are read only by the derive step. Track A ships the type and the reader: `RawMap::Rmaos` (id `rmaos`; multi-channel, never a file-name role, not in `RawMap::INPUTS`, since `rmaos` is also the §6.1 suffix of a pre-packed file), `pack::rmaos_channel` (the CS layout: R roughness, G metallic, B AO, A specular), `pack::assemble::assemble_channels` (`assemble` delegates to it), which reads alpha for `channel: Some(3)`, and provenance `A` for that channel. No cs recipe reads an `_rmaos` by channel; Track B wires that under its own ruling. `RawMap::Curves` (a 0.5-centred curvature map) and `RawMap::Cavity` join `RawMap::INPUTS` (11) but not `RawMap::ALL` (still 8), so they have no `packing.fill` and the GUI offers no fill for them. None of the three starts the cs `_rmaos` recipe.
- **CN2 Three vocabulary terms (Task 1).** `_curvature` and `_curves` read as `curves`, `_cavity` as `cavity` (packing inputs; `VOCABULARY` 34 → 37, longest first).
- **CN3 Behaviour change: such files are packing inputs (Task 1).** A file named `*_curves`, `*_curvature` or `*_cavity` was its own colour set before; it now joins its set as a packing input and is `PACK-UNUSED-INPUT` "read only by Also export as (Vanilla / Complex material)" in any plain run, cs or vanilla. It writes nothing on its own, and the set's `_rmaos` recipe is unchanged. No golden has such a file, and `B:\testdata\textures-10k` has none either.
- **CN4 Behaviour change: aliases (Task 1).** A user preset aliasing `curves`, `curvature` or `cavity` in `[suffix_aliases]` is now refused as a vocabulary term (`CFG-INVALID`), as `orm` was (Note AL6). It gets the generic "is an exporter vocabulary term (spec §4.4)" message, not a named one like `orm`'s: the named form is more than one line.
- **CN5 Track A recipe defaults (Task 2).** `engine::derive::recipe::LegacyParams`, the `[export.legacy]` keys (C4; Task 6 wires them into `sdc.toml`). Each default and its source: `brightness` k **0.9**, owner answer 1 (2026-10-17, from `11-ao-vs-brightness.md`; same-author archives fit k 0.84–0.97), which supersedes Q1's 0.65 (still settable); `ao_strength` s **0.5** (Q3) and `ao_strength_landscape` **0.3** (calibration); `curves_opacity` **0.40**, W3C soft light (Q2); `metal_darken` **0.3**, the vanilla `lerp(1, 0.3, metal)` (Q4, partial); `spec_scale` **0.66** and `spec_metal_boost` **2.0** (round-2 ruling); `landscape_spec` **2.5** (O5; 07: author mean 0.052 / recipe 0.021); `cm_dielectric_env` **0** (Q5 "either/or, default 0"; the option is 0.35); `keep_metal_brightness` **off** and `keep_metal_strength` **1.0** (owner). `check()` refuses a non-finite or out-of-range value and names the key (`export.legacy.brightness = 2: must be between 0 and 1.5`): brightness 0–1.5, spec_scale 0–2, spec_metal_boost 1–3, landscape_spec 0–5, everything else 0–1. The maths is `f32` on stored values; the `f64` settings are cast once per call.
- **CN6 Diffuse chain (Task 2, TA4).** `diffuse` runs: × k; × `lerp(1, AO, s)`; clamp to [0, 1] (CN10); `lerp(c, soft_light(c, curves), opacity)`; `lerp(c, c · cavity, opacity)`; × the metal factor; clamp to [0, 1]. The metal factor is `lerp(1, metal_darken, metal)` for `Vanilla`, `lerp(that, 1, keep_metal_strength)` for `CmKeepMetal`, and 1 for `Landscape`. TA4: the spec names no cavity opacity, so cavity multiplies at `curves_opacity`, after the soft light, and a set with both `_curves` and a cavity map gets both, curves first. That reads Q2's "optional OR … with multiply"; the owner may overrule it.
- **CN7 Non-metal env in the CM `_m` (Task 2, TA3).** R = `gloss · max(metal, cm_dielectric_env)`: a partial metal keeps its own value when it is above the option, and the 0.35 option lifts only what is below it.
- **CN8 Landscape (Task 2, TA5, O5).** A landscape `cm_m` has R = B = 0, and a landscape diffuse has no metal factor (calibration: "no metal or env"). The landscape `_n` alpha is `sat(landscape_spec · 0.66 · gloss · AO)`: the factor scales the unsaturated value, and landscape ignores metal here too (no metal boost). TA5 reads "landscape ignores metal", and O5's 2.5 was fitted on 07's prototype, which ran landscape with no metal (07 "Landscape: no metal"). `spec_alpha` applies this itself, so no caller has to zero the metal (review I1, controller 2026-10-20).
- **CN9 CM `_m` G and A (Task 2, TA6).** G = `max(1 − roughness, 5/255)` on every derived `_m` (Q6: at ≤ 4/255 the shader turns complex material off). A = the `_p` R clamped to [5/255, 250/255], one code inside the spec's open interval (4/255, 251/255), so parallax stays on; with no `_p` it is 0 (complex material on, parallax off). `nif_glossiness` = `(2/r⁴ − 2).clamp(2, 500)` (r = 0 gives 500), for the report only.
- **CN10 Diffuse clamped before the soft light (Task 2, controller ruling 2026-10-20, review M2).** `check()` allows k up to 1.5, so after steps 1-2 c can exceed 1, outside the soft light's [0, 1] domain, where a darkening `_curves` value would brighten (k 1.5, albedo 0.9, curves 0.2: 1.46 at 40 % instead of 1). `diffuse` clamps c to [0, 1] after the AO step, before the soft light, on every texel, so `_curves` 0.5 still equals no `_curves`. Side effect: with k > 1 a clipped texel stays clipped through the metal factor (k 1.5, albedo 0.9, full metal: 0.3, not 0.405). The final clamp stays.
- **CN11 Derived jobs (Task 3).** A new job kind beside `pack`, `bake` and `rnm`: `ResolvedJob::derive: Option<engine::derive::DeriveJob>` (skipped when absent, so no existing event, manifest line or golden changes). `DeriveKind` names what it writes: `vanilla_diffuse` and `cm_diffuse` (`<base>.dds`; `diffuse`, or `landscape_diffuse` for a landscape set), `legacy_n` (`_n`; `normal` or `landscape_normal`), `cm_m` (`_m`; `complex_material`), `env_m` (`_m`; `envmask`) and `grass_stack` (`<base>.dds`; `complex_grass`). `derive::assemble::assemble_derived` builds the image in `pipeline::prepare_then`'s load step, so the export and the measure-only run (Note CL20) both assemble it, and everything after Load is the ordinary path. The scalars are `assemble_channels([rough, metal, ao, _p R or Opaque])` and the `_curves`/cavity pair `[curves or 0.5, cavity or 1.0, Opaque, Opaque]` (built only when a set has one), each given only the files its channels name, so the albedo and normal are decoded once, by `load_image`. `is_float`, which picks the source transfer, comes from the colour map only (the albedo, or the normal): the scalars are [0, 1] data whatever their file type, so an EXR `_p` or roughness no longer makes the diffuse's coded values read as linear (review I1); a float colour map is taken as stored values (`shortcut:`). A channel set that names no file (a thin set: all slot defaults) is a constant image at the size every source shares. Every source must share one size (`PackError::SizeMismatch`, TA22). Per texel: a diffuse is `recipe::diffuse` (flavour `Vanilla`, `CmKeepMetal` for `cm_diffuse`, `Landscape` for a landscape set) with alpha = the albedo's alpha, or for a landscape set the `_p` R, opaque without a `_p`; `legacy_n` keeps the normal's stored RGB with `spec_alpha` (O5's factor on a landscape set); `cm_m` is `recipe::cm_m`; `env_m` is grey `env_m`, opaque; the grass stack is w × 2h, the diffuse with the albedo's alpha on top and the normal with `spec_alpha` below. The grass top half is `CmKeepMetal` only while `keep_metal_brightness` is on, `Vanilla` otherwise (with it off, CM reuses the vanilla diffuse, spec Goal 5). `has_alpha` is false only for `env_m` and a landscape diffuse without `_p`. A derived job missing the albedo or normal its kind reads fails at Load naming its input (the planner never builds one). A source changed since planning fails the job by name (`<file>: source changed since planning; re-run`), as a packed job's does.
- **CN12 Derived job identity in the manifest (Task 3).** `DeriveJob::sources` lists every file the job reads once, in slot order, with its stamp: `DeriveSource { path, role, stamp }`, `role` a string (`albedo`, `normal`, `rough`, `metal`, `ao`, `height`, `curves`, `cavity`), joined by `+` when one file fills several slots (an `_rmaos` feeding all three is `rough+metal+ao`). `PackSource` can't be used: its role is a `RawMap`, which has no albedo or normal. `sources[0].path` is the job's `input`. `DeriveJob::identity_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the job serialised without the stamps, so any setting (`LegacyParams`), slot, channel or path changes it. The record lists each source as `SourceRef::of_derive`: `derive` = the identity, `derive_role` = the role string (as `rnm` holds its role). `if-changed` compares (SHA-256, bake identity, RNM role, derive identity) per source, so a changed setting or source bytes re-encode; only the bytes decide, so a touched but unchanged source stays up to date. A derived output's profile hash is the sub-type's, unchanged by the recipe settings, which live in the identity only (C4). The identity hashes absolute paths (as specified); with the per-source SHA-256s and roles in slot order they are redundant, and their only cost is one re-encode after a project moves. Clearing them before hashing (`sources[].path`, `albedo`/`normal`, every `ChannelSource::Source.path`) is a one-time re-encode, so do it before release if at all (review 2026-10-20; `shortcut:` on `identity_sha256`).
- **CN13 Admission of a derived job (Task 3).** `api::job_bytes` adds, on the input's size, 16 B/texel for each colour map the kind reads (one; two for the grass stack, which reads the albedo and the normal), the scalars image, the `_curves`/cavity image when the set has one, and the recipe's output (twice the input for the grass stack, whose chain the existing complex-grass term counts at the input's size). The brief named "its albedo or normal"; the grass stack holds both, so both are counted. Two estimation errors roughly cancel, so don't fix one alone: the term counts the input decode again (`estimated_bytes(&job.input)` already holds it), and for the grass stack the existing complex-grass term counts the chain at w × h while the stacked chain is w × 2h (about 21 B/texel under). The net stays an over-estimate (review M3).
- **CN14 A derived grass stack needs an alpha-keeping profile (Task 3, for Task 4).** `grass::half_profile` keeps the bottom half's alpha as data only while the job's alpha policy is not `remove`, and the base complex_grass policy is `remove`; X12 makes it `cutout` only for a varying alpha. So a grass stack planned with `remove` (an opaque albedo) would lose its `_n` specular alpha. Task 3's test sets `cutout`, as planning resolves real grass; Task 4's planner must give a derived grass stack a policy other than `remove`.
- **CN15 Derive planning: placement and admission (Task 4).** `BatchRequest::derive: Option<DeriveRequest>` (default `None`). In `plan_cached`, `derive::plan::plan_derived` runs after packing pass 2 and before the shader assignment, `plan_rnm` and the bakes. It returns `DerivePlan { candidates, picks }`. Each candidate is assembled (`assemble_derived_rough`), analysed and resolved (`finish_derived`) under pass 2's admission. Pass 2 and the derive step share one helper, `api::admit_all`, generic over the work item, so the block is not copied a third time (preflight P18). The helper covers the admission on the calling thread, the spawn, `catch_unwind` with the stage cell, and one slot per item. Pass 1 keeps its own loop, because it returns an analysis and source info with each job and counts progress. The pack closure keeps its cache lookup and `put_pack` inside, and the goldens are unchanged (97). A derive candidate is admitted at the sum of its sources' estimates, since the grass stack decodes two colour maps. A load, assembly or panic failure becomes a `FailedFile` with the same §10 warning as a pass-2 failure (the shared `failure` closure). A candidate cancelled before its Load is listed in `cancelled`. `dp.picks` go into `picks` before the shader assignment. The derived jobs resolve under their derived pick: the pass-1 context is kept as `base_ctx` and rebuilt with the extended picks, and later steps use the same picks. Every job resolved here gets `provenance["target"]`, as pass 2's do, and so do the error jobs `plan_derived` pushes. The `[files]` "matches no file" check also counts the members of `d.sets` and `d.drop`, whose jobs were removed. With the `test-hooks` feature, `admit_all` calls the plan panic hook at Load, named by the item's output (so the pass-1 hook, named by the input, never fires there), and the derive closure calls it again at Resolve (review M4).
- **CN16 What the derive step removes, and sets it skips (Task 4).** Every job whose `input` or `pack.sources` path is a member of a set in `d.sets` or in `d.drop` is removed, along with those members' `PACK-CONFLICT` skips. So a set left out (C2) leaves no fallback job (TA30). The O6 exception, a landscape set's `_p` job that stays, is Task 5's (preflight P7). The vanilla set key comes from a member's job or skip, read before removal, so the derive step needs no `output_root`. Sets that can't be derived:
  - **A source the recipe needs is DDS** (`DeriveSet::dds`): one `SkippedFile` with `DERIVE-DDS-SOURCE`. Derive reads no channel from a DDS, even a planned one that M9 (BV1) counts as pre-packed. It replaces that file's own `IN-DDS-SKIPPED`, so the file is skipped once (review M2). `run` reports it as `SkipKind::DdsInput` and counts it as intentional, as `IN-DDS-SKIPPED` is.
  - **No albedo and no `_n`:** a `SkippedFile` with `DERIVE-NO-ALBEDO`. Its `SkipKind` falls to `duplicate`, the catch-all, since none fits; Task 7 reads the code. It therefore counts as unintended, and the batch exits 1 (partial): nothing could be written from the set.
  - **A source that failed to load in the vanilla plan:** no derived job. Its failure is already reported.

  Sources of different sizes (TA22) are checked at plan time with `check_sizes`, as packing does. Each derived job of the set becomes an error job with `PACK-SIZE-MISMATCH` naming every source (preflight P6). It is built by the builder packing uses, now `pack::plan::recipe_error_job` + `size_mismatch_warning`. The other sets plan.
- **CN17 The object job table, per-kind sources and picks (Task 4, TA8, TA13, TA29).**
  (amended by Note CV, item CV5)
  - **Vanilla:** `vanilla_diffuse` when there is an albedo; `legacy_n` when there is a `_n`; `env_m` when the metal slot is a real source (`ChannelSource::Source`, not a default or fill) and a scanned shape at the vanilla mesh key votes Environment Map. The mesh key is `vanilla_game_path(mesh_key(colour member's game path, its output stem without a §6.1 suffix))`. With metal but `scanned` false, the set gets `DERIVE-NO-SCAN`; with metal and no Environment Map vote, `DERIVE-NO-ENVMAP`. No metal source gives neither.
  - **CM:** `cm_m`, plus `cm_diffuse` only when there is an albedo, `keep_metal_brightness` is on, metal is a real source and the strength is above 0.
  - **Slots each job holds:** colour maps only for the kinds that read them (albedo: diffuse kinds; normal: `legacy_n`); rough, metal and AO always; `_p` only for `cm_m` (the landscape cases are Task 5's); `_curves`/cavity only for the diffuse kinds. A kind that reads no colour map (`cm_m`, `env_m`) still lists the albedo (else the normal) first, with role `size`, so a thin set's constant `_m` has a size (TA22), and `input` is a real file. The cost: an albedo edit re-encodes the `_m`.
  - **Picks:** one per set that derived anything, `ShaderPick { shader, provenance: Derived, wanted: None }`. The shader is `Envmap` when the env `_m` is written, else `Default`, and `ComplexMaterial` in CM mode. A `Derived` pick raises no `SHADER-UNAVAILABLE` (`pick_notes`), and `check_maps` returns nothing for it. `ShaderOrigin::Derived` displays and parses as `derived`; the GUI's set card shows " (derived)".
- **CN18 Vanilla paths and conflicts (Task 4, TA12).** `vanilla_rel(rel, game_path)` removes the component that mirrors the `pbr` folder directly below the game path's `textures/` (ASCII case-insensitive). It counts from the end, so a project opened at `textures` (`pbr/arm/steel.png`) folds too. It is applied to the output, which ends with the same tail. `vanilla_game_path` folds a `/` game path. A game path without `textures/pbr/<something>` folds nothing. A derived job's `InputFile` has its output and game path folded but keeps `rel`, so `project_rel` still finds the source's `[files]` key (TA15). `plan_derived` refuses a derived output that lands on a remaining job's output, or on an earlier derived one (slash-folded, lower case, as `pack::plan::other_output`): the derived job becomes an error job with `DERIVE-PATH-CONFLICT`, and the other job stays. The IN-DUPLICATE guard only sees ready jobs, so it never fires on a derived one.
- **CN19 Resolving a derived job (Task 4, TA15, TA26).**
  - **The decision:** `finish_derived` resolves with `resolve_decided`, sub-type `kind.subtype(landscape)`, provenance `recipe:<kind>`, decided. It uses the albedo's `InputFile` for a diffuse, the normal's for the `_n`, and the virtual `<base>_m` beside the colour member (`pack::plan::virtual_input_as`) for an `_m`. So `[files]` entries of those sources apply, and Track C's `drop_top_mip` follows the albedo's and normal's entries. A derived `_m` reads its own virtual key, as a packed output does (preflight 3.10). The `[files]` "matches no file" check counts that virtual key, as it does a packed output's (review M3).
  - **Alpha meaning:** a diffuse from an albedo whose alpha varies is `Unresolved` until its meaning is confirmed, as a plain diffuse is. This is not special-cased.
  - **Toksvig:** not applied to a derived CM `_m` (TA26). The bake runs after this step and reads a `normal` job of the set, which a CM plan has none of (Track C CL40's own note).
  - **Track C (Note CL):** `_flow` → Hair never reaches a PBR set. Check stats skip a derived job (CN22), and `drop_top_mip`/low detail act on the derived chain (CN11).
- **CN20 Set-level notes and the NIF suggestion (Task 4, TA11, TA16, TA28).**
  - **Where the set-level notes go:** `DERIVE-NO-SCAN`, `DERIVE-NO-ENVMAP`, `DERIVE-NO-ALBEDO` (when something is still derived; on the CM plan only when the TA8 CM diffuse would have been written, review M1) and `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED` ride on the set's diffuse job, else its first derived job.
  - **`DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED`:** one per member that fills no slot, with data `{member, reason}`. An RNM layer, by its name (`rnm::split_layer`), has the reason "detail layer not in the vanilla _n" (TA28).
  - **`DERIVE-NIF-SUGGEST`:** data `{glossiness, specular_strength: 1.0, env_map}`, where `env_map` = the metal slot is a source. It is on the `_n` job, else the diffuse. The brief's code comment says "_n (or diffuse)", and its set-level list says the diffuse; the code comment is the more specific of the two. The glossiness is `nif_glossiness` of the plain mean of the assembled roughness slot (TA16). `assemble_derived_rough` returns that mean from the scalars it builds anyway, so nothing is decoded twice.
  - **Vanilla plan only:** `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED` and the NIF suggestion are raised on the Vanilla plan only, which every Also export writes (TA30), so the report lists them once.
- **CN21 Grass stack alpha (Task 4, closes CN14).**
  - **The rule:** `finish_derived` turns a `remove` policy on a `grass_stack` job into `cutout`, recorded as provenance `recipe:grass_stack`. It does this unconditionally, even over mesh evidence or an explicit `alpha.policy = remove`, because the bottom half is the `_n` and its alpha is the specular mask.
  - **Why X12 is not enough:** the analysis is of the whole stacked image. An opaque albedo over a non-255 spec alpha is already `Varying`, so X12 gives `cutout` there; the hook covers explicit layers and mesh evidence.
  - **Tests:** `a_grass_stack_on_an_opaque_albedo_keeps_its_spec_alpha` (`tests/derive_plan.rs`) drives `finish_derived` with a hand-built stack, because Task 4 plans no grass sets. It checks the policy with and without an explicit `remove`, then encodes and reads the bottom-half alpha back as 168. Task 5 adds the planner path for `pbr_grass` sets.
- **CN22 A derived job's analysis is not cached (Task 4, preflight P25).** The derive closure never calls `put_file` or `put_pack`. Storing it under the albedo's path would replace the albedo's own analysis. `AnalysisCache::analysis(job)` returns `None` for a job with `derive`. `shortcut:` each plan assembles a derived image again; key it on `identity_sha256` if re-planning an Also export gets slow.
- **CN23 Every member of a derived or dropped set gets one terminal event (Task 4, review I1).**
  - **A file a derived job reads:** as a raw map consumed by a recipe does, `run` emits `file_skipped { kind: packed_source, reason: "derived into <output>" }`, keyed by the derived output, so the GUI's `drop_queued` removes the member's discovery row. A file feeding several derived outputs (an `_rmaos`) gets one event, naming the first.
  - **Any other member:** after the derive admission, `derive::plan::report_unread` adds a `SkippedFile` with `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED` for each member of `d.sets` and `d.drop` that no derived job reads and that has no skip, no earlier failure and was not cancelled. That covers `_g`/`_s` and RNM layers, members left out (C2), the other members of a set skipped for DDS or no albedo, and the sources of an error or failed derived job. It is keyed by the member's own output and set, reported as `SkipKind::PackingInput` (a map not converted on its own) and counted as intentional. The Info note of the same code on the set's diffuse stays, for the report.
  - No new `SkipKind` is added, to avoid a schema change. A test walks every `file_discovered` of a derive plan and run and asserts exactly one terminal event each.
- **CN24 A float (EXR) colour map is kept as stored values (Task 4, review I1's question).** No plan-time refusal and no eighth code. The `shortcut:` in `derive/assemble.rs` stands: the recipe runs on the stored floats, and the source transfer follows the colour map. Refuse at plan time only if such sets turn up, since PBR mods ship 8-bit colour maps.
- **CN25 Codes and C6 (Task 4).** Seven codes, after `CHK-UV-GUTTER`: `DERIVE-DDS-SOURCE` and `DERIVE-NO-ALBEDO` (Warning), `DERIVE-NO-SCAN` and `DERIVE-NO-ENVMAP` (Info), `DERIVE-PATH-CONFLICT` (Error), `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED` and `DERIVE-NIF-SUGGEST` (Info). The count goes from 101 to 108, and `ALL.last()` is now `DeriveNifSuggest`; recount at merge. The schemas gain the seven strings; `ShaderOrigin` is a string in the schema, so `derived` adds no schema line. Without `derive` none of this runs (C6), and the golden runs are unchanged.
- **CN26 Derive: landscape and grass (Task 5; O1, O3, O5, O6, TA5).**
  - **Which jobs:** by the set's PBR-phase pick (`DeriveSet::shader`). Under Vanilla, `pbr_landscape` gets the diffuse (`landscape_diffuse`) and the `_n` (`landscape_normal`); under CM, only the `_m` (R = B = 0, G = gloss with the floor, A = `_p` R clamped as CN16). `pbr_grass` gets the converted diffuse only under Vanilla (no `_n`, no env `_m`, no stacking, O3), and only the `grass_stack` (`complex_grass`) under CM. `pbr` is unchanged.
  - **Landscape has no metal (TA5):** no env `_m`, no `DERIVE-NO-SCAN`/`DERIVE-NO-ENVMAP`, and no CM diffuse even with Keep metal brightness. `DeriveJob::landscape` is set, so the recipe uses AO strength 0.3, ignores metal and multiplies the `_n` alpha by `landscape_spec` (2.5, O5) before saturation (CN8, CN10). The diffuse reads the set's height slot: its alpha is the `_p` R, opaque with no alpha channel when the set has no `_p`.
  - **O6, the kept `_p` (preflight P7):** under Vanilla, `plan_derived` keeps a derived landscape set's `_p` job (the `_p` member's own job, or the `Parallax` recipe job when the height is a raw `_height`) and folds its output and game path by TA12. The vanilla target never plans `Parallax`, so a Vanilla derive passes `plan_packing` the raw heights of its landscape sets (`derive_heights`). Those heights get the cs recipe `[h, R, R, opaque]` instead of `PACK-UNUSED-INPUT` (Task 5 review I1, ruling (a)). The set is empty without `derive`, so non-derive vanilla plans are unchanged (C6). In `run`, a file a recipe packs gets its `packed` event only, not a second `derived` one. It is kept only when the set is derived (no DDS member, an albedo or a `_n`). It resolves under the set's derived `Landscape` pick, so it raises no map notes (TA29). Under CM it is removed with the other members: the `_p` lives in the CM `_m` alpha and the Vanilla folder holds the file.
  - **Picks (TA29):** `Landscape` (vanilla landscape), `ComplexMaterial` (CM landscape), `Default` (vanilla grass, as the vanilla fallback of `pbr_grass` is today), `ComplexGrass` (the stack).
  - **Grass shape:** the stack is the albedo's width by twice its height. An albedo that is not square power-of-two fails with `GRASS-SHAPE` at resolve, as complex grass does today; nothing is resampled. Through `finish_derived` the stack keeps CN21's grass hook, so an opaque albedo plans `cutout`, not `remove`.
  - **NIF suggestion:** only `pbr` sets carry `DERIVE-NIF-SUGGEST`. Landscape has no NIF (it is a TXST), and the vanilla grass diffuse has no `_n`, so a glossiness would be meaningless.
  - **`DERIVE-NO-ALBEDO`:** also noted under CM for a grass set, since the stack needs the albedo. `shortcut:` a grass set with an albedo but no `_n` writes no stack under CM (its members are `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED`); build the stack on a flat normal if such sets turn up.
  - **08e-1 (b):** PBR grass under `textures/landscape/` reaches the derive step as `pbr_grass` (GRAS evidence keyed by output stem), so it is derived as grass, not landscape.
  - **Tests** (`tests/derive_plan.rs`): `landscape_puts_p_in_the_diffuse_alpha_and_uses_ao_0_3`, `landscape_without_p_has_an_opaque_diffuse`, `grass_under_textures_landscape_is_still_grass`, `grass_is_a_plain_diffuse_under_vanilla_and_a_stack_under_cm`, `a_grass_stack_of_the_wrong_shape_is_grass_shape`, `a_landscape_height_becomes_the_vanilla_p`. The grass planner test forces `alpha.policy = remove` through `[files]`, so it fails without the CN21 hook.
- **CN27 One terminal event for a member whose own output is written (Task 5, refines CN23).** A PBR set outside `textures/pbr/` has no TA12 fold, so the derived diffuse writes the albedo's own output, and a kept landscape `_p` writes its own. Such a member got the `packed_source` event and that job's event: two. Task 4's fixtures were all under `textures/pbr/`, so this was not seen before. `Engine::plan` now records, after the derive admission, the members of `d.sets` and `d.drop` whose own output key some job writes (`Plan::derive_own`). `run` emits no `packed_source` for them, and `report_unread` treats them as ended (a kept `_p` of a set with no albedo, which nothing reads). A folded member keeps its `packed_source`, because no job writes at its own key. `every_discovered_file_gets_one_terminal_event` now runs in both modes, with a landscape set, a landscape set with no albedo and a grass set. A derived candidate that fails at admission counts as writing its output, so on an unfolded set its source ends with the `file_failed` alone. The terminal-event test covers this with a truncated rough source under `textures/misc/`.
- **CN28 `[export]` in `sdc.toml` (Task 6; C3, C4, C2, TA9, TA10).** A project `sdc.toml` may hold `[export]`: `also` (`"vanilla"`, `"cm"`), `zip` (bool), `skip` (set ids, as `--set set:<id>` uses; the C2 opt-out), `[export.names]` (`pbr`, `vanilla`, `cm`) and `[export.legacy]` (`LegacyParams`, defaults k 0.9 and `landscape_spec` 2.5). Every table is `deny_unknown_fields`, so an unknown key is a parse error of `sdc.toml`. It is `ConfigFile::export: Option<ExportConfig>`, skipped when absent, so a config without it parses, and is written, as before (C6). The recipe settings are not `Profile` fields, so no profile hash moves (C4).
- **CN29 `[export]` is project-only (Task 6, TA9).** A user config (`%APPDATA%\sdc\config.toml`) with `[export]` is `EngineError::Config` (exit 2) naming `[export]` and the file, as `[files]` and `[inputs]` are. A project-only table keeps a command reproducible from the project folder.
- **CN30 Parse and check are separate (Task 6, O2).** `Engine::export_config(req)` reads the project config (the same loader as planning, now `api::load_project_config`) and returns its `[export]`, else `ExportConfig::default()`. It never calls `check()`. `ExportConfig::check()` (the `legacy` ranges, then the names) is called by `run_also` before anything else, and a failure is `EngineError::Config` naming the `[export.*]` key. Planning never calls it, so a bad `[export.legacy]` value cannot break a plain export with nothing ticked.
- **CN31 Folder names (Task 6, TA10).** `folder_names(project)` gives the configured name, else `"{project} PBR"`, `"{project} Vanilla"`, `"{project} CM"`. `check()` refuses a name that is empty, holds `/` or `\`, or ends in a dot or space (Windows drops it), and refuses two of the three final names that are equal when lower-cased. `check()` has no project name, so it compares the names with an empty project: a custom name equal to another folder's default for the real project is not caught there (`shortcut:` `run_also` compares the final names once it knows the project name).
- **CN32 Also export: three folders, three runs (Task 7).** `engine::also::run_also` checks the location (CN36), then `ExportConfig::check()`, then the final folder names (CN37), and preflights all three requests before anything is written. The phases run in order: **PBR** (the request with `output_root` = `<location>/<name> PBR`, today's plan and run, events unprefixed so the GUI's PGPatcher-JSON rows match), **Vanilla** (target `vanilla`, `derive` mode Vanilla, the copy step of CN33), **CM** (mode Cm, only the derived items). Vanilla runs whenever `also` holds `vanilla` or `cm`, because CM installs on top of Vanilla (TA30); with `also = ["cm"]` the notes say "CM installs on top of Vanilla: the Vanilla folder is written too". With no PBR set to derive (none, or all skipped), the CM phase does not run, no CM folder is made, and the note is TA30's "no PBR sets: Vanilla holds copies only; no CM folder written". The project name is the first input folder's name. `run_also` never sets `bc1_model`: the caller's request carries it, so the PBR folder equals that user's plain export (O2, `also_export_bc1.rs`, which runs alone because the BC1 model is process-global). The CM phase keeps the jobs with `derive`, and the skipped, failed and cancelled entries of a `DeriveSet` member, so a non-PBR failure counts once (in Vanilla); its planning events are held and only those of the kept items are forwarded, so a CM row never waits for a terminal event that will not come.
- **CN33 The copy rule (O4, TA25).** After the PBR run, each ready, non-derived, non-packed Vanilla job whose cs twin (a PBR-plan job with the same input) passes `also::same_identity` and is current is taken out of the Vanilla plan and copied from the PBR folder after the Vanilla run. `same_identity`: both `Ready`; equal inputs; equal `output_key`s relative to their roots, the cs key folded by `vanilla_rel` (O6's landscape `_p` copies); equal `pack`, `rnm` and `bake`; `van.derive` none; `Profile { target: Cs, ..van.profile } == cs.profile`. Current means the PBR folder's record passes `api::is_up_to_date` (now `pub(crate)`, not restated) for this run's twin, encoders, NVTT version and BC1 model, which also checks its file stamp. Any other twin is encoded, so a failed or stale PBR output is never copied and never leaves a gap. The copy record is the twin's record with `output` = the Vanilla key, `ts` = now, `output_stamp` after writing and `copied_from` = the twin's `output_stamp`. `ManifestRecord::copied_from` / `ManifestEntry::copied_from` is skipped when `None`, so no existing manifest line changes; only `manifest.schema.json` gains it. A copy is up to date when the Vanilla record's `sources` and `source_sha256` equal the twin's, its `copied_from` equals the twin file's stamp now, and its `output_stamp` matches the file (`FileSkipped UpToDate`); a changed BC1 model re-encodes the twin, its stamp moves, and the copy is redone. An existing file under `if-changed` goes through fix/pre-v2's `may_replace` with "the Vanilla record's `output_stamp` matches" as `ours`; `Kept` is `OUT-UNKNOWN-EXISTING` and the file is unchanged. `--on-existing skip` and `overwrite` act as for encodes. A copy ends with `FileDone` carrying the PBR record's validation. `shortcut:` a packed job is never copied (its raw sources' `packed_source` events belong to its encode), and a copy writes no `--sidecar`; upgrade if either matters. Copy outcomes count in the Vanilla phase's summary (up to date, skipped, failed, cancelled) and in `AlsoSummary::copied`, after that phase's `batch_done`, whose counts therefore leave them out. A dry run plans every phase and counts the copies, but writes and records nothing.
- **CN34 Event prefixes and discovery (TA10).** Vanilla and CM events go through `events::PrefixSink` with `"<Vanilla folder>/"` and `"<CM folder>/"` before each job key, so the three folders' rows never share a key; batch-level events are unchanged. Each phase has its own batch id. `BatchRequest::skip_root` (default `None`) is the folder discovery skips in place of `output_root` (`discover_reporting(.., skip)`); every phase sets it to the location, so a location inside the opened folder is never read as sources, while outputs are still built from `output_root`.
- **CN35 Preset and target (TA14, TA20, P10).** The Vanilla and CM requests are the batch request with `target = vanilla`, their folder and `low_detail = Off` (P10: the check runs once, in the PBR phase). `preset` is passed through unchanged: an explicit or configured preset id is kept (TA14); with none, the default `vanilla-quality` differs from `cs-quality` only in `target` (O4), and the PBR plan's resolved id cannot be used because all three requests are preflighted before that plan exists. A cs-only `--set` (`format=bc6h_uf16`) fails that preflight with exit 2 (`EngineError::Usage`, as `check_up_front` reports it) before any folder exists. A PBR plan whose resolved target is not `cs` is refused with `Usage("Also export needs the cs mode: the PBR folder is the cs export")` before anything runs (TA20).
- **CN36 Location (TA19, P1, P19).** `also::check_location(inputs, location, folders)` refuses a location equal to an input folder and applies `also::export_folder_problem` (the GUI rule and text, moved engine-side; Task 11 makes the GUI's a delegate) to each of the three folders: none may equal or contain an input folder. A location that contains the opened folder (MO2 `mods\`) is fine. Paths compare absolute, `/`-separated and lower-cased; `shortcut:` junctions and 8.3 names are not resolved (the folders may not exist yet).
- **CN37 Folder names (closes the CN31 shortcut).** `run_also` compares the three final `folder_names(project)` pairwise, case-folded; equal names are `EngineError::Config` naming the custom key(s) (`export.names.cm`). `ExportConfig::check()` also refuses Windows-illegal characters (`: * ? " < > |` and control characters) and the reserved device names `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`-`COM9`, `LPT1`-`LPT9`, case-insensitively and with any extension (`nul.txt`), naming the key.
- **CN38 Cancel and later errors.** `cancel` is checked between phases; a cancel, or an engine error of the Vanilla or CM phase, stops the later phases and sets `AlsoSummary::cancelled_after` to the last phase that ran (the error goes into `notes`). Errors before the PBR phase writes anything are returned as `Err`. `AlsoSummary::exit_code` is `combined().exit_code()`, but an export stopped before its last phase is at least 1 (partial) even when the phases that ran were clean.
- **CN39 Owned files (TA21).** `also::OwnedFiles` keeps the hash records of the files written outside the manifests (Tasks 8 and 9: report, zips, sums) in `<PBR folder>/_sdc/also.json`, never at the location root, keyed like fix/pre-v2's JSON records (absolute, `/`-separated, lower-cased). `write` asks `may_replace` (the recorded or the pending SHA counts as ours), records the new SHA as pending and saves, writes with `write_atomic`, then moves pending to the record and saves; a crash between the rename and the save leaves a pending SHA that matches the file, so the next export still owns it. An I/O error comes back as `Kept::Unreadable`. Every non-dry run saves the record once after the PBR phase, so `also.json` is the one file an Also export adds beside a plain export's `_sdc`. Copies and owned files use `may_replace` and add no overwrite rule of their own. `AlsoSpec::inner_layer_sets` (TA27) is carried for the report (Task 9); `shortcut:` the CLI leaves it empty.
- **CN40 One slot rule (P5).** `also::derive_sets(plan, skip)` is the slot rule of Task 4 Step 3, moved from `tests/derive_plan.rs`, whose helper now calls it. A set picked `pbr`, `pbr_landscape` or `pbr_grass` (TA11) whose id is in `[export] skip` (compared through `sets::set_key`) gives `SetNote { why: "skipped (Skip vanilla/CM for this set)" }` and its members go to `DeriveRequest::drop`.
- **CN41 A later-phase error keeps its class (Task 7 review M1; supersedes CN38's error half).** An engine error of the Vanilla or CM plan or run stops the later phases and is recorded in `AlsoSummary::error` as (phase, message, `EngineError::exit_code`); `cancelled_after` now means a cancel only. An `ALSO-PHASE-FAILED` (Error) warning naming the phase goes out batch-level, unprefixed. `exit_code()` returns that error's code (2 or 3), as a plain export that errors exits with it; otherwise `combined().exit_code()`, raised to 1 for a cancel stopped export when it is 0 or 4 (spec §8: partial beats validation). A plain `max` was not used because 4 > 3 numerically. When the Vanilla run fails after its copies, the phase is still pushed with the copies' counts.
- **CN42 Copies before the Vanilla run (Task 7 review M2; supersedes CN33's order).** `do_copies` runs before `engine.run(vplan)`, into the phase summary that `run`'s counts are then added to, so every copy event comes before the Vanilla `batch_done`. The copies read only the PBR folder and their keys are out of the Vanilla plan, so the order changes no byte. `batch_done`'s own counts still leave the copies out (they are in `AlsoSummary`'s Vanilla phase and `copied`); the GUI (Task 11) counts rows, not those numbers. The copy record keeps the twin's `profile`, `profile_sha256`, `preset` and `shader` (review L1, intended): `same_identity` already proved the bytes equal, and a later plain `--target vanilla` export into the Vanilla folder re-encodes the copies once, which is safe. `shortcut:` copies write no `--sidecar` (comment at `do_copies`).
- **CN43 A corrupt `also.json` is left alone (Task 7 review M4, M5).** `OwnedFiles::load` returns `io::Result`: a missing record is empty, but one that exists and cannot be read or parsed is an error, never read as empty. `run_also` then leaves the file exactly as it is (no rename, no rewrite), emits `ALSO-OWNED-UNREADABLE` and adds a note naming the file; Tasks 8 and 9 write no owned file (report, zips, sums) in that case. That is the safest choice: nothing it lists loses its ownership, so fixing or deleting the file is enough. Renaming it aside would make every listed file foreign at once. A missing record is created; an existing one is never rewritten by `run_also`. `OwnedFiles::write` returns `OwnedWriteError::{Kept, Io}`, and `Io`'s note reads "could not be written"; `Kept` (fix/pre-v2) is unchanged, so its exhaustive matches elsewhere are untouched.
- **CN44 Batch-level warnings once (Task 7 review M7).** The Vanilla and CM phases drop warnings with no job key (preset skips, `IN-UNREADABLE`, `CFG-FILE-UNMATCHED`, …): each re-plans the same inputs, and the PBR phase already reported them. The CM phase's `batch_started.inputs` still counts every discovered file. Two codes added: `ALSO-PHASE-FAILED`, `ALSO-OWNED-UNREADABLE` (110 codes).
- **CN45 Zip export (C8, Task 8).** `engine::zip::write_zip(folder, files)` is an in-house writer (no new dependency): method 8 through `flate2::write::DeflateEncoder` (default level), CRC-32 from `flate2::Crc`, local headers with the sizes known up front (no data descriptor), flag 0x0800 (UTF-8 names), version 2.0, the central directory and the EOCD. Entry names are `<folder name>/<rel>` with `/`, sorted; the DOS time is fixed at 1980-01-01 00:00, so the same files zip to the same bytes. Checked with Windows `tar` and .NET `ZipFile`. TA17: no ZIP64; more than 65,535 entries, or any size or offset at or over 4 GiB - 1, is `ZipError::TooLarge`, and that zip is skipped with a note. `shortcut:` the archive is built in memory, so the 4 GiB ceiling is also a RAM ceiling (upgrade: a temp file plus rename).
- **CN46 What goes in a zip (TA23, P4).** `BatchSummary` holds counts only, so each phase's `Reporter` gets a `Recorder` as its first sink: it collects the unprefixed job keys of `FileDone` and `FileSkipped { UpToDate }`, which covers the Vanilla copies (they emit through the same reporter). After the phases, each folder that ran is walked, skipping its `_sdc` and any `.sdc-*.tmp`. A file whose `output_key` is in its phase's set is zipped under its on-disk name; every other file (a kept unknown file, a stale output such as an old CM diffuse after Keep metal brightness was turned off) gets the note `<folder>/<rel>: not zipped: not written by this export`. P3: Task 8's tests assert these notes and the summary's failure count; the report text is Task 9's.
- **CN47 When zips are written.** `cfg.zip` applies after the phases, in `run_also` (the phases moved to `run_phases`, so every early return still reaches the zip step). No zip and no sums file when the cancel token is set or a phase returned `Err` (note `zip skipped: the export did not finish`), on a dry run, or when `also.json` cannot be read (CN43: `ALSO-OWNED-UNREADABLE` was raised already). File-level failures (a `GRASS-SHAPE`, a size mismatch) don't block the zips. Each folder that ran becomes `<location>/<folder name>.zip`: with `also = ["vanilla"]` that is two zips, and with no PBR sets the CM folder is not written, so not zipped (TA30).
- **CN48 Sums file (TA21).** `<location>/<project name> SHA256SUMS.txt` has one line per zip written this run, in phase order: `"{sha256}  {file name}"`, lower-case hex, two spaces, LF endings, as `tools/package-release.ps1` writes; the file is UTF-8, so it is ASCII unless a folder name is not. The zips and the sums file go through `OwnedFiles` (`may_replace` plus the pending SHA, then `write_atomic`): a zip Tessalith did not write is kept with its note and gets no sums line. With no zip written, no sums file is written.
- **CN49 Zip failures are partial (Task 8 review M1, M3, M4, M5).** A zip or sums file not written (kept as foreign, `TooLarge`, a folder walk or write error) gets its note plus an `ALSO-ZIP-FAILED` (Warning) event, and sets `AlsoSummary::zip_failed`. `exit_code()` then raises 0 or 4 to 1, as a cancel does: the user asked for zips and did not get them all. When no zip is written but an older `<project> SHA256SUMS.txt` exists, it is left alone with a note saying it still lists an earlier export's zips. An owned record that cannot be read at the zip step also sets `zip_failed`. If the start check already reported it (CN43), it is not warned about again. If it broke since, it gets its own `ALSO-OWNED-UNREADABLE` warning and note, not a silent skip. The PBR reporter moved to `run_also`, so the zip step's warnings go out under the PBR batch, like the later phases' batch-level warnings. M4: the entry limit is now 65,534; 65,535 entries is `TooLarge` because 0xFFFF in the EOCD count is the ZIP64 sentinel. This tightens CN45's "more than 65,535". Tests pin the flags (0x0800), the DOS time (0) and the date (0x0021) in both headers, a UTF-8 name and the 65,534/65,535 boundary. 111 codes.
- **CN50 Conversion report (C5, Task 9).** `engine::also::report::render(summary, rows, spec)` writes `<location>/<project name> conversion-report.md`: per-project file names (owner 2026-10-17, superseding C5's fixed names, TA21), in the location next to the three folders. It starts with `<!-- written by Tessalith; regenerated on every Also export -->`, then the folders that ran with converted, copied (Vanilla only), up-to-date, skipped and failed counts, "Cancelled after <phase>" or "Stopped: the <phase> phase failed: <message> (exit code N)", every `[export.legacy]` value (`toml::to_string`, field order), whether the mesh scan was read, one table row per converted PBR set (suggested NIF Glossiness `{:.1}` and Specular Strength 1 from `DERIVE-NIF-SUGGEST`, TA16; "Environment Map shader needed" yes/no; env `_m` written: yes / no: no scan / no: mesh not env-map / no for a set without metal; "-" for landscape and grass, which get no suggestion), each set's notes, the sets not converted with why, the CM install text and every `AlsoSummary::notes` entry verbatim (TA30's notes, "not zipped", zip failures, walk errors, `TooLarge`, the stale-sums note, an owned record that cannot be read). LF endings and no timestamp: the same inputs give the same bytes.
- **CN51 When the report is written.** Last in `run_also`, after the zip step, so it carries the zip notes; after a cancel or a phase error too. Not on a dry run, and not when `ALSO-OWNED-UNREADABLE` was raised (CN43), as for the zips and the sums file. `run_also` now loads `OwnedFiles` once for both steps. It goes through `OwnedFiles::write` (`may_replace` plus the pending SHA, then `write_atomic`): a report Tessalith did not write is kept, its `Kept::note` goes into `AlsoSummary::notes`, and `AlsoSummary::report` stays `None`. Task 9 review (controller ruling), matching CN49: a report kept or not written (an I/O error) also raises `ALSO-REPORT-FAILED` (Warning) and sets `AlsoSummary::report_failed`, which raises an exit of 0 or 4 to 1 (partial). 112 codes.
- **CN52 Where the rows come from.** Read from the plans before they run (`run` consumes them). The Vanilla plan gives everything: the NIF suggestion and the not-converted notes live there only (Task 4); its `DERIVE-*` job warnings, its error jobs' warnings and its load failures become set notes; a set it skipped whole (`DERIVE-DDS-SOURCE`, `DERIVE-NO-ALBEDO`) becomes a `SetNote` in `AlsoSummary::sets` (beside C2's skipped sets) and gets no row. The CM plan adds only its derived error jobs (`report::derive_error`: `recipe:<derive kind>` on a PBR-set member; a CM size mismatch or path conflict, prefixed `CM:`), never a plain error job the Vanilla phase reports already (review M2); its `DERIVE-NO-ALBEDO` and not-converted items would repeat the Vanilla ones. A member reported both as a set-level `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED` note and as `report_unread`'s per-file skip is listed once, keyed by its path, with the note's reason (it carries TA28's "detail layer not in the vanilla _n").
- **CN53 Per-set lines (TA26, TA27, P22).** "Toksvig not applied" for a set whose derived `LegacyN` `_n` in the Vanilla plan passes CL40's opt-in test, now `bake::plan::gloss_bake_opted` (extracted from `plan_gloss_bakes`, same test), when the CM folder is ticked. "inner-layer `_p` copied unchanged" for a set in `AlsoSpec::inner_layer_sets` (ids compared through `sets::fold_id`).
- **CN54 The install line (P2).** `also::cm_lines(cfg)` is the one copy of the CM install text: "Install the CM folder on top of the Vanilla folder.", plus "It holds only the `_m` files." with Keep metal brightness off. - **CN90 Measured (2026-10-21; Skyking Signs vanilla 1.7 / PBR 2.3, Vanaheimr Landscapes AIO 1k vanilla 7.1 / PBR 7.0): the diffuse and landscape checks pass; the `_n` k check passes only as the per-author median of two authors, i.e. their mean (neither author is in the band; see CN91).** Skyking: 34 pairs, diffuse R² 0.952, fitted k 0.890; `_n` k 0.044 (n 4, corr 0.05). Vanaheimr: 158 pairs (107 landscape), 7 skipped for size (each an `_rmaos` at half the albedo size, as the test prints); diffuse R² 0.795 (objects 0.776, landscape 0.805), fitted k 0.861 (objects 0.925, landscape 0.847); `_n` k 1.215 (n 148, corr 0.50); landscape `_n` alpha mean derived 0.0991 against shipped 0.0775, ratio 1.279 (1 shipped `_n` opaque). Over authors: diffuse R² 0.874 (≥ 0.8) and `_n` k 0.629 (in [0.45, 0.83]). The fitted k reproduces 05 R2.3 (Skyking 0.89, Vanaheimr 0.86, `_n` k 1.15-1.24), so the loader and the pairing match that study.
- **CN91 Caveats of CN90.** Only two authors are in the data, so "median over authors" is the mean of two. The `_n` k band is Aokili's (05 R2.3), and Aokili's archives are not in this data set: 0.629 is the mean of a near-empty spec author (0.044) and a weak fit (1.215), both of which R2.6 calls weak, so passing that assertion says little about the spec defaults. The landscape shipped mean (0.0775) is higher than 07's 0.052 because this check weights by texel over every paired landscape `_n` (one opaque); the ratio is still inside the band. Vanaheimr's diffuse R² alone is 0.795, just under 0.8, with k fixed at 0.9 against its fitted 0.86.

So the Vanilla (and CM) diffuse applies the soft light and the cavity multiply of spec step 3, and the member is read by the diffuse job instead of being reported `DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED`. Goldens do not move: only derived outputs change.
- **CN93 Zip cancel and RAM (final review M1).** `zip::write_zip` takes the `CancelToken` and checks it before each entry; a cancel returns `ZipError::Cancelled`, so nothing is handed to `OwnedFiles::write`: no partial file, the old zip stays, and the zip gets the usual "not written: cancelled" note and `zip_failed` (CN49). Correction to CN45's `shortcut:`: peak RAM is about twice the zip size (the new zip in memory plus the old one `may_replace` reads to compare), near 8 GiB at the 4 GiB ceiling. Every Also export that finished (no cancel, no phase error) walks each folder that ran, zip on or off (`this_runs_files`, the walk TA23's zip used): a file that is not among the job keys this run wrote or found up to date (copies included) is kept and gets a note `<folder>/<rel>: not written by this export; kept as it is` (`NOT_WRITTEN`), or with the zip on the existing `not zipped: not written by this export` (`NOT_ZIPPED`), one note per file. The notes reach the report and the GUI's export notes. After a cancel or a phase error nothing is listed, since most files were not reached; "finished" is decided before the zips, so a cancel while zipping does not change it. `cm_lines(cfg, grass, stale)` now describes what the CM folder holds this run: with Keep metal brightness off "only the `_m` files", or "the `_m` files and the complex-grass stacks of the PBR grass sets" when a PBR grass set that is not skipped is exported (`grass`); and, in the report only, "It also holds files this export did not write, listed under Notes …" when the walk found any in the CM folder (`stale`).
