## Note CS — Shader flags that need a shader type (owner, 2026-10-21)
The letters CO are provisional: take the next free letter on `main` at merge and rename this note if CO is taken.
- **CS1 Skin tint and FaceGen detail are tied to their shader types (owner ruling S-P1).** SLSF1 bit 21 FaceGen_RGB_Tint off shader type 5 (nif.xml "Skin Tint") crashes the game; SLSF1 bit 10 Facegen_Detail_Map off type 4 ("Face Tint") renders black; type 4 without bit 10 is wrong too. Each is an Error on the SLSF1 field (`validate::type_flag_errors`) that blocks export even in an untouched source (`ALWAYS_BLOCK`, like B-P39's env scale), with a one-step fix labelled "Clear the flag" or "Set the flag". A shader type change in the Shader tab adds the needed SetBits to the same push (one undo step) and shows one notice line until the next change. Bits 21 and 10 are greyed off their type, with the reason on hover. Evidence: the crash and the black are the owner's in-game facts; CS picks FACEGEN / FACEGEN_RGB_TINT from the technique (= shader type, ShaderCache.h:638-639), samples tint t3 and detail t4 only under FACEGEN (Lighting.hlsl:352-354, 679-688), and reads the flags only as the SSS skin gate (SubsurfaceScattering.cpp:508). Corpus: no vanilla shape breaks any of the three (52,822 vanilla lighting shapes in the scan, plus 21,917 vanilla FaceGen and LOD shapes walked separately; every vanilla type 4 has bit 10 and every bit 21 is on type 5); mods break them 1, 9 and 2 times. Not ruled: type 5 without bit 21 (380 mod shapes, vanilla 0), type 16 without Eye_Environment_Mapping (22 vanilla shapes), Hair_Soft_Lighting (never off type 6, no harm shown).
- **CS2 Orphan shaders are skipped (ruling S-P2).** A BSLightingShaderProperty no shape uses is never drawn, so it cannot crash or render black: the CS1 rules skip it, and it never blocks export (the Shader tab could not reach it to fix it anyway).
- **CS3 Skin Tint may carry the FaceGen detail flag (owner, 2026-10-21).** CS1's "bit 10 off type 4" became "bit 10 off types 4 and 5": all 9 mod shapes that broke it are type 5 (USSEP fine-clothes boots `bootsf_0`/`bootsf_1`, RaceMenu `face_overlay`, UBE `elfear`, five Next-Gen Decapitations heads), and the owner agrees the boots do not render black. Bit 10 is no longer greyed on type 5, and a type change between 4 and 5 keeps it. The reverse case stays an error: bit 21 off type 5 (for example on Face Tint) crashes.

## Note CR — NIF v2 Phase C: named clips (NIF team, 2026-10-21)
The letters CN are provisional: take the next free letter on `main` at merge and rename this note if CN is taken. Branch `nif/v2c-clips` from nif/main de46c46 (main + Phases A, B and D + key fixes + CM35). Plan: `2026-10-17-nif-edit-v2-phase-c-plan.md` in the NIF team's plan folder. The rulings were made while building as C-P1 to C-P34 (SDD ledger `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-17-nif-edit-v2-phase-c-plan/progress.md`). C-P1 to C-P24 are the pre-flight findings F0 to F23 (C-P(n) = F(n-1)), accepted as proposed except F16 (C-P17'); C-P28 accepted every open decision of the C3 to C5b briefs as recommended. Commits carry no attribution line (C-P23).
- **CR1 What Phase C adds.** Four ops and one helper: `AddSequence` (a clip with tracks), `RemoveSequence`, `RenameSequence` and `ConvertChainToClips`; `SplitAlpha` now works on an alpha a clip drives. Each new op carries `at: Anchor` with `Role::Root` and finds a clip by (name, nth) in the root manager's list order at apply time (C-P4). Track anchors inside `ClipTrack` are resolved on every apply; `rebase` never writes them back. No new `Role` variant. The Controllers tab gains New clip, Rename, Remove, Convert to clips (C5) and a colour strip under colour curves (C5b).
- **CR2 Encoders and the corpus census (C-P2, C-P6, C-P7, C-P24, C-P26, C-P27).** `nif::clips` encodes the manager, sequence, object palette, text keys, MTTC and blend interpolator, and has raw readers (`read_sequence_out`, and `ctrl::read_manager`, which gained `cumulative`) that keep every field the model drops, so the round trip can be byte-identical. The encoders are fallible (`NifError::Encode`, for example a note-array count or an MTTC target count past u16; the text-key count is u32). Corpus gate over the vanilla BSA: 1051 managers, 3989 sequences and 1051 MTTCs round-trip byte-identical, with 0 mismatches (loose corpus: 24 managers, 96 sequences). The census fixed what C2 writes. Manager: flags 0x4c in all 1051, Cumulative 0, frequency 1, phase 0, start `FLT_MAX`, stop `-FLT_MAX`, next block always an MTTC. MTTC: flags 0x6c (one has 0x16c), always with extra targets, target the root, frequency 1, phase 0, start `FLT_MAX`, stop `-FLT_MAX` (C-P29). Blend interpolator: flags 1, array size 2, threshold 0, Value `#INV_FLT#` in all 6722. Sequence: weight 1, array grow-by 1, no notes, `start` and `end` text keys, every sequence listed by a manager; cycle Clamp 2768, Loop 1221; accum root is the root's name in 73 %. Controlled block priority 0. Palette Scene is the root in 1051 of 1051. The constants are `MANAGER_FLAGS`, `MTTC_FLAGS` and `BLEND_FLAGS`; C-P26 replaced the brief's placeholders (0x48, no targets, size 0).
- **CR3 The controlled-block string convention (C-P1, C-P19, C-P21).** A Float or Colour block's Controller ID is the variable in decimal text; a TestRef block's Controller ID is null (-1), not `""` (corpus: 1696 of 1696 TestRef blocks are null, and the binder requires it); every block's Interpolator ID is null; Property Type is `BSLightingShaderProperty` or `NiAlphaProperty`. The block's Node Name is the shape's own name index, never a lossy decode, and the palette entry uses the same raw bytes. A shape with no name ("This shape has no name: a clip cannot find it.") or a name another shape also has ("Two shapes are named X: a clip cannot tell them apart.") is refused, since nothing in v2 renames a shape. A clip name is refused when empty, not encodable in Windows-1252, or equal to another clip of the same manager ignoring ASCII case.
- **CR4 Object palette upkeep (C-P9, C-P31, C4-D5).** The palette lists each animated shape once, matched by AV Object pointer. An add or a split appends the entries it lacks and re-emits the palette only then; entries are never removed. Rule for any future op that renames a shape: patch the CB Node Names and re-emit the palette entry together (no such op exists, so C2's rename-shape test was dropped). The split keeps the MTTC's extra targets in step through one shared helper (C-P31); a later add that binds a new shape does the same (C-P29).
- **CR5 The MTTC is kept (C-P5, C-P26, C-P29).** The first add builds root controller → manager → MTTC → the root's previous first controller (a 4-byte patch of the root's Controller ref, no prefix re-emit). Vanilla always has an MTTC after the manager, so one is always written for parity, with the clip's shapes as targets (the plan's "empty MTTC" became the census form). The manager's own clock is the census base in CR2.
- **CR6 Which clips exist (C-P3).** `read_model` lists only live sequences: when the file has at least one `NiControllerManager`, those some manager lists; with no manager, all of them. Remove unlinks the clip and leaves the block in the file, and an unlisted sequence never plays in game. Any remove releases each controller it drove that no other live clip drives (the last clip that drives a controller): it clears 0x20 there and puts back the interpolator ref. An unreadable listed sequence refuses Remove and Split (C-P29).
  - Export drops these orphans: Note CQ.
  - Removing the last clip now also unlinks the emptied manager and its MTTC (the game crashes on an empty manager): Note CU8.
- **CR7 Adding a clip (C-P8, C-P11, C-P12, C-P20, C-P22, C-P28).** Every track appends a fresh keyed interpolator and data from its keys; the controller's old interpolator becomes an orphan. Indices are known before the appends (the order is fixed in C2: manager placeholder, MTTC, palette, then the tracks). The add sets root BSX bit 0. A track on an alpha with more than one user is refused ("This alpha is shared by N shapes: split it before editing."). Authored track keys get the three key Errors of CM10 (`validate_ops` learned `AddSequence`); converted source keys are not checked (B-P29). Nothing is appended until every check passes.
- **CR8 Convert to clips (C-P13, C-P28, C-P30).** (Placement superseded by Note CZ15.) Convert takes a property's free controllers (known class, Active, not managed, keys present, no Play Backwards) into one clip, named `SpecialIdle` by default (`CONVERT_NAME`, with the hover `CONVERT_HOVER`). They must share cycle and frequency bits and have phase 0, else "These controllers run on different timings: they cannot share one clip." The clip takes the union of start and stop; keys are not rescaled. Each controller's start and stop must be finite before the union (C-P30). Controllers that are keyless or of another class stay free. `convert_check` can say Ok where the op still refuses (zero keys, a broken chain); the button tries the op and shows the refusal.
- **CR9 Split on a clip-driven alpha supersedes CI21 (C-P10, C-P14, C-P31).** For each CB bound to the original chain: a CB whose Node Name is the edited shape moves to the copy, and a new CB for the original names the first remaining user; any other CB gets a new CB for the copy that names the edited shape. A string-bound CB that moves becomes bound by ref. A new CB shares the interpolator. The C5 in-game check confirmed all three alpha branches follow the clip (CR12).
- **CR10 Clips UI (C-P17', C-P25, C-P28, C-P33).** (Placement superseded by Note CZ15.) Rename and Remove sit under the Preview list and act on the picked clip. New clip defaults to Clamp. Enter never removes a clip, and a corrected rename clears its refusal. A nameless clip says "This clip has no name: it cannot be renamed or removed here." (C-P33). NIF colours are stored sRGB (CS linearises EmitColor, spec 6.2) while egui's picker takes linear RGB, so the Shader-tab picker and the key swatch convert at the widget edge only (C-P17'); a picker outside 0-1 or NaN is disabled (C-P25). The colour strip uses the swatch's mapping, so a key and its strip agree (C-P17, C-P16): `strip_colours` is pure and unit-tested, an HDR sample (any channel outside 0-1) gets a dashed band along the strip's top and an outlined swatch, and the strip has its own 12 px allocation under the graph.
- **CR11 What the preview does with clips (C-P32, C-P34).** Under Free chains, a clip named SpecialIdle (ASCII case-insensitive) plays with its own frequency, range and cycle, and wins over any other listed clip that binds the same controller. Every other managed controller holds the first key of the first clip the managers list for it, not its property value. With no clip to play and a range of zero length, there is no clock and the values show at t = 0. This revises G2 for a file that has a manager; 0x20 without a manager still shows the property value.
- **CR12 C5 in-game results (cell with six captures, no crash).** PLAY yes: a converted clip plays both tracks (LSCF and LSCC). AUTO-SI yes: a SpecialIdle clip starts by itself, in phase with the global clock; the `CONVERT_HOVER` text ("loops constantly") holds. SPLIT yes: all three alpha branches follow the clip, 39 to 81 of 255 against 81.2 predicted, by ref and by new CB (C4-D2, F13). IDLE-NM, medium confidence (one capture group): a managed controller whose non-SpecialIdle clip is never called holds that clip's first key, not the property value; this is what CR11 mirrors. The clock moves the global multiple at 0.05 per second in every group.
- **CR13 Open items.** F14 (C-P15): no op edits an existing clip's cycle type, frequency or range, and keys added past a clip's stop never play; to change them the user removes and re-adds the clip. A later `SetSequenceTiming` is the owner's call. F17 (C-P18): the refusal "This clip has several interpolators for this controller: editing them needs Phase C." now reads "...: they cannot be edited.". The key swatch and strip show the stored colour, not the in-game colour (CS multiplies by Emissive Multiple), so a dim strip beside a bright game colour is expected. Removing the last clip on a controller gives it that clip's keys, so the remove order decides which keys come back (C-P29 as ruled): remove a converted SpecialIdle last to get the original curve back; removed first, its curve stays only in an orphaned block (final review M4).
- **CR14 Parked minor.** Two managers, or two SpecialIdle sequences, binding one controller are untested: both play in the preview and the later track wins. The in-game phase of SpecialIdle against the preview clock was only checked against the global clock. A nameless sequence ("Clip N") cannot be renamed or removed by name. An empty NiControllerManager after the last remove (its MTTC, palette and the BSX Animated bit stay) is untested in game (final review M5).
  - Two managers and two SpecialIdle clips are now tested: Note CU5. The empty manager crashed the game (C6E); the editor no longer leaves one: Note CU8.
- **CR15 Final review fixes (C-P35).** The pre-merge review (Opus, "yes with fixes") found two Important and seven Minor items; C-P35 ruled one fix round.
  - I1: `SetKeys` gains `clip_name` (serde default, skipped when None, so older documents load and write unchanged). The GUI fills it from the picked clip. At apply, a sequence at `clip` with a different name is a Conflict ("The clip X is no longer at its place in the file."), because a revert of an earlier AddSequence can move another clip onto that block. If this is wrong, a stale key edit is refused and the user makes it again. `Playing::Clip(block)` can still switch clips after a revert (display only, unchanged).
    - The Preview no longer switches clips: Note CU1.
  - I2: New clip copies a controller's own keys only when they are Linear or Quadratic. TBC, XYZ and CONST keys start flat, like keyless ones, with the hover "Its keys are not linear or quadratic: the clip starts flat.", so a new clip never adds the export-blocking key Error.
  - M1: AddSequence refuses a cycle type past 2 ("The cycle must be Loop, Reverse or Clamp.") and a stop that is not after start ("Stop must be after start."). Convert of controllers whose ranges are all empty, or whose cycle bits are 3, refuses through the same check; `convert_check` still says Ok and the click shows the refusal, as CR8 allows.
    - `convert_check` now predicts both refusals: Note CU3.
  - M2: a NiControllerManager on the root's chain that does not read refuses AddSequence ("The root's controller chain cannot be read.") instead of getting a second manager in front of it. Remove and Rename give the same refusal; `clip_key` gives None.
    - Widened to any unreadable entry on the root's chain: Note CU4.
  - M3: a split grows each palette and MTTC once, with the union of the shapes of every manager that uses it, so two managers sharing one no longer overwrite each other's additions. One manager gives the same bytes as before.
  - M6: the New clip ticks clear when the file or the shape changes. The refusal line's `Arc` pointer identity is parked (rare, display only).
    - The refusal line keys on a revision now, and the shape half has a test: Note CU2, CU6.
  - M7: CR2 and CR6 corrected; gui.md reworded.

## Note CQ — Export drops orphan blocks our edits made (owner, 2026-10-21)
The letters CQ are provisional: take the next free letter on `main` at merge and rename this note if CQ is taken. Branch `nif/f-export-gc` from nif/main 81c70c5. Remove Controller, Remove clip, New clip, key-edit copies and splits leave the blocks they appended in the file (CM11, CR6, CR7). An eye mesh of 9 blocks exported with 32 after add/remove/add/clip/remove-clip/remove/add/clip. The owner chose to clean up on export.
- **CQ1 Where.** `nif::edit::compact(bytes, source_blocks)` runs only on the bytes **Export NIF** writes. `apply`, the preview and the edit history keep every block, so op block numbers stay stable. The recorded export hash is the hash of the written (compacted) bytes, so the overwrite guard compares like with like.
- **CQ2 What stays.** Every source block stays at its index, even unreferenced. An appended block stays when a Ref or Ptr of a kept block names it, to a fixed point from all source blocks and the footer roots. The rest are dropped; refs to appended blocks are renumbered in every kept block and the footer; the header's block count, type list (unused types dropped, indices remapped, the top bit of each type index kept) and size list are rewritten. The string table is copied as it is: leftover strings stay (harmless).
- **CQ3 No orphan, no change.** When nothing is dropped the bytes are returned unchanged, so an export without orphans is byte-identical to before, and `compact` is idempotent.
- **CQ4 Which refs are read.** Appended blocks are read whole, by kind: NiAlphaProperty, the three edit controller classes and NiAlphaController (next, target, interpolator), NiFloatInterpolator, NiPoint3Interpolator, the blend interpolators (item refs when not manager-controlled), NiControllerManager, NiMultiTargetTransformController, NiDefaultAVObjectPalette, NiControllerSequence (CB interpolator and controller, text keys, manager, note arrays), and the no-ref kinds (key data, texture sets, text keys, the editable extra data). Source blocks are read only for the ref fields an op can patch: shapes (NiObjectNET extras and controller, shader and alpha refs), nodes and the root (NiObjectNET), BSLightingShaderProperty (NiObjectNET, texture set), BSEffectShaderProperty and NiAlphaProperty (NiObjectNET), every controller (next, target; interpolator for the known classes), keyed interpolators (data), managers, MTTCs, palettes and sequences. Ops patch no other ref field of a source block, so other kinds are leaves.
- **CQ5 Doubt means no compaction.** A reachable appended block of another kind, a block that does not read at its exact size, a ref past the file or a file that does not parse makes `compact` return Err, and the export writes the patch uncompacted. The ref-free kinds are read too (key data, texture sets, text keys, extra data at their exact size) before they count as ref-free. The export still succeeds and records the hash of the bytes it wrote; one plain line under **Export NIF** says "Exported without cleanup: <reason>." until the next export or edit (fix round 1, coordinator ruling).
- **CQ6 Cost.** Linear in blocks and types: used types are marked in one pass over the kept blocks, then remapped in one pass over the type list (a hostile header may list 65535 types).


## Note CT — Derive identity without paths (main session, 2026-10-21)
- **CT1 Change.** `DeriveJob::identity_sha256` now blanks every path before hashing: `sources[].path`, `albedo`, `normal` and the path of each `ChannelSource::Source` slot. Stamps were already blanked. Settings, slots, roles, channels and `invert` still change the identity. This does what CN12 left for before release; the `shortcut:` on `identity_sha256` is removed.
- **CT2 Why.** The per-source SHA-256s and roles in slot order already identify the job, so the paths were redundant. Hashing them made every derived output re-encode once after a project moved.
- **CT3 Cost.** Each existing derived output re-encodes once, the first time `if-changed` runs after this change, because its recorded identity no longer matches. Encoded bytes are unchanged, so goldens are unchanged.
- **CT4 Test.** `derive_identity_ignores_paths_but_not_roles_or_settings` (engine, `derive::assemble` tests) fails on the old code: a moved job hashed differently.

## Note CU — Parked NIF editor fixes (owner, 2026-10-21)
The letters CU are provisional: take the next free letter on `main` at merge and rename this note if CU is taken. Branch `nif/f-parked-fixes` from nif/main 1678071 (= main). The items parked by Phase B (CM), Phase C (CR14, CR15) and the export cleanup (CQ). Each fix started from a failing test.
- **CU1 The Preview never switches clips after a revert (CR15 I1 sibling).** `NifEdit` keeps the picked clip's name next to `Playing::Clip(block)` (the enum is unchanged). After every apply, the clip stays picked only while the sequence at that block still has that name; otherwise the Preview goes back to Free chains. A rename of the picked clip through an edit carries the new name, so the clip stays picked. Limit: undoing or redoing that rename while the clip is picked goes back to Free chains (the name is the only thing that tells two clips apart; their bindings can be identical). Test: `preview_never_switches_clips_after_a_revert` (pick Open, revert its AddSequence: Close now sits on Open's block; before, the Preview showed Close).
- **CU2 The refusal line keys on a revision, not an address (CR15 M6, part 1).** `NifEdit::rev` gets a new process-unique number (`next_key`) on every apply: every edit, undo, redo, revert, Keep mine, Take source and source reload, a failed apply included. `bytes_tag` uses it instead of the `Arc` pointer, which a later state can reuse after the old bytes are freed. Tests: `every_apply_gives_a_new_revision`, `a_refusal_line_goes_on_undo_and_stays_gone`.
- **CU3 Convert to clips is off when the click would be refused (CR15 M1).** `convert_check` now makes AddSequence's two checks on the clip Convert would build: cycle bits 3 ("The cycle must be Loop, Reverse or Clamp.") and a union range that is not longer than zero ("Stop must be after start."). AddSequence and `convert_check` share the two texts as constants, so the hover and the click say the same. CR8's "convert_check can say Ok where the op refuses" still holds for zero keys and a broken chain. Tests: `convert_check_predicts_the_cycle_and_range_refusals` (nif), `convert_is_disabled_for_cycle_3_and_an_empty_range` (gui).
- **CU4 Any unreadable entry on the root's controller chain refuses (CR15 M2).** `root_manager` refused only when the unreadable entry was itself a NiControllerManager. An unreadable controller of another class in front of the manager ended the walk, so AddSequence put a second manager in front of the real one. Now any entry before the chain's end that does not read refuses AddSequence, Remove and Rename ("The root's controller chain cannot be read."), and `clip_key` gives None. A class `nif::ctrl::read_ctrl` does not read at all (one not ending in `Controller`, such as the particle `...Ctlr` classes) on the root's own chain refuses too. That was not measured on the corpus; the CR2 census found every vanilla manager's next block to be an MTTC. Test: `add_sequence_refuses_an_unreadable_controller_in_front_of_the_manager`. Extended past the first manager by CU9.
- **CU5 Two managers or two SpecialIdle clips on one controller (CR14).** Pinned as it is: both clips play under Free chains and the track applied last wins; managers count in block order, each in its own list order. Test: `the_later_special_idle_track_wins`. No code change.
- **CU6 New clip ticks clear on a shape change (CR15 M6, shape half).** Pinned: ticks on one shape are gone on another shape and when you come back. Test: `new_clip_ticks_clear_when_the_shape_changes`. No code change.
- **CU7 Env map scale added after the In game simulation was cached (CM, Phase B parked).** Pinned: the var-8 check is made outside the simulation cache, so a controller added later still gets the Edited source Warning (from the cached simulation) and the In game red line. Test: `env_map_scale_added_after_the_simulation_is_cached_still_warns`. No code change.
- **CU8 Removing the last clip unlinks the manager (C-P36).** The in-game check `C6E-results.md` (NIF team plan folder `nif-edit-v2`) crashed Skyrim in Load3D (a null read with the NiControllerManager in RCX and RDI) on a NIF whose manager listed no sequences. That is what RemoveSequence left after the last clip (CR6, C-P29). Now, when a remove empties the root's manager, the manager and the MTTC after it leave the root's controller chain: the link that named the manager names what followed the MTTC, or -1. Export cleanup (Note CQ) then drops the manager, the MTTC and the palette when this edit made them. A source manager stays in the file, unlinked. Controllers are released as before (CR6); the BSX Animated bit stays. Removing one of two clips keeps the manager. Undo puts it back. A later New clip or Convert builds a new manager. `validate` gives an Error, "This file has a NiControllerManager with no clips: the game crashes on it.", for an empty manager the root's chain reaches; `NifModel::managers` counts each manager's list. One that the source file already has is shown as a Warning (`validate::demote_source`) and never blocks export (R14). Census (`empty_manager_census`, `#[ignore]`, SDC_BSA and SDC_NIF_CORPUS): Skyrim - Meshes0.bsa 18862 NIFs, Meshes1.bsa 3185, the loose corpus 416, with 0 empty managers in any of them. Tests: `removing_the_last_clip_unlinks_the_manager_and_its_mttc`, `removing_one_of_two_clips_keeps_the_manager`, `an_empty_manager_on_the_root_chain_is_an_error_unless_the_source_has_it` (nif), `removing_the_last_clip_unlinks_the_manager_and_undo_restores_it` (gui). Four older tests that asserted the empty manager stays were updated (`remove_last_clip_clears_0x20`, `another_manager_keeps_the_clip_live`, and in compact.rs the owner scenario's block counts and indices: the second add now builds a new manager).
- **CU9 Fix round 1: the whole root chain is checked (review I1, supersedes the scope of CU4).** `root_manager` keeps the first manager but walks the chain to its end: every entry must read, every manager's payload must read, and there must be no loop and no link outside -1 and the file. Anything else refuses Add, Remove and Rename with "The root's controller chain cannot be read." and the bytes stay unchanged. Test: `clip_ops_refuse_a_broken_root_chain_after_the_manager` (a truncated controller after the MTTC, an unreadable second manager, a loop back to the manager).
- **CU10 Fix round 1: clip names decode as Windows-1252 (review I2).** `ctrl::read_sequence` decodes `Sequence.name` as Windows-1252 (`text::lossy`), the encoding the editor writes, not as lossy UTF-8. Every byte maps to one character, so the name is an identity. The Preview's picked name (CU1), the SetKeys clip-name guard (CR15 I1) and Rename now agree. Before, "é" and "ö" both read as U+FFFD, and a rename to "Café" dropped the Preview to Free chains. A SetKeys saved before this with a non-ASCII clip name compares against the new decode and turns into a Conflict once; the user makes the key edit again. Test: `preview_tells_non_ascii_clip_names_apart`.

## Note CV — Trace-debug fixes 2026-10-21 (main session, 2026-10-21)
- **CV1 NIF edit source ignores path spelling (trace 2; points at Note CI29).** `pick_source` skips the edit mod's own copy by comparing the copy root with the edit mod folder. It compared raw text, but MO2 store roots use `/` after the instance folder while the export folder picker gives `\`. After a rescan the edit mod's own export was then picked as the source, ops turned into conflicts and the link to the original was lost. It now uses the same comparison as `same_dir` (separators, trailing separator and ASCII case ignored). It only widens a match; roots in modscan are not changed.
- **CV2 `patch-header --dry-run` no longer prints the real code (trace 4).** A dry run printed `DDS-HEADER-PATCHED` ("header patched") with exit 0 while the file was untouched, so a script counting that code over-counted. It now prints `<file>: would patch: <fixes>` and no code; a real patch still prints the code, after the write. Cost: anything that read the code from a dry run must read the text instead.
- **CV3 NVTT timeout and cancel kill the whole process tree (trace 5; points at AF3).** The per-level timeout and cancel killed only the program `--nvtt` named. A launcher or wrapper left the real encoder running, the one-at-a-time slot (NV7) was freed while it still ran, and the temp folder could not be removed. The level loop now uses the same `kill_tree` as the probe. Stock `nvcompress` is unchanged.
- **CV4 A quoted dotted `[files]` key is a config error (trace 15).** `[files."x"]` with `"alpha.policy" = "cutout"` (one quoted key containing a dot) passed the field check and then read as null, so the value was silently dropped. It is refused, naming the field and saying to use a nested table or an unquoted dotted key (`alpha.policy = ...`), which is how Project-Config documents the form. Cost: a project that had such a line, which did nothing, is now a config error until the line is fixed (the CLI run fails; in the GUI the folder still opens and sdc.toml is marked as a config error with the message, read-only until fixed).
- **CV5 The env-map gate asks for the colour member's own key (trace 17; Notes CN17 and CN68).** CN17 says the vote key is the output stem "without a §6.1 suffix"; CN68 says the GUI asks for the colour member's own key (`colour_mesh_key`, the output stem as written). They differ only when the colour member is `_d`: the vanilla file keeps the name (`steel_d.dds`, Note BQ colour-term rule), the GUI asked for `textures/arm/steel_d` and the engine looked up `textures/arm/steel`, so the vote was never found (DERIVE-NO-ENVMAP). The file name that gets written is what a vanilla mesh references, so CN68 is the intended form: with an albedo the engine uses the stem as it is; a set with no albedo (its anchor is the `_n`) still drops the suffix, as before, and the GUI does not ask for it. Sets without `_d` are unchanged.
- **CV6 Recursive discovery follows links (trace 27).** `discover` walked with links off, so a symlink or junction to a folder was skipped with no message. It now follows them (walkdir `follow_links(true)`), as vfs `loose.rs` does. A link loop or a dead link is reported through the existing skipped list (IN-UNREADABLE), never dropped. A file reached through two paths is still kept once (BQ1); when it is reachable both directly and through a link, the path that is kept, and so the output name, follows walk order. A link into the output folder is skipped by its resolved path, so outputs are not read back. Following links makes walkdir's open-folder errors lose the path, so the unreadable sub-folder is named by probing the parent. Cost: a project that links to a large outside folder now converts it.
- **CV7 A disabled action still owns its key (trace 7; amends AG32 and AG23).** Ctrl+Shift+Z with nothing to redo matched Ctrl+Z, because a disabled Redo was dropped from the key table and egui ignores an extra Shift, so it ran Undo. A disabled action now stays in the match when an enabled action uses the same key; it eats the key and runs nothing. Disabled actions whose key nothing else uses (arrows, Enter) still let the key through to widgets, as before. So a disabled shortcut that shares its key with an enabled one (different modifiers) is now consumed, where AG32 left it unconsumed. A disabled pair with exactly the same key and modifiers as an enabled one is dropped, so the enabled twin wins.
- **CV8 An exact slot with no known path shows an empty pill in the JSON editor (trace 18; Note V, item V10).** "+ key > Match > exact slot N" wrote `matchN = ""` for a slot Tessalith has no path for, and the editor draws no pill for an empty match, so the click looked like it did nothing. It now adds a pending pill (nothing is stored until a path is typed or picked), as "path contains" already does; the set's Matching header keeps its own empty rows (V10). Slot 1 is unchanged. A `matchN = ""` row stored before this fix still shows no pill in the editor; remove it by hand (it matches nothing).
- **CV9 A mode change on a pending match pill moves the pill (trace 20).** The drop-down on a pill that has no path yet stored nothing, so it snapped back. It now moves the pending pill to the new mode (and drops a stored empty key of the old one). A pending pill may also move to exact slot 1: it is drawn like slots 2-8 (pending slots are 1-8) and keeps waiting while slot 1 is turned off (`match1 = ""`), instead of vanishing. Slot 1 stays unselectable while the set's own derived or stored match1 holds it.
- **CV10 Removing a delete section moves its pending keys with the sections after it (trace 21).** Pending keys are held per section index; after Remove the later sections shift up, so their pending pills now shift too, and the removed one's is gone instead of showing on its neighbour.
- **CV11 The JSON editor Rename box refuses device and map-suffix names (trace 9).** The PGPatcher `rename` value only checked path characters, so `CON`, `nul` and `wall_n` were accepted and blocked nothing. It now runs the same check as the Rename dialog and the output-name entry (`check_named`: no reserved Windows device name, no map suffix such as `_n`), and the error names the `rename` field. Cost: a hand-typed rename that ends in any name the engine reads as a map role is now refused: a Skyrim suffix (`_n`, `_d`, `_s`, `_m`, `_p`, `_g`, `_f`, ...), an exporter term (`_albedo`, `_color`, `_normal`, `_height`, `_ao`, ...) or a layer term (`_detail`, `_bump`, ...), so `rock_albedo` and `rock_d` are refused as well as `wall_n`.
- **CV12 The Also gate names the project as the engine does (trace 10).** The GUI took the project name from the opened folder's last component and used an empty name for a drive root, so the gate stayed green and the engine then refused the run. The GUI now calls `engine::also::project_name` (made public), and its error ("has no folder name") is the gate reason.
- **CV13 A file dropped on a slot card keeps the slot 3/7 clash guard (trace 11; AO7, AG98).** `drop_file_on_slot` skipped `slot_conflict`, so `_f` onto a card holding `_cnr` (or `_g` with `_sk`) was accepted and showed as a red row. It is now refused with the same text as a drop on the set, as AO7 says a drop that would make a clash is. Cost: dropping `_f` on the slot 7 card that holds the only `_cnr`, meant as a swap, is now refused too; remove the `_cnr` first.
- **CV14 Fill from names checks clashes inside its own batch (trace 12; AG99).** The clash check only saw slots held before the batch, so `_cnr` and `_f` (or `_g` and `_sk`) could both be proposed. Each accepted row now counts as held for the rows after it; the later one is blocked with the clash text. Cost: the user cannot tick the later row even when the earlier one is unticked, as with "another file above takes this slot".
- **CV15 The bulk Encoder row honours the NVTT-not-found lock (trace 13; Note NV).** Choosing NVTT in the bulk panel wrote it to every selected texture when NVTT was missing, and Export was then blocked. Such textures are now skipped with "NVTT not found: set its path in Advanced"; a texture already on NVTT and a Built-in pick are unaffected.
- **CV16 Rename Inputs blocks two rows that write one output (trace 14).** `a.png` and `b.tga` renamed to `x.png` and `x.tga` have different names but both write `x.dds`; Apply was enabled and the next plan then showed IN-DUPLICATE. The second row now gets a problem ("<first> is renamed to write x.dds too") and Apply is blocked, like the existing same-name check.
- **CV17 The Meshes path filter folds ASCII only (trace 25; BF1).** The filter lower-cased what you typed with Unicode rules, but stored paths fold ASCII only, so `Éclair` never matched a path holding `Éclair`. It now folds ASCII only, like the paths. Cost: typing `éclair` no longer finds `Éclair` (the same two paths are different on disk for the scan and the store).
- **CV18 An edit that changes no text leaves the document clean (trace 28).** Writing a value that is already stored (the bulk panel, a field left as it was) marked `sdc.toml` as changed with no undo step, so closing asked to save. The edit now puts the unsaved flag back as it was when the text is unchanged. Undoing back to the saved text still counts as unsaved, as before.
- **CV19 The GUI finds an extension-less `[files]` key (trace 29).** The engine reads `[files."a/wall"]` as naming `a/wall.png`, but the GUI looked for the full name only, so the row showed the value as its own while Reset did nothing, and setting a value added a second table. The GUI now reuses the extension-less key. Cost: an edit through that key also changes the same-stem sibling (`a/wall.tga`), as the engine already applies it to both. This includes Reset all: on `a/wall.png` it drops the shared `[files."a/wall"]` table, so `a/wall.tga` loses its settings too (undoable).
- **CV20 Moving a file back splits a shared extension-less `remove` key (trace 30; AG100).** With `remove = ["a/f"]` and both `a/f.png` and `a/f.tga` on disk, moving `a/f.png` into the set did nothing: the key could not be lifted without bringing `a/f.tga` back too. The key is now replaced by an exact `remove` for each other same-stem file, so only the moved file returns. Cost: a hand-written key becomes one exact line per sibling, sorted and without repeats; only image and DDS files count, the inputs the engine reads (not a `.txt` or a folder).
- **CV21 A path that is not Unicode no longer stops `gui.toml` saving (trace 31).** One folder name with a lone surrogate in `recent` (or the export, NVTT or Meshes folder) made every settings save fail, losing the session's settings. That path is now left out of the file. Cost: it is not remembered after a restart.
- **CV22 Encode now during an export waits for it, as the notice says (trace 32).** The press was dropped and the notice stayed, so the user had to click again. It now encodes once the export ends (Live encode on or off) and the notice goes then.
- **CV23 The loose mesh walk skips only the actor facegen folder (trace 3; touches the NIF-team crate `vfs`).** It pruned every folder named `facegendata` at any depth, so `Meshes/Armor/FaceGenData/helmet.nif` was dropped from loose scans but kept when it came from a BSA. It now prunes only `meshes|textures/actors/character/facegendata`, the same rule the BSA side uses. Cost: a mod that keeps real meshes in such a folder now shows them.
- **CV24 A replaced model load drops its queued shader compiles (trace 16; touches the NIF-team crate `render3d`).** The compile pool is a plain queue, so opening a second mesh while the first one's shaders were still compiling made the new mesh wait behind them (cold cache only). Each load now has a number; the pool skips a job from an older load, and the same program is queued again for the new load. Cost: a compile already running still finishes (its result only fills the cache), and a skipped one is compiled again if the old mesh is reopened.
- **CV25 Game text files tolerate a BOM and ANSI bytes (trace 24; touches the NIF-team crate `modscan`).** `plugins.txt`, `Skyrim.ccc`, `Skyrim.ini` and `SkyrimCustom.ini` were read as strict UTF-8, so one ANSI byte emptied the plugin list and a BOM hid `[Archive]`. A BOM is now dropped and non-UTF-8 text reads as Latin-1 (UTF-8 files are unchanged). No schema change. Cost: a plugin name with a non-ASCII character in an ANSI file may not match the file on disk (it was lost before as well); no note is shown for the fallback. `modlist.txt` is not changed. Per-line decoding: Note DA.

## Note CW — Trace-debug fixes 2026-10-22, main side (main session, 2026-10-22)

Two fixes from the NIF team's trace-debug run (report items 4 and 5). Neither was reproduced in the app; each has a test that fails before the fix. The other four items of that run belong to the NIF team (Note CX, provisional).

- **CW1 A scan start re-issues the mesh-evidence read that is in flight (trace 4; extends BY6).** A read started by a finished plan could end after the Scan click, when `begin_scan` had disabled every origin, and land empty votes, alpha and GRAS. BY6 only guarded reads started after the click. Starting a scan now repeats a pending read at once: it lands the evidence already held and the worker's answer becomes stale, and a read that continued a plan still finishes that plan. Cost: a pending read is dropped and not waited for, and the UV coverage cache is cleared when the pending read was not a plan tail (as for any scan-finished refresh). A scan-finished read re-issued by an immediate second Scan click keeps the evidence from before the scan that just completed, and an export queued behind it starts on that older evidence.
- **CW2 Only a PGPatcher-running stop restores the settled flag (trace 5; amends BY6).** BY6 treats every scan that does not complete as leaving the store unreadable. "PGPatcher is running" stops before `begin_scan`, so the store is as it was, yet the flag stayed set and the Used-by lists and UV coverage stayed off until a scan completed. That stop now restores the flag to its value when the scan was started (so an earlier cancel still keeps it set). "Another scan is already running" (Busy) does not: the other process holds the scan lock mid-scan and has already disabled every origin, so the store reads empty and the flag stays set. Cost: a failure before `begin_scan` for another reason (an unreadable MO2 instance, a first `Store::open` error) still counts as unsettled, because the scan error does not say whether the store was touched. "Untouched" is approximate even for PGPatcher-running: `Store::open` may rebuild the database after a schema bump before the stop, so the store can already be empty then. After a Busy stop the lists stay off until this app's own scan completes, as before. This touches `crates/gui/src/model/meshes.rs` (a flag set in `finished`), a file the NIF team also edits.

## Note DA — MO2 text files read per line (NIF team, 2026-10-22)
Renamed from CW at merge (main's Note CW, trace items 4 and 5, took the letter). Branch `nif/f-mo2-encoding` from main 5b516d4. It finishes what Note CV25 left parked.
- **DA1 Per line, not per file.** `modlist.txt`, `ModOrganizer.ini`, `plugins.txt`, `Skyrim.ccc`, `Skyrim.ini` and `SkyrimCustom.ini` are read by one function (`modscan::read_text`). A UTF-8 BOM is dropped, then each line is decoded alone: valid UTF-8 stays UTF-8, any other line reads as Latin-1. A UTF-8 mod name no longer turns to mojibake because another line of the file is ANSI, and a BOM or an ANSI byte no longer fails the scan or hides the first modlist line. A missing `modlist.txt` or `ModOrganizer.ini` is still an error. No schema change. Cost: the fallback is Latin-1, not Windows-1252 (no table in the workspace, no new crate), so an ANSI byte in 0x80-0x9F (for example a curly quote) reads as a control character; a line that mixes UTF-8 and ANSI bytes reads wholly as Latin-1.

## Note CX — Trace-debug 2026-10-22 fixes (NIF team, 2026-10-22)
The letters CX are provisional: take the next free letter on `main` at merge and rename this note if CX is taken. Branch `nif/f-trace-1022` from nif/main 31751fc. Findings: the trace-debug report of 2026-10-22, items 1, 2, 3 and 6. Items 4 and 5 are in main-team files and are left to the main team.
- **CX1 The missing fill survives another shape's edit (async).** `set_material` evicts every texture-less missing entry from the texture cache, not only the edited shape's. A shape still compiling then bound white instead of the missing fill when its program landed. `bind_textures` now also reads `evicted_missing` for a path with no entry, as `plain_srv` already did. Only the diagnostic colour changes.
- **CX2 A swap that fails on device loss keeps the `device removed` prefix.** `replace_texture` put the path in front of the error, so the GUI's replay check (`starts_with(DEVICE_REMOVED)`, Note BS1) missed it and the swap was not replayed after the rebuild. `replace_texture` and `override_slot` now add their context after the message on a lost device (`device removed: … [path]`); other errors read as before. The `default texture:` prefix in `bind_textures` is not changed: `set_material` puts a failed build in the shape status and returns `Ok`, so the edit is logged either way. Tested on the helper only, since device loss cannot be made in a test.
- **CX3 `copies_of_path` reads the copy's derived flag.** `PathCopy.derived` came from the origin (`derived_by`), which overwrite never has, so a mesh PGPatcher wrote into overwrite (listed in its diff) counted as a source. A NIF edit then read the patched mesh, placement said "below overwrite" and export did not ask for a PGPatcher rerun. It now reads `nif_copy.is_derived`, as every other reader does (spec 05 §4(c)). Callers checked: `pick_source` and `rerun_pgpatcher` (nif_edit.rs) and `placement` (export.rs) all mean "PGPatcher output", so none changes otherwise; a whole PGPatcher mod still reads derived because the scan marks each of its copies. Not added: the spec's "PGPatcher output is in Overwrite" warning on the Meshes page.
- **CX4 The Unused note says LOD textures are left out.** The note said LOD textures are listed, but `unused_textures` drops them. No DECISIONS note rules on LOD in Unused. The esp scanner plan (2026-10-12) said LOD textures are listed; commit 2a29162 the next day ("keep LOD textures in the walk, hide them from Unused only") and the `lod_skip.rs` test made hiding them the intended behaviour, and the note was not updated. The query is kept and the text is fixed: "textures\pbr\ (PGPatcher output) and LOD textures are left out. Interface and engine textures are listed too."

## Note CY — Structural-op trace fixes (NIF team, 2026-10-22)
The letters CY are provisional: take the next free letter on `main` at merge and rename this note if CY is taken. Branch `nif/f-structural-1022` from nif/main 31751fc. Findings 1-5 of the 2026-10-22 structural trace; each fix started from a failing test.
- **CY1 A controller edit never moves to its twin (CR15 I1 for controllers).** `resolve` keeps a Ctrl anchor's recorded block only when it is the nth controller of its class and variable on the chain. When it is not, but the recorded block is still on that chain with the same class and variable, the anchor is now a Conflict ("ambiguous: this controller is no longer at its place on the chain."). Before, the edit silently went to the nth twin: remove S0, edit S1, revert the remove, and S0 took the edit. Keep mine cannot resolve it (the anchor does not resolve, so the op stays as it is); the user takes the source (drops the edit) and makes it again, as for CR15 I1. When the twin was removed before the edit in the list and the nth no longer exists, the Conflict now says "ambiguous" instead of "missing". Not index-first: indices of appended controllers shift when an earlier add is reverted, so the nth rule stays and only the twin case conflicts. Cost: a false Conflict when an appended twin moved onto the recorded index. This narrows the Phase A plan's resolution rule (A8) for controllers. Test: `a_ctrl_edit_never_lands_on_its_twin_after_a_revert`.
- **CY2 The writer never writes what its parser rejects.** `NifDoc::append` and `NifDoc::string` now return a `Result` and refuse (`WriteError::Refused`) a new block type at index 0x8000 or more (the parser masks bit 15, so it read back as type 0), a block past `MAX_BLOCKS`, or a string past `MAX_BLOCKS` strings. The op becomes Refused ("This NIF already lists too many block types or blocks." / "...strings."). Only a crafted header reaches it. Tests: `append_never_writes_a_type_index_the_parser_masks`, `string_never_writes_past_the_parsers_string_cap`.
- **CY3 Removing the last clip unlinks the manager from the root's own chain.** When the manager is not the root's first controller, `unlink_manager` walks the root chain from the root's controller ref and patches the link whose next is the manager. Before, it took the lowest-numbered controller of any chain whose next was the manager, so a shader chain merged into the manager was cut and the root chain kept the empty manager (CU8 then blocked export). Malformed merged chains only. Test: `removing_the_last_clip_unlinks_the_manager_from_the_root_chain`.
- **CY4 Add controller refuses a chain whose tail another property lists.** AddController linked the new controller after the chain's last link, so when another property's chain shared that tail, the new controller (targeting the first property) joined both chains. It now refuses with "This controller chain is shared by several properties: a controller cannot be added.", using the same owners check as RemoveController (`owners`, shared). Chains that share a tail stay merged to the end, so only the last link is checked. The GUI still offers Add; the click shows the refusal. Test: `add_refuses_a_chain_shared_by_two_properties`.
- **CY5 Remove clip binds controllers once per sequence.** `release` called `bound_cbs` once per known controller, and each call walked every lighting and alpha property: controllers x properties, minutes on a crafted file with tens of thousands of alpha properties. `anim::bound_map` now gives every controller's CBs of one sequence from one pass over the properties (same rules as `bound_cbs`: by-ref CBs count even when no property lists the controller). `release` builds it once for the removed clip and once per other listed clip. Behaviour unchanged. `cb_plan`, `rewrite_cb_ids` and `clips_of_in` keep the per-controller call (same pattern, smaller; not ruled). Test (pin): `remove_releases_only_controllers_no_other_clip_drives`; no timing test.

(6) Pins: a row warning sits under its own row; after a Known Add the picker is back on Custom… and the entry reads "Already on this shape"; an existing Known row shows the tooltip on its name. Tests: `known_values_are_required_trimmed_and_duplicates_ignore_case`, `a_known_add_falls_back_to_custom_and_rows_show_the_tip`, `an_extra_row_shows_its_warnings`.
- **CZ19 Heel height (T5b; T5b-heel-height.md "In-game results" and "Editor rules (revised)").** A Known entry "Heel height (RaceMenu)" (`KnownValue::Heel`, a row of its own: `heel_row`) on a shape only; on the root it is off with "The game ignores heel height here. Put it on a shape." (the editor has no shader extra list, so a shader is never offered). Set heel height is one undo step: HH_OFFSET (NiFloatExtraData) = Z, an EditExtra of the shape's first HH_OFFSET when it has one (a second is ignored in game), else an AddExtra; when the shape has an SDTA, its first SDTA's last "NPC" entry gets the same Z, other entries kept (`sdta_with_npc_z`; an SDTA that is not a JSON list is left as it is, a `shortcut:`); no second SDTA is ever added, and a new one only when "Also write SDTA (OStim and others read it)" is ticked (off by default). The field starts at HH_OFFSET, else the SDTA's last NPC Z, else 0. Warnings come from `validate` (nif crate) under the rows: heel data on the root or on a property (`HEEL_NOT_ON_SHAPE`), and heel data on a shape after the first shape that has some (`HEEL_EARLIER_WINS`; shape order = model order). The heel row repeats the second for a shape that has no heel data yet. `NifEdit::weight_sibling` (set when the session opens, when the scan has the other `_0`/`_1` file, `weight_sibling_of`) adds "Apply the same value to the other weight file (…)."; there is no cross-file write. Corpus check (`heel_height_calculation_against_the_corpus`, #[ignore], SDC_ACHERUS, read-only, loose NIFs under mods): 215 shapes with stored heel data; within 0.5: 146, within 1.0: 182, within 2.0: 202, median 0.40, max 8.70. The large misses are ground models (`_gnd`, `GND`, `_go`) and one BodySlide ShapeData source, where the stored value is not used in game; on the 140 worn models: within 0.5: 100, within 1.0: 130, all within 2.0 (max 1.60). The Add-row state (the Known pick, the Custom fields, the heel field) is keyed by a new per-session id (`NifEdit::session`), so it never reaches the same block of another NIF or session (`heel_field_follows_undo_and_stays_in_its_session`). - **CZ25 Controllers line outside Edit (T8, owner 2026-10-22; supersedes CZ10's "edit mode only").** No modscan schema bump: when a NIF is selected, `load_shapes` starts one worker thread that reads the shown copy (`read_file` of its store location), runs `read_model` and the same `card_ctrls` the edit session uses (now `pub(crate)` in `nif_edit.rs`), and sends the per-shape lines back. `MeshesModel::scan_ctrls` caches them by copy id (a copy is read once; `reload` after a scan clears the cache, as the files may have changed); the Shapes column takes the answer with `poll_card_ctrls` and repaints every 50 ms only while a read runs. Until the answer arrives the cards show no line (no placeholder, no flicker); a file that does not read or parse gives an empty entry: no line and no error. Inside Edit the cards keep the edited model's lines. Text and style are the Edit-mode line's. ## Note DB — Version 1.0.0, first official release (owner, 2026-10-22)

- **DB1 Version.** The workspace version moves 0.9.0 → 1.0.0 for the first official (non-alpha) release (owner: "bump engine to 1", "this will be an official release build"). 0.9.0 was never released, so the CHANGELOG's 1.0.0 section covers everything since 0.8.0-alpha.2. As in CH1, `ENGINE_VERSION` follows `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` and is part of `is_up_to_date`, so every `--on-existing if-changed` run re-encodes each recorded output once after upgrading. No preset or pixel output changes; goldens are unchanged. `docs/presets-changelog.md` gets a 1.0.0 entry and README names the version. The release zip is built without a suffix (`Tessalith-1.0.0-win-x64.zip`) and the commit it is built from is tagged `v1.0.0` locally; the owner pushes. (Superseded for later versions by Note DM: per-type encode versions.)

## Note DC — Photoshop DDS plugin (owner, 2026-10-24)

The letter DC is provisional (next free letter on main at 2026-10-24); rename at merge if taken.

- **DC1 Licence grant.** The owner grants Tessalith's own code in `crates/engine` and `crates/encoders-sys` under `MPL-2.0` (no Exhibit B) so the Photoshop plugin (`crates/psdds`, `photoshop/`, MIT) can link them. Adobe's SDK licence (section 12) bars software licensed under the GNU GPL, so the plugin carries no GPL, not even as one choice of a dual licence. MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft and lets Tessalith, which stays GPL-3.0-or-later, keep linking the two crates (MPL section 3.3). The vendored encoders in `crates/encoders-sys/vendor` keep their own licences. The plugin never links GPL, LGPL or AGPL code.
- **DC2 (R1) sRGB per format.** sRGB applies only to formats with an sRGB variant (BC1, BC3, BC7, RGBA8). With Colour + BC4/BC5 the sRGB control greys and shows Off. (Colour no longer offers BC4/BC5: DC32.)
- **DC3 (R2) Alpha.** Alpha is kept (`AlphaPolicy::Blend`, no coverage preservation) when the document has alpha and the format stores it (BC3, BC7, RGBA8); otherwise `AlphaPolicy::Remove`. No alpha-test option.
- **DC4 (R3) Base profile.** Each texture type starts from the built-in `cs-quality` profile (`Target::Cs`): Colour -> `Subtype::Diffuse`, Normal -> `Subtype::Normal`, Linear mask -> `Subtype::GenericData`; the dialog's values then override `format`, `color`, `mips.filter`, `mips.levels`, `alpha.policy` and the quality field. `resize = none`, `drop_top_mip = false`.
- **DC5 (R4) Quality lists.** Per format, the same values the GUI preset editor offers (`crates/gui/src/ui/presets.rs`): BC7 -> `encoder.effort`; BC1/BC3 -> `encoder.rgbcx_level`; BC4/BC5 -> `encoder.bc45_search_radius`; RGBA8 greyed. Default = the `cs-quality` value for the type.
- **DC6 (R5) Input scale.** The plugin passes float RGBA in [0, 1]: 8-bit `v / 255`, 16-bit `v / 32768` (Photoshop's 16-bit range is 0..32768). Transfer `SourceTransfer::Stored`. (Amended by DF3: a 32-bit Colour document passes Photoshop's linear samples unscaled with `SourceTransfer::Linear`.)
- **DC7 (R6) No cancel or progress** during encode. Revisit if an 8k BC7 Max save is reported as unusable.
- **DC8 Quality fallback.** A quality index outside the format's list (one remembered from another format, e.g. BC7 Veryslow = 4 with BC4) is not an error: `psdds_resolve` replaces it with the `cs-quality` default for that texture type and format (the base profile's `encoder.effort` / `encoder.rgbcx_level` / `encoder.bc45_search_radius` as a list index; RGBA8 -> 0). Out-of-range format, texture type, sRGB, filter or mips still return -1.
- **DC9 sRGB sets content and tag.** Superseded by DC39 (sRGB sets only the tag). The sRGB control sets both colour fields: On -> `color.content = srgb`, `color.tag = srgb`; Off -> `linear`, `unorm`. Normal and Linear mask are always Off, so linear / unorm. A `cs-quality` sub-type whose tag is `n/a` would keep its colour fields untouched; none of Diffuse, Normal or GenericData has one today. So Colour + sRGB Off is linear content, not the preset's Diffuse `srgb` / `unorm`.
- **DC10 Backend follows the format.** After the format override, `encoder.backend = engine::policy::default_backend(format)` (BC1/BC3/BC4/BC5 rgbcx, BC7 bc7e, RGBA8 uncompressed). DC4's list omits it, but the base profiles are bc7e.
- **DC11 Quality-list source.** The lists in DC5 come from `crates/gui/src/ui/settings_panel.rs` (`options_of` and the rgbcx slider), which the preset editor uses; `presets.rs` only names the fields. They are copied into `crates/psdds/src/settings.rs`, because psdds must not depend on the GPL-only gui crate: BC7 effort Ultrafast..Max (7), BC4/BC5 radius Default / Maximum / Fast (preview), BC1/BC3 rgbcx levels "0".."18". The GUI has a slider there, not labels. The 0..=18 range is a `shortcut:` copy of `encoders_sys::RGBCX_MAX_LEVEL`, which psdds cannot name; `quality_lists_are_pinned` checks it against that constant through a test-only dependency.
- **DC12 The dialog shows the filter the encoder uses; a size limit (review I1, I2).** (Amended by Note DD6: the size rule and its text now live once in `psdds_check_size`; the wording is unchanged.)
  - `psdds_resolve` takes the document's `has_alpha`. For Colour, it builds the profile with a non-box probe filter and asks the engine's own rule, `engine::filter::filter_allowed`. That function is unchanged and is the gate `mips::effective_filter` uses; no copy of the rule exists. Where the rule refuses, the filter greys and shows Box: sRGB Off (linear content), BC4/BC5 (sRGB forced Off; Colour no longer offers them, DC32), and alpha kept in BC3/BC7/RGBA8 (Blend gives alpha-weighted mips). `psdds_encode` uses the same resolved settings.
  - `psdds_encode` refuses a width or height above 16384, or a pixel count whose byte size exceeds `isize::MAX`, before reading the caller's buffer. The error reads "This image is larger than 16384 pixels on a side, the most Skyrim supports." This keeps a huge document from aborting Photoshop on a failed allocation.
- **DC13 PiPL as embedded JSON (Task 5).** The plugin's PiPL is `photoshop/PiPL.json`, compiled in by `TessalithDDS.rc` as a resource named `JSON_PIPL` of type `JSON`. The 2026 SDK documents this as the current form (PiPL Resources, PiPL JSON Syntax, FAQ 3.2.1) and marks `Cnvtpipl.exe` deprecated: it converts `.r` resource files, not JSON. The plan's "Cnvtpipl on PiPL.json" step is dropped. Keys follow `pipl-schema.json` where the HTML pages disagree with it (`CodeEntryPointWin64`, `FormatMaxSize` as a 2-item array). JSON has no comments, so PiPL.json is the one plugin file without the MIT header line.
- **DC14 Open stays off until Task 7.** PiPL `CanRead` is false, so Photoshop never routes Open to the plugin before the read selectors exist. `ReadExtensions` is already listed. Superseded by DC20: Task 7 sets `CanRead` true.
- **DC15 Debug also uses /MT.** `psdds.lib` carries the encoders' vendored C++ objects, built for the release static CRT; linking them into a `/MTd` plugin fails (LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary and _ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL mismatch). The Debug configuration is unoptimised with the same `/MT` runtime.
- **DC16 Save writes through `dataFork`.** The Windows file handle Photoshop opened, written with `WriteFile`. The newer `posixFileDescriptor` is a C-runtime descriptor from Photoshop's runtime, which a static-CRT plugin cannot use.
- **DC17 Save reads the image in row bands (Task 5 review I1).** WritePrepare sets `maxData = 0` (the plugin uses its own memory, PIFormat.h `maxData`). WriteStart/Continue request bands of whole rows of at most 64 MiB each (`band_rows`, 64-bit math) and convert each band straight into its rows of the one float image, so only one band buffer exists at a time. The 16384-per-side limit is checked in WriteStart before anything is allocated.
- **DC18 Spot channels are never alpha (review M3).** The PiPL does not claim spot-channel support (`pipl-schema.json` has no `CanWriteSpotChannel` key, so the flag stays off). The write path also reads the document's `alphaChannels` list (`channelType == ctSpotColor`) and skips spot channels when choosing the alpha plane; a document whose extra channels are all spot saves opaque.
- **DC19 Save options and remembered settings (Task 6).**
  - The dialog is shown in OptionsStart (PIFormat.h: the place to "get any file options from the user"). Cancel returns `userCanceledErr` (-128); a non-zero OptionsStart result stops all later selectors, so no file is written. A dialog that cannot be created (`GetModuleHandleExW` fails, `DialogBoxParamW` returns -1 or 0) reports "the Tessalith DDS options dialog could not be shown." through `errReportString` (review M1).
  - The chosen settings reach the write selectors through PluginMain's `data` value, which Photoshop keeps for the plugin across calls (SDK Plug-in Module Interface). It points to one `Globals` (settings + the per-save image buffers), allocated on first use and kept while the plugin is loaded; the buffers are freed at the end of each write. The Globals are intentionally never freed: freeing them in WriteFinish would break the OptionsStart -> Write handoff of a later save (review M4). If the host skips OptionsStart, WriteStart loads the remembered settings (every save: the flag is cleared with the per-save buffers, final review M2).
  - The dialog keeps the user's raw picks; greyed controls show `psdds_resolve`'s effective value but keep the raw one, so Normal -> Colour restores sRGB On. The raw values are stored and passed to the write, which resolves them again. A quality index from another format is kept raw and shown (and encoded) as the format's default, as DC8 rules.
  - Storage: Descriptor Registry, persistent, key `3845e6ae-fbf3-46dc-9b93-f505f11cd107`, six integers under four-char keys. (A seventh, `disc`, came with DC36; when missing it loads as 0.) On load (validated by `psdds_resolve` with the document's has_alpha), a missing key, a value `psdds_resolve` refuses, or missing suites give `psdds_defaults(Colour)` without an error. Settings are stored on OK only.
  - The dialog's has_alpha is the write path's own `alpha_plane` on the OptionsStart record (`planes` is documented as set before OptionsStart; `transparencyPlane` and `documentInfo` are not stated, and `alpha_plane` tolerates a missing `documentInfo`).
  - The host's playInfo is honoured (review I1, PIActions.h dialogPlayEnum): with `descriptorParameters` present, the dialog shows only for `plugInDialogDisplay`. For `plugInDialogDontDisplay` and `plugInDialogSilent` (scripts, actions, batch runs with dialogs off), OptionsStart shows nothing and saves with the remembered settings. Without `descriptorParameters` (an interactive Save) the dialog always shows. Amended by DC21: not when the document carries revertInfo.
  - shortcut: the descriptor's contents are neither read nor written, so a script or action cannot carry its own settings; they always come from the remembered ones. Upgrade when recorded actions need their own settings.
- **DC20 Open (Task 7).** PiPL `CanRead` is true (supersedes DC14).
  - ReadStart takes the file size from `dataFork` (`GetFileSizeEx`) and refuses anything over `kMaxDdsFileBytes` (pixels.h: 16384² RGBA8 with a full 15-level mip chain, plus magic, header and DX10 header = 1,431,655,912 bytes) before allocating: "this file is too large to be a DDS this plugin can open." It then reads the whole file with `ReadFile`, decodes the top mip with `psdds_decode` and drops the file bytes before handing pixels over. Peak memory is about file + 2 x image (psdds holds the decoded pixels and its RGBA copy while the file bytes are alive): roughly 3.4 GB for a 16384 x 16384 RGBA8 file with mips. A decode refusal (HDR, cube map, array, truncated, unsupported) shows psdds's text, first letter lower-cased after Photoshop's "because". Out of memory on a read selector reads "there is not enough memory to open this DDS."
  - FilterFile (PIFormat.h) claims a file only when it has the DDS magic and its header (and DX10 header) describe something Open can read; anything else gets `formatCannotRead`, so Photoshop shows its own message or tries another plug-in. Declined: BC6H and float DXGI formats, legacy float FourCCs (D3DFMT 111-117), cube maps (caps2 0x200, DX10 misc 0x4) and texture arrays (DX10 array size > 1), so another installed DDS plug-in can open those (`dds_header_openable` in pixels.cpp). A file shorter than the headers is still claimed, so the reader can say why it fails. ReadStart also refuses an empty file and a zero-width or zero-height image with a clear message.
  - The document is 8-bit RGB, 72 ppi. Pixels go to the host as planar bands of whole rows (`deinterleave_rgba8_to_planes`, `band_rows` with the 64 MiB cap shared with Save, DC17); ReadPrepare sets `maxData = 0`.
  - Alpha: 4 planes when the decoded alpha has any value below 255, otherwise 3. psdds reports `has_alpha` for every BC3/BC7/RGBA8 file; a fully opaque one opens without transparency so a re-save keeps the Colour mip filter instead of the alpha rule's Box (DC12). With 4 planes, `transparencyPlane = 3` when the host passed -1 (PIFormat.h: "set to -1 by hosts that support transparency"), so the document opens as a layer with transparency; a host passing 0 gets plane 3 as an alpha channel. Threshold superseded by DC23 (alpha >= 254 is opaque).
  - shortcut: no ICC profile is attached to sRGB files and `convertMode` / `preferredColorModes` are ignored; Photoshop assigns its working space. Add a profile if colour-managed users see shifts.
- **DC21 revertInfo: a plain Save after Open reuses the remembered settings (Task 6 review M3).** PIFormat.h `revertInfo`: NULL at ReadStart means "set up a handle with what is needed to read the file without querying the user and, if possible, to write it"; non-NULL means revert, do not query; options calls must leave it able to revert. Open has no options, so the handle's presence is the information: ReadStart (after a successful decode) and every OptionsStart that does not cancel give the document a 4-byte host handle (`hostNewHdl`, else `handleProcs->newProc`; "TDDS" written when the lock procs exist). Photoshop owns and disposes of it. OptionsStart without descriptor parameters skips the dialog when `revertInfo` is set and saves with the remembered settings (Descriptor Registry, DC19); a script asking for the dialog (`plugInDialogDisplay`) still gets it. Consequences: Ctrl+S on a document opened from DDS, or already saved as DDS, shows no dialog; Save As to DDS from such a document may also skip it, depending on whether Photoshop passes the document's `revertInfo` there (owner check). The settings handle is not per-document: the remembered settings are the last ones chosen anywhere. Superseded by DC22: the skip and the handle are removed.
- **DC22 Interactive saves always show the dialog; no revertInfo (final review I1, supersedes DC21).** `ShouldShowDialog(has_descriptor, play_info)` is `!has_descriptor || play_info == plugInDialogDisplay`: Save, Save As and Ctrl+S without descriptor parameters always show the dialog, preselected with the remembered settings; only scripts, actions and batches with dialogs off skip it (DC19). DC21's skip used global settings, so Ctrl+S could silently re-save an opened BC5 normal as sRGB BC7, and if Photoshop also passes the sticky revertInfo on Save As, the dialog could never be reached again. With no skip, revertInfo has no purpose (Open has no options to remember), so the plugin no longer sets it. Cost: one dialog per Ctrl+S of a DDS.
- **DC23 Open treats alpha >= 254 as opaque (final review I2).** `opens_with_transparency` (pixels.cpp): 4 planes with transparency only when psdds reports alpha and some alpha byte is below 254; otherwise 3 planes. The engine guarantees only alpha >= 254 for opaque BC7 when `alpha.exact_opaque` is off (Notes A, C, D, Spike S5b), and Tessalith's own opaque BC7 diffuse files decode with 254 on many texels; without this they opened as transparent layers and a re-save switched to the alpha rule's Box filter (DC12). Cost: an image whose alpha uses only 254 and 255 opens opaque (one alpha step lost). Reversible. (Amended by Note DD6: the rule is `psdds_opens_with_alpha`, called by Photoshop and the other hosts.)
- **DC24 Save estimate covers every format (final review M3).** EstimateStart sets `minDataBytes` to BC1/BC4 without mips (8 bytes per 4x4 block + 128) and `maxDataBytes` to RGBA8 with a full chain + 148 (`dds_size_range`), from `imageSize32` only when the host supports 32-bit coordinates (else `imageSize`). The old single value assumed BC7 and was 4x low for RGBA8.
- **DC25 The plugin pins itself in memory (owner crash report, 2026-10-25).** Photoshop 2025 26.9.0.15 crashed after a save: BEX64, `TessalithDDS.8bi_unloaded`, 0xc0000005, offset 0x9483. With the PDB of that exact build (PE timestamp 0x6ADDC216), offset 0x9483 is the instruction after `call WaitOnAddress` in `std::sys::sync::condvar::futex::Condvar::wait`. A stack walk of the threads left after a save shows 16 rayon workers (the engine's global pool, started by `engine::memory::encode_image`) parked there via `rayon_core::registry::WorkerThread::wait_until_cold`. Photoshop unloads the plugin after the save; the workers keep sleeping in its unmapped code and crash on their next wake-up. A harness that loads the .8bi, saves, calls FreeLibrary and alerts those threads crashes with 0xc0000005 at exactly +0x9483. (Amended by Note DD3: the pin moved into psdds itself and applies to every host that loads the DLL.)
  - Fix: on the first PluginMain call, `GetModuleHandleExW(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_PIN | FROM_ADDRESS)` pins the module, so FreeLibrary never unmaps it; it stays until Photoshop exits, and a later load reuses it and its already-running pool.
  - Why pin and not shut the pool down: the global pool is a leaked static registry with no shutdown; a private `rayon::ThreadPool` drops asynchronously (its threads exit after `drop` returns, still running module code), and rayon has no synchronous join. Joining our own spawn-handler threads after every save would work but needs every engine path wrapped in `install`, and would still leave other module-lifetime state (Rust TLS destructors, the static CRT) exposed to an unload. Pinning removes the whole class with one call. Cost: the .8bi (about 4 MB of code plus idle threads) stays loaded for the session.
  - Ruled out: the dialog (DialogBoxParamW is modal and ends before OptionsStart returns; no window class is registered), other threads (psdds starts none; the engine's `thread::scope` joins), CRT atexit/TLS callbacks (they run during unload, inside mapped code, and would fault elsewhere).
  - Regression test: `photoshop/tests/unload_test.cpp`, run by `build.ps1 -Test` (which now builds the plugin first): load, save, FreeLibrary, wait 2 s; it fails if the module is unmapped while the save's threads still run.
- **DC26 PiPL claims layer support so Save As lists the format (owner request, 2026-10-25).** Owner: Tessalith DDS showed only under Save a Copy, while Intel Texture Works showed under plain Save As. The 2026 SDK does not state the rule: it only says format plug-ins "appear in the format pop-up menu in the Open, Save As and Save a Copy dialogs" (PGPlugInTypes), and documents no key for it. Evidence instead: Intel's PiPL (resource `PIPL` 16000, read as data from the owner's IntelTextureWorks.8bi) carries `fmsl` = 0x80, which PIPL.r defines as `FormatLayerSupport` with `doesSupportFormatLayers`; ours had none. Its other differences (`fmtf` 0x3E, which adds CanCreateThumbnail; `mxch` 24 for every mode against our 4; Grayscale, Multichannel and 32-bit modes) are not taken. Since Photoshop 22.4 (Adobe's release notes, not the SDK), Save As lists only formats that keep the whole document; claiming layers is the one PiPL difference that can explain Intel's listing.
  - PiPL.json sets `"FormatLayerSupport": true` (pipl-schema.json). The plugin still saves the composite from WriteStart/Continue, as before.
  - The six layer selectors (ReadLayer and WriteLayer Start/Continue/Finish, PIFormat.h 35-40) are answered with `noErr`, `data = nullptr` and an empty rect, so no layer pixels are ever requested. ReadStart sets `layerData = 0` (PIFormat.h: on read the plug-in sets it "to tell host how many layers are in the document"), so Open still gives one composite image.
  - Cost: the format now appears in Save As for layered documents too, although layers, extra alpha channels and spot channels are dropped, which Save a Copy would have warned about. README says so and keeps the Save a Copy / "Enable legacy Save As" route.
  - Unverified without Photoshop: whether 26.9 still sends the composite through WriteStart when the PiPL claims layers, and whether Open is unaffected. Owner checks these. To undo, remove the PiPL key.
  - Possible second lever if a document with two or more alpha channels still lands only in Save a Copy: `FormatMaxChannels` ("so that Photoshop can warn the user that alpha channels will be discarded"). Not changed.
- **DC27 A save that never gets its image fails and writes nothing (follow-up to DC26).** DC26's open question: if Photoshop sent a layered save only through the WriteLayer selectors, the plugin would have returned success with no bytes, leaving an empty or stale file (a Save As over an existing .dds would destroy it).
  - `write_finish` reports "Tessalith DDS could not read the image from Photoshop, so nothing was saved." (errReportString) when the save state still exists, i.e. the last band never arrived (WriteFinish is called "if and only if formatSelectorWriteStart returned without error", also after Escape). Errors from WriteContinue are reported there and not overwritten.
  - `write_layer_finish` reports the same when no WriteStart succeeded in this save. Basis: PIFormat.h `layerData` is set "prior to calling Start", so layers follow WriteStart. A `write_started` flag (last field of Globals) is set by WriteStart and cleared by OptionsStart and the new `write_prepare`. shortcut: a host that sends layers with neither OptionsStart nor WritePrepare sees the previous save's flag; add a per-save token if that order is ever seen.
  - The DDS is written in one place only, after the encode succeeded (the last WriteContinue), so nothing touches the file before the bytes exist. `SetEndOfFile` after that write drops an old tail if the host passed an existing file without truncating it.
  - The SDK does not say whether Photoshop keeps or deletes the destination when a format plugin returns an error; it only says that on WriteStart "the file to be written is open, and the file pointer is positioned at the start of the file". The plugin therefore relies on writing nothing, not on the host's clean-up.
  - Test: `photoshop/tests/host_test.cpp` (renamed from DC25's `unload_test.cpp`, which it still contains) case `save_without_image_fails`. With a 20,000-byte existing file opened without truncation: layer selectors only, and WriteStart then WriteFinish, must return the error and leave the file byte-identical; composite then layers must save a DDS with no old tail.
- **DC28 Selector trace, off by default.** With the environment variable `TESSALITH_DDS_TRACE=1` set for Photoshop, PluginMain appends two lines per call ("in" and "out") to `%TEMP%\TessalithDDS-trace.txt`: tick count, selector name and number, result, image mode, depth, planes, transparencyPlane, size, layerData, the layer fields (visible, blend, opacity, group divider and start, text, name), the requested rect and planes, and whether data, advanceState and descriptor parameters are present. The variable is read once per load. Purpose: capture the host's real selector order when an SDK reading proves wrong (DC26).
- **DC29 FormatLayerSupport reverted; DDS stays under Save a Copy (owner test, 2026-10-25; supersedes DC26 and DC27's layer part).** Superseded by DC38 (the merged composite is read through channel ports). In Photoshop 26.9, with `FormatLayerSupport`, a Save As of a 4096 x 4096 document with one non-background pixel layer ended with DC27's "could not read the image" error. File > Save a Copy, which worked before, failed the same way with and without its Layers checkbox. So claiming layers moves every save of a layered document onto the layer selectors, and the host does not deliver the merged image through WriteContinue.
  - What the SDK shows: PIFormat.h documents only `layerData` ("Set by host prior to calling Start to tell plugin how many layers are in the document. Set by the host prior to calling WriteLayerStart to tell the plugin which layer it is sending data for") and the per-layer fields (`isVisible`, `blendMode`, `opacity`, `isGroupDivider`, `layerName`). The layerformat sample writes its header in WriteStart, then one record per layer from WriteLayerStart/Continue (pulling rows with `advanceState`), and its reader skips `numLayers - 1` records after the first. Its file therefore holds exactly one record per layer: for a layered document, WriteContinue does not deliver a separate composite. No documented way to get the merged result on the layer path exists.
  - Choice: revert. On the layer path the plugin would have to composite itself (blend modes, opacity, masks, groups, adjustment layers); the coordinator ruled that out, and a single-layer-only path would break Save a Copy of every multi-layer document. Without the key, Save a Copy gets the flattened composite as before. README: Save a Copy, plus Preferences > File Handling > "Enable legacy Save As" for those who want it under Save As.
  - Removed: the PiPL key, the layer-selector handlers, `layerData = 0` on ReadStart, and `write_layer_finish` with its `write_started` flag. Kept from DC27: WriteFinish's "nothing was saved" error when the last band never arrived, the single write after the encode, and `SetEndOfFile`.
- **DC30 Error messages carry no full stop.** Photoshop shows `errReportString` as "... because <message>." and adds the full stop itself; the owner saw "nothing was saved..". `report_error` now drops any trailing full stops, so every message (the plugin's own and psdds's, which go through it via `as_reason`) ends cleanly. The source literals are unchanged.
- **DC31 Save decides alpha from the pixels; the dialog opens after the pixels are read (owner report "the mip filter is always greyed out", controller ruling 2026-10-25; supersedes DC12's and DC19's has_alpha-from-planes rule and DC19's dialog placement).** A document whose content is a normal (non-background) layer always has a transparency plane, so the planes said `has_alpha = 1` and the encoder took `AlphaPolicy::Blend` with its Box-only mips, even for a fully opaque image. (Amended by Note DD6: the save-side scan is `psdds_alpha_used`, called by every host.)
  - Rule: Open's DC23 threshold applied to the float image. Alpha is kept only when some alpha is below 254/255: an 8-bit byte below 254, or a 16-bit sample below 254/255 of 32768 (`floats_have_transparency`, limit 254/255 − 1e-6).
