Otherwise `has_alpha = 0`, and psdds removes alpha as for an RGB document. Tessalith's own opaque BC7 floor (254) therefore re-saves opaque.
  - Flow:
    - OptionsStart only loads the remembered settings and applies the playInfo rule (DC19/DC22) to set `show_dialog`.
    - WriteStart/Continue read every band into the float image, as before.
    - On the last band, the dialog opens with the pixel-derived `has_alpha`, so greying shows what the encoder will do. OK stores the settings, then the image is encoded and written. Cancel returns `userCanceledErr` before anything is written (WriteFinish then has no state and returns noErr).
    - Scripts and batches with dialogs off still skip the dialog.
  - SDK basis for UI inside the write: the PiPL key docs say formats that "show UI after the formatSelectorWriteStart entry should not allow background save". The plugin does not claim `SupportsBackgroundSave`, so UI there is allowed. On WriteStart "the file to be written is open, and the file pointer is positioned at the start of the file". The SDK does not say whether the host truncated it; the plugin writes only after the encode (DC27). Cost: the dialog appears only after Photoshop has handed over the image (a moment for 16k). Open question for the owner: whether Photoshop leaves an empty file when Cancel is pressed during a save to a new name.
  - Tests: `pixels_test` `save_alpha_rule` (8/16-bit edges). `host_test` `dialog_after_pixels` plays the dialog from a second thread: an opaque layer document has an editable filter and a Kaiser pick gives different bytes from Box; alpha 254/255 counts as opaque; real transparency greys the filter at Box; Cancel returns -128 and the existing file is unchanged.
- **DC32 Formats per texture type (owner request, controller ruling 2026-10-25; amends DC2 and DC12).** Owner: "bc4 should only be in linear masks, 5 should be in normals and masks." Colour offers BC1, BC3, BC7, RGBA8; Normal adds BC5; Linear mask offers all six (BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC7, RGBA8).
  - psdds owns the table: `settings::format_allowed`, exported as `psdds_format_allowed(texture_type, format)` (1/0; 0 for unknown values). The dialog lists only the allowed formats.
  - `psdds_resolve` replaces a format the type does not offer with the type's default format (`psdds_defaults`, BC7 for all three) and returns 0, as DC8 does for quality. A remembered or scripted Colour + BC4 therefore saves as BC7, and `psdds_encode` follows (it encodes the resolved settings). The quality index is then checked against the effective format's list: an index in range is kept (as DC8 keeps any in-range index), otherwise the preset's.
  - Out-of-range format, texture type, sRGB, filter or mips still return -1.
  - With mips 0, `psdds_resolve` greys the filter too (`filter_enabled = 0`, value kept): without mips it does nothing (the Mipmaps checkbox, DC33). The rule lives in psdds with the other greying rules. Test: `filter_greys_without_mips`.
  - DC2's Colour + BC4/BC5 sRGB rule can no longer occur; BC4/BC5 still have no sRGB form, and for Normal and Linear mask sRGB is always Off.
  - Tests: `crates/psdds/tests/settings.rs` `formats_allowed_per_type`, `disallowed_format_falls_back_to_the_default`; the BC4/BC5 encode tests now use Linear mask.
- **DC33 Save dialog layout: checkboxes for sRGB and Mipmaps (owner request, controller ruling 2026-10-25; amends DC19's dialog description).** Owner: "Make SRGB a checkbox next to type. Mipmaps should be a checkbox and filter should be beside it."
  - Fixed layout, no moving controls (`photoshop/src/dialog.rc`; amended by DC37, which adds a Preset row first and a Discard transparency row, and moves initial focus to Preset): row 1 "Texture type" [list] then the checkbox "sRGB"; row 2 "Format" [list]; row 3 the checkbox "Mipmaps" then "Filter" [list]; row 4 "Quality" [list]; OK / Cancel. The sRGB and Mipmaps lists (On/Off, Full chain/None) are gone.
  - Tab order is the resource order, which is the visual order: Texture type, sRGB, Format, Mipmaps, Filter, Quality, OK, Cancel. Each list's label is the static right before it (screen-reader name and mnemonic: T, F, i, Q); a checkbox's text is its own label (s, M). Initial focus: Texture type.
  - The sRGB checkbox shows `psdds_resolve`'s effective sRGB (unticked when greyed) and is greyed where it reports sRGB not editable. The Filter list is greyed with Mipmaps unticked, a rule in psdds (DC32), or by DC12's Box fallback.
  - The Format list holds only `psdds_format_allowed` formats for the shown type; it is rebuilt when the type changes and keeps the selection while still allowed, else shows the type's default (BC7). The Quality list is rebuilt when the shown format may have changed.
  - Raw picks (DC19) still apply to the format: after Normal + BC5 -> Colour the list shows BC7, but the raw pick stays BC5 unless the user picks a format, so switching back to Normal shows BC5 again. OK stores the raw values; a stored Colour + BC5 resolves to BC7 on load and on encode (DC32), so remembered settings and scripts keep working.
  - Tests: `dialog_test` `dialog_controls_follow_type_and_mips` (format list per type, sRGB checkbox state, filter with Mipmaps on/off); `host_test` `dialog_after_pixels` now also clicks the Mipmaps checkbox in the real dialog (BM_CLICK), checks the filter greys, the Colour list has four formats and the saved DDS has one level.
- **DC34 sRGB is off by default for every type (owner decision 2026-10-25; amends DC2's and DC9's defaults).** `psdds_defaults` returns `srgb = 0` for Colour too (was 1). Owner's reason: Skyrim's non-PBR diffuse textures are UNORM, and the engine flags sRGB on non-PBR diffuse as `TAG-SRGB-NONPBR`. Presets never turn sRGB on (DC35).
  - Consequence under DC9 (not changed here): the checkbox sets content and tag together, so a default Colour save is now *linear content*, UNORM, and DC12 then mips it with Box and greys the filter — the "filter always greyed" look the owner reported before DC31, now for the default rather than for alpha. The engine's own cs-quality Diffuse is sRGB content with a UNORM tag, which is what the owner's reason describes. Recommended follow-up ruling: make the checkbox set only the tag (content stays the type's preset, sRGB for Colour), which would keep gamma-correct mips and an editable filter with sRGB off. Not done: DC9 is a recorded ruling.
  - Tests: `defaults_follow_the_preset` (srgb 0 for all types); `host_test` `dialog_after_pixels` now checks that the default dialog greys the filter and that ticking sRGB frees it.
- **DC35 Seed presets (owner decision 2026-10-25).** psdds holds the five presets that seed a new preset store (`settings::seed_presets`; C ABI `psdds_preset_count`, `psdds_preset_name`, `psdds_preset_settings`): "Colour BC7" (Colour, BC7), "Colour BC1 (small, opaque)" (Colour, BC1, discard transparency on), "Normal BC7" (Normal, BC7), "Mask/data BC7" (Linear mask, BC7), "Greyscale mask BC4" (Linear mask, BC4). All: sRGB off, mipmaps on, the type's default filter, the format's preset quality (the `cs-quality` value, as DC8's fallback), discard transparency off except the BC1 one. The proposal's "Colour + alpha BC3" and "Normal BC5" are dropped. Each seed is a fixed point of `psdds_resolve` (with or without document alpha), so the dialog can show it as matched. Test: `seed_presets_are_pinned`.
- **DC36 Discard transparency (owner decision 2026-10-25; amends DC3 and DC31's alpha rule).** `PsddsSettings` gains a 7th field, `discard_alpha` (0/1; 2+ is refused by `psdds_resolve` like the other fields). With 1, the profile's alpha policy is `Remove` whatever the pixels, so the DDS is opaque. The rule lives only in `build` (the profile builder); DC12's filter probe goes through `build`, so the filter is no longer greyed because of alpha. With 0, DC31's alpha-from-pixels rule applies as before. Tests: `discard_transparency_removes_alpha` (settings), `discard_transparency_saves_opaque` (encode: identical to the opaque pixels' file, different from the alpha-kept one).
  - Remembered settings: a seventh registry key, `disc`, stores it (amends DC19). A stored descriptor without `disc` (saved before DC36) loads with `discard_alpha = 0` instead of falling back to the defaults, so upgrading keeps the user's settings; the six older keys are still required.
  - Dialog: the checkbox "Discard transparency" sits on its own row under Format (DC37 layout). It is always enabled, also where it changes nothing (a document without alpha, or BC1/BC4/BC5, which drop alpha anyway); no ruling greys it.
- **DC37 Presets in the Save dialog (owner decisions 2026-10-25, with the owner's simplification: no protected built-ins).**
  - Row 0 of the dialog: "Preset" [list] then the buttons "Save preset..." and "Delete". The list holds "Custom" first, then the stored presets in file order. Layout, top to bottom: Preset row; Texture type + sRGB; Format; Discard transparency; Mipmaps + Filter; Quality; OK / Cancel. Tab order is that order (mnemonics P, v, D, T, s, F, r, M, i, Q); initial focus is the Preset list. The dialog is 250 x 136 dialog units.
  - Picking a preset sets all seven raw values, and the dialog then shows what `psdds_resolve` makes of them. Matching rule: the list shows the first preset whose *effective* values (`psdds_resolve` with the document's has_alpha) equal those of the current raw values, else "Custom". So editing a control shows Custom, editing it back shows the preset again, remembered settings reopen on their matching preset, and a difference only in a greyed control (e.g. Normal with a remembered sRGB On) still matches. Picking "Custom" changes nothing.
  - Store: one UTF-8 file, `%APPDATA%\Tessalith DDS\presets\presets.txt`: a header line without tabs, then one preset per line, the name and the seven `PsddsSettings` values separated by tabs. Why a file and not the Descriptor Registry: a list of named presets needs the ActionList suite (lists of descriptors and strings) on top of the descriptor suite the remembered settings use. That means more host surface to fake in every harness, while a file is plain Win32 that the console tests can exercise in a temp folder. Intel Texture Works also keeps presets as files. One file instead of one file per preset, so names need no filename sanitising (`a/b:c?` is a valid preset name).
  - Seeding: when the file does not exist, it is created with psdds's five seed presets (DC35). From then on they are ordinary presets: they can be replaced and deleted. An existing empty file means no presets, and the list shows only Custom. A file that exists but cannot be opened gives an empty list and is never overwritten by the seeding.
  - Writing: the whole list goes to `presets.txt.tmp`, then `FlushFileBuffers`, then `MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING | WRITE_THROUGH)` (the C++ counterpart of `write_atomic`). A failed write leaves the old file and shows "The preset could not be saved." Save and Delete write immediately, even if the dialog is then cancelled.
  - Loading: the file is capped at 1 MiB. Lines with the wrong number of fields (the header has none of the tabs, so it fails here; a name may start with `#`), hold a non-decimal value, have an invalid name, or that `psdds_resolve` refuses (has_alpha 0) are skipped. Values are kept raw, like the remembered settings. shortcut: skipped lines are lost at the next Save or Delete. Upgrade to keeping unknown lines if the file ever gains other content.
  - Names: trimmed of white space, then 1 to 64 characters (UTF-16 units), with no control characters (tab, line break). Unique ignoring case (`CompareStringOrdinal`, ignore case). Saving an existing name asks "A preset named "X" already exists. Replace it?" (default No); Yes replaces it in place. The name prompt is prefilled with the matching preset's name. Delete removes the preset currently shown (greyed on Custom) after "Delete the preset "X"?" (default No). The preset stores the raw values.
  - Test isolation: the environment variable `TESSALITH_DDS_PRESETS_DIR` replaces the folder (precedent DC28). `host_test` sets it to a temp folder before loading the plugin, so no test touches the user's `%APPDATA%`.
  - Tests: `dialog_test` `presets_store_round_trip` (seed on an absent file, round trip of all seven values and a UTF-8 name, empty store stays empty, corrupt lines skipped) and `preset_names_and_matching` (name rules, case-insensitive find, preset -> edit -> Custom -> edit back, discard as part of a preset, effective-value matching, empty store). `host_test` `dialog_after_pixels` sees "Colour BC7" at start and "Custom" after ticking sRGB in the real dialog; the run checks the store was seeded in the temp folder. Not tested automatically: the Save preset and Delete buttons (the name prompt and message boxes).
- **DC38 Save As lists Tessalith DDS; a layered save reads Photoshop's merged composite through channel ports (owner probe 2026-10-25; supersedes DC29's revert and restores DC26's PiPL key).** Scope: `F:\ai\dds\photoshop-plugin\2026-10-25-layer-merge-scope.md` (Route A); probe branch `probe/layer-merge` d8d38e55, kept as a record.
  - Probe evidence (Photoshop 26.9, 16-bit RGB 4096 x 4096, layered documents): with `FormatLayerSupport` the format is listed under plain File > Save As. Every layered save had `layerData` = layer count on OptionsStart and WriteStart, a non-null `documentInfo` (version 0..6, mode RGB48, depth 16, layers 5), `channelPortProcs` version 1 with `readPixelsProc`, and merged Red/Green/Blue `ReadChannelDesc`s at depth 16 with the document's bounds (tiles 728 x 722); 4 x 4 test reads succeeded. `mergedTransparency` was null (those documents had a Background layer). Host order: OptionsStart, WriteStart, one WriteLayerStart ("Background"), WriteFinish. Merged and target reads use the same scale (an opaque white target layer read 32768; a single-layer document's merged and target samples were equal), so 16-bit ports are 0..32768 like the FormatRecord bands. A second build adding `FormatLayerSupportReadOnly` (`slRO`) kept the band path but was **not** listed under Save As, so it was dropped.
  - SDK basis: PIFormat.h `documentInfo` "The document info for the document being written", `channelPortProcs` "Suite for passing pixels through channel ports"; PIGeneral.h `mergedCompositeChannels` / `mergedTransparency`, `ReadPixelsProc` (equal source and destination rectangles: unscaled), `PixelMemoryDesc` `colBits` (each channel is read straight into its slot of the interleaved band).
  - PiPL.json: `"FormatLayerSupport": true`. ReadStart sets `layerData = 0`, so Open still gives one composite; the six layer selectors answer noErr with no pixels.
  - Save with `layerData > 0` (Save As and Save a Copy, Layers on or off): WriteStart reads the merged composite in bands of up to 64 MiB through `readPixelsProc` at the document depth, converts with the band path's `to_rgba_floats` (8-bit /255, 16-bit /32768), then runs the last-band step unchanged (alpha from the pixels DC31, Discard transparency DC36, the dialog after the pixels, encode, one write, `SetEndOfFile`) and leaves `theRect32` empty, so the host sends no WriteContinue. Alpha source, the same policy as the band path: `mergedTransparency`, else the first non-spot entry of `alphaChannels`, else none. Cancel and every error return from WriteStart, which frees the save state itself (WriteFinish follows only a successful WriteStart).
  - `layerData == 0`: the band path as before.
  - Refused with DC27's "could not read the image from Photoshop, so nothing was saved", file untouched: no `documentInfo`, no channel ports, fewer than three merged colour channels, a channel without a port or with another depth or size than the image, a failed or short read. A fault inside the host's read is caught (SEH) and fails the save. The trace (DC28) names the reason and, on WriteStart, describes `documentInfo` and the merged, merged-transparency and alpha channels.
  - Memory: unchanged; the float image (4 GiB at 16384²) dominates and the band buffer is reused for the port reads.
  - Tests: `host_test` `merged_composite_save`: 8-bit merged save with no bands asked; 16-bit 0/32768 checks give the same DDS as 8-bit 0/255 checks (pins 32768 = white); 16-bit merged equals the 16-bit band path on the same samples; an alpha channel listed after a spot channel gives the same DDS as merged transparency and differs from opaque; a failed read, no `documentInfo`, a depth mismatch and a missing merged channel each return the error with a 20,000-byte existing file unchanged.
- **DC39 The sRGB checkbox sets only the DDS tag (owner ruling 2026-10-25; supersedes DC9).** On -> `color.tag = srgb`, Off -> `unorm`; `color.content` stays the type's `cs-quality` base profile's: Colour keeps the Diffuse profile's sRGB content (mips filtered gamma-correctly), Normal and Linear mask stay linear. A sub-type whose tag is `n/a` still keeps both fields.
  - Consequence: Colour + sRGB Off + opaque is no longer "linear content", so DC12's probe no longer greys the filter there; it greys only where the engine mips with Box anyway (alpha kept: Blend, alpha-weighted), and Normal and Linear mask keep their greyed preset filter. Kaiser is honoured with sRGB Off, and sRGB On and Off give the same mips, differing only in the DXGI format (BC7 98 vs 99).
  - Tests: psdds `settings.rs` `colour_keeps_srgb_and_filter_editable` (Off: filter editable, content sRGB, tag UNORM), `filter_greys_where_the_engine_uses_box` (greyed only for kept alpha; Kaiser for opaque sRGB Off in BC7, BC1, RGBA8); `encode.rs` `kaiser_applies_only_where_the_dialog_shows_it` (Kaiser changes the sRGB Off mips) and `srgb_sets_only_the_tag` (On and Off: the same blocks after the 148-byte header, DXGI 99 vs 98); host_test `dialog_after_pixels` (the filter is editable before sRGB is ticked). Both new psdds expectations failed before the change.
- **DC40 Review fixes for Route A and presets (2026-10-25).**
  - Layered save with no alpha source: not refused. Real traces (4096x4096, 16-bit, 5 to 10 layers, always a Background layer) show `mergedTransparency` null, `transparencyPlane` 0 and `alphas` 0 even for layered documents, so none of those fields can tell "no Background layer" from "Background present"; every probed document had a Background. `ReadLayerDesc::transparency` (null for a Background layer) is the one candidate but is unobserved. So the save keeps writing an opaque DDS; WriteStart traces "layered save without an alpha source" with transparencyPlane, layers and alphas, and the `doc` trace line now lists the first 8 layers (`layerlist {"name" T0/T1}`). Upgrade to a refusal once a trace of an erased, Background-less document shows a reliable field. Owner step: save such a document and check the transparent area.
  - A preset file that is not read in full (open fails other than not-found, over 1 MiB, short read) is never written: `LoadPresets` reports it (`PresetFileInfo::complete`), Save preset and Delete show "The preset file could not be read, so presets can't be changed". A missing file counts as complete (seeds). Lines that do not parse (typo, invalid UTF-8, future fields, comments) are kept verbatim and written back after the parsed presets.
  - The dialog remembers the picked preset and keeps showing it while its effective settings match; Delete and Save use it; an edit falls back to the first match. Discard transparency is ignored in the match when the document has no alpha.
  - WriteStart's early refusals reset the per-save flags (`have_settings`, `show_dialog`) like every other end of a save. CleanPresetName's NBSP and U+3000 are written as escapes (no dependence on the compiler code page). `make_dirs` skips the `\\server\share` prefix so a UNC %APPDATA% works.
  - Tests: `dialog_test` `presets_file_is_protected` (locked and oversized files incomplete, bad lines survive a save), `preset_names_and_matching` (picked twin, discard without alpha, escapes). Not tested: the dialog's Save/Delete message and the WriteStart flag reset (no harness reaches them), UNC creation.
- **DC41 MPL-2.0 for engine and encoders-sys (owner, 2026-10-25).** An earlier draft of DC1 offered the two crates under a GPL-or-MIT dual licence. Adobe's SDK licence (section 12) bars software licensed under the GNU GPL by name, and anything that could force disclosure of other software, so a dual licence that includes the GPL was judged a risk. The owner (sole copyright holder) chose plain `MPL-2.0` instead: file-level copyleft, no Exhibit B, no GPL in the expression. The branch was never pushed, so its history was rewritten before the first push and no commit grants MIT on the two crates. Each crate carries the MPL-2.0 text as `LICENSE`; `photoshop/about.toml` accepts `MPL-2.0`. MPL section 3.2 requires telling the binary's recipients where the source is: the release zip's `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names the public repository and the commit the plugin was built from, and `photoshop/README.md` names the repository. Push the release commit before publishing the zip, or that pointer leads nowhere.
- **DC42 Alpha source: the first alpha channel wins (owner ruling 2026-10-25; supersedes the alpha-source order of the spec's "Save dialog" rule, DC12 and DC38).** Owner bug: a layered document with no Background layer and its transparency painted in "Alpha 1" saved with the layers' transparency, so Alpha 1 was ignored; with a Background layer Alpha 1 worked. The order was merged/layer transparency first, then the first non-spot alpha channel. The order is now the same in the band path (`alpha_plane`) and the merged path (`merged_source`, DC38): the first non-spot alpha channel if the document has one; else the transparency plane (band path) or merged transparency (merged path); else none. Spot channels never count (DC31's rule stays). In the band path the transparency plane, when present, sits before the channels, so the channel planes start after it. DC36 stays on top: Discard transparency overrides everything. DC31 stays: has_alpha is still decided from the pixels (any byte below 254) of whichever source was picked, so an opaque alpha channel saves an opaque texture even over transparent layers. Tests: host_test `merged_composite_save` (layered doc with both sources: the channel's values are in the DDS) and `band_alpha_plane` (planeMap picks the channel plane). Both failed before the change.
- **DC43 Save dialog: Discard transparency moves under sRGB (owner request 2026-10-25; amends DC33 and DC36's placement).** The checkbox sits in the right column on the Format row, directly under sRGB; the Texture type and Format combos share one width (85 dialog units) so the column is wide enough for the label; the row the checkbox used to occupy is gone (the dialog is 18 units shorter) and every other control keeps its order and alignment. host_test checks the widths, the column and that the label fits.
- **DC44 PiPL allows 24 channels in RGB modes, so Save As lists documents with alpha channels (owner report 2026-10-25; follows DC26's second lever).** Owner: after DC42 the alpha channel saves correctly, but Tessalith DDS no longer shows in plain Save As for that document. `FormatMaxChannels` was 4 for RGB and RGB48, and a document with Alpha 1 has more channels than that, so Photoshop's Save As (which lists only formats that keep the whole document) leaves the format out. Intel Texture Works declares 24 for every mode (DC26), and it is listed. Both RGB entries are now 24, and the other modes stay 0 (EnableInfo limits the modes). Cost: Save As no longer warns that alpha channels after the first are dropped; the first one is the DDS alpha (DC42). To undo, set the entries back to 4.
- **DC45 Picking Custom stays on Custom (owner report 2026-10-25; amends DC37 and DC40).** Owner: choosing Custom in the preset list while the settings still match a preset snapped straight back to that preset, which looks like a glitch. The dialog now keeps a `custom` flag: picking Custom keeps the settings and shows Custom (Delete greyed, Save preset proposes no name) until another preset is picked or a preset is saved. Edits made while Custom is shown stay Custom, even if they land on a preset's values. The next time the dialog opens, matching works as before (DC37). Test: host_test `dialog_after_pixels` picks Custom over Colour BC7.

## Note DD — Shared psdds.dll for host plugins (owner, 2026-10-25)

The letter DD is provisional: main ends at DC, and this note is renamed at merge if DD is taken. The owner approved the controller's recommendations on 2026-10-25. Branch `feat/psdds-dll`, first cut from the Photoshop branch at DC37 and rebased onto main e5d812e4 (DC1-DC45) after that branch was rewritten and merged; DC39 (sRGB sets only the tag) and DC41 (engine and encoders-sys under MPL-2.0) apply to everything below. The same `crates/psdds` that Photoshop links statically is now also a DLL for other hosts (Paint.NET, GIMP, chaiNNer). Their plans start from the tip of this branch. Rulings S10, S11, M1-M12 and D1-D6 are the controller's, made at pre-flight and per task; each states its cost.

- **DD1 A cdylib beside the staticlib.** `crates/psdds` builds as `staticlib`, `cdylib` and `rlib`. `crates\psdds\build.ps1` builds it with a static CRT into `target\psdds` (kept out of the gates' target), at `target\psdds\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\release\psdds.dll`, the folder Photoshop's build already used. `psdds.lib` stays the static library Photoshop links; MSVC names the DLL's import library `psdds.dll.lib`. The script checks `dumpbin /dependents` (no `VCRUNTIME`, `MSVCP` or `api-ms-win-crt`) and `dumpbin /exports` (must equal the `psdds_\w+(` declarations in `psdds.h`, so export drift fails the build). `-Test` also runs `examples/dll_host.rs`, which loads the built DLL by path. Cost: one release build serves all hosts, so a host cannot use a different feature set.
- **DD2 ABI version 2, exact match.** `PSDDS_ABI_VERSION` is 2 and `psdds_abi_version()` returns it; `psdds_version()` returns the workspace (engine) version as static UTF-8. A host refuses a DLL whose version is not exactly its own. The header's bump rule: any change to its declarations or documented behaviour. 2 is the header with the 7-field `PsddsSettings` (DC36), the `psdds_preset_*` exports (DC35) and `psdds_resolve`'s DC39 behaviour (sRGB sets only the tag, so an opaque Colour save keeps an editable filter), plus this branch's additions; 1 was the 6-field struct and never shipped (S10; cost if wrong: a renumber). DC39 changed documented behaviour after S10 set the baseline, but no build exposing the earlier behaviour has shipped, so 2 is kept. Each host ships its own copy of the DLL, so exact match costs nothing. No Windows version resource, no cancel hook and no BGRA8 entry point (R18; DC7 stands until the Paint.NET plan measures a problem). Export count: 11 from the Photoshop plugin plus 9 new = 20. (Amended by DF2: ABI 3.)
- **DD3 The DLL pins itself (DC25 for any host).** DC25 was a Photoshop-only fix (the plugin pinned itself). It moves into psdds: `pin_self()` runs once (`std::sync::Once`) at the start of `psdds_encode`, `psdds_decode` and `psdds_rmaos_encode`, calling `GetModuleHandleExW(PIN | FROM_ADDRESS, pin_self)` through a hand-declared kernel32 extern (no new crate, `--offline`). Nothing runs in `DllMain`. The rayon workers the engine starts therefore never outlive their code, whichever host unloads the DLL. In the staticlib build it pins the `.8bi`, which Photoshop already pins; pinning twice is harmless. `dll_host` fails if the DLL is unmapped after `FreeLibrary` (RED on the unpinned build, GREEN with it). Cost: the DLL stays mapped for the life of the process.
- **DD4 Thread safety is a stated guarantee.** Every export may be called from any thread, concurrently. The only shared state is `OnceLock`/`once_flag` initialisation. `tests/concurrency.rs` is its own test binary and races the first calls cold (four encodes and a pair on separate threads), comparing each result with a serial run.
- **DD5 One clamp rule, in psdds.** `clamp01` (NaN to 0, -inf to 0, +inf to 1, else clamp to [0,1]) is applied by `psdds_encode` in its existing copy and by `psdds_rmaos_encode` to every source and the normal. The engine does not clamp: `pack_rmaos` briefly did (Task 5) but the file path never does, so it was removed in Task 6 to keep the packing rule single (M8; this supersedes R6's sentence that the engine clamps). In-range input is unchanged, so Photoshop's bytes cannot change. Pinned by `tests/clamp.rs` (RED before: the engine does not clamp level 0 or the mips averaging). (Amended by DF3: for a 32-bit Colour document, `psdds_encode_depth` keeps RGB above 1.0 only for BC6H and RGBA16F (the engine's float path handles NaN, negatives and the half range) and clips it to 0..1 for the 8-bit formats (DF3). Depth 8 and 16 and every old export still clamp, so their bytes are unchanged.)
- **DD6 The host helpers are the one copy of the host-side rules.** `psdds_check_size(w, h, err, cap)` is the size rule (DC12 text for a side over 16384; a zero side says "This image is empty"); `psdds_encode`, `psdds_decode` and `psdds_rmaos_encode` call it and return its text unchanged (M3). `psdds_dds_openable` is the openable rule ported from `pixels.cpp` with its test cases. It and `psdds_decode` refuse a `len` over `isize::MAX` (0, or an error) before building a slice, like the alpha helpers, so a caller's bad length cannot abort the host (final review 10). `psdds_opens_with_alpha` is DC23 (open: alpha byte below 254), `psdds_alpha_used` is DC31 (save: some alpha below 254/255, limit `254/255 - 1e-6`; the result goes to `psdds_encode`'s `has_alpha` and to `psdds_resolve`), and `psdds_max_file_bytes` is the bound a host applies before reading a file (16384^2 RGBA8 with the full chain, plus magic and headers; `psdds_decode` does not check it). Photoshop's `pixels.cpp` functions are one-line calls into them and `pixels_test` links `psdds.lib`; every other host takes its has_alpha from the same calls, so a Tessalith BC7 with alpha 254 opens opaque and re-saves opaque everywhere. `psdds_max_side` was declined (R1): the refusal wording is a rule too. Cost: Photoshop's `kMaxDdsFileBytes` stays a compile-time constant and a Rust test pins the same number; `decode` calls `check_size` only for headers with both sides non-zero, and keeps `read_dds`'s own error for empty or truncated headers; the one side over 16384 and the other 0 case gives that read error instead of the size text. DC12's size text and DC23/DC31's thresholds are unchanged: this note moves their implementation, not their wording. (Amended by DF4: `psdds_dds_openable_float` is the sibling rule that also claims the float formats `psdds_decode_depth` opens; `psdds_dds_openable` is unchanged.)
- **DD7 One packing rule and one bake rule, from memory.** `engine::memory::pack_rmaos` packs channels from in-memory images through `assemble_channels_with(size, load)`; the file-backed `assemble_channels` is the same path and keeps its second "file replaced since check" mismatch check and one-source-at-a-time decoding (R10, D3: it calls the existing `check_sizes`). The bake rule is extracted, not copied (R11): `bake::plan::decide_bake` (the sRGB, opt-out and `bake_shift` rules, returning Bake, Never or Off with the SET-BAKE-RATIO warning) is called by `attach` (with `bake_set`'s R6 opt-out flag) and the memory path; `bake::lengths_from` is `load_lengths` minus the load (D5: a free function over the fields it uses); `memory::encode_image_with(img, profile, bake)` is `encode_image` with the bake. `encode_rmaos_set` validates the source set before encoding the `_n`. `RmaosSet.baked` is true only when the engine's bake actually ran, and `RmaosSet.bake_note` says why not (no `_n`, an sRGB `_rmaos` never bakes, a size that cannot bake) (M5). **`mips = 0` follows the batch** (M5 amended after the Task 6 finding): with a larger `_n` the engine chain bakes mip 0 when the shift is 1 or more, exactly as a batch with `mips.levels = none`; at shift 0 the bytes are equal either way. Proof is `tests/memory_rmaos.rs`, which plans a temp folder with the real `Engine::plan` and `Engine::run` and compares profiles and bytes (M7). Fixture names that plan as a TruePBR pair: `iron_n`, `iron_roughness`, `iron_ao` with suggestions accepted at High. The new engine code is under the crate's licence, `MPL-2.0` (DC1, DC41); psdds stays MIT.
- **DD8 `psdds_rmaos_encode` (R9, R12, R19).** Replaces chaiNNer's draft pack entry. Inputs: a `PsddsRmaosJob` with four `PsddsSource` (one channel of a 1-4 channel interleaved float image; NULL `px` means no source, and roles may share an image with different channels), per-role `fill` (-1 unset, 0..255, anything else an error), `quality` (a BC7 effort index; out of range means the profile's), `mips` (0 top level only, 1 the rmaos profile's chain; 2 and above is refused with "mips <v> out of range 0..2"), and an optional `normal` with its `PsddsSettings`. Output: the `_rmaos` and, when a normal is given, the `_n` encoded with the **`pbr_normal`** profile and the dialog's Normal settings (format, sRGB, filter, mips, quality), not `psdds_encode`'s Normal; `defaulted` has bit `1<<c` for each channel that took a neutral default; `baked` and `note` report the bake. On any error both buffers are empty and the reason is in `err`. Size check runs before packing and uses `check_size` (M4: a non-NULL oversize source gets that text). Roles that point at the same image (same pointer, width, height and channel count) share one clamped copy; a test shows two views of one buffer with different channel counts are not merged. **`normal_settings.discard_alpha` is validated (0 or 1, 2 is refused by resolve) and ignored (S11, R19):** the `_n` is built without alpha and the `_rmaos` alpha is the specular data channel, which DC36 (an image-alpha rule) does not touch. Cost if wrong: one added branch later. Other DC34-DC37 points as they reach the DLL: the 7-field struct is the same one `psdds_resolve` uses; no test assumes sRGB-on defaults (a test that needs sRGB sets `srgb = 1`); the five seed presets are exported by the existing `psdds_preset_*`; there is no preset store in the DLL (DC37 stays the Photoshop host's file; other hosts choose their own). Tests: `tests/rmaos.rs` (layout sizes and offsets per D4, the cases in the plan, and `a_pair_equals_the_batch`, which breaks if `PbrNormal` is swapped for `Normal`).
- **DD9 The `_rmaos` alpha step is a shortcut.** The batch planner turns the specular channel's alpha to `remove` when the analysis says it is constant 255 (High-confidence suggestion), which fires whenever specular took its neutral default. The profile bytes are the same either way for a constant alpha, but to match the batch profile exactly `encode_rmaos_set` runs the planner's own `analyse` and `suggest_alpha` on the packed image and encodes with that profile; the returned `RmaosSet` carries the profiles used. It is applied unconditionally, marked `shortcut:` in `memory.rs`. Cost: a caller that sets an alpha policy on purpose is overridden; psdds passes builtin profiles only, so it is fine today. Upgrade by adding the planner's explicit-layer test before the step.
- **DD10 Error text (R15; DC30 stands).** No literals changed. Every message is one plain sentence and may end with one full stop; psdds passes engine text through unchanged; a host that adds punctuation trims trailing full stops (Photoshop does) and never re-words. Panics read "internal error: ...". New psdds texts carry no full stop.
- **DD11 Notices (R16, M10).** `crates\psdds\notices.ps1 -Binary <name> -Product <name> -Out <file>` runs the cargo-about check (`--fail`) and writes third-party notices for any psdds binary. `about.toml` and `about.hbs` moved from `photoshop/` to `crates/psdds/`; the template has a `{{binary}}` placeholder the script fills (cargo-about has no custom variables). `photoshop/package.ps1` calls the script. Acceptance: the `.8bi` notices differ from the old block by the one config-path line. After the rebase onto main, `about.toml` accepts `MPL-2.0` and the script carries DC41's sentence (MIT except the MPL-2.0 engine, the repository URL and the `git rev-parse HEAD` commit, which it refuses to omit) for every binary, with `$Product`/`$Binary` substituted; the template heading names `{{binary}}` instead of the Photoshop plugin. The script needs `cargo-about` on PATH.
- **DD12 Parked, with costs.**
  - `photoshop/src/write.cpp` keeps its own empty and 16384 check (a second `16384` literal in the Photoshop host only): it is the Photoshop session's active write path and needs host wording.
  - `check_sources` runs twice in `encode_rmaos_set` (a small repeated scan).
  - `psdds_rmaos_encode` copies each distinct clamped image in full (4 GiB at 16384x16384 with 4 channels): a memory cost on huge 4-channel sources.
  - `psdds_decode` has no closeness check against `psdds_dds_openable`; `dll_host` module naming and the test env save/restore are duplicated (no functional cost).
  - `dll_host` is `#![cfg(windows)]`, so `cargo build --examples` has no `main` off Windows.
  - The opt-out of the `_n` is tested at `decide_bake` only, because memory has no provenance (`encode_rmaos_set` always passes `false`).
  - The `psdds.h` comment additions (clamp, thread safety, process exit) are behaviour text under ABI 2, not a bump, by the 2 baseline above.
  - Size errors from `psdds_rmaos_encode` (a 0x0 or oversize source or normal) are `psdds_check_size`'s text unchanged and do not name the role, while the channel and fill errors do (M3). Cost: a host log does not say which input was wrong.
  - The batch opt-out now reads image headers: an opted-out set used to return before `attach`; now `attach` runs `post_resize_dims` for the `_n` and every member, then gets `Never`. Outputs, warnings and provenance are unchanged. Cost: extra header I/O for opted-out sets.

## Note DE — chaiNNer nodes (owner, 2026-10-25)

The letter DE is provisional: main ends at DD, and this note is renamed at merge if DE is taken. The owner said "go with your recommendations" on 2026-10-25 and approved decisions 11-13 by name. Branch `feat/chainner-dds`, files in `chainner/`. Three nodes in chaiNNer's Image category, group "Tessalith DDS", on top of the shared `psdds.dll` (Note DD). The nodes add no rule: the Python adapts chaiNNer's images and asks psdds for every setting, list and visibility answer. DC31, DC32, DC33, DC34, DC36, DC39 and DC45 below are the Photoshop rulings as they apply here; the rest of Note DC is not repeated.

- **DE1 Distribution.** A drop-in folder `tessalith_dds` inside `packages/chaiNNer_standard`, because chaiNNer imports every `.py` under that package and imports nothing from a package it was not told about. `chainner\install.ps1` copies the nodes, `psdds.dll` and the notices there. It builds the folder beside the target and swaps it in, and checks the staged DLL (psdds version and ABI, through chaiNNer's own Python) before the swap, so a failed copy or a wrong DLL leaves the old install in place. It refuses while chaiNNer is running. **Re-run it after every chaiNNer update:** an update installs a new `app-<version>` folder and deletes the old one with the nodes in it. Cost: chaiNNer has no setting for another node folder, so there is no way around the re-run. An upstream pull request stays a later option.
- **DE2 Node set.** Save DDS (Tessalith), RMAOS (Tessalith), Save Normal (Tessalith). A wrong or missing DLL, or an ABI other than 2, raises at import, so only our nodes go missing and chaiNNer's other nodes still load. The naming rule and `CHECK_LEVEL=error` load pass.
- **DE3 Load DDS is not in v1.** The owner's recommendation was to build it only if wanted. chaiNNer's Load Image already reads DDS through texconv; what is lost is DC23's rule (alpha 254 and above opens opaque). The owner can ask for it later; psdds already has the entry points.
- **DE4 One writer for RMAOS and Save Normal.** RMAOS has no side effects and one output of its own type, `TessalithRmaos`; it writes nothing. Save Normal is the only node that writes `_n` and `_rmaos`. With RMAOS connected, one `psdds_rmaos_encode` makes both buffers (the `_n` with the `pbr_normal` profile, baked when the engine's size rule allows, as in a batch), and both are written after both exist. A lone Save Normal writes `_n` with `psdds_encode` Normal, the same bytes as Save DDS with type Normal. A lone RMAOS is removed by chaiNNer as a dead node and writes nothing. Reason: the other direction (Save Normal into RMAOS) makes two side-effect nodes, so the `_n` would be written twice, with and without the bake. `_rmaos` without a `_n` is not offered (decision 13).
- **DE5 Pair skip-existing.** Skip only when both `_n` and `_rmaos` exist; otherwise write both, so the pair stays consistent (decision 12). A lone Save Normal skips on its own file.
- **DE6 Save Normal inputs that apply to the pair.** Format, Mipmaps and Quality change the pair's `_n`, so they stay. Discard transparency does not (the pair's `_n` has no alpha, Owner decision 15), so only it is hidden while RMAOS is connected. Hidden is the only state chaiNNer has; nothing is greyed.
- **DE7 Channel mapping.** chaiNNer images are BGR or BGRA, so the R/G/B/A dropdown maps R=2, G=1, B=0, A=3. A grey image, and an HxWx1 one, is channel 0 and hides the dropdown. A pick outside the image (A of a 3-channel image) is the engine's error text. Sources pass without a copy; Save DDS and the normal get the BGR to RGB copy. One image may feed several roles with different picks, so an `_orm` is wired as AO=R, roughness=G, metallic=B. No `np.clip`: psdds clamps (DD5).
- **DE8 Fills.** Each RMAOS role has a Fill dropdown, Default or Custom, and a number 0-255 shown only for Custom. Default passes -1 (the engine's neutral value for that role); Custom passes the number. chaiNNer has no optional number input, hence the dropdown. The roughness default stays the preset's (decision 9). PACK-DEFAULTED is logged, not an error (decision 8). Generated AO, glossiness, `_orm` and `_rfaos` roles are not in v1 (decision 4).
- **DE9 Presets (DC35, DC37, DC45).** Preset 0 is Custom (default) and shows every setting; 1-5 are psdds's five seeds, names and values read from `psdds_preset_*`, and hide them. There is no user preset store and no Save or Delete: a chain file or a copied node is the saved setup (decision 14). DC45 holds by construction: Custom is a plain choice with no matching, so it keeps the values the inputs held and never snaps back (decision 16). DC40's matching and preset file have nothing to attach to.
- **DE10 Alpha and visibility (DC31).** `has_alpha` comes from `psdds_alpha_used` on the pixels at encode, and Discard transparency (DC36) passes 0 without measuring. chaiNNer decides which inputs are visible before pixels exist, so visibility is probed with `has_alpha` 0, the wider set. Deviation: when the pixels carry alpha and psdds greys the filter to Box, the input stays visible; the DEBUG log shows the filter used, resolved with the measured `has_alpha`.
- **DE11 Settings (DC32, DC33, DC34, DC39).** One Format dropdown per texture type, options from `psdds_format_allowed`; each type keeps its own pick. sRGB defaults to off (DC34) and sets only the tag (DC39), so the filter stays visible with sRGB off and hides only for Mipmaps off, Normal, Linear mask or a seed preset. A format the type does not allow resolves in psdds.
- **DE12 Overwrite.** Like Save Image: overwrite, with Skip existing files. Encode first, then write a unique temp file beside the target (`.<name>.dds.<random>.tmp`, so concurrent saves to one name cannot interleave and a user's own files are never touched), flush, `os.fsync`, `os.replace`, so a failed encode never touches an existing file (decision 7). "Never overwrite a file Tessalith did not write" stays a project-export rule. Errors are psdds's text unchanged (DD10); the nodes add no punctuation, so nothing is trimmed.
- **DE13 Not applicable.** DC38, DC42, DC43 and DC44 are Photoshop-only (merged composite, alpha-source order, dialog layout, the PiPL channel count); a chaiNNer image is one array (decision 17). The input order already follows the dialog's tab order. DC7 and DC19 do not transfer: no cancel, no dialog.
- **DE14 Licences (DC41).** The nodes are GPL-3.0-or-later (SPDX header in each file), matching chaiNNer's GPLv3. `chainner\COPYING` is the GPL text for the nodes. `chainner\LICENSE` is psdds.dll's MIT text, because `notices.ps1` points to "see LICENSE"; the engine and encoders-sys code inside the DLL is MPL-2.0 and the installed `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` carries the source pointer. Not legal advice.
- **DE15 Left to others.** 16-bit and HDR output belong to the NIF team; chaiNNer's images are float32 in [0, 1] and are written as 8-bit. No psdds, engine or header change was made.
- **DE16 Not run in the app.** Tested with the bundled Python 3.11 (`-I`) against the built DLL, and loaded with `CHECK_LEVEL=error`, never inside chaiNNer. For the owner's check: the three nodes appear under Image > Tessalith DDS; the `TessalithRmaos` type connects RMAOS to Save Normal only; inputs show and hide as above (Preset, Fill, channel picks, Discard transparency while RMAOS is connected); a pair writes `_n` and `_rmaos`, a lone RMAOS writes nothing; skip-existing, overwrite and an error message look right; four nodes running at once; `install.ps1` on the real install, then again after a chaiNNer update.
- **DE17 RMAOS inputs (owner, later 2026-10-25; amends DE8).** Roughness is a required image (no fill). Metallic, AO and Specular drop the Default/Custom dropdown: an unconnected role shows its 0-255 value, preset to the engine's neutral default (metallic 0, AO 255, specular 255, `pack::default_for`), so untouched values write the same bytes as a -1 fill; `PACK-DEFAULTED` is no longer logged for them. The retired dropdown ids 20-23 and the roughness value id 30 stay unused. A specular-only RMAOS can no longer be built.
- **DE18 No glossiness input.** The owner asked for glossiness support (a glossiness map handled as glossiness, not an inversion helper). psdds has no glossiness role, and adding one needs a psdds/engine change, which host plugins don't make (DE15), so it was dropped (owner: drop it if it needs engine code). Invert with chaiNNer's own nodes until psdds gains a role.
- **DE19 Blank window (fix 7f064545).** chaiNNer's frontend evaluates group conditions in its built-in type scope, so a condition naming `TessalithRmaos` blanked the window. Save Normal's Discard condition uses `any` instead; `test_load_nodes` now runs the frontend's enum and type-name checks.
- **DE20 Save DDS crashed the editor when placed.** chaiNNer evaluates a dropdown condition together with that dropdown's own conditions, so the sRGB input, whose visibility named sRGB, recursed until the stack overflowed. Visibility now names type, format and, where it matters, Mipmaps (psdds's rules never depend on sRGB; `_ui` raises at import if that changes). `test_load_nodes` checks every input for such a cycle.
- **DE21 BC6H and RGBA16F, with a Linear HDR input switch (owner, 2026-10-26).** Save DDS offers BC6H and RGBA16F for Colour. chaiNNer images are float32 and do not say whether they are sRGB-coded 0..1 or linear light, so a "Linear HDR input" checkbox (id 17, default off) chooses the psdds depth: off = 16 (sRGB-coded, clamped, BC6H/RGBA16F decode to linear), on = 32 (linear, values above 1 kept for BC6H/RGBA16F, 8-bit formats clip and convert; DF3). Every format that existed before writes exactly the bytes it wrote at depth 8 (DF3), pinned by a test. No rule lives in Python.
- **DE22 Lists and visibility are probed at depth 16 and 32.** Format lists come from psdds_format_offered; _ui raises at import if offering differs between the two depths. Visibility is probed with psdds_resolve_depth at both depths and names the switch (Condition.bool) only where a control differs between them; today none does, so no condition names it, and none names its own input (DE20). BC6H brings a fourth quality group (input id 16); Save Normal keeps three groups so ids 7-9 and the RMAOS id 10 do not move.
- **DE23 Discard transparency is hidden where psdds does not enable it.** discard_enabled = 0 (BC1, BC4, BC5, BC6H; DF2) hides the input, as a probed control; chaiNNer cannot grey. This supersedes DF8's sentence that chaiNNer still shows the box editable. Seeds and the debug log use the effective settings at the chosen depth.
- **DE24 Release zip (owner, 2026-10-26).** `chainner\package.ps1` builds `dist\TessalithDDS-chaiNNer-<version>.zip`: `install.ps1`, `tessalith_dds\` (the nodes and `psdds.dll`), README, COPYING (GPL-3.0), LICENSE (psdds MIT) and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. `install.ps1` uses the shipped DLL and notices when `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` sits beside it, so the zip installs without the repo or cargo-about; a checkout builds them as before. The package check asserts the file list, the DLL hash, the licence texts, no engine-MIT wording, and a test install of the unzipped zip into a temporary chaiNNer folder that must report ABI 4.

## Note DF — Photoshop plugin: 16-bit, 32-bit and HDR (owner, 2026-10-25)

- **DF1 32-bit read probe (first step; the owner checks the merged path before later tasks build on it).** The PiPL lists RGB96Mode in EnableInfo, and FormatMaxChannels grows to 17 entries with index 16 (plugInModeRGB96) set to 24, like RGB and RGB48 (DC44). `write_start` accepts RGB96 with depth 32; its refusal text for other modes is now "Tessalith DDS saves only 8-bit, 16-bit and 32-bit RGB documents." (save side) 32-bit samples are copied to the float image unchanged (`to_rgba_floats` depth 32: no scale, no clamp, NaN kept). With `TESSALITH_DDS_TRACE` on, every save traces one line per path after the pixels arrive: `samples <band|merged> depth <d> channels <n>: px (r,g,b,a) x up to 4 r[min,max] g[min,max] b[min,max] a[min,max] nan N above1 N below0 N` (`%.9g`; min and max over finite values, alpha included; counts over RGB only). A 32-bit save then refuses before the dialog with "Tessalith DDS cannot save 32-bit documents in this build, so nothing was saved" and writes nothing (`// shortcut: probe refusal`, removed in the HDR plan's Task 6). The 8-bit and 16-bit save bytes and the 8-bit Open planes are pinned by FNV-1a hashes in host_test (`eight_bit_bytes_pinned`). The trace line buffer in `trace_note` grew from 256 to 768 bytes. Result of the owner check in Photoshop (band and merged `samples` lines agree to 1e-6, maximum about 4.0, 0.25 and 0.5 not encoded, merged channels at depth 32): **PASS** (owner, Photoshop 26.9, 2026-10-25). Marmoset 32-bit normal PSD, 2048x2048, Save a Copy, merged path: doc mode 16 depth 32, merged channels depth 32; `px (0.499992371,0.499992371,1,1)`, r[0.17685,0.67715] g[0.20398,0.75689] b[0.85948,1], nan 0 above1 0 below0 0 (raw vectors, not linearised). Test document 64x64 at 32 bits, left half 0.25/0.5/1.0, right half white, Exposure +2 on the whole image (expected 1/2/4 and 4/4/4): all four saves (flattened Save As, layered Save As, layered Save a Copy, a repeat) went through the merged path (layerData >= 1 even after flattening, so Photoshop did not exercise the band path) and read identical values: `px (1,2,4,1)`, r[1,4] g[2,4] b[4,4] a[1,1], above1 10240, nan 0, below0 0. No clipping, no display or exposure transform, merged channels depth 32, mergedTransparency present (type 16, depth 32) on the layered document. Consequence for Task 6: 32-bit saves use the merged path and the flatten-first fallback is not needed; the band path stays for hosts that send layerData 0.
- **DF2 psdds settings: BC6H and RGBA16F, depth-aware greying (ABI 3).** Formats 6 (BC6H) and 7 (RGBA16F) are Colour only (Normal and Linear mask do not list them). Depth enters the greying rules: psdds_resolve_depth(input, has_alpha, depth, effective, controls, discard_enabled) takes 8, 16 or 32 (anything else is -1), and psdds_format_offered(type, format, depth) lists the HDR formats only for 16 and 32-bit documents; at depth 8 they fall back to the type's default (BC7) by DC32, keeping the quality index. The old psdds_resolve, settings::resolve and profile_for are the depth-8 forms. BC6H has a 4-level quality list (Veryfast, Fast, Basic, Veryslow: the four ISPC levels bc6h_level reaches; seven efforts would show duplicates), default the base effort's level; RGBA16F has none. HDR formats grey the mip filter at Box and show it (the engine's HDR rule allows only Box and Tent, DC12's probe finds it by itself); cost: Tent, which the engine allows for HDR, is not offered. sRGB is greyed and 0 for both, and the colour tag is n/a (engine Note S4). RGBA16F keeps alpha (Blend unless Discard transparency); BC6H removes it. **Discard transparency is ticked and greyed (discard_enabled 0, effective discard_alpha 1) for every format that stores no alpha: BC1, BC4, BC5 and BC6H, at every depth (owner, 2026-10-25). This amends DC36**, which left BC1, BC4 and BC5 editable. Encoded bytes for 8-bit and 16-bit documents do not change (R2 already removed alpha for BC1, BC4 and BC5); the dialog state and the remembered setting do. A stored preset with discard 0 on those formats still matches, because matching compares effective settings. The seed Greyscale mask BC4 now has discard 1 so it stays a fixed point of resolve. Earlier psdds_resolve calls with format 6 or 7 returned -1; they now give the depth-8 result, and only format 8 and up is refused. The 'existing exports keep behaviour' constraint therefore reads: except the changes recorded here. ABI version 3 (PSDDS_ABI_VERSION 3u).
- **DF3 Encode by depth: the engine's transfer parameter and `psdds_encode_depth`.** `engine::memory::encode_image_with` takes a fourth parameter, `SourceTransfer`; `encode_image` and `encode_rmaos_set` pass `Stored`, so every existing byte, and every golden, is unchanged (MPL-2.0 engine file, API change only). `psdds_encode_depth(rgba, w, h, has_alpha, depth, settings, out, err, err_cap)` is the new export and `psdds_encode` is its depth-8 form. A depth other than 8, 16 or 32 is refused as "depth <d> out of range" (no full stop, DD10), after the size check and before `rgba` is read. **One rule, in psdds, chosen from the resolved settings (never the raw ones):** with effective type Colour and depth 32 the RGB samples go to the engine unchanged as `SourceTransfer::Linear` (Photoshop's 32-bit samples are linear light) and alpha is `clamp01`; the engine then does the rest: NaN and -inf become 0, +inf becomes 65504 for HDR formats and 1 otherwise (the spec is silent; this is the engine's existing `sanitize_non_finite` rule), `max(0)` for HDR, and `clamp_half` (0..65504) or `linear_to_srgb(clamp01)` for the LDR formats, so 4.0 saved as BC7 is 1.0. **Amended (final review, owner ruling):** for the 8-bit formats (anything but formats 6 and 7) psdds first clamps the RGB to 0..1 (NaN to 0) and still passes SourceTransfer::Linear, so mip 0 bytes are unchanged and the smaller mips are made from the clipped image, as the 16-bit path does; before, a small hot spot of 50.0 brightened every mip level above it. Pinned by colour_32_bit_hot_spot_is_clipped_before_mips. Every other case (any type at 8 or 16 bits, Normal and Linear mask at 32) is `clamp01` on all four channels with `Stored`, exactly DD5's path; Normal and Linear mask are data, not light, so 32 bits are clamped, not converted. 16-bit Colour saved as BC6H or RGBA16F is decoded from the stored (sRGB) coding to linear before the half is written (spec call 1): 0.5 reads back as 0.2140. Changed existing behaviour: only a 32-bit Colour document, whose RGB was not accepted before (the host did not offer 32 bits), so no existing export changes; DD5's one clamp rule no longer holds for that case (pointer added there), and DC6's transfer note has a pointer. Old calls: Colour with BC6H through `psdds_encode` is the DC32 fallback to BC7, keeping the quality index (DF2), so it equals BC7 at that index. Pinned in `crates/psdds/tests/encode.rs` and `clamp.rs` (`clamp_holds_at_depth_8_and_16`) and `crates/engine/tests/memory.rs` (`linear_transfer_skips_the_srgb_decode`).
- **DF4 Open HDR as floats: `psdds_decode_depth` and `psdds_dds_openable_float`.** `psdds_decode_depth(dds, len, w, h, has_alpha, depth, out, err, cap)` reports `*depth`: 8 for every format `psdds_decode` opens (bytes and `has_alpha` identical; both exports share one decode path), 32 for BC6H UF16/SF16, RGBA16F and RGBA32F, where `out` is `w*h*16` bytes of native-endian f32 RGBA from `engine::decode::decode_level_rgba` (the buffer is bytes, alignment not promised, hosts read it with memcpy; `psdds_free` unchanged). On Open, NaN becomes 0 and ±inf becomes ±65504 (the half range); negatives and values above 1 are kept in RGB, and alpha is clamped to 0..1. The engine decode is untouched; the rule runs in psdds before the output is built. Alpha is decided by psdds: BC6H is 1.0 with `has_alpha` 0; RGBA16F/RGBA32F set `has_alpha` 1 only when `helpers::alpha_used` (DC31) finds an alpha below 254/255. The spec's "other >8-bit formats open as 16-bit" covers no format: `DdsPixelFormat` has no integer format wider than 8 bits, and BC4/BC5 decode to 8-bit, so no 16-bit Open path is built and spec call 2 does not apply. `psdds_decode` still refuses HDR with the old text, and `psdds_dds_openable` does not change (claiming files `psdds_decode` refuses would regress every DLL host); `psdds_dds_openable_float` (`helpers::dds_openable_float`) is the sibling that also returns 1 for DXGI 2, 10, 95, 96 and D3DFMT 113, 116 (DXGI 94 and the other float formats stay 0). Cube maps, arrays, the size rule and low memory are refused as before. Shortcut: the Open file cap is unchanged (`kMaxDdsFileBytes`, 16384² RGBA8 with chain), so an RGBA16F above about 11.6k² or an RGBA32F above about 8k² is refused with the existing "too large" text; raise the cap if the owner meets one. A second shortcut sits in `decode` (the engine allocates the float image infallibly). Pinned in `crates/psdds/tests/decode.rs` (`float_open_round_trips`, `ldr_open_is_unchanged`, `float_open_sanitises_non_finite`, `float_open_still_refuses_cube_and_array`) and `helpers.rs` (`float_headers_are_claimed`).
- **DF5 Save dialog follows the document depth.** `FromResolve(input, has_alpha, depth)`, `ShowSaveDialog(owner, has_alpha, depth, inout)` and `MatchPreset(list, raw, has_alpha, depth, preferred)` take the depth (write.cpp passes `r->depth`); matching compares settings resolved at that depth through `psdds_resolve_depth`. **The Format list lists only the formats `psdds_format_offered` allows, it does not grey them:** the spec said "greyed", but a standard combo box cannot grey single items, and DC33 already lists only a type's formats. An 8-bit document therefore sees the old six formats; a 16- or 32-bit Colour document also sees "BC6H (HDR)" and "RGBA16F (uncompressed)", after RGBA8. The combo keeps its fixed 85-unit size (DC43); its drop-down (CB_SETDROPPEDWIDTH, pixels) is sized from the longest Format label measured in the combo's own font plus the scroll bar and edges, never narrower than the combo, so it follows DPI and font scaling. The Discard transparency checkbox is disabled when `discard_enabled` is 0 (BC1, BC4, BC5, BC6H) and shows the effective value, ticked (DF2). `LoadPresets` and the remembered settings still validate through the depth-8 `psdds_resolve`, which accepts formats 6 and 7, so a BC6H or RGBA16F preset and a remembered HDR pick survive; at depth 8 they show BC7 (DC32) and the raw pick is kept for the next HDR document. Pinned in `photoshop/tests/dialog_test.cpp` (`formats_follow_document_depth`).
- **DF6 Save 32-bit documents through psdds_encode_depth.** (Save side; Open uses RGBColor with depth 32, DF7.) The write path calls psdds_resolve_depth and psdds_encode_depth with the document depth at every depth (equal to the old calls at 8 and 16), and the Task 1 probe refusal is gone. Both read paths take 32-bit, per the DF1 owner check (Photoshop 26.9: the merged composite delivers raw 32-bit floats, 1/2/4 kept, no clipping or display transform; every 32-bit save arrives with layerData >= 1): a layered RGB96 document reads the merged composite through the channel ports and writes the same bytes as the band path on the same samples, and a port depth mismatch writes nothing. The band path stays for hosts that send layerData 0. The size estimate (amends DC24): dds_size_range(w, h, depth, ...) keeps the minimum (BC1, no mips) and, above 8 bits, takes the maximum as RGBA16F (8 bytes a pixel) with a full chain and the DX10 header; at 16384 x 16384 and 32-bit that is (cap - 148) * 2 + 148. Depth 8 is unchanged. Known limit (preflight B11): a 32-bit save near 16384 x 16384 allocates about 4 GiB of floats plus the engine's work, and an RGBA16F file of that size (about 2.9 GB) exceeds the Open cap, so Tessalith could not reopen it; a // shortcut: comment marks the allocation and nothing refuses early.
- **DF7 Open 32-bit documents.** Open calls `psdds_decode_depth` (DF4). At depth 8 it is the old path byte for byte (pinned by `eight_bit_bytes_pinned`). At depth 32 (BC6H UF16/SF16, RGBA16F, RGBA32F) the document is `plugInModeRGBColor`, depth 32 (not RGB96), `colBytes` 4, `rowBytes` width*4, `planeBytes` pixels*4, planes 3 or 4 from psdds's `has_alpha` (no `opens_with_transparency` for floats; a host passing `transparencyPlane` -1 gets 3 when four planes are sent and 0 otherwise), bands sized by `band_rows(width * planes * 4, ...)` and filled by `deinterleave_rgba32f_to_planes` (memcpy, no alignment assumed). Values above 1 and negatives are kept; NaN/inf were already made finite by psdds. Open sets imageMode plugInModeRGBColor with depth 32, not RGB96: Photoshop 26.9 rejected RGB96 on read (owner trace 2026-10-25, ReadFinish straight after ReadStart); the deep mode follows from depth. **No ICC profile is set** (spec call 3): 32-bit Photoshop documents are linear and the host picks its own working profile. **FilterFile now claims these formats**: `dds_header_openable` calls `psdds_dds_openable_float`, which amends DC20's declined list (BC6H, RGBA16F, RGBA32F, FourCC 113/116 are claimed; DXGI 94 and the other float formats, cube maps and arrays are still declined). **Cost** (see DF4): the Open file cap is unchanged, so an RGBA16F above about 11.6k^2 or an RGBA32F above about 8k^2 is refused with the existing "too large" text; a 32-bit open holds the file bytes only while decoding, then 16 bytes a pixel of f32 plus one band, so a 16384^2 BC6H file (1 byte a pixel, within the cap) needs about 4 GB for the decoded image. Shortcut: the multi-band 32-bit hand-off is covered by `band_rows` and the 8-bit band tests, not by a host test larger than one band.
- **DF8 chaiNNer nodes follow ABI 3.** `chainner/tessalith_dds/_psdds.py` now needs ABI 3 and its tests expect the new mismatch text and the Greyscale mask BC4 seed with discard 1. Discard transparency is effectively ticked for BC1, BC4 and BC5 in psdds (DF2); chaiNNer's own UI still shows the box editable, because the nodes add no rule (DE). Output bytes are unchanged, since R2 already dropped alpha for those formats.

## Note DH — Alpha is transparency, a per-save choice (owner, 2026-10-26)

The letter DH is provisional: DG is the GIMP branch's letter, so rename at merge if DH is taken. Owner report: in the Paint.NET plugin a PNG with alpha, saved with Discard transparency off, had the colour under its alpha-0 pixels repainted (the controller measured a mean error of 181 there, colour elsewhere intact). Cause: psdds kept alpha as `AlphaPolicy::Blend`, and for Blend the engine runs `dilate_under_zero_alpha` and alpha-weights the mips. The owner: in Skyrim texture sets alpha is usually data (masks), not transparency, so it is a per-save choice. Branch `feat/psdds-alpha-mode`; this phase covers psdds, Photoshop and chaiNNer. GIMP and Paint.NET adopt ABI 4 on their own branches. The engine is not changed.

- **DH1 The setting.** `PsddsSettings` gains an eighth field, `alpha_mode`, at the end: 0 = alpha is data (`AlphaPolicy::Data`), 1 = "Alpha is transparency" (`AlphaPolicy::Blend`, the old behaviour). The default is 0 for every type (`psdds_defaults`) and every seed preset (DC35). 2 and above are refused by `psdds_resolve` like the other fields. Checked in the engine without changing it: for Data, `alpha_weighted_mips()` is false (config.rs), so `preprocess_with` skips `dilate_under_zero_alpha` (ops.rs, the `alpha_present && p.alpha_weighted_mips()` gate), the mips are not alpha-weighted (mips.rs `weighted_rgb`), and `filter::filter_allowed` does not refuse a non-Box filter. No other engine path on psdds's encode route reads the policy (coverage is off for both; `encode_image_with` runs no policy checks). Kept alpha (`alpha_present`) is the same for both.
- **DH2 Where it applies.** Only where alpha is kept: the document has alpha, effective Discard transparency is 0, so the format stores alpha (BC3, BC7, RGBA8, RGBA16F; DF2 already forces Discard to 1 for the others). Everywhere else the policy is Remove as before. `PsddsControls` gains `alpha_mode_enabled` (fourth field), 1 exactly there, reported by `psdds_resolve` and `psdds_resolve_depth`. Hosts grey (Photoshop, GIMP, Paint.NET) or hide (chaiNNer) the control when it is 0.
- **DH3 A disabled alpha_mode is effectively 0.** Where it is disabled, `psdds_resolve` reports effective `alpha_mode = 0`, so a raw 1 there resolves exactly like 0 and never makes a preset look different (no spurious "Custom"); preset matching keeps comparing effective settings (DC37, DC40) and needs no host-side rule for it (unlike DC40's Discard rule). The Photoshop dialog shows the raw pick on the greyed checkbox (it has no effect there), so the choice comes back when alpha is kept again.
- **DH4 ABI 4.** `PSDDS_ABI_VERSION 4u`; `PsddsSettings` is 32 bytes (`alpha_mode` at offset 28, after `discard_alpha`), `PsddsControls` 16 (`alpha_mode_enabled` at 12). `PsddsRmaosJob` embeds the settings and stays 168 bytes with the same offsets. Exact-match ABI checks stay in every host. Pinned by `crates/psdds/tests/abi.rs` (`settings_layout_is_eight_fields`, which also checks the header's field order) and `tests/rmaos.rs`; `examples/dll_host.rs` passes 8 values.
- **DH5 Bytes.** With `alpha_mode = 1` every output equals the ABI 3 bytes: `crates/psdds/tests/alpha_mode.rs` pins FNV-1a hashes recorded on main 448e54fb for the five seeds, Colour BC3, Colour RGBA8 and Colour RGBA16F (depth 16) on a 32x32 noise image with an alpha-0 quarter. With `alpha_mode = 0` and alpha kept, the bytes change (intended) and are pinned in the same test; the colour under alpha-0 pixels survives (`data_keeps_the_colour_under_clear_pixels`: largest RGB error under 0.02 after decode for BC7, BC3, RGBA8 and RGBA16F on a two-colour fixture, against over 0.3 with transparency). Outputs without kept alpha (the BC1 and BC4 seeds, Discard on, no document alpha) are the same in both modes. `psdds_rmaos_encode` is unaffected: `normal_settings.alpha_mode` is range-checked and ignored, like `discard_alpha` (DD8, R19); a test shows 0 and 1 give the same pair. Engine goldens are untouched (`cargo test -p engine --test golden`).
- **DH6 Consequence: the filter is editable for kept alpha as data.** DC12's probe greys the Colour filter at Box only where the engine would mip with Box anyway; with Data it does not, so with alpha kept and `alpha_mode = 0` the filter stays editable and Kaiser (etc.) is honoured. With `alpha_mode = 1` it greys at Box as before. This amends DC12's and DC39's "greys where alpha is kept" to "where alpha is kept as transparency"; psdds tests `filter_greys_where_the_engine_uses_box`, `kaiser_applies_only_where_the_dialog_shows_it` cover both.
- **DH7 Photoshop.** The checkbox "&Alpha is transparency" (mnemonic A, free in the dialog: P, v, D, T, s, F, r, M, i, Q were taken) sits in the right column directly under Discard transparency, on its own row; the Mipmaps/Filter row, Quality row and OK/Cancel move down 18 dialog units (the dialog is 250 x 136). Tab order is the resource order: ... Format, Discard transparency, Alpha is transparency, Mipmaps, Filter, Quality. It is greyed by `alpha_mode_enabled` and shows the raw pick (DH3). Remembered settings gain an optional eighth registry key, `alph`; a descriptor without it (saved before DH) loads with 0. Presets (DC37, DC40): lines are written with 8 values under a new header; a 7-value line loads with `alpha_mode = 0` (so old presets keep working) and the old header is recognised and dropped rather than kept as an unparsed line. DC40's "never write a file not read in full" is unchanged. Tests: `dialog_test` (greying, the old/new line formats, matching), `host_test` `dialog_after_pixels` (a transparent layer keeps the filter editable by default; ticking the box greys it at Box and changes the bytes; Discard greys the box; layout, label width and tab order). `eight_bit_bytes_pinned` (DF1) is unchanged: its fixtures are opaque.
- **DH8 chaiNNer.** `_psdds.py` needs ABI 4 and carries both new fields. Save DDS gets the BoolInput "Alpha is transparency" (input id 18, default off), placed after Discard transparency; no id moved. Its visibility is probed with `has_alpha = 1` (a deviation from DE10's has_alpha 0 probe, which would hide it everywhere) and gated on Discard transparency off; Discard's own condition never names it (DE20), checked by `test_ui` and the cycle check in `test_load_nodes`. Save Normal and RMAOS get no control and use the default 0 (DH9).
- **DH9 Amended rulings.** DC3 and DC36 (alpha kept = Blend) and DF2's "RGBA16F keeps alpha (Blend unless Discard transparency)" now read: kept alpha is Data unless `alpha_mode` is 1. DD2/DF2's ABI number is 4. DE10's probe has the DH8 exception. DE4 (a lone Save Normal writes the same bytes as Save DDS with type Normal) still holds, so a lone Save Normal of a normal map whose pixels carry real alpha with Discard off now keeps that alpha as data instead of Blend (no dilation under alpha 0); a normal without alpha, and the RMAOS pair's `_n` (built without alpha), are unchanged.

## Note DI — Paint.NET DDS file type (owner, 2026-10-25)

Written as Note DF; renamed DI at the rebase onto main 60b8db78 (main's DF is the Photoshop HDR note, DG is the GIMP branch's, DH is Alpha is transparency), so items DF1-DF37 of this branch are DI1-DI37. Branch `feat/paintdotnet-dds`, plugin in `paintdotnet/`, built on the shared `psdds.dll` (Note DD; ABI 2, ABI 4 since DI38). The owner approved the recommendations on 2026-10-25 ("go with your recommendations"). The note carries Note DC over to Paint.NET; Photoshop-only items are marked n/a. Rulings made by the controller during the tasks state their cost.

- **DI1 No Open route.** Paint.NET opens every `.dds` with its built-in DDS type. `FindFileTypeForLoadingExtension` returns the first type that can load the extension, built-in types are listed first, and the bundled `DdsFileTypePlus` is built in (`DdsFileType : FileTypeProxy` in paintdotnet.dll). No setting turns a bundled type off. A plugin that claims `.dds` is never chosen by File > Open, drag and drop or the recent list, so DC20 and DC23 (open rules) do not apply and nothing declines HDR, cube or array files. `LoadExtensions = .dds` stays only because the Save dialog's preview loads the encoded result back. The README tells users once to use Save As for files opened from DDS.
- **DI2 Save alpha comes from the pixels (DC31).** `has_alpha` is `psdds_alpha_used` on the converted float RGBA buffer (alpha below 254/255 counts). This supersedes the earlier 254 byte-scan proposal, so a Tessalith BC7 file with alpha 254 re-saves opaque, as in every other host. The written file never depends on the dialog's copy: `OnSave` measures its own.
- **DI3 Formats per type (DC32).** The Format list holds only the formats `psdds_format_allowed` gives for the shown texture type. A stored format that is no longer allowed resolves to BC7 and the raw value is kept. C# holds display labels only, no format table.
- **DI4 Checkboxes and layout (DC33, DC37, DC43).** sRGB and Mipmaps are checkboxes. Rows: Preset with Save preset and Delete; Texture type with sRGB; Format with Discard transparency under sRGB; Mipmaps with Filter; Quality. Texture type and Format lists have one width. Tab order is Preset, Save preset, Delete, Texture type, sRGB, Format, Discard transparency, Mipmaps, Filter, Quality (DI39 adds Alpha is transparency after Discard transparency, mnemonic A). Labels and mnemonics are `dialog.rc`'s (P, v, D, T, s, F, r, M, i, Q), including "Discard t&ransparency". Initial focus is on Preset. Message texts match `dialog.cpp` exactly, including its final full stop where it has one (Paint.NET adds none). A preset pick runs the full refresh (rebuild Format and Quality, then greying), as `dialog.cpp` does. Layout replaced by DI37 (one column).
- **DI5 A custom widget, not IndirectUI.** The dialog is a WinForms `SaveConfigWidget` mirroring `photoshop/src/dialog.cpp`. IndirectUI cannot show a greyed control's effective value while keeping the raw pick (DC19): its read-only rules leave the stored value on screen. The widget keeps raw picks, so Normal then Colour restores sRGB On, and Normal with BC5 then Colour then Normal shows BC5 again.
- **DI6 has_alpha arrives from the preview pass.** The widget is never given the Document; the preview's `Save` is. The preview measures the pixels and hands the result to the open widget. The value arrives on the preview's worker thread: it is cached with a volatile read and write, marshalled to the UI thread with `BeginInvoke`, and dropped after the widget is disposed. The widget refreshes only when the value changes and never refills the Format or Quality lists then (fix round 1 of Task 6), so an open dropdown does not collapse. Before the first measurement the image counts as opaque, matching the brief and Photoshop.
- **DI7 The preview re-encodes on every change, with no cancel (DC7 extended).** Paint.NET's Save dialog encodes on open and on every token change, then waits for the running preview on OK before the real save. `SupportsCancellation` is false and the progress callback is unused. A slow format costs that time per dropdown change and once more on OK; Task 9 measures it. No cancel hook (shared plan R18).
- **DI8 ABI check and size check live in psdds.** `Psdds` compares `psdds_abi_version()` with the header's `PSDDS_ABI_VERSION` on first use and refuses any other value. `OnSave` calls `psdds_check_size` before allocating the float buffer and uses 64-bit arithmetic; its text goes to the user. C# has no size limit, alpha threshold or format table.
- **DI9 Missing or mismatched psdds.dll fails when the Save dialog is built.** The widget constructor and `OnCreateDefaultSaveConfigTokenT` call psdds, so a missing or ABI-mismatched DLL stops the dialog from opening with a raw exception, not a clean save error. Decided in Task 6 and deferred to the owner check (Task 9); cost if wrong: a raw error text. .NET also caches a failed native load, so after the DLL is replaced Paint.NET must be restarted. The README says so.
- **DI10 Remembered settings belong to the host.** The token's serialisable portion is `int[7]` (DC36's discard last; `int[8]` since DI40). A six-int portion still loads with discard 0 (one line; it protects only a developer machine). Anything else is rejected without throwing into the host, and the fallback is `psdds_defaults(Colour)`. The host stores it under `"<Namespace>.<TypeName>.BinaryFormatter"`. `IsReflexive` is not overridden (obsolete; IL shows false).
- **DI11 The FileType class and namespace are frozen.** `Tessalith.Dds.TessalithDdsFileType` is Paint.NET's settings key. Renaming the class or the namespace after release forgets every user's remembered settings. Never rename.
- **DI12 sRGB is off by default and sets only the tag (DC34, DC39).** Start values come from `psdds_defaults` for every type; nothing in C# turns sRGB on. sRGB sets only the DDS format tag, so sRGB Off does not grey the filter. A default Colour save keeps Kaiser; the filter greys only where psdds says so (alpha kept, Mipmaps off). No test expects sRGB Off to grey it.
- **DI13 Discard transparency (DC36, DC43).** A checkbox, always enabled (amended by DI38: ticked and greyed for BC1, BC4 and BC5), in the right column on the Format row directly under sRGB; the seventh raw value. Ticked, the encode is given `has_alpha = false` (psdds removes alpha anyway) and the pixel rule decides nothing. The preview still measures, so the widget has the value after an untick (the alternative, a second pass over up to 1 GiB of floats on a UI event, was declined). Layout replaced by DI37 (one column).
- **DI14 Custom stays Custom (DC45, DC40).** `PresetSelection` (Core) holds the Custom flag and the picked preset. Picking Custom keeps the settings and shows Custom (Delete greyed, Save preset proposes no name) until another preset is picked or one is saved; edits made while Custom is shown stay Custom even when they land on a preset's values. While a picked preset's effective values still match it, it stays shown (twins). `Match` zeroes Discard transparency in the comparison when the image has no alpha. `CanDelete` is true when a user preset is picked; Delete resets the pick and re-matches (`dialog.cpp:206`).
- **DI15 The preset file is protected (DC40).** `Load` reports `Complete`. A file that is not read in full (open fails other than not-found, over 1 MiB, short read) is never written; Save preset and Delete then show "The preset file could not be read, so presets can't be changed". Lines that do not parse are kept as raw bytes and written back after the parsed presets. The header and empty lines are not kept, so two load and save cycles leave the file byte-identical. A missing file counts as complete and seeds. Delete is greyed when the file is unreadable (`dialog.cpp:129`), so the read-only message shows only through Save preset.
- **DI16 Presets are the plugin's own (DC35, DC37).** Paint.NET has no preset feature (Owner decision 10). The Preset row is in the widget and the store is `%APPDATA%\Tessalith DDS\presets\paintdotnet.txt` in the Photoshop line format (8 values a line since DI41), not shared with Photoshop's `presets.txt`, so a rewrite in one host cannot disturb the other. The five seeds are read from `psdds_preset_count/name/settings` on first creation and written to the file; no seed name or value is in C#. Seeds are ordinary presets (no protected built-ins), Custom comes first, matching uses effective values, names are unique ignoring case, replace and delete confirm with No as default, writes are atomic (temp, flush, replace), a file that exists is never re-seeded, and `TESSALITH_DDS_PRESETS_DIR` redirects the store for tests. Name trimming uses `CleanPresetName`'s character set, ported and tested for NBSP and U+3000 both ways, not `string.Trim()`. The widget buttons and prompts are checked by hand in Task 9, as DC37 does.
- **DI17 Preset names are up to 64 UTF-16 units.** The limit counts UTF-16 code units, as the .NET string length does; the Task 9 check opens a 64-unit name in the list, and the dropdown is widened to fit long names.
- **DI18 Dialog appearance.** The name prompt and the message boxes stay light under Paint.NET's dark theme. DPI is scaled when the control is created only; a move to another monitor with a different DPI is not handled. Both are noted for Task 9 and the README.
