- **DI19 DC38 is n/a.** The layered-save route is Photoshop-only (PiPL layer support, channel ports). Paint.NET hands the plugin one rendered `Surface` (`input.CreateRenderer().Render(scratch)`).
- **DI20 DC42 is n/a.** A Paint.NET document has no alpha channels beside the layers' own alpha; the composite's alpha is the only source, so there is no source order to choose.
- **DI21 DC44 is n/a.** The 24-channel limit is a Photoshop PiPL entry (`FormatMaxChannels`); Paint.NET has no such declaration.
- **DI22 Licence of the engine inside psdds.dll (DC41).** The `engine` and `encoders-sys` code inside `psdds.dll` is MPL-2.0, not MIT; only the `psdds` crate is MIT. This item applies to the licence text and notices only: no plugin code changes. The MPL source pointer (repository URL and commit) is in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **DI23 Licence of the plugin.** The plugin's C# is GPL-3.0-or-later with a section 7 additional permission for Paint.NET and its `PaintDotNet.*.dll` (the FSF linking-exception template). Nothing in the vendored encoders, the MPL-2.0 crates or the Rust dependencies blocks this. Not legal advice.
- **DI24 Licence files in the zip (all three hosts).** `COPYING` is the plugin's GPL-3.0 text with the section 7 Paint.NET permission and a short licence-split paragraph. `LICENSE` is `psdds.dll`'s MIT text (`crates/psdds/LICENSE`). `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` comes from `crates\psdds\notices.ps1`, so its "(see LICENSE)" points at the MIT text. This is the controller's ruling for Paint.NET, GIMP and chaiNNer alike; it supersedes the plan's LICENSE/COPYING swap and GIMP's `LICENSE-psdds.txt`. Cost if wrong: rename two files. The C# source headers point to `paintdotnet/COPYING`.
- **DI25 Paint.NET's licence clause.** Paint.NET's `License.txt` bars derivative works. The package ships no Paint.NET file and references `PaintDotNet.*.dll` only at build time (`Private=false`), as the bundled plugins do; the README says "not made or endorsed by dotPDN LLC". `package.ps1` fails if any `PaintDotNet*.dll` is staged. Not legal advice.
- **DI26 The zip holds exactly seven files under `TessalithDDS\`.** `COPYING`, `LICENSE`, `psdds.dll`, `README.md`, `TessalithDds.deps.json`, `TessalithDds.dll` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The list is explicit, so a Release `.pdb` is not shipped, and `package.ps1` fails on any other count. Package with `pwsh`: Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Compress-Archive` can write backslash entry names. The zip and its `.sha256.txt` are written atomically.
- **DI27 No pin from the plugin (DC25).** Plugin load contexts are not collectible, .NET never frees a library bound by `LibraryImport`, and psdds pins itself on its first encode or decode (DD3). The plugin does nothing.
- **DI28 x64 only.** Paint.NET also ships ARM64; this build is x64, and an ARM64 load shows a "64-bit Intel/AMD build" error (the BadImageFormat message). Install location in the README: the per-user `Documents\paint.net App Files\FileTypes\TessalithDDS\` first, Program Files second, confirmed in Task 9.
- **DI29 Input and output (DC6, DC27, DC30).** 8-bit `v / 255` with `SourceTransfer::Stored`, from the flattened straight-alpha BGRA composite. The encode goes to a `PsddsBuf` first, then one `stream.Write`; the host's `SaveTransaction` keeps the old file if anything throws. Messages go into the exception text under Paint.NET's generic save error, with trailing full stops trimmed from psdds text.
- **DI30 Resource handling.** Every `PsddsBuf` is freed exactly once, also on exceptions, and the float buffer in `finally`. Save logic is in Core (`DdsSave`), and `src/Core/` names no `PaintDotNet` type, so the test project compiles it without Paint.NET. The scratch surface is read through `GetRowPointer` after its size is asserted.
- **DI31 Build and test rules.** `build.ps1` runs `crates\psdds\build.ps1` and uses the fixed `psdds.dll` path in `target\psdds`; csproj references use the full `PaintDotNet.<name>` names with `HintPath` under `$(PdnDir)`; root namespace is `Tessalith.Dds`. Tests never touch `%APPDATA%\Tessalith DDS` or Paint.NET's settings, and no `.dds` fixture is in the repo.
- **DI32 Native resolution.** The plugin folder is `FileTypes\TessalithDDS\`; Paint.NET's resolver finds `psdds.dll` next to `TessalithDds.dll`, and the plugin pins the lookup to its own folder (Task 2 fix round 1). `psdds.dll` is not mistaken for a plugin because it is not managed.
- **DI33 No scripted save.** Paint.NET shows the dialog on every Save, Save As and Ctrl+S and has no batch or scripting path, so DC19 and DC22 hold with no code.
- **DI34 Left as it is.** The MSB3277 build warning is left. `runtimeconfig.json` is not shipped. The `EntryPointNotFound` branch of the DLL check has no test. Cost: none known.
- **DI35 Checks owed to Task 9.** The owner check covers the Save dialog on a machine without the DLL and with a mismatched one, preview timing on a large image (DI7), a 64-unit preset name, dark-theme prompts, DPI across monitors, and the WinForms layout, which has not been seen on screen before then.
- **DI36 Widget never reads `FileType` (Task 9 crash).** Save As then Cancel or OK crashed Paint.NET 5.1.12 with `InternalErrorException: Unexpected null reference 'base.FileType'` from `TessalithDdsWidget.Dispose`. Cause (IL of PaintDotNet.Data.dll): the `SaveConfigWidget(FileType)` ctor only calls `InitializeComponent`; `SaveConfigWidget.fileType` is set only by ``SaveConfigWidget`2.InitFileType``, which only the parameterless base ctor calls, and paintdotnet.dll never calls it. So for a widget built with `base(fileType)` the `FileType` property is null for its whole life and its getter (`NotNull`) throws; the host does not null it at Dispose. Fix: the widget keeps the constructor's file type in a readonly field and subscribes and unsubscribes `HasAlphaMeasured` through it; nothing reads `FileType`. `SaveConfigDialog.Dispose` cancels the preview task without waiting, so `OnMeasured` can still run after the widget is disposed; it already checks `IsDisposed` and catches the disposed-handle exceptions. The widget never reads `Token` (`CreateTokenFromWidget` uses the raw settings field).
- **DI37 Options in one column (Task 9 scrollbar).** At 2.75x the options area showed a horizontal scrollbar. The dialog cannot be widened for it (IL of `SaveConfigDialog.OnLayout`, paintdotnet.dll 5.1.12): the settings column is `ConvertDipsToPixelsInt(200)` (IL 0154-0160) and `saveConfigPanel.Width` is set to it on every layout (022E-023B); extra form width goes to the preview. The host then sets `saveConfigWidget.Width = panel.Width - VerticalScrollBarWidth` (0246-025C), calls `PerformLayout` and places Defaults below `Min(panel.Height, widget.Height)` (0329-034F). The scrollbar came from the widget's `AutoSize`, which overrode that width with dialog.rc's three-column grid. So the widget now keeps the host's width (no `AutoSize`), stacks DC33's rows in one column in the same order and tab order (each label above its list, checkboxes on their own rows, as Paint.NET's own option panels), lets the lists fill the column, and sets its height to the content. The closed lists truncate; the open Type, Format and Preset lists are as wide as their longest entry. Save preset... and Delete wrap onto two lines when they do not fit side by side. A vertical scrollbar on a short dialog is the host's (it reserves that width). No pure logic came out of this, so no new test; the owner checks the layout.
- **DI38 psdds ABI 4 (Notes DF2, DH4 on main).** The C# `PsddsSettings` has eight fields (32 bytes, `AlphaMode` at 28) and `PsddsControls` four (16 bytes, `AlphaModeEnabled` at 12), as `photoshop/psdds.h`; `ExpectedAbiVersion` is 4. `discard_enabled` is not a struct field in the header but an out-parameter of `psdds_resolve_depth`, so the struct follows the header and `TryResolve` calls `psdds_resolve_depth` with depth 8 (Paint.NET documents are 8-bit; at 8 it is `psdds_resolve` plus `discard_enabled`). Encode and decode keep the 8-bit `psdds_encode` and `psdds_decode`. **Discard transparency greys** where `discard_enabled` is 0 (BC1, BC4, BC5) and shows the effective value, ticked, as `dialog.cpp` does; this amends DI13. Consequences pinned in the tests: the Greyscale mask BC4 seed has discard 1; a BC1 preset with discard 0 matches the BC1 seed also when the image has alpha (effective discard is 1 for both); with alpha kept as data the filter stays editable (DH6), so the old greying tests now set alpha_mode 1.
- **DI39 "Alpha is transparency" checkbox (Note DH).** Label `&Alpha is transparency`, mnemonic A: the widget already uses P, v, D, T, s, F, r, M, i and Q, and Paint.NET's OK, Cancel and Defaults buttons do not use A (Photoshop chose A for the same reason, DH7). It sits directly under Discard transparency in the one-column layout (DI37), on its own row; tab order is Preset, Save preset, Delete, Texture type, sRGB, Format, Discard transparency, Alpha is transparency, Mipmaps, Filter, Quality. It is greyed where `alpha_mode_enabled` is 0 and, as `dialog.cpp`, shows the raw pick also when greyed (DH3), so the choice returns when alpha is kept again. Default unticked (`psdds_defaults`). Until the first preview has measured the image it counts as opaque (DI6), so the box starts greyed and becomes editable when the preview finds alpha, like the filter. The widget is checked by the owner (Core tests cannot load Paint.NET).
- **DI40 Remembered settings are `int[8]`.** `AlphaMode` is last. An `int[7]` portion (saved before this) loads with alpha_mode 0, an `int[6]` with discard 0 and alpha_mode 0; any other length, a negative value or values psdds refuses give `psdds_defaults(Colour)` as before. The FileType class and namespace are unchanged (DI11).
- **DI41 Preset lines carry 8 values (as `presets.cpp`, DH7).** `paintdotnet.txt` is written with 8 values a line under the header `# Tessalith DDS presets: name, format, type, sRGB, filter, mips, quality, discard transparency, alpha is transparency`. A 7-value line (written before this) loads with alpha_mode 0 and is written back with 8 values on the next save. The old header is recognised and dropped on load, not kept as an unparsed line. DC40 and DI15 are unchanged: a file not read in full is never written, and unparsed lines are kept byte for byte.
- **DI42 Bytes.** With alpha_mode 0 (the default) an RGBA8 save of an image with alpha-0 pixels decodes back to the source RGB under alpha 0 as well (`SaveDecodesBackToTheSourcePixels` lost its exemption for those pixels); this fixes the Task 9 caveat that the colour under alpha 0 was repainted. With alpha_mode 1 the plugin's bytes equal `psdds_encode` of the same pixels with alpha_mode 1, the old transparency bytes (DH5), and differ from alpha_mode 0. Tests: 62 before, 67 now (struct layout, token 6/7/8 ints, preset 7/8-value lines and both headers, Discard and Alpha is transparency greying, bytes).

## Note DG — GIMP DDS export plug-in (owner, 2026-10-26)
- **DG1 Route and ABI.** The plug-in is Python (GIMP 3.0's own interpreter) calling `psdds.dll` through `ctypes`, in the folder `plug-ins\tessalith-dds\` (`tessalith-dds.py`, `psdds_ctypes.py`, `tdds_pixels.py`, `psdds.dll`). The DLL is loaded by absolute path from the plug-in's own folder; one copy per install. On first use the wrapper calls `psdds_abi_version()` and refuses any value other than `EXPECTED_ABI` (3, Note DF2/DF3), with a short message. The environment variable `TESSALITH_PSDDS_DLL` overrides the DLL path; it exists for the tests only, and the run scripts restore it. No rule, number or message of psdds is copied into `gimp/` (greying, formats per type, seeds, alpha, clamp, size limits all come from psdds); a grep for `16384|254|1431655912|Max side` finds nothing there.
- **DG2 Process per call (the DC25 equivalent).** The procedures do not call `persistent_enable`, so GIMP runs every load and export in a new process, as measured on 3.0.4. psdds's own pin keeps `psdds.dll` mapped for the life of that process.
- **DG3 Priority -1 and delegation.** Load and export are registered with magic `0,string,DDS`, extension `dds`, priority -1, so Tessalith is the default `.dds` handler and "DDS image" stays selectable by type. GIMP has no runtime decline (an error from a load does not fall through), so the load procedure calls `file-dds-load` through the PDB for files `psdds_dds_openable` refuses (HDR, cube maps, arrays) and returns its result. Open is the top mip as 8-bit RGB(A); alpha of 254 or 255 everywhere opens opaque (`psdds_opens_with_alpha`, DC23). Open of HDR files stays with GIMP's DDS plug-in; psdds's DF4 float open is not used here. GIMP marks a loaded image dirty again after any load procedure returns (file-dds too), so this is not fixable in the plug-in. GIMP caches a registration until the `.py` file's mtime changes, so a missing or wrong-ABI DLL leaves export unregistered (printed to stderr) until the plug-in is reinstalled.
- **DG4 Dialog mechanism and deviations from `dialog.rc` (DC33).** `GimpUi.ExportProcedureDialog` with rows built by `fill_box` (M6: the typelib has `fill_box` and `fill_flowbox`, no `_list` forms): row 0 Preset; row 1 Texture type then sRGB; row 2 Format then Discard transparency in the same right-hand slot (DC43, best effort); row 3 Mipmaps then Filter; row 4 Quality. Greyed controls show the effective value while the raw arguments keep the pick (DC19) through auxiliary `shown-*` properties and `*-enabled` flags: `shown-format`, `shown-mip-filter`, `shown-quality` (int combos on an IntStore that is rebuilt in place under a re-entry guard), `shown-srgb`, `shown-discard-alpha` (bool). A choice aux argument crashes 3.0.4 at `Gimp.main` (GIMP_IS_CHOICE assertion), so `shown-mip-filter` is an int combo; the raw `format`, `texture-type` and `mip-filter` stay choices. Deviations: widths and label alignment are GIMP's; no mnemonics (nicks carry no underscores, they show in the PDB browser); tab order is widget order; the button row is GIMP's (Help, Reset, Cancel, Export); no Save preset or Delete buttons (DG6). Labels are Photoshop's verbatim.
- **DG5 Save order and alpha (DC31, DC36).** The pixels are read, `psdds_alpha_used` runs, then the dialog opens with that `has_alpha`, then the encode. `has_alpha` never comes from the layer's alpha channel, so a layer without alpha and an alpha of 254 or 255 both export opaque. **Review L1 (changed in Task 5b):** the encode gets the pixels' `has_alpha` unchanged; before, the plug-in restated DC36 as `has_alpha and not discard_alpha`. psdds removes alpha when `discard_alpha` is 1, so bytes are identical (pinned by an RGBA8 + Discard batch case), and the encode's resolve now sees the same `has_alpha` as the dialog.
- **DG6 Presets: seeds only (preflight M3, supersedes owner decision 11).** GIMP 3.0.4 has no native procedure-dialog Presets: `GimpUi.ProcedureDialog` and `ExportProcedureDialog` have no Presets or Settings class (spike, Task 5). v1 is the "Preset" list of Custom plus the five psdds seeds (`psdds_preset_*`, DC35), matched by effective values (DC37, DC40: Discard ignored in the comparison when the image has no alpha; the picked twin stays shown). The plug-in keeps no preset file and no user presets; the owner may ask for them later. One index base (M4): `PresetState` stores the seed index 0..4, or None for Custom; the list index is seed index + 1 and the conversion happens only at the widget boundary. The pure logic (`apply_preset`, `match_preset`, `PresetState`, `plan_refresh`, `preset_event`) lives in `psdds_ctypes.py` and is unit-tested without gi (M5); `refresh` (gi) is covered by the Task 7 owner check. DC34 (sRGB off by default) and DC39 (sRGB sets only the tag, the filter stays editable with it off) hold through psdds. DC45: picking Custom stays on Custom until a seed is picked. DC38, DC42, DC44 and DC40's preset-file protection are n/a: GIMP hands the plug-in one merged image, the exported layer's own alpha is the only alpha source, GIMP has no PiPL, and there is no preset file (owner decision 13).
- **DG7 Formats per type (DC32).** The Format list is rebuilt from `psdds_format_offered(type, format, depth)` when the type changes, keeps the raw pick, and shows the type's default (BC7) when the pick is not offered (BC6H and RGBA16F are offered for Colour at depth 16 and 32 only, Note DF2).
- **DG8 Export works on a flattened copy only (preflight M7).** The plug-in uses the export image GIMP hands over, or duplicates the image, merges the visible layers on that copy, resizes the merged layer to the canvas, reads it, and deletes the copy (libgimp requires the delete). The user's image is never resized, flattened or changed. Batch cases cover a single layer, two layers, an offset layer, all layers hidden (error "There are no visible layers to export."), and one visible layer among hidden ones. A save writes `<path>.tmpsave`, flushes, `fsync`s and `os.replace`s, so a failed encode leaves an existing file byte-identical (Note BC10 equivalent). psdds's error text is passed through unchanged, because GIMP adds no full stop (DC30 analogue).
- **DG9 Run modes, owner decision 2026-10-26 (branch review I1).** INTERACTIVE shows the dialog; Cancel writes nothing. WITH_LAST_VALS (File > Overwrite, Export to) and NONINTERACTIVE show no dialog; GIMP loads its remembered values over the passed arguments (measured). **Overwrite and Export to run with the last values without a dialog, also for a freshly opened DDS** (review I1 pointed out that such an image has no per-image values, so GIMP falls back to the global last values: an opened BC5 normal map can be re-saved with the settings of the last diffuse; the Photoshop DC22 hazard). The owner chose to keep owner decision 4 and not to add a first-time dialog. Cost: that silent re-save. The README warns of it and names File > Export As. Task 7 checks it on an opened normal map.
- **DG10 No-UI guard and the Task 5 incident.** On Windows `gimp-console -i` does not stop a dialog: during Task 5 a mutation check opened a real "Export Image as Tessalith DDS" window on the owner's desktop (temp profile only; the batch runner's kill failed because `taskkill.exe` was not on PATH, and the agent killed the processes by hand; no real profile was touched). Rule since: `refuse_ui()` is the first statement of `show_dialog`, before any GimpUi import, and raises when `TDDS_NO_UI` is set; `run_batch.ps1` sets it, uses `taskkill` by full path with `/T`, takes `-TimeoutSec` (default 240) and prints `FAIL timeout`. `run.ps1 -KillProbe` proves the kill (a windowless sleeping child must be gone). Batch tests run headless with an isolated profile (`GIMP3_DIRECTORY`, `GIMP3_CACHEDIR`, update check off) and never start the GIMP GUI. Known gap: the guard does not cover the delegated `file-dds-load` in INTERACTIVE mode (review L5).
- **DG11 Reset inference (review F3) and its Task 7 gate.** GIMP 3.0.4 has no public Reset response id; "Reset to Initial Values" and "Reset to Factory Defaults" arrive later as property notifies. The plug-in treats any response other than OK, Cancel, Help or delete as "reset pending" and reads the next unguarded `preset` notify through pure `preset_event`: a pending 0 or an already-shown value is a reset (clears the Custom latch, refreshes), anything else is a user pick. This is unproven against the real dialog. **Task 7 is a hard gate:** after each Reset entry the list shows the matching seed, then picking Custom keeps it on Custom. Known edges: Reset opened and dismissed, then Custom picked, reads as a reset, so no latch; "Initial Values" with a seed other than the one shown arriving before the raw notifies reads as a pick of that seed (it overwrites only greyed raw values); re-picking Custom while Custom is shown fires no notify, so it does not latch; the `shown-discard-alpha` and other `shown-*` resets can write a shown value into a raw argument (review N1). Fallback if the gate fails: never latch Custom (the owner's call; it loses DC45).
- **DG12 Image precision to depth (Task 5b, ABI 3).** `tdds_pixels.precision_depth(precision, texture_type)`: U8 gives 8; U16 and U32 give 16; HALF, FLOAT and DOUBLE give 32. **u32 maps to depth 16 (owner brief; the review had 32) and double maps to 32.** The export calls `psdds_resolve_depth` and `psdds_encode_depth` at that depth; `psdds_encode` is the 8-bit form. Read format: Colour at depth 8 and 16 is read as `"R'G'B'A float"` (sRGB-coded, babl converts), at depth 32 as linear `"RGBA float"` (psdds's one rule for 32-bit Colour, DF3: BC6H and RGBA16F keep values above 1, the LDR formats clip). **Normal and Linear mask are read in the image's own encoding (ruling, 2026-10-26): linear-TRC precisions as `"RGBA float"`, non-linear and perceptual ones as `"R'G'B'A float"`; no transfer conversion, because they are data.** Cost, on purpose: an 8-bit linear Normal or Linear mask image now writes different bytes than before Task 5b (the old read converted it to sRGB-coded); 8-bit non-linear images, GIMP's default, are unchanged and pinned. Alpha is the same in either read format, so DC31's order holds; the pixels are read again after OK only when the effective type switches between Colour and data. This supersedes the earlier read ruling (always `"R'G'B'A float"`, owner decision 6) for depth 16 and 32 and for the data types. A `shortcut:` marks that the float buffer and the copy stay alive across the modal dialog (16 bytes a pixel, about 4 GiB at 16384 x 16384). Task 7 checks switching type on a 32-bit or linear image.
- **DG13 Discard transparency greys per psdds (Note DF2, amends DC36).** `discard_enabled` from `psdds_resolve_depth` greys the checkbox and shows it ticked (effective 1) for BC1, BC4, BC5 and BC6H, at every depth, through `shown-discard-alpha` and `discard-alpha-enabled`. The raw `discard-alpha` argument (bool, default off) is stored, scriptable and remembered like the others; an older settings file loads it as off.
- **DG14 Licence layout (controller ruling 2026-10-25, supersedes M8; applies to all three hosts).** The zip ships `COPYING` (the plug-in's GPL-3.0-or-later text, the full text copied from `chainner\COPYING`), `LICENSE` (psdds.dll's MIT text from `crates\psdds\LICENSE`, because `notices.ps1` writes "(see LICENSE)"), `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (from `notices.ps1`, plus one closing paragraph naming the split), `README.md`, and `tessalith-dds/` with the three `.py` files and `psdds.dll`. The plug-in's `.py` files are GPL-3.0-or-later (GIMP's own Python plug-ins are too); only the psdds crate is MIT; the engine and encoders-sys code inside `psdds.dll` is MPL-2.0 (DC41, source pointer in the notices); the vendored encoders keep their own licences. Nothing linked blocks a GPL-3.0-or-later plug-in, and nothing in the package or docs may call the engine MIT.
- **DG15 Package check.** `gimp\package.ps1` runs `crates\psdds\build.ps1`, stages, zips to `dist\TessalithDDS-GIMP-<workspace version>.zip` plus `.sha256.txt` (`dist\` is not committed), then asserts: the zip holds exactly that file list (every `.py` the plug-in folder has, which the plug-in imports); the packaged `psdds.dll` equals the built one byte for byte; `COPYING` is the full GPL-3.0 text and `LICENSE` the MIT text; the notices carry the MPL-2.0 text; and the packaged wrapper loads the packaged DLL, which proves `psdds_abi_version()` equals `EXPECTED_ABI` (3). It needs `cargo-about` and fails when it is missing. The DLL path is `target\psdds\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\release\psdds.dll`.
- **DG16 Open follow-ups.** Branch review lows still open when this note was written: L2 (fixed `.tmpsave` name, truncated on open), L3 (raw OSError text), L4 (`run.ps1` leaks `TESSALITH_PSDDS_DLL` into the caller's shell), L5 (UI guard and delegation); N2 (a DDS psdds refuses by size is not handed to file-dds). The Task 7 owner check is the gate for the dialog (layout, Reset, native widgets) and for the Overwrite behaviour in DG9.
- **DG17 ABI 4 and Alpha is transparency (Task 5c, owner 2026-10-26, Note DH).** `EXPECTED_ABI` is 4 (supersedes the 3 named in DG1 and DG15, which stay as history). The ctypes `Settings` has the eight fields of `psdds.h` (`alpha_mode` last, offset 28, 32 bytes) and `Controls` four (`alpha_mode_enabled` at 12, 16 bytes); a unit test reads both structs from the header and compares names, order and sizes. `psdds.dll` and the zip are rebuilt; the package check asserts `abi 4`.
- **DG18 The checkbox.** "Alpha is transparency" is a raw boolean argument `alpha-mode` (default off, from `psdds_defaults`; an older `.last` or per-image settings file without it loads as off, which is alpha_mode 0), with aux `shown-alpha-mode` and `alpha-mode-enabled`, the same shown/raw pattern as Discard (DG13): the shown value is the effective `alpha_mode` from `psdds_resolve_depth`, the box is greyed by `alpha_mode_enabled` (DH2), and a click on a greyed box never reaches the raw argument, so the pick comes back when alpha is kept again. Deviation from Photoshop (DH7, which shows the raw pick on the greyed box): here a greyed box shows unticked, like every other greyed GIMP control (DG4). It sits in its own row directly under the Format and Discard transparency row, left-aligned (the right-hand slot holds sRGB and Discard); the Mipmaps/Filter and Quality rows follow. Seed picks write `alpha_mode` with the other seven values (all seeds have 0, DH1).
- **DG19 Presets and bytes.** Matching compares effective settings (DC37, DC40, DH3), so a raw `alpha_mode` 1 on an image without kept alpha still matches its seed and no host rule was added; with kept alpha, ticking the box shows Custom. The export passes `alpha_mode` to `psdds_encode_depth` unchanged and no Python rule reads it. DH6 holds: with kept alpha as data the filter stays editable. Batch case `export_alpha_mode_keeps_colour_or_transparency`: 8x8 image, left half colour (200,30,60) at alpha 0, BC7, Discard off; the default export equals psdds with alpha_mode 0 and the decoded colour under alpha 0 is within 12 of the source; with `alpha-mode` on it equals psdds with alpha_mode 1 and the colour is changed. `export_8_bit_bytes_unchanged` keeps its default-settings expectations, so 8-bit bytes with kept alpha changed with the DLL, as DH5 says. The unit suite is 49 tests (layout, greying, effective matching, encode pass-through).
- **DG20 Task 7 additions.** (a) The "Alpha is transparency" box sits directly under Discard transparency, is unticked at first, and is greyed on an opaque image, with Discard transparency ticked, and for BC1, BC4, BC5 and BC6H; it is editable for BC3, BC7, RGBA8 and RGBA16F on an image with transparent pixels. (b) Ticking it on such an image greys the filter at Box and shows Custom; unticking restores both (DH6). (c) Reset (DG11) covers this control: after Reset to Initial Values and Reset to Factory Defaults the box is unticked and the Preset list shows the matching seed, and picking Custom afterwards stays on Custom. (d) Re-saving with Overwrite (DG9) uses the remembered `alpha-mode` like the other values.
- **DG21 Final review follow-ups (controller, 2026-10-26).** `gimp\tests\run.ps1` now restores `TESSALITH_PSDDS_DLL` on exit (closes DG16's leak item and makes DG1 true); the package's engine-MIT check can now fail; a type switch in the dialog frees the first pixel read before the second. Known limit, not measured: data maps (Normal, Linear mask) are read with bare babl names, which assume sRGB primaries, so an image carrying a non-sRGB colour profile may be colour-converted on read. Upgrade if a user reports it: drop the profile on the plug-in's own copy for data types before reading.

## Note DJ — Multi-layer parallax flag on an Environment Map shader (NIF session, 2026-10-27)

- **DJ1 (in-game finding).** Sphere `ShaderSpheres01:9` was changed from type 11 to type 1 (Environment Map) with SLSF2 bit 24 (Multi_Layer_Parallax) left set and no PBR bit. The game crashed the first time it drew it: an access violation under CS `PBR_BSLightingShader_SetupMaterial`, reading through a pointer of 0x3F800000 (1.0f, the Envmap material's env scale).
  - The A/B rerun cleared only bit 24 and kept the shape's two U/V offset float controllers. It drew and did not crash.
  - Record: `nifparseref\plan\cubemap-up-axis\results.md`.
- **DJ2 (validator).** Bit 24 without bit 23 on a drawn type-1 shader is an Error in `ALWAYS_BLOCK` (`MLP_ENV_MAP`), with a fix that clears the bit.
  - With bit 23 set, bit 24 is the CS two-layer coat, so it is left alone.
  - Other non-11 types keep the existing Warn: only type 1 is confirmed (`shortcut:` comment in `validate.rs`).
- **DJ3 (type change).** Changing the shader type away from 11 clears bit 24 in the same undo step, with a notice (`type_slsf2_fix`), unless PBR is on. This applies to every target type, because without type 11 the flag does nothing (the existing Warn).
- **DJ4.** The controllers are not guarded: the A/B cleared them of blame. `set_shader_type` stays a pure re-emit, so the ops stay explicit.

## Note DL — The preview's panorama mapping runs clockwise, like a 360° photo (NIF team, owner-directed, 2026-10-27)

- **DL1 (in-game finding).** `hdri::dir_to_uv` had `u` grow counter-clockwise seen from above (east, then north). A normal 360° photo runs the other way.
  - A cube made with that mapping showed a panorama's N sector on world south in game, while E and W were correct (`nifparseref\plan\cubemap-up-axis\results.md`, "Second check").
  - So the preview's backdrop, ambient and env cube showed the bundled studio HDRI mirrored.
- **DL2.** The mapping is now `u = 0.5 − (atan2(y, x) + YAW) / 2π`, and `uv_to_dir` inverts it.
  - This is used by `dir_to_uv`, `uv_to_dir`, `cube_faces` and the backdrop shader, one definition as before.
  - The yaw sense is unchanged: a feature at azimuth φ shows at φ + yaw.
  - Test: `moving_right_in_the_image_turns_clockwise`.
- **DL3.** `YAW` goes from −2.798 to 0.774 (= −2·atan2(0.8, 0.5) + 2.798), so the HDRI's key light stays at the default sun's azimuth. `studio_key_light_faces_the_default_sun` holds unchanged.
- **DL4 (tests).** The mirrored sky gives env-cube averages whose sums are not exact halves. WARP stores those rounded toward zero, not to nearest. The composite tests' `assert_store` now accepts nearest-even or toward-zero on every channel, where before it allowed toward-zero only on exact ties. D3D11 allows either rounding for a float-to-f16 store, and the two forward DC tests go through it too.
- **DL5 (for the main team).** The cubemap plan's equirect importer uses this same lat-long definition at yaw 0 (centre column = east), so it inherits the clockwise sense. The owner is directing the plan fix.

## Note DM — Per-type encode versions for if-changed (owner, 2026-10-26)

The letter DM is provisional (DJ, DK and DL are taken on main as of 2026-10-27); rename at merge if taken.

- **DM1 The table.** `manifest::encode_version(Subtype)` is an exhaustive `match` keyed by `Subtype` only, so a new sub-type fails to compile until it has an arm. Its value is the engine version of that type's last output change. A record without `encode_version` (written by 1.0.0) counts as `LEGACY_ENCODE_VERSION`, 1.0.0. `if-changed` compares the record's `encode_version` with the current arm instead of the engine version.
- **DM2 Baseline (Task 1).** The v1.0.0 tag and the branch were run on the same corpus under both targets. `differing` is empty and `encoders-differ` is none. All 29 sub-types were produced and are identical under cs (46 outputs), and the 30 vanilla outputs are identical. Under vanilla, 13 cs-only sub-types are refused identically by both builds (CFG-UNAVAILABLE); they are ruled not differing, since they cannot exist under vanilla. So every arm is 1.0.0 and upgrading from 1.0.0 re-encodes nothing.
- **DM3 `ManifestRecord.encode_version` is an `Option`.** Also export deserialises twins written by 1.0.0, which have no such field. A copy made by Also export records the current version.
- **DM4 What the guard hashes, and its blind spots.** `cargo test -p engine --test encode_versions` (feature `test-hooks`) hashes the encoder input, not the encoded bytes: the DDS header, per mip level a u64 LE length plus the texels (Ldr bytes in order; Hdr as u16 LE), the SHA-256 of the resolved profile JSON, and the validation verdict (`passed`). It runs the fixture under both targets and pins 55 outputs: 35 under cs, covering all 29 sub-types (`UNGUARDED` is empty), and 20 under vanilla (keys prefixed `vanilla/`), covering the 16 sub-types vanilla allows. Vanilla refuses the 13 cs-only sub-types (CFG-UNAVAILABLE, `CS_ONLY` in the test), and the test asserts exactly those, plus the two `_rmaos` set members, are refused. A change to any of those must come with the type's arm moving to the new engine version, or the test fails. Blind spots, which a human must bump for: validation-verdict changes that do not show in `passed` on the fixtures; the engine's post-encode steps in `encode.rs` (`bc7_opaque_fix`, the grass corner guard, `pack_uncompressed`); the profile-to-encoder-parameter mapping in `encode.rs` (`bc7_level`, `radius`); paths without a fixture (NVTT outputs, derived jobs); and an output key renamed and changed in the same commit (check_pins pins the new key fresh). Stated risk: the hash assumes the engine's float path is deterministic for one source tree. `.cargo/config` sets no `target-cpu`, and the thread-count check (RAYON_NUM_THREADS 1, 8 and default) passed.
- **DM5 Profile pin and the optional-field rule.** A second pin hashes every built-in profile: 6 ids x 2 targets x 29 sub-types = 348 keys. `registry.profile` returns Ok for every combination, and the test asserts all 348 keys are observed, so a combination that newly becomes Err fails it. A new `Profile` field must be `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]` and skipped at its default, so existing profile hashes do not move.
- **DM5b `RELEASED_ENGINE_VERSION`.** The spec's rule "pass if the entry equals ENGINE_VERSION" would accept every change while the engine still carries a released version (today every arm is 1.0.0 = ENGINE_VERSION). So a changed hash passes only when the arm equals `ENGINE_VERSION` and `ENGINE_VERSION` is not `RELEASED_ENGINE_VERSION`. The release commit sets `RELEASED_ENGINE_VERSION = ENGINE_VERSION`.
- **DM6 No test override.** The spec's Testing section asked for a test-only table override. `encode_current` unit tests replace it with the same coverage, so shipped code has no override hook.
- **DM7 Supersedes DB1.** DB1's "re-encodes each recorded output once after upgrading" no longer holds for later versions: only a type whose arm moved re-encodes.
- **DM8 Semantic versioning (owner, 2026-10-27, https://semver.org/).** From 1.0.0 on, the workspace version follows MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. MAJOR: a change that breaks existing use (a removed or renamed `sdc.toml`/preset key, CLI flag or exit code, a manifest a previous version cannot read, a removed feature). MINOR: a new backward-compatible feature (new sub-type, setting, command, export). PATCH: a backward-compatible bug fix, including one that changes some type's output (that type's `encode_version` arm moves to the patch version). Pre-releases use `-alpha.N` / `-rc.N`. Cubemap support is the next minor: 1.1.0.

## Note DN — A lost graphics device closes the app with a message instead of a panic (owner asked for a fix, 2026-10-27)

Follows Note AR. No `crash-*.log` with the AR5 "wgpu device lost" line has been recorded since, so what loses the device is still unproven. This is handling, not a cause fix.

- **DN1 Where the app can step in.** wgpu-core 30 `Device::handle_hal_error` calls `lose()`, which runs the device-lost callback synchronously on the thread that made the failing call: the GUI thread, inside frame N's submit, present or acquire. egui-wgpu's panic comes in frame N+1's `paint_and_update_textures`, after `SdcApp::ui` for N+1 has run. So `ui()` is the last point before the panic.
- **DN2 What it does.** The callback sets `crash_log::DEVICE_LOST`. The first thing `SdcApp::ui` does is check it and call `crash_log::close_after_device_loss`. That writes the unsaved documents' recovery files (AR6's snapshot, the same `write_recovery`), adds a line to the run's crash log, shows an error dialog listing the `.recovery` files (rfd, no GPU), and runs `std::process::exit(1)`. `ViewportCommand::Close` would not work, because eframe still paints that frame. `on_exit` does not run, so a layout change in its 2 s wait is lost.
- **DN3 No recovery in place.** eframe 0.36 cannot recreate its device, so the app still closes. Relaunching itself with the same folder was left out: `main` takes no folder argument, and it would need a guard against a relaunch loop. That is the next step if the owner wants it.
- **DN4 Test.** `device_lost.rs` asserts `device_lost()` is false before `destroy()` and true after. The dialog and the exit are not tested, because they would end the test process.

## Note DO — Set header: the JSON editor button no longer covers the name; the input name list works in a project without a `textures` folder (owner report, 2026-10-27)

- **DO1 Button beside the name.** On a JSON set the header row is `egui::Sides` with `shrink_left().truncate()`: the "TruePBR JSON editor…" button lays out first on the right, and the set's name takes what is left, truncated with the full name on hover (egui-ui-rules 3.3). The row is capped at the visible edge, because a wider card below widens the scroll content (rule 3.8). Before, a long name ran under the button and pushed it past the panel edge.
- **DO2 Input name paths in the set's form.** A project with no `textures` folder in its path names its sets `clutter/...` (`discover::game_path` falls back to `rel`), while every scan path starts with `textures/`. So nothing fell under the path lock, and the ▾ list said "No known paths yet: scan your mods". `model::input_name::in_form_of` now drops `textures/` from the offered paths when the set's own name has none, for the ▾ list, the live rows and the gray completion. A pick then names the set in the project's own form, which `input_name_plan` accepts (its prefix is empty there).
- **DO3 The empty-list line tells the truth.** When the scan has paths but none fall under the lock, the ▾ list says "No known paths under <prefix>: move the path lock left to see more." "No known paths yet" stays for an empty scan.
- **DO4 Match selector (owner, 2026-10-27).** On a TruePBR JSON set (`is_json_set`), a combo beside the input name box picks the slot the ▾ list works on: "Match 1 · diffuse" (the default) to "Match 8 · backlight", using the JSON editor's `SLOT_NAMES` in its list. The box itself reads "Match 1" (64 pt), and it is drawn only in the 2D view: a wider one, or one in the 3D view's header, wrapped that row at 1024×768 and cost the 3D frame its height (`set_preview_layout` tests). Slot 1 is the existing list: paths under the lock, and a pick renames the set's inputs. Slots 2–8 list `known_textures(Some(n - 1))` (no lock; `textures/pbr/` left out, AO8), and a pick stores `match{n}` through `stored_set_match` with `\` separators, as the JSON editor's picker does. Owner's ruling: a slot 2–8 pick sets that match only and renames nothing. Other matches, `match1` included, stay as they are (the Matching group's × removes one).
- **DO5 All slots and the auto switch.** The list's **All slots** box lists `known_textures(None)`. A pick goes to `input_name::pick_slot`: the selector's slot when the scan saw the path there or never saw it in slots 1–8, else the lowest slot it was seen in. So a normal picked from "All slots" under Match 1 sets `match2` and moves the selector to Match 2; a diffuse picked under Match 2 renames the set.
- **DO6 Not stored.** The selector and All slots live in egui memory per set for the session; nothing goes to `sdc-project.toml`. shortcut: the selector does not start from the set's existing matches; derive it from the lowest active `matchN` if owners expect that.

## Note DP — Generate button under Assign, zoom in the Generate preview, one Z warning with Rebuild Z (owner request, 2026-10-27)

Three small changes to Generate from normal map (Note CO) and to the warning a short normal gets.

- **DP1 Where the button goes.** "Under Assign" means a button directly below the **Assign…** button, in the slot row's format column. **Assign…** shows only on an empty slot. On a filled Height or RMAOS row the button goes in the same place, below the format combo.
- **DP2 Hidden for packed.** There is no button when the slot's item is `ItemKind::Packed`, its own or borrowed (a Share). The slot menu's "Generate from normal map…" entry (Note CO) stays. Measured in Task 1: the button shares its accessible name with that menu entry. A disabled button's hover shows the full label, a newline, then `gen_entry`'s reason. A slot filled through the slot menu's path link (`SlotLink`) only writes `slotN` into the set's settings and draws no row item, so it never shows the button.
- **DP3 Zoom in place.** The dialog stays modal and one window. Zoom works inside the preview tiles, which stay 160 pt (the first plan grew them to 240 pt; the final review showed that pushes Strength and Relief out of view, and the owner's "keeping the editor visible" outweighs bigger tiles, so zoom makes up for the size). They wrap only as a fallback: three tiles fit one row at the 640 pt body. The wheel zooms 1 to 16 times around the pointer, a drag pans, a double-click fits. All tiles share one crop, read once per frame. The zoom resets when the dialog reopens. The line under the tiles is always reserved, so the dialog does not resize when zoom starts. Measured in Task 2: in egui 0.36.2 `ScrollArea` reads `smooth_scroll_delta` in `Prepared::end`, after its content (`containers/scroll_area.rs` about 1219-1247). Zeroing it inside a hovered tile therefore stops the dialog body scrolling, but only when the wheel changed the zoom: at fit (wheel out) and at 16 times (wheel in) the delta passes through and the body scrolls. 0.36.2 has no `raw_scroll_delta` field.
- **DP4 One warning for a short normal, in the engine.** `policy::contradictions` drops its "does not decode to unit normals" line, because CHAN-NORMAL-LENGTH fires on the same condition. That fixes the CLI and the texture panel too. SUG-CONTRADICTION stays for its other causes (grayscale source, complex material with solid 255 alpha, a colour map that looks like a normal). One row until you fix it; the last export's row stays until you export again. `problems()` skips a last-export row whose job maps to exactly one item that has a live warning with the same code (any code), because the live row is the current truth and carries the fix button. After Rebuild Z the live warning is gone, so the export row comes back: the file on disk is still short until the next export. It has no button.
- **DP5 Rebuild Z.** The remaining CHAN-NORMAL-LENGTH Problems row has a **Rebuild Z** button that sets the file's `channels.reconstruct_z` (`set_field`). It is disabled with the read-only reason (`fix_off`), as the other fix buttons are. Its hover says it is only for normal maps, because it replaces the blue channel.
- **DP6 Encode versions (Note DM).** Removing the contradiction changes a warning, not a validation verdict or an output byte. `cargo test -p engine --test encode_versions` and `--test golden` pass unchanged, so no `encode_version` arm moved and no pin JSON was rewritten.
- **DP7 Known limits (final review, left as they are).** (a) gen_entry runs every frame for the Height and RMAOS rows of the open set, at most two calls a frame, and bumps gen_lookups() each time. (b) The slot-row Generate button and the slot menu entry share one AccessKit name; tests scope by rect (menu_generate). (c) The zoom reset compares gen_opens with an egui temp value, so an AppModel rebuilt while the egui context lives on could keep a stale zoom for one reopen; main.rs builds the model once. (d) After Rebuild Z on an already exported file, the Texture row goes and a File row with the same text and no button comes back until the next export. (e) With Height + AO or all three maps ticked at 800 pt, the 160 pt tile row is cut at the fold (10 to 50 pt measured at 1100x800); Strength stays in view and the body scrolls.

## Note DQ — A diffuse made Advanced skin switches its set's packed RMAOS to RFAOS (owner report, 2026-10-27)

- DQ1. Setting the Diffuse-slot member's sub-type to `skin_albedo` also sets `packing.recipe = "rfaos"` on the set's packed output (`set_packing_recipe`), in the same undo step. Before, the set became Advanced skin but kept packing `_rmaos`. Picking RFAOS on the packed card already did the reverse (it moves the diffuse to `skin_albedo`).
- DQ2. A set that cannot build `_rfaos` (metallic-only sources, `PACK-RECIPE-UNBUILDABLE`) still takes the sub-type and keeps `_rmaos`.
- DQ3. It works both ways (owner, same day): taking the diffuse off `skin_albedo` to another sub-type sets `packing.recipe = "rmaos"` on the set's packed `_rfaos`, in the same undo step. A reset of the diffuse's sub-type changes no recipe, because it falls back to the engine's suggestion, which is `skin_albedo` again while the set packs `_rfaos`. A pre-packed `_rfaos` file (not a packed output) is never touched.

## Note DR — A skin _f fills the RFAOS fuzz mask (owner, 2026-10-27)

The letter DR is provisional; rename at merge if taken.

- DR1. Fuzz PBR and Advanced skin fuzz are two different things. A PBR `_f` is RGBA (fuzz colour plus weight) and converts alone as `pbr_fuzz`. A skin `_f` is a greyscale mask like a metallic map, which CS reads as the RFAOS G channel (`skinFuzzMask`).
- DR2. In a cs set that is already Advanced skin by other evidence (`set_is_advanced_skin`: an explicit `packing.recipe = rfaos`, which Note DQ writes when the diffuse becomes skin_albedo; an `_rfaos` member; or a `_fuzz`/`_sheen` raw map), a `_f` whose sub-type no user, rule or project-file choice named is a packing input with role `Fuzz` (`policy::resolve_file_with`). It is read like a `_fuzz` map into the `_rfaos` G channel and, like any consumed raw map, is not exported as its own `_f.dds`.
- DR3. `_f` never makes a set Advanced skin by itself. `_f` is not in `RawMap::INPUTS`, so `set_is_advanced_skin` does not see it (no cycle). `_ao` + `_roughness` + `_f` on auto still builds `_rmaos` and `_f` stays a `pbr_fuzz` job. A set with only a diffuse and `_f` is not skin either.
- DR4. Plumbing. `plan_packing` takes the role from the job's `JobStatus::PackingInput { role }` when the file name has none. `api::map_members` skips jobs with that status.
- DR5. A failed or cancelled skin `_f` fails the recipe. It has no job, so `plan_packing` recognises it with `pack::plan::is_skin_f` (suffix `f`, no requested sub-type, set already Advanced skin) and gives it the `Fuzz` role; the `_rfaos` is then Failed by Note M11 instead of building with G at its default. Limit (shortcut): a sub-type named by a rule needs the analysis a failed file lacks, so a failed `_f` that a rule typed is still treated as fuzz; `--set` and `[files]` choices are honoured.
- DR6. Encode version. No arm moved. `golden` and `encode_versions` pass unchanged, and no fixture holds a skin set with `_f`. Only the `_rfaos` of a skin set that has a `_f` changes (G was the default, now the mask). The pipeline records every packed source (`pipeline.rs`) and `api.rs` compares them for if-changed, so that output is re-encoded without a version bump.
- DR7. A real `_fuzz`/`_sheen` wins G (review). `skin_f_candidate` is false when the set's suffixes hold the `fuzz` role (`_sheen` canonicalises to it, `group.rs`), because `_f` sorts first by path (Note M13) and would take G and leave `_fuzz` PACK-UNUSED-INPUT. Such a set keeps `_f` as a `pbr_fuzz` job, as before this note.
- DR8. One predicate (review). `pack::plan::skin_f_candidate` (image, suffix `f`, no Fuzz raw map, set already Advanced skin) is shared: `policy::resolve_file_with` adds its provenance check and `is_skin_f` adds `!subtype_requested`. Policy now also requires an image, as `raw_role` does. The `plan_packing` job-status fallback admits images only, so a re-encoded raw-map DDS (`x_roughness.dds`) keeps its old behaviour. No test: a raw-map DDS reaching `PackingInput` needs a re-encode request plus a valid DDS fixture, which the engine tests do not build.
- DR9. Stale `_f.dds` (review). A skin set's `_f` is no longer written, so a `_f.dds` from an earlier export stays in the export folder and is not removed. Note CQ does not cover it: CQ compacts the blocks of an exported NIF and deletes no texture. No cleanup of exported DDS files exists; the owner deletes the stale file by hand.

## Note DS — Cubemap support v1 (owner + builder, 2026-10-26)

- **DS1 Cube maths moves into the engine.** `cube_dir`, the lat-long `dir_to_uv`/`uv_to_dir`, `Hdr` and `decode_rgbe` (with `MAX_SIDE`/`MAX_PIXELS`) moved from `render3d::hdri` into `engine::cube` (`cube/mod.rs`, `latlong.rs`, `rgbe.rs`), plus `engine::cube::FACES`. Owner decision 2: the cubemap pipeline and the preview share one definition. The engine `dir_to_uv`/`uv_to_dir` take a `yaw` parameter (same formulas and operation order, the clockwise mapping of NIF Note DL); render3d's `YAW` is a preview calibration and stays in render3d, whose `dir_to_uv(d)`/`uv_to_dir(u, v)` now call the engine with `YAW`. render3d re-exports `cube_dir`, `decode_rgbe` and `Hdr`. Every render3d test is untouched and now exercises the engine copy; no behaviour change.

- **DS2 Separate cube entry points, no `DdsDesc.cube` field.** Single cubemaps are written by `dds::dds_bytes_cube` and `dds::header_bytes_with(desc, mips, true)` (`header_bytes` is `header_bytes_with(.., false)`); `DdsDesc` does not gain a `cube` field as the spec said. A field would break 45 `DdsDesc` literals across engine, bench and the GUI for no behavioural gain, and 2D bytes are untouched either way. Cube files carry COMPLEX even at one mip, caps2 `0xFE00`, DX10 misc 4, and are refused unless square (`DdsError::CubeShape`). `DdsFile::surfaces()` lists all six faces' levels; `check_header` applies cube rules (COMPLEX, caps2 exactly `0xFE00` else "partial cube", square, DX10 dimension 3 / array 1 / misc 4) when `is_cubemap`.

- **DS3 Two Task 3 acceptance tests adapted to what the geometry allows.** (a) `blur_one_flattens` uses an arrow-like cube with muted face colours (0.40 + 0.04·face) and passes at std-dev below 1/3 of the input's, not 1/4: the plan's blur (σ = 22.5°, cut at 45°) brings five faces to 0.15–0.19, but on −Z the +Y and −Z white bands meet at one edge and form a band twice as wide, which stays at 0.26. With the saturated Task 5 `arrow_faces` the ratio is 0.41–0.53 for any correct cone blur, because a 45° cone mixes the neighbouring faces' colours into each face; do not swap that helper into this test without a new criterion. (b) `adjacent_edges_match_at_every_level` applies the flat 0.02 only at sizes ≥ 32 (at 2×2 a texel spans 45°, so neighbours on a smooth gradient differ by far more); at every size ≥ 2 the jump across a seam must stay below the in-face step beside it + 0.02. (c) `fetch` at a cube corner: the bilinear tap that falls outside the face in both x and y takes the mean of the other three taps (the classic seamless-cube corner rule), so the corner direction reads the three meeting faces in equal thirds; averaging only the two edge taps would give ¼, ⅜, ⅜.

- **DS4 `Subtype::Cubemap`, the `cubemap` section and styles.** `cubemap` is appended last to `Subtype` (category Color; `_e` or a `cubemaps` folder component suggests it at High). `sdc-base` 1.2.0 gives it `color = { content = "srgb", tag = "unorm" }`; everything else comes from `[defaults]` (BC7, alpha remove, full mips). `Profile.cubemap` (`CubemapSpec`) has every key optional and skipped at its default, and Resolve resets it (and drops `cubemap.*` provenance) for every other sub-type, so no 2D `profile_sha256` changes (the pin file gained only the 12 `*/cubemap` keys). The 14 `cubemap.*` keys are in `overrides::FIELD_PATHS`, so `--set`, `[files]`, rules and presets accept them. `cubemap.style` fills, after `--set`, the keys no explicit layer set, at sub-type-table reach without a pin, so the backend follows the style's format (BC1 → rgbcx): `vanilla_metal` 32 / bc1 / blur 0.6 / saturation 0.8, `room` 128 / bc1 / 0.35, `eye` 256 / bc7 / 0.35, `hd` 512 / bc7 / 0.1. `color.tag` is set UNORM the same way; an explicit sRGB stays and is refused.

- **DS5 Cube checks.** Encodings: BC1, BC3, BC7 or RGBA8 with UNORM, anything else `CFG-INVALID` (so `allowed_encodings(cubemap, t)` is exactly those four under both targets). The source-size `DIM-NPOT`/`DIM-SMALL` checks are skipped for a cube (its source is a cross, strip or panorama, not a face); Task 5 adds face-size checks. `mips.levels = none` (or a count of 0 or 1) warns `CUBE-NO-MIPS`. Ranges, `CFG-INVALID`: `face_size` a power of two in 4..=4096, `face_rotate` each 0/90/180/270, `blur` 0..=1, `exposure` −10..=10, `brightness`/`contrast` −1..=1, `midtones` 0.1..=10, `saturation` 0..=2, `highlight_clamp` ≥ 1. The low-detail check (CHK-LOW-DETAIL) never runs on a cube. New codes `CUBE-FACES` (Error) and `CUBE-NO-MIPS` (Warning).

- **DS6 Version 1.1.0.** `encode_version(Cubemap) = "1.1.0"` and the workspace is 1.1.0 in the same commit (semver MINOR: a new feature, Note DM8); every 2D arm and `RELEASED_ENGINE_VERSION` stay 1.0.0, so `if-changed` re-encodes no 2D output. Until Task 5's cube writer exists, the encode-versions fixture `h/cubemap.png` (64×64 RGB) encodes through the 2D path and is pinned as such (cs and vanilla); Task 7 re-pins with a 6:1 strip fixture (384×64; a square cube has no layout, DS8); Task 8 re-pinned both once cube encoding existed (the strip now encodes as a 64² cube; only the two `*/cubemap` pins moved, DS10). The guard accepts both because the arm is bumped in this unreleased cycle.
- **DS7 Raw-face layouts and cube DDS input (Task 5).** A one-image cubemap source is a cross or a strip, found from its exact aspect ratio (4:3 h-cross, 3:4 v-cross, 6:1 h-strip, 1:6 v-strip; square and anything else is not a layout) or set with `cubemap.layout`; cell offsets are texassemble's. A guessed cross whose unused cells are not flat (any channel spread over 2/255) is refused as a picture; a layout the user set is trusted. Face size is `cubemap.face_size`, else the largest power of two within the source cell, and the cube's DIM checks read that face (after `drop_top_mip`): DIM-RESIZED when it differs from the cell, DIM-SMALL below 4, never DIM-NPOT; with no layout there are no DIM checks (the planner marks the file unclear). A float cube source with peak luminance above 1 and no `cubemap.highlight_clamp` gets LOSS-CLAMP-HDR naming that key (it replaces the generic float notice for cubes). The S6 2D-only guard is lifted for single cube DDS files (arraySize 1) only: the file loads as a 6:1 strip of its mip-0 faces (`SourceMeta.dds_cube`, `Analysis.dds_cube`), is decided as a cubemap (`cube-dds` analysis fact) unless an explicit sub-type says otherwise (then CFG-INVALID, "a cube DDS can only be re-encoded as a cubemap"), and still needs re-encode opt-in like any DDS (`IN-DDS-SKIPPED`). Cube arrays stay refused, and `sdc patch` keeps refusing cubes.

- **DN7a (fix round 1).** `load::image_size` on a cube DDS is the face size (the MAX_DIM cap is about the face, intended) while the load is 6w x h; `api::input_dims` compensates (header-only read of caps2 / the DX10 misc flag), so admission, `input_bytes` and the filter/resize terms see the real strip. A cube DDS is always an h-strip after load: `analysis.dds_cube` wins over a face tag in the name and over `cubemap.layout`, and an explicit layout other than hstrip is CFG-INVALID ("a cube DDS loads as its six faces; remove cubemap.layout for this file"). The GUI output-size estimate is not cube-aware yet (a later task).

- **DS8 Batch planning of cube jobs (Task 7).** `cube::plan::face_tag` (moved from `layout`) reads a trailing `_posx` .. `_negz` or `_px` .. `_nz`. `group::split_suffix_with` splits `x_e_posx` as base `x`, suffix `e`, so the six faces of an `_e` map join set `x` and the shader check sees one `_e`; any other face-tagged stem is untouched (`rock_px` is its own set, and each `cubemaps/sky_posx` is its own set: the merged `sky` job keeps the +X face's set key). `plan_cubes` runs after pass 1 and the 6c re-resolve, right before `plan_packing`. It takes the pass-1 analyses' loaded size and cube-DDS flag by path (`InputFacts`) instead of the plan's `files`, so it reads no header twice and sees the numbers policy saw. The layout comes from `policy::cube_layout_of`, the helper `check_profile` uses (a cube DDS is an h-strip, then `cubemap.layout`, then a face tag means `faces`, then the aspect ratio), so the two cannot drift; a face-tagged cube DDS is therefore a one-file cube, not a face. Face sets are keyed by folded output folder and folded stem without the tag; checks run in this order, each one `CUBE-FACES` (Error) naming the fault: two files for one face, missing faces, a face not square, faces of different sizes, faces whose `profile_sha256` differs ("faces resolve to different settings"). A broken set is one Error job whose input is the first face found (job order), with the untagged output and `cube = { faces, [the lead file] }` (never run; it lets the run report the lead file consumed into that output). A good set becomes one job: the +X face's profile, provenance and warnings, the untagged `output` and `game_path`, `cube = { layout: faces, sources: +X..-Z with their stamps }`, and the merged status (any Error → Error, else Blocked, else Unresolved, codes, reasons and needs united, else Ready). A one-file cube gets `cube = { layout, [the file] }`; `faces` on an untagged file, or a layout that does not fit the image, is `CUBE-FACES` ("hstrip layout does not fit 512x512"); no layout is Unresolved with the reason "cube layout unclear for WxH: set cubemap.layout for this file in sdc.toml (hcross, vcross, hstrip, vstrip, equirect, mirror_ball, angular, photo)" (list widened by DS22) and no `needs` (there is no GUI control for it in v1), so it skips with `SUG-LOW-CONFIDENCE` through `unresolved_code`, accepted as is. A merged cube's output was never a discovered file, so `plan_cubes` checks it against every other job's output (case-folded): on a hit both jobs are skipped `IN-DUPLICATE`, one skip per input file (six faces plus the other file). `job_bytes` adds the other sources' estimates and `6 × face² × 16 × 3` (base, blur copy, mip chain; face from `layout::face_size`); a cube DDS's own estimate already counts its 6:1 strip. A six-file cube records each face as a manifest source with `cube_face` (`posx` .. `negz`) in face order and `current_sources` matches it; a one-file cube records no extra source (`source_sha256` covers it). The recording in `process_file` lands here so `if-changed` works from this task on (Task 8 finds it in place). `check_stamps` checks every face and names the file that changed. Every face file ends with a terminal event (review fix 1): a six-file cube's faces are reported like packed sources (`FileSkipped` `packed_source`, "cubed into <output>"); the other faces of a broken set are skipped with code `CUBE-FACES` ("part of <first face>'s cube set", reported as a duplicate-kind skip, as any code without a kind of its own); a collision skip names each file's own output. A merged Error or Blocked cube also carries the other faces' warnings whose code it lists. The encode-versions fixture `h/cubemap.png` became Unresolved as a 64×64 square, so Task 7 re-pins with a 6:1 strip fixture (384×64, only the two `*/cubemap` pins move); Task 8 re-pins once cube encoding exists.

- **DS9 Display-space filter defaults (Task 6 review).** The brightness/contrast step is skipped when both are 0, so a display-space pass run only for midtones, saturation or tint skips `(v + 0 - 0.5) x 1 + 0.5`, which is not bit-exact in f32. Saturation's luma is Rec.709 (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722) on the display-space values, not on linear light; display space is the game's 1.6 gamma since DS11 (it was the sRGB curve before).

- **DS10 Encoding a cube job (Task 8).** `cube::run::prepare` replaces the 2D stages for every job with `cube` set (branch in `pipeline::prepare_then` right after the stamp check and source hashing): each source is loaded with `load_image_as` and run through `preprocess_with` with `resize = none` (a cube is sized only by `cubemap.face_size`); a raw layout is cut with `layout::import_raw` (`auto` when `cubemap.layout` is unset), six files are taken as the six faces (a source count other than 1 or 6, or faces that are not equal squares, fail the file at Load instead of panicking); each face is brought to `layout::face_size` (area resample per face going down, direction-space `sample::resample` going up); then `filter::colour`, `sample::blur(cubemap.blur or 0)`, and `sample::mip_chain` with `mips::level_count`; `drop_top_mip` drops level 0 of every face; every level of every face is quantised with `to_encoder_input` against the preprocessed `Work` with its image emptied. Working domain: everything from the colour filters to the last mip runs on linear light, decoded and re-encoded with the game's 1.6 gamma (DS11, which supersedes the sRGB-curve wording this item first had); so mips average linear light across face edges, solid-angle weighted. `Prepared.faces` is 6 for an encode or measure, and `inputs` and `dims` are face-major (`dims` repeated per face), so `encode_levels` is unchanged; `process_file` writes with `dds_bytes_cube`, `expected_levels` is mips per face, and the encode-input test hook hashes the cube header (`header_bytes_with(.., true)`). `base_coverage`, `source_peak` and `detail_ratio` are `None` for a cube (no coverage, BC6H or low-detail check). A preview (`Keep::Preview`/`SourceOnly`) is the +X face's chain only (`faces = 1`, a `shortcut:` until the GUI step brings a cross preview). `validate` decodes `DdsFile::surfaces()` (every face) instead of `levels`; on a cube each per-level message reads `face F mip M` (2D wording unchanged), and `validation.mips = smallest` checks each face's smallest mip. `face_rotate`/`face_flip` apply to every layout, six separate face files included (spec Scope item 4: sources made with other conventions; fix round 1): `layout::orient` turns then flips face k and is called by `import_raw` and by the six-file branch; the v-cross -Z 180-degree turn stays raw-only. The arrow-cube BC7 golden decodes at 99 dB on every face (flat-colour blocks encode exactly). `two_d_outputs_unchanged` (golden.rs) asserts every non-cube sub-type pinned in `encode_inputs.json` still has its `encode_version` at `RELEASED_ENGINE_VERSION`, which is what makes the encode-versions guard fail on any 2D change; the guard's re-pin moved only the two `*/cubemap` keys.

- **DS11 Cube transfer is Community Shaders' game gamma (owner, 2026-10-27).** CS decodes static cube samples with `TransferFunctions::GameGammaToLinear` = `pow(c, 1.6)` (`Lighting.hlsl:2126-2131`, `Common/TransferFunctions.hlsli:13-15`, CS build 2026-10-03), not the sRGB curve. So on a cube, `color.content = "srgb"` means game-gamma colour: `ops::GAME_GAMMA = 1.6`, `ops::game_gamma_to_linear(v) = max(v, 0)^1.6`, `ops::linear_to_game_gamma(v) = clamp(v, 0, 1)^(1/1.6)`. `cube::run::prepare` preprocesses with `color.content = linear` (no sRGB decode, domain `Stored`), decodes an integer source's RGB with `game_gamma_to_linear` (a float `.hdr`/`.exr` source is linear already and is not decoded), runs resampling, the colour filters, the blur and the mip chain on linear light, then re-encodes every level's RGB with `linear_to_game_gamma` (alpha untouched) and quantises those values as stored. The colour filters' display space (brightness, contrast, midtones, saturation, tint) is the same 1.6 curve, so a slider move matches the cube in game (DS9 amended). The config value stays `srgb` (no new `ColorContent` variant, no schema or profile-hash change); 2D textures keep sRGB and no 2D path calls the game-gamma pair. Tests: `game_gamma_round_trips_every_8bit_code`, `game_gamma_is_a_1_6_power`, `cube_mips_average_in_game_gamma` (0/255 checkerboard faces average to code 165, sRGB would give 188), `cube_float_source_is_only_reencoded` (linear 0.25 is code 107). The two `*/cubemap` encode-input pins moved again (arm 1.1.0, unreleased); no 2D pin moved.
- **DS12 Cube checks in inspect and validate (Task 10).** `cube::checks::inspect_issues(game_path, file)` adds four messages to `sdc inspect`'s header issues and, as `VAL-HEADER` warnings that fail the verdict, to `sdc validate`: a cube with one mip (width > 1), a 1x1 cube whose +Y texel is non-black, a cube in an `_SRGB` format, and a 2D file where a cubemap is expected (a `textures` component directly followed by `cubemaps`, so a `cubemaps` folder above `textures` does not count, or a stem ending `_e`, ASCII case-insensitive, either separator, Note BF). The last one changes validate verdicts for 2D `_e` and `cubemaps\` files: they now FAIL. This is intended, because the game reads those as cubes. Other 2D files are unchanged. The marker keeps its colour on +X and +Y black, so any `--color` reads as a dynamic marker and raises no issue. `sdc validate` judges a cube file as `cubemap` when no `--subtype` is given.
- **DS13 World-to-cube basis from the in-game test (Task 12).** Measured in Skyrim SE 1.6.1170 with Community Shaders CommunityShaders_AIO-2026-10-03T06-46Z (d2026.10.11.0), cell anse2StudioV2, a 64x64 static `_e` cube on a type-1 sphere (NIF team, F:\ai\dds\nifparseref\plan\cubemap-up-axis\results.md). The game samples with the world-space reflection vector (not view or object space) in plain D3D TextureCube addressing; Dynamic Cubemaps left the static cube alone. Table, world direction -> face (index), row-0 band, column-0 band: up +Z -> +Z (4), N, W; down -Z -> -Z (5), N, E; north +Y -> +Y (2), down, W; south -Y -> -Y (3), up, W; east +X -> +X (0), N, up; west -X -> -X (1), N, down. So `cube::world::WORLD_TO_CUBE` is the identity, `UP` = [0, 0, 1], determinant +1 (world X east, Y north, Z up). `bands_match_d3d_addressing` checks every band against `cube_dir`. `render3d::hdri` matches, so the NIF HANDOFF gets no line and render3d is untouched. The panorama finding (counter-clockwise u mirrors N/S) is already met: the plan and `cube::latlong` use the clockwise mapping (NIF Note DL).
- **DS14 Equirect panoramas, yaw and mirror (Task 13).** A 2:1 image (`w == 2*h` exactly; 4096x2049 stays unclear) is `cubemap.layout = "equirect"`; its default face size is the largest power of two within `w/4`. The importer (`cube::import_dir::equirect`) uses the standard 360-degree panorama mapping measured in game by the NIF team (results.md "Second check", 2026-10-27): u = 0.5 faces world east and u grows clockwise seen from above (u 0.25 north, 0.75 south, row 0 up); render3d uses the same function (NIF Note DL, 2026-10-27). Task 17 confirms with the real importer. Each texel is the mean of 3x3 bilinear samples (u wraps, v clamps) through `world::to_world` and `latlong::dir_to_uv` at yaw 0. `cubemap.yaw` (degrees, -360..=360, positive clockwise seen from above as Skyrim headings turn, so 90 moves east to south) and `cubemap.mirror` (swap world east and west) are new keys, skipped at their defaults so no profile hash moves; both are skipped at their defaults in the pipeline too (a resample is not the identity). Run order inside `cube::run`: import, face rotate/flip, yaw, mirror, exposure/clamp/colour, (Task 16: ground fill), blur, mips; all on linear light, the transfer untouched (DS11). The brief's round-trip test (`equirect_of_a_cube_round_trips`, arrow cube to a 512x256 equirect and back at 64) asked for per-face PSNR above 30 dB; the arrow cube's saturated hard edges soften by about a texel through the two bilinear passes and cap it at 27.3-28.5 dB, while every texel away from those edges round-trips exactly (infinite PSNR), so the test asserts above 26 dB whole-face and above 40 dB away from the edges (the DS3 precedent). Fix round 1: an explicit `cubemap.layout = "equirect"` reads any non-empty image (the importer resamples; only auto-detection needs exact 2:1, so 4096x2049 is unclear until the user sets it), and DIM-RESIZED names the equirect cell `w/4` as `face_size` does. Yaw turns in world space through `to_world`/`to_cube`, as mirror does. A smooth-field round trip (0.5 + 0.5 sin(6 d) per channel, 512x256 to 64) measures about 70 dB per face, so there is no sub-texel offset. `shortcut:` the importer's fixed 3x3 taps alias when `face_size` is far below `w/4`.
- **DS15 Mirror-ball and angular-map importers (Task 14).** Both are explicit-only: `cubemap.layout = "mirror_ball"` or `"angular"` on a square (or any non-empty) image; `detect` never returns them. Camera frame (ruled): the camera stands at world south looking north, image right = east, image up = `UP`; with `c = (d.east, d.up, d.south)` and `d` the world direction of a cube texel (through `world::to_world`, so east = (1,0,0), north = (0,1,0), up = (0,0,1)): mirror ball `n = normalize(c + (0,0,1))`, `(u, v) = (n.x, n.y)` in the unit disc, radius clamped to 0.98 so the back pole is filled from the outer ring (exact north, where `c + (0,0,1)` is zero, reads the ring point at image right instead of dividing by zero); angular map `r = acos(-c.z) / pi` along `(c.x, c.y)` (centre = north, rim = south, east at (0.5, 0), up at (0, 0.5)); pixel = `((u + 1) / 2 w, (1 - v) / 2 h)`, bilinear with both axes clamped. Same 3x3 supersampling as the equirect importer (one shared `project`), linear-light input, run order unchanged. Source cell and default `face_size` are the largest power of two within `w / 2` (the disc's radius), and `fits` accepts any non-empty image. `shortcut:` the 3x3 taps alias for a source far larger than the face; the mirror ball's near-north texels are stretched, as in any ball photo. The in-game check of the frame is Task 17's.
- **DS16 Single-photo approximation (Task 15).** `cubemap.layout = "photo"` is explicit-only (`detect` never returns it; `fits` takes any non-empty image). `import_dir::photo_panorama` builds a fake 2:1 panorama of width `W = 2*img.w`, height `W/2`, and `import_dir::equirect` samples it, so the source cell is `img.w/2` (= W/4, like equirect) for `face_size` and DIM-RESIZED. Recipe: the photo (unscaled, since W/2 = img.w) fills the front half centred on `u = 0.5` and the horizon row; the back half is it mirrored about `u = 0.25` and `u = 0.75`; above and below the photo each column fades linearly from its edge texel to the mean of the photo's top or bottom row (row 0 and row H-1 are exactly those means when the photo is shorter than it is wide; when `h >= w` there are no fill rows, and a portrait photo, `h > w`, is cropped to its middle `w` rows: DS26). Seam ruling: panorama column 0 shows photo column W/4-1 and column W-1 shows photo column W/4 (the two centre columns, adjacent), so the wrap seam is continuous in the mirror sense and matches within 1/255 only for a smooth photo; the test uses a smooth gradient and checks the mirror identity exactly. A photo defaults to `cubemap.blur = 0.6` (`Provenance::Builtin`, applied after the style fill, so it replaces a style's blur) unless `cubemap.blur` is set explicitly. Input is linear light after the CS 1.6 decode, so the panorama is built on linear values. Wiki: Cubemaps.md "Single photo" (written in Task 18).
- **DS17 Ground fill and horizon (Task 16).** `cubemap.ground_fill` (unset = no fill; `horizon` alone does nothing) is `"gradient"` or `[r, g, b]`; `cubemap.horizon` is -45..=45 degrees (NaN rejected like `yaw`). Runs after the colour filters and before blur, on linear light, RGB only (alpha untouched). Elevation `e = asin(to_world(dir).z)`. Horizon colour = mean of texels with `e` in [horizon, horizon+5]; if no texel falls there (very small cubes) two passes find the smallest elevation `e0 >= horizon` over all texels, then average the texels with `horizon <= e < e0 + 0.5` degrees, so it never divides by zero. A bad `ground_fill` value errors with `expected "gradient" or [r, g, b] with each 0..=255`. Below `horizon - 1` a colour fills with its code values decoded by `ops::game_gamma_to_linear` (CS game gamma 1.6, not sRGB); a gradient is `horizon colour * (1 - 0.5 t)`, `t = (horizon - e)/(horizon + 90)` clamped to 0..1. Between `horizon - 1` and `horizon + 1` it blends linearly with the original. Only `*/cubemap` pins can move; no 2D output changes. Docs/wiki: Cubemaps.md "Ground fill and horizon" (written in Task 18).
- **DS18 In-game check of an equirect-made cube (Task 17, owner OK 2026-10-27).** The engine itself made the cube this time (the up-axis results.md "Second check" used a script stand-in): a 2048x1024 PNG coloured by `latlong::uv_to_dir(u, v, 0.0)` per pixel (north red, east blue, south yellow, west green, elevation above 40 degrees white, below -40 black, plus a white bar in the west half of the north sector only, azimuth 100..125 degrees, elevation within 15 degrees) went through `sdc convert` with `cubemap.layout = "equirect"`, `face_size = 256`, BC7, full mips (`sdc inspect`: BC7 unorm, 256x256, 9 mips, cubemap, size = 6 faces). Decoded face centres before the game: +X blue, -X green, +Y red, -Y yellow, +Z white, -Z black; +Y showed black at the top and the bar on the left, the measured DS13 addressing. In game (Skyrim SE 1.6.1170, CS AIO 2026-10-03, cell `anse2StudioV2`, the up-axis test's Environment Map sphere `cubeaxis.nif` as `000CC79E` TestTeapot01 at angle 0 0 0, cube at its slot-4 path `textures\cubemaps\test_axes_e.dds` in s6), native screenshots from five sides, read by hue script and by eye: from the south the centre is yellow, left green, right blue, top white, bottom black; from the east the centre is blue, left yellow, right red; from the west the centre is green, left red, right yellow; from the north the centre is red, left blue, right green; from above the centre is white, screen-top red, left green, right blue, bottom yellow. The north bar sits right of centre from the north (0.09..0.33 r; facing south, right is west), at 0.78..0.90 r on the north side from the east and 0.47..0.66 r on the north side from the west, and in the left (west) half of the red sector from above; mirror-free reflection predicts 0.09..0.30, 0.77..0.89 and 0.46..0.64 r. **Verdict: no swap and no mirror; a normal 360-degree panorama imported with the equirect layout lands with north, south, east and west correct in game.** Screenshots and scripts: `C:\Users\Curti\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\F--ai-dds\49eff4fe-678e-49ca-bf23-c355548da443\scratchpad\task17\` (`shots\adhoc\default\T17_*.png`, `sheet.png`; scratch). The five s6 files were removed afterwards, the game was quit with `qqq`, and CS `SettingsUser.json` is unchanged (same SHA-256).

- **DS19 Photo panorama in admission (final review I1).** `job_bytes` adds `2 × w × w × 16` for `cubemap.layout = "photo"` (`w` = the input width from `input_dims`): the fake 2w × w float panorama `import_dir::photo_panorama` builds is alive beside the source and the new cube. Other layouts add nothing new. Test `api::tests::a_photo_cube_is_admitted_for_its_panorama`.
- **DS20 An auto face below 4 is CFG-INVALID (final review I2; amends DS5 and DS7).** Next to DIM-SMALL (Blocking, acknowledgeable), a cube whose shown face is below 4 also gets CFG-INVALID ("cube face N px is below 4; only `sdc cubemap-marker` writes a 1x1 cube"), which `allow` / `--allow` cannot acknowledge, so a batch-wide `--allow DIM-SMALL` no longer writes a 1x1 or 2x2 picture cube (the trap of the spec's "below 4 is refused except by the marker"). An explicit `face_size` below 4 was already CFG-INVALID. `cube_mips_average_in_game_gamma` now uses 4x4 checkerboard faces with no `allow`; mip 1 reads 167 there (the solid-angle weights of a 2x2-texel footprint favour the texel nearer the face centre), so its tolerance is 3, still far from sRGB's 188. So `textures/mymod/cubemaps/x.png` stays 2D in both conversion and validation, matching Texture-Types (`textures\cubemaps\`). The suggestion reason reads "under textures/cubemaps". Test: `suggest::tests::underscore_e_and_cubemaps_folder_suggest_cubemap`.
- **DS24 No wasted cube copies in `cube::run` (final review M6).** `filter::yaw` runs only for a non-zero `cubemap.yaw` and `sample::blur` only for a blur above 0 (both returned a clone at their defaults), and the pre-blur cube is dropped before `mip_chain` instead of living on under a shadowed name, so peak memory falls by up to one face-size float cube (1.6 GB at 4096); still inside DS8's three-cube admission term. Output bytes are unchanged: the goldens and encode pins pass unmoved.

A whole-number float such as `10.0` is accepted as 10. Test: `config::tests::bad_ground_fill_names_the_accepted_forms`.
- **DS26 A portrait photo is cropped, and the photo faces east (final review M9; amends DS16).** `photo_panorama` keeps the photo's middle `w` rows when it is taller than wide (`h > w`): its top and bottom are lost, with no warning, and there are no fill rows when `h >= w`. That stays the behaviour (a single photo is an approximation); the wiki's Single photo section now says so, tells the user to crop to choose, and says the photo's centre faces east (`cubemap.yaw = -90` turns it north). DS16's wording is amended. The wiki also lists `photo` (0.6) as a blur default in the Blur section, and Troubleshooting's DIM-SMALL row says a cube face under 4 cannot be acknowledged (DS20).
