## Note DU — Set cleanup: remove missing members, Advanced Skin sets skin_albedo (owner + builder, 2026-10-28)

Owner: "missing textures cannot be removed from a set, ensure both right click has an option, as well as in messages; setting advanced skin as the shader type should automatically switch albedo to skin albedo". The red "?" chip on a set card is a line of the set's `[[sets]]` entry in `sdc-project.toml` that matches no file (K12): an `add` or `remove` path naming no file, a `borrow` from a set that is gone or has nothing in that slot, or the whole entry when none of its files is left. Nothing could remove one before: the set menu's Remove member lists live members only.

- DU1. **Remove from set on the "?" chip.** The chip is now a button (AccessKit name "Missing: <line>") with a right-click menu holding **Remove from set**. An `add`/`remove` path leaves both lists as written (`SetsDoc::drop_entry`, case-folded id match, no file is moved because none exists); one undo step labelled "Remove from set", re-planned. `SetView::missing` is now `Vec<Missing>` (`NoFilesLeft`, `File`, `Borrow`), so the fix acts on the line's kind instead of parsing its text; `Missing::text()` keeps the old wording in hovers.
- DU2. **A dead borrow** is dropped with `set_borrow(id, n, None)`. A pinned (locked) slot keeps its borrow and the removal is refused with "slot locked" (F3a Task 8, AF6). **An entry with no files left** offers **Delete set** instead (the existing `delete_set`; the chip goes through the set column's delete confirmation, the Problems button deletes directly as one undoable step).
- DU3. **Problems row.** Each missing line is a `Level::Warning` row on its set, "No file matches <line>" ("No texture of this set is left in the folder" for a whole entry), whose fix button is **Remove from set** (or **Delete set**), named "Remove <line> from <set>" for AccessKit so rows stay distinct; a whole-entry row's **Delete set** is named "Delete set <set>". `Problem` gains `missing: Option<Missing>`. These rows count against "ready": a set with a dead line no longer shows the green dot. The owner's "messages" is read as this Problems list; the Messages log and the set editor's "no file matches" lines get no button.
- DU4. **Read-only.** `sdc-project.toml` read-only greys the buttons with "sdc-project.toml is read-only: <error>" (`AppModel::sets_read_only_reason`), and `remove_missing` refuses with it. In practice a parse error that makes the file read-only also hides its entries, so the greyed state is rare.
- DU5. **An own member's chip** also has **Remove from set** in its right-click menu (after the slot commands, or alone for a member in no slot), running the existing `remove_member` with its refusals (packed map, only automatic member, locked slot) shown in the Refused dialog. A borrowed chip gets none: the slot's **Clear** drops a borrow.
- DU6. **Advanced Skin sets skin_albedo.** Choosing **Advanced Skin** in a set's shader combo (cs target only) also sets the set's own Diffuse-slot member to `skin_albedo` through `edit_subtype`, so Note DQ's recipe follow turns a packed `_rmaos` into `_rfaos` and the PBR member follow runs as for a hand edit, all in one undo step with the shader. `batch_edit` is now re-entrant (a batch inside a batch joins the outer step); before, a sub-type edit with DQ's recipe follow inside a bulk edit closed the outer batch early.
- DU7. **Leaving Advanced Skin reverts.** Choosing any other shader, or Auto, puts the diffuse back to the `[files]` sub-type it had before (none: inferred; or `diffuse`) when Tessalith made it `skin_albedo` and it still holds `skin_albedo`. The revert writes the old sub-type through `edit_subtype` first (an explicit `diffuse` when there was none), so DQ3 sets the packed output back to `_rmaos`, then clears it when there was none. A bare clear would not revert: with `_rfaos` still packed the engine suggests `skin_albedo` again (DQ3). The packed card is left with an explicit `packing.recipe = "rmaos"` it may not have had before; that resolves the same as no recipe. Tessalith's switches are recorded in `sdc-project.toml` `[project] auto_skin = { "<file>" = "<old sub-type or empty>" }` (GUI bookkeeping, as `auto_pbr`).
- DU8. **A sub-type the user changes is theirs.** Any sub-type edit of a recorded diffuse (even choosing `skin_albedo` again by hand, single or bulk) drops it from `auto_skin`, so leaving Advanced Skin later keeps it.
- DU9. **What is never switched.** A diffuse whose sub-type a user, rule or `[files]` entry set to anything but plain `diffuse` (provenance other than the engine's suggestion, as `follow_of` reads it), one already `skin_albedo`, one in a pinned slot, a borrowed diffuse (only the set's own Diffuse-slot member leads, as in the PBR follow), and any set under the vanilla target. Read-only `sdc.toml` leaves only the shader change.
- DU10. **Limit.** shortcut: `auto_skin` keeps a line for a file that is later deleted or renamed; it is inert (the revert needs the file to still hold `skin_albedo`). Prune it on write, as `auto_pbr` does, if stale lines show up in real projects.
- DU11. **A pinned diffuse is left alone both ways (review).** The slot lock that stops the switch also stops the revert: a diffuse pinned after Tessalith made it `skin_albedo` keeps `skin_albedo` (and the set its `_rfaos`) when the shader changes; its `auto_skin` line stays, so an unpin and a later shader change still revert it.

## Note DV — Existing Advanced Skin sets use skin_albedo (owner, 2026-10-28)

Owner: "yes switch existing advanced skin sets automatically". Note DU's switch fires only when the shader is picked, so a set saved with Advanced Skin before DU kept a plain diffuse and packed `_rmaos`. This note moves the rule into the engine; it extends DU6-DU9.

- DV1. **The engine reads the chosen shader as skin evidence, in two independent parts.** A set's explicit shader (`ShaderOrigin::Set`: the GUI's `[[sets]] shader`, sent as `BatchRequest::set_shaders`, or `--set set:<id>.shader`) being Advanced Skin (cs only; elsewhere the pick falls back) does two things. (a) **Sub-type** (`policy::decide_subtype`): the set's diffuse member (a file with no suffix, or `_d`) resolves to `skin_albedo` when its top suggestion is `diffuse` or `pbr_albedo` (provenance `shader:advanced_skin`) or its written sub-type is plain `diffuse` (DV3; the written provenance is kept, so the choice stays protected from packing, `resolve_file_with`), whatever the set can pack: a diffuse-only set, a set whose packed map is a pre-packed `_rmaos` (kept as it is, CO109) and a metallic-only set (keeps `_rmaos`, as DQ2) all get it (review issue 1). (b) **Packing** (`pack::plan::chosen_recipe`): when neither packed key names a `packing.recipe`, the recipe is `rfaos` if the set can build one, else `auto` with no notice. A built `_rfaos` makes `set_is_advanced_skin` true, so `_sk`/`_wet`/`_f` take their skin readings as before. Step 6c re-resolves the members of such a set (pass 1 runs with no shader picks). No project file is rewritten, so existing projects switch on the next plan. Other members are never re-typed (re-review): an `_i` inner layer keeps its `diffuse` guess, and a raw-map-named file the user typed `diffuse` (`x_roughness`) stays `diffuse` and converts alone (`skin_subtypes::only_the_diffuse_member_becomes_skin_albedo`).
- DV2. **GUI and CLI agree.** Both reach `explicit_shaders`, so the GUI's saved choice and `--set set:<id>.shader=advanced_skin` plan alike (`skin_subtypes::the_gui_choice_and_the_cli_set_plan_alike`). The CLI still never reads `sdc-project.toml` (`engine::sets`, S-shader-2): a project's saved shader reaches the CLI only through `--set`, as before.
- DV3. **Written values (controller ruling on review issue 2).** A written plain `diffuse` (a `[files]` entry, `--set` or a rule) is read as `skin_albedo` on an Advanced Skin set: the same narrow exception DU6 applies on a fresh pick, so an existing set and a re-picked one agree. Any other written sub-type stays (`pbr_albedo`, say). A written `packing.recipe` still decides the packed output alone. Consequence: while the shader is Advanced Skin the diffuse cannot be plain `diffuse`; choosing `diffuse` by hand there (DQ3 then writes `rmaos`) gives `skin_albedo` with `_rmaos`. To get a plain diffuse, leave Advanced Skin. Vanilla is untouched. A set that cannot build `_rfaos` keeps `_rmaos` with no PACK-RECIPE-UNBUILDABLE: nobody wrote a recipe.
- DV4. **Pins hold the file, not the sub-type (controller ruling on review issue 3).** On an Advanced Skin set the diffuse reads as `skin_albedo` unless the user set a non-diffuse sub-type, pinned or not. A pin (`lock = ["slotN"]`) holds which file fills the slot; it is GUI data that never reaches the engine. The GUI still writes nothing into a pinned slot (DU6's switch and DU7's revert skip it), but the engine's reading follows the shader. This supersedes DU9's and DU11's pin exception for the reading: pinning a diffuse, then choosing Advanced Skin, reads it `skin_albedo` (nothing written); a pinned diffuse that DU made `skin_albedo` keeps that written value when the shader changes. docs/gui.md says so under Pin slot and the Advanced skin card. A borrowed diffuse is not a member of the borrowing set in the engine, so it is never re-typed (as DU9).
  Superseded by DW.
- DV5. **DU's GUI switch stays.** On a loaded set the diffuse already resolves `skin_albedo`, so `skin_follow` returns nothing and choosing Advanced Skin again writes nothing (`set_cleanup::an_existing_advanced_skin_set_opens_with_rfaos`). On a fresh pick the plan has not run yet, so DU6 still writes `skin_albedo` and the `rfaos` recipe and DU7 can revert them; for an inferred diffuse that write is now redundant but harmless. Leaving Advanced Skin on a set DU never switched writes nothing and the engine goes back to `_rmaos`.
- DV6. **Encode version: no arm moves.** The `skin_albedo` and `skin_rfaos` encodings are unchanged; what changes is which type an existing set resolves to. The diffuse's profile hash differs (`is_up_to_date` compares it), and `_rfaos` is a new output, so `if-changed` re-encodes both without a version bump (as DR6). `golden` and `encode_versions` pass unchanged: no fixture chooses Advanced Skin explicitly.
- DV7. **Limits.** shortcut: `join_skin_wet` runs before set edits and explicit shaders, so an `x_wet` does not join a set that is skin only by its shader; move the explicit shaders before it if such a project shows up. Step 6's packing prediction still adds `rmaos` to the set's suffixes, as for a written `packing.recipe = "rfaos"`. The old `_rmaos.dds` stays in the export folder (as DR9).

## Note DW — A pin blocks the Advanced Skin reading (owner, 2026-10-28)

Owner ruling: a pin blocks the automatic Advanced Skin reading. This supersedes DV4 (a pin held the file, not the reading) and restores DU9's and DU11's pin exception for the engine's reading.

- DW1. **A pinned diffuse turns DV1 off for its set.** When the set's own diffuse member (the file DV1(a) would convert: a member with no suffix, or `_d`) is in a pinned slot, DV1 does not apply to that set: (a) the diffuse resolves as without DV (an inferred guess stays as guessed, `diffuse` or `pbr_albedo`; a written plain `diffuse` stays `diffuse`), and (b) packing keeps its pre-DV choice (no automatic `rfaos`). Step 6c does not re-resolve the set for it either, so the set plans exactly as before Note DV. One predicate, `pack::plan::chosen_skin`, decides all three (`skin_subtypes::a_pinned_diffuse_blocks_the_advanced_skin_reading`).
- DW2. **Written values still win.** A diffuse DU already wrote `skin_albedo` (with its written `packing.recipe = "rfaos"`) keeps both while pinned (DU11 unchanged; `skin_subtypes::a_pinned_written_skin_albedo_keeps_it`).
- DW3. **How the engine learns of pins.** The GUI sends `BatchRequest::pinned_files`: the `[files]` keys of the items in a locked slot of their own set (`sets::pinned_files`, from `locked_items`; a borrowing set's lock is left out, so it never changes the owner set's reading). `BatchRequest` is not serialized, so the field is a plain `BTreeSet<String>`, empty from `BatchRequest::new`. The engine keeps the hits that are diffuse-named (`FileScopes::skin_pinned`, file indices as `TextureSet::members` holds them). The CLI sends none and never reads `sdc-project.toml`: unchanged. The pinned files are part of the GUI's `EngineInputs`, so the plan settles like the other set inputs.
- DW4. **Pinning re-plans.** A lock or unlock (`set_slot_lock`) now re-plans, so the cards update (`set_cleanup::pinning_the_diffuse_of_a_loaded_skin_set_flips_its_reading`); before, a lock never reached the engine. Every slot's lock re-plans, not only the Diffuse slot's: the pinned files are an engine input, and an unplanned change to them would leave the plan unsettled for export.
- DW5. **Unchanged.** A borrowed diffuse is never re-typed (DV4/DU9). Vanilla is untouched (DV1 is cs only). DU6's switch and DU7's revert still skip a pinned slot. No encode-version arm moves and `golden`/`encode_versions` pass unchanged, as DV6: the change only selects which existing type a set resolves to.

## Note DY — Helper textures (owner + builder, 2026-10-28)

Owner request 2026-10-27 (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-helper-textures-design.md`, approved with Claude's calls; owner rulings 2026-10-28: no `encode_version` arm moves, and `_cnr` alpha is offered, never suggested). Plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-helper-textures.md` (Rulings 1-16). A helper is a source file that fills a channel of another output of its set (AO, metallic, roughness/gloss, specular, opacity, fuzz, fuzz and subsurface weight, height, RNM layers). Every helper is listed, its role, targets, read channel and inversion can be corrected, and it fills the channel it belongs in, in the GUI and the CLI alike. The branch was built under the letter DT; main took that letter (cubemap GUI) and nif/main DU-DW. It was then renamed DX, which main took for the analysis disk cache, and the owner asked to skip DX for this note anyway (DX10 already names the DDS header), so the letter is DY and every code and test reference was renamed (owner 2026-10-28). Base: main 92f876eb, which holds the cubemap work (Note DS) and Note DR, the plan's precondition.

Pointers: **Note W11** is overturned for listing (DY16: layer files are helper rows, still never tiles; the RNM section is unchanged). **Note M2 / spec §14 #19** (raw maps without a recipe) is reopened: opacity, specular, fuzz weight and subsurface weight now fill alphas (DY6). **Note M13** (one source per role, first by path) is kept as the suggestion rule; an assigned helper or a card pick overrides it (DY9). **Note DR** is now the name guess of the `fuzz` role (Fuzz mask (skin)); its behaviour stays the default. **Notes H / M4** are kept: "not used" rows are the GUI form of PACK-UNUSED-INPUT / IN-PACKING-INPUT, and no new code was added (plan Ruling 16). **Note DM**: no arm moved; the fill source recorded on the output does the work, as DR6 (DY14, DY15; owner 2026-10-28).

- DY1. **Selectors and ids (plan Rulings 1-3).** Four per-file selectors in the helper file's own `[files]` entry, also `--set file:<glob>.helper.<field>=`: `helper.role` (string), `helper.fills` (array of target ids; `[]` = not used), `helper.read` (`"r" | "g" | "b" | "a" | "luma"`), `helper.invert` (bool). They are selectors, never `Profile` fields, so no `profile_sha256` moves. Role ids: `none` (Not a helper); the `RawMap` ids `roughness metallic ao specular glossiness height opacity fuzz orm curves cavity`; new `fuzzweight` and `subsurfaceweight`; the layer ids `bump bump2 bumpmask bumpmask2 detailnorm detailnorm2 detailnormmask detailnormmask2 bent bentmask` (`LayerTerm::canonical()`, no prefix, no rnm.py aliases). `rmaos` is not a role. Labels: `fuzz` = "Fuzz mask (skin)" (DR1), `fuzzweight` = "Fuzz weight (PBR)". Target ids (18): alpha `diffuse.a n.a f.a s.a cnr.a`; packed `rmaos.r|g|b|a`, `rfaos.r|g|b|a`, `m.r|g|b|a`, `p.r`. Normal-type roles have no `helper.fills`; their target is the existing `rnm.target`. One validator (`helper::value_error`) serves `--set` and `[files]` loading, and each message names the field. `HelperRole::all()` and `FillTarget::all()` back the parse, the schema enums and a round-trip test.
  - DY1a. A `subtype:` scope is refused, as for `rnm.target`. **An unscoped `--set helper.<field>=` is refused too** (controller ruling, Task 1): `helper.role is set per file: use file:<glob>.helper.role=<…>`. It would make every image a helper. Cost if wrong: one extra error a user could hit.
  - DY1b. Preset and config `rules` that carry `helper.*` fail profile validation as unknown fields, as `rnm.target` does.
- DY2. **Hand role precedence, "Not a helper", images only (Rulings 12-13).** A hand-set `helper.role` applies to images only (`InputKind::Image`, as `raw_role` and DR8); on a DDS it is ignored. A role other than `none` makes the file a helper even if a rule or `[files]` names its sub-type. `none` makes it an ordinary converted file, which replaces "set a sub-type to convert it alone" for helpers; the sub-type escape hatch still works. `policy::resolve_file_with` reads the hand role first: `Raw(r)` gives a `PackingInput` job, a layer role a `NormalLayer` job, `none` skips the vocabulary, skin-`_f` and layer branches. `plan_packing` takes an image's role from its job before the file name, so `x_gloss` hand-set to roughness packs as roughness, not inverted gloss. A failed or cancelled helper keeps its hand role (`helper_requested`), so its recipe fails by Note M11 instead of building with a default.
  - DY2a. **A hand-role file with no recognised suffix joins its base set** (controller ruling, Task 1): `group::join_helpers` moves `x_mask.png` (role other than `none`) into set `x` when that set exists in the same output folder, else it stays in its own set. A packed output such a helper starts is named after the set (`x_rmaos`, not `x_mask_rmaos`): `joined_helper_names` names it from the set member whose parse produced the set, so a base that itself ends in a term (`x_ao`) is not cut twice; the output's own `[files]` key applies. Cost if wrong: a grouping rule a user may find surprising.
  - DY2b. A raw-named image set to `none` counts as typed (like a requested sub-type) and is an ordinary member of the shader member map. The IN-PACKING-INPUT text of a hand-set role names `helper.role = "none"` as the way to convert it alone.
- DY3. **`FuzzWeight`, `SubsurfaceWeight`.** Two `RawMap` variants, appended and kept out of `ALL`/`INPUTS`: no file name carries them (no new name heuristics); they come only from a hand-set role. `FillSpec::get` returns `None` for them. `unused_reason` gains Opacity (replacing "no recipe packs opacity yet"), FuzzWeight and SubsurfaceWeight texts. Schemas: `RawMap` gains both ids in `event` and `manifest`.
- DY4. **`pack::recipes_for_sel` (Task 2).** `recipes_for_with` delegates with an empty selection map, so every existing caller is unchanged. With selections: an input with hand-set `fills` stays out of the M13 role pass; a valid hand-set packed target starts its recipe if the set has none; inputs land in path order and the first per (recipe, channel) wins, a later one gets "`<id>` is filled by `<winner>`"; a final pass applies `invert ^= sel.invert` and the explicit read to every channel fed by a selected path. A packed target is valid per set: cs `p` → Parallax; cs `rmaos`/`rfaos` only for the set's own cs pack (prepacked layout, else `rfaos` iff `packing.recipe = rfaos` or `auto` with a suggested fuzz source, else `rmaos`); vanilla `m` → complex `_m`, or env-mask `_m` with R only. Refusals: "`<id>`: the vanilla target packs no _rmaos", "the env-mask _m has only R", "the set packs _rfaos". Gloss into a roughness slot (or the reverse) is inverted by role (`slot_of`).
  - DY4a. **A hand-built recipe keeps the set's suggested sources in its other channels** (controller ruling, Task 2; the brief said Missing/Mirror/Opaque): a lone `_specular` takes A of a hand-forced `_rmaos`. A channel with no suggested source is today's `Missing(slot)`. Cost if wrong: a channel the user expected empty gets a source.
  - DY4b. A hand-set role counts as assigned in packing too (Ruling 8): the M13 pass sorts by (not assigned, path), so a hand-role source beats a name-guessed one of its role; between a hand role and a hand fill, the first by path wins.
  - DY4c. `packing.recipe` holds for a hand-built output: `chosen_recipe` probes `recipes_for_sel` under auto, rfaos and rmaos, so a set whose only packed recipe comes from a hand fill still reads its configured recipe (`configured_rfaos_builds_for_hand_fill_alone`).
- DY5. **Read and invert (Ruling 9).** Unset read = today (R, or luma where the recipe says `grayscale_source = luma`; alpha fills read R). A is never chosen automatically (a palette PNG with tRNS has alpha; `palette_helper_with_trns_reads_r`). Explicit `r|g|b|a` maps to `ChannelSource::Source.channel = Some(0..=3)`; `luma` to `Some(pack::LUMA_CHANNEL)`, `LUMA_CHANNEL = 4` (Rec.709, the shared `pack::assemble::luma`), so no new field and no JSON change for existing jobs; provenance prints `luma`. An explicit read exempts that source from CHAN-NOT-GRAY, as Note AL exempts `_orm`.
  - DY5a. **`helper.read` on an `_orm` overrides each slot's channel** (controller ruling, Task 2): read is explicit user intent. Cost if wrong: an `_orm` with a read set packs one channel thrice.
- DY6. **Alpha targets (Rulings 4-5).** `diffuse.a` = a job of sub-type Diffuse, PbrAlbedo or SkinAlbedo (never ComplexGrass, UiSky, LandscapeDiffuse); `n.a` = Normal (so a PBR set's PbrNormal never is); `f.a` = PbrFuzz; `s.a` = PbrSubsurface; `cnr.a` = CoatNormal. A target is a plain file job: `pack`, `derive` and `cube` all `None`, status not Error/PackingInput/NormalLayer, input not the helper. Suggested alpha targets: opacity → `diffuse.a`, specular → `n.a`, fuzzweight → `f.a`, subsurfaceweight → `s.a`. **`cnr.a` is offered, never suggested** (owner 2026-10-28: base roughness is not coat roughness); it fills only when assigned. Packed suggestions stay exactly today's recipes; a role can have both (specular feeds `rmaos.a` or `m.r` and `n.a`). Targets follow the active target: a helper with no planned target is "not used: no `<colour texture | non-PBR _n | _f | _s | _cnr>` planned", plus " under vanilla" there.
  - DY6a. When several jobs of one sub-type match in a set (`x.png` and `x_d.png`, both Diffuse), the first by input is the target (builder call, accepted). Cost if wrong: the second diffuse never gets the fill.
- DY7. **Empty (Ruling 6).** A suggested alpha fill applies only when the target's pass-1 analysis of the original source says empty: `alpha == None || alpha == Constant255 || A min == max`. Otherwise it is skipped, "`<target>` already has alpha". An assigned fill ignores emptiness and replaces a PNG's real alpha.
- DY8. **Sizes (Ruling 7).** A suggested alpha fill of another size is skipped and the helper is not used ("512x512, target 1024x1024: sizes differ"), so an existing project never starts failing. An assigned one turns the target into an Error job with PACK-SIZE-MISMATCH (`size_mismatch_warning`, both sizes). That helper counts as used (it went into the error) and the error job keeps `fill`, so the run, which never runs it, ends the helper with "filled into <output>" (builder calls, accepted). A size that changes between plan and run fails the target at load: "`<helper>`: size changed since planning; re-run". Packed channels keep today's rule (recipe Error).
- DY9. **Two helpers on one channel (Ruling 8).** Assigned (`HelperSel::assigned()`: a hand-set role other than `none`, or hand-set fills) beats suggested; among equals the first by path wins (M13); the loser is "`<target>` is filled by `<winner>`".
  - DY9a. **An assigned fill without facts reserves its target** (controller ruling, Task 3): a helper or target that failed to load has no `AlphaFacts`; the assigned helper is "`<file>` was not analysed", and no suggested helper falls back onto that target this run. The user's choice is never silently replaced. Cost if wrong: one run with an empty alpha until the helper loads.
- DY10. **Fill before analysis (Ruling 10) and plan order.** `Engine::plan`: pass 1, `alpha_facts` from pass 1 beside `cube_facts`, `plan_cubes`, `helper::plan::plan_fills`, `plan_packing(.., &fills)`, pass 2, then the fill step, then derive. The fill step loads each target with `load_image_as(target, alpha.exr_straight)`, applies `helper::apply_fill`, analyses the filled image and re-resolves the job as step 6c does, so alpha policy, format policy, coverage mips and cutout all see the filled alpha. The filled image's `SourceInfo` is the target's with `has_alpha = true`, `channels = 4`; bit depth and float-ness never come from the helper. The pipeline applies the same fill right after the 2D load, so plan and run see one image. `ResolvedJob.fill: Option<FillJob>` (`serde(default, skip_serializing_if)`; plain derives), `provenance["fill.a"]` in the packed wording (`source:x_opacity.png:R`, `1-` when inverted).
  - DY10a. **Alpha fills stay active when `packing.enabled = false`** (controller ruling, Task 4): `packing.enabled` governs packed outputs; a fill creates no output. A helper an alpha fill uses is consumed whatever packing did. Cost if wrong: a user who turned packing off still sees a diffuse gain alpha.
  - DY10b. The filled re-analysis keeps the pass-1 ICC and DDS-format flags (the pixel-only load cannot see them). A fill that changes the resolved `alpha.exr_straight` reloads once under the final setting.
  - DY10c. A fill-step load failure or cancellation removes the target's job (FailedFile at Load, or cancelled), as for a pass-2 recipe.
  - DY10d. Terminal events: a helper ends once, "filled into <first output>"; if a recipe also packs it, only "packed into". `Plan.fill_ends` ends a consumed helper whose target job is gone (failed, cancelled, size mismatch) with that target's output. In an Also export a fill source is a member of its derive set; when a derive replaces its target, the helper ends with DERIVE-NOT-CONVERTED.
  - DY10e. `job_bytes` admits the helper's estimated decode bytes beside the target's.
- DY11. **Cubes and derived jobs never fill (Rulings 11, 15).** A cube job is never a target nor offered (`prepare_then` returns before the 2D load); a face file of an `_e` set has suffix `e` and is no helper; a hand-set role on a cube source is honoured and the cube reports the missing face (CUBE-FACES). Derived (Also export) jobs never take a fill; the fill step runs before derive.
- DY12. **Value fills (Ruling 14).** `packing.fill.*` applies only when no helper targets the channel; a `Source` channel never consults `fill_for`. No new codes (Ruling 16).
- DY13. **`Plan.helpers` (Task 5).** `helper::report::reports` gives one `HelperReport` per helper, by set key then file name: role and whether hand-set, fills and whether hand-set, read, invert, `options`, `not_used`, `skipped_targets`, `outputs`, `rnm_target`. The GUI renders and edits only this; it computes no target, suggestion or verdict.
  - DY13a. Who is a helper: images only; `none` never; a hand-set role always; else the file's own `PackingInput`/`NormalLayer` job; a file with no job takes the role of the pack or fill source it is (never `Rmaos`), else its name role. A file converted on its own is no helper.
  - DY13b. `options`: the Ruling 4 alpha targets planned in the set, plus the packed channels the set accepts (cs: the planned `_rmaos`/`_rfaos`, else `_rmaos`, all four channels, and `p.r`; vanilla: `m.r`, all four when complex). Empty for normal-type roles. **Not filtered by role** (controller ruling, Task 5): packing honours any hand-set role in any packed channel, so the list matches what would be honoured. Cost if wrong: the Add target list offers targets a role cannot sensibly fill.
  - DY13c. **`FillTarget::Rnm(RnmTarget)` is report-only** (controller ruling, Task 5): a layer's fill (`rnm.n`/`rnm.cnr`, label `<base>_n`/`<base>_cnr`), never in `FillTarget::all()`, so `helper.fills` cannot name it. A layer's fills follow its base's `j.rnm`; with `rnm.enabled = false` on the base it is "RNM is off for <output> (rnm.enabled = false)".
  - DY13d. `not_used` (only when `fills` is empty): "no targets chosen" for `helper.fills = []`; else the helper job's PACK-UNUSED-INPUT / IN-PACKING-INPUT / RNM-* text, a base's RNM-LAYER-SHADOWED note, RNM off, or the alpha planner's reason.
  - DY13e. **`HelperReport.rnm_target`** (Task 8 review): the `rnm.target` in effect for a normal-type role (hand-set, else the name's prefix, else `_n` falling back to `_cnr`, Note W4), from `rnm::plan::effective_target`, which `targets()` now uses too. `None` for other roles.
- DY14. **`SourceRef.fill` and if-changed.** A filled output records its helper last (after the RNM inputs) as a source with `fill = FillJob::identity()` (`a:<r|g|b|a|luma>` plus `:inv`). A packed source with an explicit `helper.read` records `read:<id>` (`pack::read_of`, from `PackSource.read`, set for every source of the recipe including a pre-packed `_rmaos`/`_rfaos` image, CO103/CO104). `current_sources` builds the same list and `up_to_date` compares `fill`, so a changed helper, read or invert re-encodes that output. Outputs without a helper record no `fill` key and packed sources without a read record none, so existing manifests are unchanged. Schema diffs: `manifest` `fill`, `event` `FillJob`, `HelperRead`, `fill`, `PackSource.read`.

## Note DZ — Analysis disk cache (owner, 2026-10-28)

Built as Note DU, merged into main as Note DX, renamed DZ on nif/main (owner 2026-10-28: skip DX as a note letter, since DX10 already names the DDS header and mixed `DX` greps get confused).

An on-disk store behind `AnalysisCache` (`engine::analysis_store`), so a project opened before decodes nothing unchanged. The GUI turns it on in Task 2; `Session::with_disk_cache(dir)` is the switch, and the CLI and every test leave it off.

- **DZ1 The hints are part of every cache key, in memory as well as on disk (implementer).** `AnalysisCache::file` and `pack` take the `AnalyseHints` the lookup will use (`dims` does not, see DZ2); an entry made with other hints (checks on or off, another suffix after an alias change) is a miss. The memory cache used to ignore hints and could serve a stats-less analysis to a checks-on lookup: a latent mismatch, closed here.
- **DZ2 `dims` keeps its signature and stays memory-only (implementer's call).** The GUI asks it for output sizes without the plan's hints. The admission check in `plan_cached` instead asks `file` with `hints_for(split_for(item).suffix, cache.checks)`, exactly the hints the load will use, so `cached` at admission means a hit at load, and a disk hit there fills memory so the load does not read the entry twice.
- **DZ3 `ANALYSIS_VERSION` alone versions the cache; a pin test catches an analysis change without a bump (owner, 2026-10-28).** The engine version is not in the key, so a release does not empty the cache. `tests/analysis_version.rs` hashes the serialized `analyse_with` results (five fixtures, five hint sets) and the thumbnails, and pins `{analysis_version, sha256}` in `tests/analysis_version.json`. The same hash under the same version passes; a new hash under the same version fails with "bump ANALYSIS_VERSION"; a bumped version rewrites the pin (as `encode_versions`).
- **DZ4 What the pin covers (review fixes).** `tests/analysis_version.rs` hashes, with the old hand-built images: PNGs generated in the test (8-bit RGBA, 16-bit RGB, gray) through `load_image_meta`; DDS files written with the engine's own writer (`dds_bytes`, from deterministic block bytes so no encoder, whose output can differ by CPU, is involved) for 2D BC1, BC5 and BC7 and one single-cube BC1, loaded through the same entry (`load_dds` including the 6:1 cube strip); two packs through `pack::assemble` (gray members, and a `channel: Some(..)` extraction from an RGBA member with an inverted channel plus a non-gray 16-bit member read by luma); and `schemars::schema_for!(Analysis)`, so a field added with a serde default still moves the pin. Not covered: PSD and Krita/ORA decoding (the engine has no PSD or ORA writer, and no dev-dependency makes one), packs with members of other sizes (`assemble` refuses them), and EXR/HDR/TGA sources. Bump `ANALYSIS_VERSION` by hand when those change. Bump it too when decoding, `analyse_with`, thumbnails or pack assembly change their results. It stays 1: nothing has shipped.
- **DZ5 Same size and same mtime is "unchanged", exactly as the memory cache already treats it.** Not a defect.
- **DZ6 An analysis that does not read back bit for bit is not stored.** serde_json writes a non-finite float (`corner_err` of an empty image is infinite) as `null`, which does not read back. `put` reads the header back and compares the analysis. To make that comparison exact, the engine's `serde_json` has the `float_roundtrip` feature (without it an f64 can read back one ulp off and every entry would be refused). No new package; `Cargo.lock` is unchanged.
- **DZ7 A disk entry without a thumbnail is a miss when the cache wants thumbnails.** `Engine::plan` (CLI) caches none and never reads the disk.
- **DZ8 Prune keeps the newest 200 MB, by modification time (write time, not last use).** Run once in `with_disk_cache`. `shortcut:` an entry in use but old goes first; touch entries on a hit if that costs reloads. `prune` also deletes `.sdc-*.tmp` files a crashed write left behind, once they are a day old.
- **DZ9 Every read or write error is a miss or a skipped write.** A truncated or corrupt file is a miss and the next put replaces it. Entries are written with `write_atomic`. The key uses the absolute path (`std::path::absolute`, not `canonicalize`, which fails on missing files and adds `\\?\`), so a relative input never matches another folder's file after a cwd change. Its spelling and case are as given, and the path is written with `display()`, lossy only for non-Unicode names. A different spelling or case misses. Two different non-Unicode names that display the same (both lossy-replaced) share a key, so with equal size and mtime one could hit the other's entry; not realistic for names made in Explorer.
- **DZ10 Only `main.rs` reads `LOCALAPPDATA` for the store; the GUI builds one Session (Task 2).** The GUI creates its Session once, in `build_model`; nothing replaces it at runtime, so no path is carried in the model. `build_model` reads the variable and passes it to `sdc_gui::with_analysis_cache`, which gives the Session `with_disk_cache(<base>\sdc\analysis-cache)`; with the variable unset there is no store. The function is in the lib so a test can call it (`app_no_local_store.rs`: a plan with a tempdir base fills the folder, `None` writes nothing); `SdcApp::new` never creates the folder. The CLI and `Engine::plan` stay memory-only.
- **DZ11 The GUI session is the `Session::new` default (thumbnails and checks on), so the cache holds thumbnails and check stats.** The ignored test `load_time_cold_then_warm` (set `SDC_LOADTIME_DIR`) plans a folder twice with fresh Sessions over a tempdir store, prints both times and the warm `loads()`, and asserts it is 0. Measured 2026-10-28 on the owner's `F:\texture tool\input` (41 PNG + 1 PSD, 3.8 GB; dev-profile test build at cec91320): cold 37.2 s (60 decodes), warm 0.16 s (0 decodes).

## Note GA — NIF trace fixes 2026-10-28 (NIF team, 2026-10-28)
Fixes from the main team's trace-debug report of 2026-10-28 (findings 1, 43, 44, 37, 27, 28). The brief called this Note EA; it is GA because the owner split note letters by team the same day (NIF team: G, I, K).
- **GA1 One shared copy per string-table entry (#1).** `Header` keeps a lazy `OnceLock` per entry: `name_arc` (Windows-1252 decoded, `Arc<str>`) and `string_arc` (raw, `Arc<[u8]>`). `ShapeHead.name`, `ShapeModel.name` and `Sequence.name` are `Option<Arc<str>>`; `Extra.name`, the `CtrlBlock` strings and the text-key values stay raw bytes, now `Option<Arc<[u8]>>` (raw kept so their byte comparisons and the GUI's extra rows did not change). Judgement call: the brief asked for the ctrl.rs byte budget to become per file; it is removed instead: the reader keeps one shared copy per entry, so holding many references is cheap, and a per-file budget would refuse valid files with many sequences that the per-sequence one accepted. Decoding is the expensive part, so it is bounded where text is decoded or joined: `text::lossy_capped` stops at `text::DISPLAY_CAP` (64 KiB) and appends "…", never decoding past it, and `Sequence::text_keys_line` (the controller panel's "Text keys" line) uses it (fix round 1; test `text_key_line_is_capped`: 100k keys naming one 100 KB string). This supersedes the budget of B7 fix round 1 (B-P36): `sequence_strings_past_file_length_share_one_copy` (was `..._are_an_error`) and `text_keys_cannot_amplify_one_large_string` now assert one shared copy. No 64 KiB string cap (it could refuse valid files). The consumers keep the shared name too (fix round 1): `modscan::store::ShapeView.name` (the GUI's shape cards) and render3d's `ParsedShape`, `ShapeInfo`, `ShapeDraw` and the GUI's set-preview `ShapeRow` are `Option<Arc<str>>` / `Arc<str>`, so a shape card, a drawn shape or a preview row holds a pointer, not a copy. The scan store still writes the name once per row on disk (parked). Its readers intern names within one call (fix round 3): `shapes_of` and the texture-user `match_rows` (`MatchRow.shape_name`, now `Option<Arc<str>>`) read each row's name as a borrow and share one `Arc<str>` per distinct name, with a `HashSet` that lives for the call only. Not changed: `geom::av` and `props::object_net` names, `ExtraValue::Str` values, and the warning and error texts that name a shape (render3d `parse` writes one per skipped shape) still copy per block. Tests: `crates/nif/tests/string_amplification.rs` (scan, extras, sequences) and gui `shape_cards_share_one_name_across_many_shapes` (2000 shapes, one name allocation), and modscan `shapes_of_shares_one_name_across_rows` (2000 stored rows, one 100 KB name).
- **GA2 `read_model` pairs shape refs with shapes by index (#43).** `shape_refs` is pushed with `m.shapes`, so a zip replaces the per-shape search. Test: `read_model_is_linear_in_the_shape_count` (80k vs 10k shapes under 24x; measured about 8x, 66x before the fix at 16k vs 2k).
- **GA3 Validate decodes texture paths and BSX names as Windows-1252 (#44),** as apply compares and writes them, so the "Not relative to Data" fix applies and a non-ASCII BSXFlags name keeps its External_Emittance fix. One decoding policy (fix round 1): validate, apply's texture-path check and rebase all use `text::lossy` (Windows-1252, no BOM sniffing); apply and rebase used `WINDOWS_1252.decode`, which drops leading EF BB BF, so a slot starting with those bytes got a fix that always conflicted. Tests: `texture_path_fix_with_a_non_ascii_byte_applies`, `external_emittance_fix_with_a_non_ascii_bsx_name`, `texture_path_fix_with_leading_bom_bytes_applies`.
- **GA4 `CreateBlendState` maps its error with `gpu.fail`, and the env-cube error is wrapped with `with_context` (#37),** so both keep the `DEVICE_REMOVED` prefix the GUI rebuilds on. Fix round 1: one function builds the text, `device::gpu_error(removed, what, e)` (`removed` is the `GetDeviceRemovedReason` result): an `e` that already starts with the prefix keeps it with ` [what]` appended, else a removed device gives `device removed: reason (what: e)`, else `what: e`. `Gpu::fail`, `with_context` and both call sites use it; the env cube now calls `gpu.fail`, so it is prefixed even when its inner error was not. The blend-state site has a GPU-free seam, `blend_state_with` (the device calls passed in as closures): `a_blend_state_on_a_removed_device_keeps_the_prefix` fakes a `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED` create and fails if that site formats its own text. The env-cube site has no such seam (its error branch needs a device for the black fallback), so that half stays parked. Tests: `a_removed_device_error_starts_with_the_prefix`, `an_inner_removed_error_keeps_its_prefix` (synthetic `windows::core::Error`s; only the prefix and `what` are checked, the system message text is locale-dependent).
- **GA5 `diffuse_curve` without a white-mid gap (#27)** (`white - mid <= 1e-6`, or a non-finite result) gives the `FEATURE_FLOATS` default curve. Judgement call: the default, not 1.0, so a nonsensical hand-edited file previews like CS's defaults. Test: `diffuse_curve_without_a_white_mid_gap_keeps_the_default`.
- **GA6 `load_fixture` rejects an empty crop (`w == 0 || h == 0`) (#28)** with an Err naming mrt.json, before `seeded_depth` can reach `chunks_exact(0)`. Test: `load_fixture_refuses_a_zero_crop`.
- **GA7 A name inside a message kept per shape is a short label (#1, fix round 2).** `nif::text::label` keeps the first `text::LABEL_CAP` (256) chars and appends "…". `DISPLAY_CAP` is not used here: 64 KiB times 2000 shapes is still about 128 MB. Every per-shape message that names a shape uses it: render3d `parse`'s warnings, errors and `skipped` entries, `bind_textures`' two texture warnings, the failed-shape report line, the override-kind error, and the GUI's set-preview `ShapeRow::text` (rebuilt for every row). The shape's own `name` stays whole and shared (GA1). Before the fix, the hostile 2000-shape file (one 100 KB name) made 1.2 GB of message text. Tests: render3d `skipped_shape_messages_use_a_short_label` (under 4 MB, every label at most 256 chars plus "…") and nif `label_keeps_256_chars`.
